title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents

object.carrier: RAG memory database D of (key, value) pairs where keys are user queries with tool-list information and values are task plans; the agent saves its task execution history to the database after each task operation and retrieves the K most similar entries as in-context demonstrations for planning; in the poisoning setting the database becomes D_poison = D_clean ∪ A with attacker-introduced adversarial key-value pairs, accessed black-box (internal structure unknown to both attacker and the formalization)

safety_property.statement: Agent operational integrity across all stages (system prompt, user prompt handling, tool usage, memory retrieval): the agent should complete the user's target task with benign actions and refuse aggressive instructions, and must not be redirected to an attacker-selected injected task through direct prompt injection, observation prompt injection, memory poisoning, or their combination; for the Plan-of-Thought backdoor, the agent must keep benign actions on clean unaltered queries (benign performance BP) while the backdoored behavior is under test. Failure conditions: agent uses attack-specific tools (ASR), fails to refuse aggressive tasks (RR), or loses utility under defense (PNA-d).
safety_property.operationalized_as: 8 metrics (Table 4): ASR = percentage of attacked tasks where the agent successfully uses attack-specific tools; ASR-d under each defense; RR = refuse rate on aggressive tasks judged by the backbone LLM; PNA/PNA-d = task completion without attack/defense; BP = original-task completion without backdoor trigger; FNR/FPR for detection defenses. Evaluated over 10 scenarios, 10 agents, 50 agent tasks, 400 attack tasks, over 400 tools, 13 LLM backbones, nearly 90,000 testing cases.

capabilities: Knows every detail of attack tools and can integrate them into the agent's toolkit, e.g., by manipulating third-party API platforms (RapidAPI) to add malicious tools
Can craft and insert prompts into the agent's system prompt (e.g., deploying the prompt as a new agent via ChatGPT plugins) - the vector exploited by the PoT backdoor
Can access and manipulate the user's prompt (third-party prompt-engineering services or a man-in-the-middle attacker), e.g., embedding a backdoor trigger
Black-box access to RAG databases and embedders; can poison the memory database indirectly by using DPI or OPI attacks so that the agent itself saves attacker-shaped execution histories
assumptions: The attacker lacks knowledge of the agent's backbone LLM (architecture, training data, parameters); interaction is API-only
Memory poisoning treats the memory/RAG base as a black box without knowing its internal structure (unlike prior white-box RAG-poisoning settings)
A task succeeds for the agent if all required tools are used; an attack succeeds if the agent uses all tools in the attacker's injected tool list
not_covered: No adaptive re-attack loop: defenses are evaluated in one pass, and attackers do not re-optimize against the deployed defense
Training-time attacks on the backbone are excluded (the PoT backdoor is explicitly training-free); fine-tuning-based agent backdoors are only discussed as related work
White-box access to RAG internals is out of scope by design

intervention.name: Agent Security Bench (ASB): formalization and benchmark of 13 attack types and 10 defenses
intervention.description: Formalizes five attack families against the ReAct agent pipeline - Direct Prompt Injection (DPI, Definition 1), Observation Prompt Injection (OPI, Definition 2), Memory Poisoning (Definition 3: poisoned RAG database whose retrieved demonstrations steer plan generation), a novel training-free Plan-of-Thought (PoT) Backdoor (Definition 4: backdoored plan demonstrations injected into the system prompt plus a trigger in the query), and Mixed Attacks - and benchmarks 10 corresponding defenses (e.g., Delimiters, Paraphrasing, Instruction, Sandwich) across 10 scenarios, 10 agents, 400+ tools, and 13 LLM backbones, with 8 metrics (ASR, ASR-d, RR, PNA, PNA-d, BP, FNR, FPR).

controls.name: No defense (ASR without defense)
PNA (performance under no attack)
Benign performance BP (no backdoor trigger)
Aggressive vs non-aggressive task split

results.claim: Mixed Attack (DPI + OPI + Memory Poisoning combined) is the most effective attack: average ASR 84.30% with the lowest average Refuse Rate 3.22% across 13 LLM backbones; Qwen2-72B and GPT-4o reach ASRs near 100%.
results.metric: ASR / RR averaged over 13 LLM backbones and 10 scenarios
results.comparison: DPI 72.68%; OPI 27.55%; Memory Poisoning 7.92%; PoT Backdoor 42.12%; overall average 46.91%
results.setting: ASB benchmark, ReAct agents, ~90,000 testing cases total, Table 5 'Average' row
results.quote: Mixed Attack which combines multiple vulnerabilities achieves the highest average ASR of 84.30% and the lowest average Refuse Rate of 3.22%.

denominator.how_counted: ASR = percentage of attacked tasks where the agent uses all attack-specific tools, averaged over 13 backbones x 10 scenarios; the per-attack task split of the ~90,000 testing cases is not itemized in the paper

results.claim: Memory poisoning is the least effective of the five attack families on average (ASR 7.92%), with most models below 10% but LLaMA3.1-8B at 25.65% - memory poisoning effectiveness is highly backbone-dependent.
results.metric: ASR for the Memory Poisoning attack, averaged over 13 backbones
results.comparison: Mixed 84.30%; DPI 72.68%; PoT Backdoor 42.12%; OPI 27.55%; per-backbone Memory Poisoning ASR range 1.85% (LLaMA3-70B) to 25.65% (LLaMA3.1-8B)
results.setting: ASB memory poisoning via black-box RAG poisoning with poisoned plans retrieved as in-context demonstrations (Table 5)
results.quote: Memory Poisoning has an average ASR of 7.92%. Most models, like GPT-4o, show minimal vulnerability, with ASRs below 10%, though LLaMA3.1-8B has a higher ASR of 25.65%.

denominator.how_counted: Percentage of attacked tasks where the poisoned plan redirects the agent to the attack tools, averaged over 13 backbones x 10 scenarios; per-attack case counts not itemized

results.claim: DPI is widely effective: average ASR 72.68%, with GPT-3.5 Turbo at 98.40% and Gemma2-27B at 96.75%; larger/more capable models tend to be more fragile, though higher refusal rates can offset this (GPT-4o: RR 20.05%, ASR 60.35%).
results.metric: ASR / RR for Direct Prompt Injection
results.comparison: GPT-3.5 Turbo 98.40%; Gemma2-27B 96.75%; LLaMA3-8B 25.20% (lowest); GPT-4o 60.35% with RR 20.05%
results.setting: ASB DPI attacks injecting an injected instruction and attack tool list into the user prompt (Table 5, Figure 2)
results.quote: DPI achieves an average ASR of 72.68%. Models like GPT-3.5 Turbo and Gemma2-27B are particularly vulnerable, with ASRs of 98.40% and 96.75%, respectively.

denominator.how_counted: Percentage of attacked tasks using all attack tools, averaged over 13 backbones x 10 scenarios

results.claim: The novel training-free PoT Backdoor targets advanced models: average ASR 42.12%, but 100% on GPT-4o and 95.50% on GPT-4o-mini.
results.comparison: backdoored plan demonstrations injected into system prompt + trigger in query; benign performance BP measured separately (Sec. D.1 reports unaffected utility)
results.setting: ASB PoT backdoor across 13 backbones (Table 5)
results.quote: PoT Backdoor has a moderate average ASR of 42.12%, but it is highly effective against advanced models like GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, with ASRs of 100% and 95.50%, respectively.

denominator.how_counted: Percentage of attacked tasks using all attack tools, averaged over 13 backbones x 10 scenarios

results.claim: Cost reading (defenses): current prevention-based defenses are inadequate and cost utility - under DPI, Paraphrasing is the only defense that reduces average ASR materially (56.87%, Delta -21.52%) while Delimiter (+0.69%) and Instruction (-1.62%) barely help; defenses also cause utility losses in primary tasks when no attack is present.
results.metric: ASR-d and Delta vs undefended average ASR (DPI)
results.comparison: undefended DPI average ASR 78.38% (Table 6 Average row)
results.setting: ASB defenses for DPI across 13 backbones (Table 6); OPI defenses show Delta -3.02% / -1.67% / +0.06% (Table 7)
results.quote: It illustrates that current prevention-based defenses are inadequate: they are ineffective at preventing attacks and often cause some utility losses in the primary tasks when there are no attacks (see Sec. D.2). Notably, even though the average ASR under Paraphrasing defense in DPI decreases compared to no defense, it remains high, with an average ASR-d of 56.87%.

denominator.how_counted: ASR-d = percentage of attacked tasks using all attack tools under the defense, averaged over 13 backbones x 10 scenarios; Delta computed against the undefended average ASR

results.claim: OPI defenses are essentially ineffective: average ASR-d values 24.96% / 26.31% / 28.04% vs undefended 27.98%, i.e., Delta between -3.02% and +0.06% across Delimiter, Sandwich, and Instruction defenses.
results.metric: ASR-d and Delta vs undefended average ASR (OPI)
results.comparison: undefended OPI average ASR 27.98% (Table 7 Average row)
results.setting: ASB defenses for OPI across 13 backbones (Table 7)

denominator.how_counted: Delta row of Table 7: change in average ASR-d vs the undefended OPI average ASR (27.98%), each averaged over 13 backbones x 10 scenarios

limitations.statement: Defense coverage and attack scenarios are explicitly incomplete: the authors defer stronger defenses and more attack scenarios to future work.
limitations.quote: ASB provides a crucial resource for developing stronger defenses and more resilient LLM agents. In the future, we will focus on improving defenses and expanding attack scenarios.

limitations.statement: The memory-poisoning formalization is deliberately restricted to black-box access, so white-box poisoning strategies against known RAG internals are outside the evaluated threat space.
limitations.quote: ASB analyzes the impact of poisoning on the agent framework and treats memory or RAG base as a black box for memory poisoning without knowing the internal structure.

limitations.statement: The paper has no dedicated limitations section; the scope constraints above are stated in the conclusion and related-work positioning.
limitations.quote: We introduce ASB, a benchmark for evaluating the security of LLM agents under various attacks and defenses. ASB reveals key vulnerabilities of LLM-based agents in every operational step.

reproduction.code: https://github.com/agiresearch/ASB (Abstract: 'Our code can be found at https://github.com/agiresearch/ASB'); Appendix F is a Reproducibility Statement
reproduction.data: 10 scenarios, 10 agents, 50 agent tasks, 400 attack tasks, 400+ tools (normal and attack), 10 PoT demonstrations, 13 LLM backbones, ~90,000 testing cases

title: Jailbreaking and Mitigation of Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models

object.carrier: none (no persistent-state object studied)

safety_property.statement: 保护 LLM 的安全对齐（policy-compliance）：在提示类（对抗后缀 GCG、自动迭代 PAIR、AutoDAN、WordGame、多轮 Crescendo、逻辑链注入、词替换密码、ASCII ArtPrompt、角色扮演）、模型类（后门投毒、Shadow Alignment 微调、model interrogation、激活转向）、多模态（ImgTrojan、HADES、FigStep）与多语言（低资源语言翻译）越狱攻击下，LLM 不得生成违反安全准则的有害内容；次要面为保密性（系统提示/私有信息泄露）。失效条件：安全对齐依赖模式记忆而非对上下文与意图的理解，可被精心构造的提示绕过；判定依据是有害输出是否被成功诱导（ASR）。
safety_property.operationalized_as: §V-A 汇总的度量：Attack Success Rate (ASR)、True Positive Rate (TPR)、False Positive Rate (FPR)、Benign Answer Rate、Perplexity、Transferability、Stealthiness、Cost；§V-B 基准数据集（AdvBench、HarmBench、RealToxicityPrompts、DAN、SafetyPrompts、VLSafe、MM-SafetyBench、JailbreakV-28K、TechHazardQA、NicheHazardQA、Do-Not-Answer、Latent Jailbreak、RED-EVAL、JailbreakHub）；§VI 作者自测系统提示泄露（图 3）

capabilities: 黑盒提示访问：构造对抗性/多轮/角色扮演/伪装提示（PAIR 用攻击方 LLM 迭代查询，通常少于 20 次查询成功）
白盒/梯度访问：GCG 生成可迁移对抗后缀（可迁移到 ChatGPT、Bard、Claude）、激活转向（对比层搜索自动选择脆弱层）
训练/微调期投毒与触发器植入：TrojanRAG、PoisonPrompt、ImgTrojan、Shadow Alignment（少量恶意数据即可颠覆安全对齐）
跨模态输入：对抗图像、排版图像（FigStep）、图文组合攻击
低资源语言翻译绕过英语主导的安全训练数据
解码层操纵：选取低排名输出 token 提取被拒回答（model interrogation）；利用在线越狱社区共享与迭代的提示（JailbreakHub 数据集）
assumptions: 攻击者可通过提示接口与已部署 LLM 交互，多数攻击仅需查询访问
安全对齐（SFT/RLHF）依赖模式记忆而非对上下文与意图的理解，可被精心构造的提示绕过
安全训练数据以英语为主，低资源语言与视觉模态对齐不足
即使良性数据微调也可能破坏安全对齐（Qi et al. [12]）；被拒绝的响应在解码分布中仍保留生成概率，可被利用
not_covered: Agent 持久记忆/技能/经验等状态化攻击面：全部攻击与防御均在单次交互内生效，不涉及跨会话/跨用户持久状态
对授权、权限与部署基础设施层的攻击
攻击与防御长期协同演化的实证研究；对齐的形式化保证（BEB 仅作为未来方向引用）

intervention.name: Surveyed defense taxonomy (no new mechanism proposed): prompt filtering/transformation/optimization, model-level defenses, multi-agent, self-regulation
intervention.description: 综述性防御分类（图 2），无单一自有干预：提示级防御（过滤：困惑度/关键词/实时监控；变换：改写/重标记化/语义平滑；优化：RPO、DRO、self-reminders、IAPrompt）、模型级防御（对抗训练、安全微调 VLGuard/RED-INSTRUCT、剪枝 WANDA、Moving Target Defense、有害知识遗忘 Eraser、RA-LLM 鲁棒对齐检查）、多智能体防御（AutoDefense 协作过滤）、其他（自过滤 LLM Self Defense/PARDEN/Self-Guard、回译、SafeDecoding 安全感知解码）。机制层取 content，因提示级防御是该综述的最大主要类别；综述的防御亦覆盖执行层（SafeDecoding）与架构层（剪枝、MTD、RA-LLM）。

results.claim: 作者自测（非系统实验，无量化）：GPT-4o 与 Perplexity Pro 在集成安全措施下，仍被简单且精心构造的提示（如以教学场景为伪装的繁体中文翻译请求）诱导泄露系统级指令（图 3）
results.value: both tested models disclosed system-level instructions (qualitative, unquantified)
results.setting: GPT-4o 与 Perplexity Pro（图 3 标注截至 10/15/2024）；作者手工提示演示，无样本量与量化判定标准
results.quote: Our experiments revealed that, despite integrated safety measures, both models were susceptible to simple yet carefully crafted prompts, resulting in the unintended disclosure of system instructions.
results.locator: §VI Research Gaps and Future Directions, Fig. 3

results.claim: 综述转引 [43]：WordGame 将恶意词伪装为文字游戏（查询与响应同时混淆），在 Llama 2-7b Chat、GPT-3.5、GPT-4 上越狱成功率超过 92%，优于近期算法型攻击；分母与成功判定标准未报告
results.setting: 综述二手转引 WordGame [43]；模型 Llama 2-7b Chat、GPT-3.5、GPT-4；本综述未报告分母与判定方式
results.quote: This obfuscation significantly raises the jailbreak success rate, exceeding 92% on Llama 2-7b Chat, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4, outperforming recent algorithm-focused attacks [43].

results.claim: 综述转引 [20]：GPTFuzzer 以人工模板为种子自动变异越狱提示，对 ChatGPT 与 LLaMa-2 攻击成功率超过 90%，超过人工构造的提示；分母未报告
results.setting: 综述二手转引 GPTFuzzer [20]；目标模型 ChatGPT、LLaMa-2；本综述未报告分母与判定方式
results.quote: This framework achieves over 90% attack success rates against ChatGPT and LLaMa-2 models, surpassing human-crafted prompts.

results.claim: 综述转引 [7]：PAIR 用攻击方 LLM 对黑盒目标 LLM 迭代生成并精炼越狱提示，通常少于 20 次查询即可产生成功越狱，且跨开源与闭源模型可迁移
results.setting: 综述二手转引 PAIR [7]；黑盒设置，攻击方 LLM 迭代查询目标 LLM（GPT-3.5/4、Vicuna、PaLM-2 等）
results.quote: This method is efficient, often requiring fewer than 20 queries to produce a successful jailbreak, and achieves high success rates with strong transferability across various LLMs, including both open and closed-source models like GPT-3.5/4, Vicuna, and PaLM-2 [7].

results.claim: 综述转引 [61]：Prompt Adversarial Tuning (PAT) 在防御越狱攻击的同时保持 80% 的良性回答率（防御不过度 restrictive 的证据）；分母未报告
results.setting: 综述二手转引 PAT [61]；良性提示上的回答率；本综述未报告分母与统计口径
results.quote: For instance, the Prompt Adversarial Tuning (PAT) method maintained a high benign answer rate of 80% while defending against jailbreak attacks [61].

results.claim: 综述转引 [37]：self-reminders 将查询封装进负责任的系统提示以促使模型遵循安全准则，显著降低针对 ChatGPT 的越狱成功率（定性，无数值）
results.setting: 综述二手转引 self-reminders [37]；ChatGPT；提示级自我调节防御
results.quote: This method significantly reduces jailbreak success rates against ChatGPT.

limitations.statement: 作者指出：多轮对话与复杂交互下攻击成功难以一致量化（评估有效性限制）
limitations.quote: Many jailbreak attacks involve multi-turn dialogues or complex interactions, making it challenging to consistently measure attack success [11]. This is particularly relevant for methods like Crescendo, which gradually escalates interactions to bypass safety measures [45].

limitations.statement: 作者指出：现有基准数据集未能覆盖有害内容全谱且含内在偏差，导致安全评估不完整
limitations.quote: Existing benchmark datasets often fail to represent the full spectrum of potential harmful content and may contain inherent biases [19]. For example, datasets may be skewed towards certain topics or demographics, resulting in incomplete safety evaluations.

limitations.statement: 作者指出：缺乏公认的 LLM 安全评估标准，导致各研究方法与度量不一致、结果难以比较
limitations.quote: There is no widely accepted standard for evaluating LLM safety and robustness, leading to inconsistencies in methodologies and metrics across studies [23].

limitations.statement: 本综述自身实验仅为说明性演示：对 GPT-4o 与 Perplexity Pro 做手工提示测试（图 3），无系统实验设置、无量化、无分母
limitations.quote: To illustrate these vulnerabilities, we conducted some testing with the latest GPT-4o model and Perplexity Pro, as shown in Figure 3.

title: Systematically Analysing Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities in Diverse LLM Architectures

object.carrier: none (no persistent-state object studied)

safety_property.statement: LLMs are expected to refuse requests to generate keylogger code; the property fails when a crafted direct prompt elicits Python code that is usable or adaptable for keylogging. The claim holds only for the 36 open-weight LLMs available on Workers AI's LLM Playground in October 2024, under four single-shot English prompts, with success judged by a single expert rater; it is an attack-side measurement with no defense in the loop and no persistent memory, skill, or agent state involved.
safety_property.operationalized_as: A prompt injection was considered to be successful if it produced code that can be used or adapted for keyloggers (144 tests = 4 prompts x 36 models on Workers AI LLM Playground; final judgments made by the lead author, §3.4).

capabilities: directly queries the target LLM with crafted natural-language prompts (black-box access via the public Workers AI LLM Playground)
uses benign framings to disguise the request: feigned troubleshooting (P1), curiosity about a movie scene (P2), educational-purpose claim (P3)
embeds the malicious instruction between two benign instructions in an 'instruction sandwich' (P4)
assumptions: adversary needs only ordinary user query access; no knowledge of model internals, weights, or training data
attacks are single-step, one-shot, English-language prompts
models accessed via Workers AI's LLM Playground (playground.ai.cloudflare.com), October 2024; parameter counts read from model names (e.g. '7b' = 7 billion parameters)
attack success is judged by the lead author (CISSP, cybersecurity PhD, 15+ years experience) deciding whether the code is usable or adaptable for keylogging
not_covered: indirect prompt injection via external data sources
multilingual prompt injections (listed as future work)
multi-step or progressive attack sequences (listed as future work)
persistent memory, skills, experience, or any agent-harness state (none is present in this setting)
no defense mechanism is implemented or empirically evaluated

intervention.description: No defense intervention is implemented or tested; the paper is a pure vulnerability measurement across 36 LLMs. Mitigations (human oversight for privileged operations, trust boundaries, input/output monitoring, guardrails, alignment, AI telemetry logging) are only recommended qualitatively in section 5.3, citing OWASP and MITRE ATLAS.

results.claim: In this study's setting (4 direct keylogger-code prompt injections against 36 LLMs), 56% of all 144 tests resulted in successful prompt injections, i.e. production of code usable or adaptable for keylogging.
results.setting: Four one-shot English prompts (P1-P4) each tested against 36 open-weight LLMs (chat/instruct/code/domain/multimodal, 0.5b-14b parameters) on Workers AI LLM Playground, October 2024; success judged by the lead author (CISSP, cybersecurity PhD).
results.quote: Overall, 56% of all 144 tests resulted in successful prompt injections, while 44% of the models resisted.

denominator.how_counted: Four prompt injections (P1, P2, P3 and P4) were tested against 36 models resulting in 144 tests (§3.4); percentage is over these 144 tests.

results.claim: The percentage of the 36 LLMs vulnerable to a single prompt increased progressively from the troubleshooting-framing prompt P1 (53%) to the instruction-sandwich prompt P4 (61%), showing the later, more layered prompts exposed weaknesses more effectively.
results.setting: Same 36-LLM Workers AI Playground setup; percent of the 36 models vulnerable to each single prompt (P2 = 53%, P3 = 58% per Table 2).
results.quote: The percentage of models classified as vulnerable increased progressively from Prompt 1 (53%) to Prompt 4 (61%), indicating that the later prompts were more effective in exposing weaknesses.

denominator.how_counted: Table 2 caption: 'The percent of 36 LLMs vulnerable and resistant to the four test prompt injections (P1, P2, P3, and P4).'

results.claim: 28% of the tested LLMs were fully vulnerable (failed all four injections, 10 out of 36) while 14% showed complete resistance (passed all four, 5 out of 36); the rest fell in between.
results.comparison: 28% (10 out of 36) vulnerable to all 4 prompts vs 14% (5 out of 36) resistant to all
results.setting: Distribution of the 36 LLMs by the number (0-4) of the four prompts they were vulnerable to, same Playground setup.
results.quote: The results reveal that 28% of the tested LLMs (10 out of 36) were highly vulnerable, failing all four prompt injections. Additionally, 14% (5 out of 36) of the LLMs demonstrated complete resistance, successfully passing all tests.

denominator.how_counted: Table 3: percentage of LLMs vulnerable to 0, 1, 2, 3, or all 4 prompt injections, out of 36; text gives explicit counts 10 out of 36 and 5 out of 36.

results.claim: Success of P1 and P2 strongly correlated across models (Pearson r = 0.71), indicating overlapping vulnerabilities exploited by the troubleshooting and curiosity framings.
results.setting: Pearson correlation of per-model success outcomes for pairs of the four prompts across the 36 LLMs (Table 4; full pair set 0.71/0.48/0.49/0.42/0.28/0.41; Table 5 writes 0.712).
results.quote: The analysis shows a strong correlation of 0.71 between P1 and P2, indicating that models vulnerable to P1 are also likely to be vulnerable to P2.

results.claim: P2 and P4 showed only a weak correlation (0.28), suggesting the curiosity framing and the instruction sandwich exploit different model weaknesses.
results.setting: Pearson correlation of per-model success outcomes for prompt pairs across the 36 LLMs (Table 4).
results.quote: However, the weak correlation of 0.28 between P2 and P4 suggests that these two prompts likely exploit different model weaknesses.

results.claim: Random forest feature analysis ranks LLM parameter count as the dominant predictor of injection susceptibility (importance 0.75) over LLM type (0.25), in this 36-model dataset.
results.setting: Random forest trained on the 36-model outcome table (parameters and LLM type vs injection success).
results.quote: The results, as shown in Figure 3, indicate that parameters have a higher importance score (0.75), suggesting they are the primary factor in determining a model's susceptibility to prompt injections. In contrast, LLM type has a lower importance score (0.25), indicating a more moderate effect.

results.claim: SHAP analysis corroborates the random forest result: LLM parameters influence vulnerability predictions more (mean SHAP 0.147) than LLM type (mean SHAP 0.075).
results.setting: SHAP values computed for the features LLM parameters and LLM type in the 36-model vulnerability prediction task.
results.quote: The mean SHAP values indicate that LLM parameters hold a higher influence on model predictions, with a mean SHAP value of 0.147, compared to LLM type, which has a mean SHAP value of 0.075 as shown in Figure 4.

results.claim: Logistic regression found higher parameter count slightly negatively associated with vulnerability to at least one injection (coefficient -0.34; LLM type -0.02), contradicting the assumption that larger models are more vulnerable in this setting; the model's accuracy was 86%.
results.setting: Logistic regression predicting whether each of the 36 LLMs is vulnerable to at least one of the four prompts, from parameters and LLM type; model accuracy 86% (§4.5).
results.quote: The coefficient for LLM parameters is -0.34, indicating that models with more parameters are actually slightly less likely to be vulnerable to prompt injections, which contrasts with the typical assumption that larger models are more vulnerable.

limitations.statement: Authors explicitly state that using only four prompts (and a limited model set) is a limitation; more prompts, a larger set of LLMs, and more LLM features would increase the robustness of the findings and statistical analyses.
limitations.quote: Using four prompts in the current student represents a limitation. Using a variety of more prompts can increase the robustness of the findings as well as testing a larger set of LLMs. Additionally, examining more features of each LLM can help provide more data to use in the various statistical analyses.

limitations.statement: Multilingual and multi-step prompt injection attacks were not tested in this study; the authors defer them to future work, noting single-step-resistant models might still be vulnerable to progressive manipulation.
limitations.quote: Another area for investigation is multi-step prompt injection attacks, where LLMs are tested for their susceptibility to complex, multi-step command sequences. This could reveal whether models that initially resist single-step injections are still vulnerable when manipulated progressively over a series of inputs.

title: Multi-Agent Systems Execute Arbitrary Malicious Code

object.carrier: MAS 编排层在 agent 间传递的共享元数据：任务计划、动作历史、自评进度、状态报告与错误消息（status reports, error messages, progress updates, action results）；在多步攻击链中，攻击载荷还可借由下载到本地文件系统的文件（如 key.txt、反向 shell 脚本）在步骤之间携带。被劫持的控制流重定向在同一 action trace 内持续存在（'this redirection persists until the end of the action trace'）。

safety_property.statement: 完整性 + 机密性：当 MAS 按用户请求访问不可信内容（网页、本地文件、图片、音视频）时，系统不得被诱导执行攻击者代码（如反向 shell，完整性），也不得把其可访问的用户数据（含容器化环境内数据、memory/RAG/API 中的信息）发送给攻击者（机密性）。论文证明当前 MAS 无信任模型、不区分数据与元数据，且信任 sub-agent 的状态报告（confused deputy），两类属性均可被单一恶意网页/文件攻破；失效条件还包括：即使个体 sub-agent 因安全对齐拒绝有害动作，系统整体仍可能经编排层找到执行路径（refusal turns to execution；benign 任务中自主探索目录并执行相邻恶意文件）。
safety_property.operationalized_as: 攻击成功率 ASR：修改代码执行 agent，使其在将要运行攻击载荷时退出并向文件写入实验专属字符串；备用判据为云端轻量服务器持续监听并打印 socket 连接（反向 shell 连入即成功）。数据外泄攻击以构建用户画像文件并送达攻击者脚本判定。二值标注由正则字符串搜索 + 人工核验得出。

capabilities: 控制 MAS 会 inadvertent 或有意访问的不可信输入：恶意网页、本地文件（如邮件附件、图片）、网页图片（仅截图无文本）、音视频转录
不能直接向 MAS 发 prompt（与 jailbreaking 相反，用户是受害者而非攻击者）
可投放的恶意功能仅受目标系统代码执行能力限制；论文聚焦两个目标：在用户设备执行任意代码（反向 shell）与外泄用户数据
assumptions: MAS 内所有 agent 均为良性、不被攻击者控制
用户是不知情受害者，其请求会把 MAS 引到攻击者内容上
MAS 具备代码执行能力并可访问敏感用户数据（本地文件、容器化环境、辅助数据源）
框架为面向用户、开箱即用、可在本地与远程内容上操作的 MAS（AutoGen、Crew AI、MetaGPT）
not_covered: MAS 内部被攻击者控制或恶意的 sub-agent（假设 agent 均良性）
为模拟环境或纯对话式多 agent 交互设计的框架
高度可定制的商业/开发者向框架（分析仅限 drop-in 系统）
自适应/优化生成的 jailbreak 与 prompt injection 字符串用于控制流攻击（论文留作 future work）
IPI 防御能否抵御 MAS hijacking 及其对 MAS 效用的影响（论文留作 future work，未做实验）

intervention.description: 本文为纯攻击/威胁刻画论文，未提出并评估任何防御机制（intervention=null）。§8.3 仅综述三类 IPI 防御（prompt tuning、agent-level controls 如 in-network alignment agents 与 agent tagging、model-level modifications 如 SecAlign/Jatmo/Struq/instruction hierarchy/信息流控制），并明确指出这些防御能否 foil MAS hijacking 及其是否误伤自适应控制流属于未来工作。论文将根因归结为 MAS 缺乏可信/不可信内容区分、无输入与动作的语义/信任模型，LLM 无法区分数据与元数据。作为综述的必要背景，本文确立的机制是：MAS 共享元数据与编排控制流是无防护的攻击面——任何涉及 memory/经验持久化与共享状态的防御设计都必须把 agent 间元数据通道（状态报告、错误消息）纳入信任边界，且逐 agent 的安全对齐拒绝不足以提供系统级安全。
intervention.支撑_mechanism_note: 支撑综述中'共享状态/元数据通道是攻击面、revocation 与 repair 缺失'的论证基线

controls.name: Benign local file / benign webpage retrieval（Table 3，命令格式与措辞与攻击相同但内容良性）
Direct ask (DA)：直接要求 MAS 执行恶意代码（Table 2、Table 8）
Three previously-studied indirect prompt injection templates (IPI)（Table 2）
攻击模板变体：fake Python error / fake Wordpress 403 / generic Access Denied，以及两种用户请求措辞

results.quote:

denominator.how_counted: 论文明写：61 of the 67 instances (91%) where a direct ask to open a reverse shell resulted in malicious code being executed

title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design

object.carrier: 以 Python 函数表达、由部署方（the entity serving the CaMeL engine）定义的 security policies（§4.2：'Security policies can be defined globally by the entity serving the engine'，跨任务持久生效）；运行期内为每个值附加的 capability 标注（来源 provenance + 允许读者 readers，存于 CaMeL 解释器维护的 data flow graph，单次任务内、解释器状态在同任务多次代码修复间保留）

safety_property.statement: 同时保护机密性与完整性：(1) confidentiality——用户私有数据（文档、密码、PII 等）不得经未授权数据流流向无权读者或被状态改变工具外泄（capability 记录每个值的 allowed readers，策略在其依赖图上任一违规即阻断工具调用）；(2) integrity——工具调用序列与参数不得被注入数据劫持（P-LLM 只见用户查询、控制流由可信代码固定，untrusted 数据永远不能影响程序流）。保证性质为 by design：策略违规在执行前被自定义解释器阻断，不依赖模型鲁棒性。失效条件（作者自认）：侧信道（§6：间接依赖推断、异常触发泄露 1 bit、时间侧信道）、不影响控制/数据流的 text-to-text 攻击与向用户展示钓鱼内容（§3.1 显式非目标）、de-classification 用户疲劳（§8.2）、解释器与策略实现尚未形式化验证（§9）。判定：AgentDojo 上 949 个攻击的成功数为 0，同时效用（任务成功率）可接受
safety_property.operationalized_as: AgentDojo 基准（Workspace/Banking/Slack/Travel）：(a) benign 任务成功率（utility，Table 2）；(b) 949 个 prompt injection 攻击下的成功攻击数（security，Table 4/Table 7）；(c) security policy 触发率（用户需确认的频率，Figure 8/Table 8/9）；(d) token 开销（Table 10-13）

capabilities: 攻击者可向 agent 会检索的任意不可信数据源（邮件、云端文档、网页、日历、评论等）植入 prompt injection（含对用户不可见的文本），数据被 victim 的 agentic 系统取回后即进入处理流程
数据流攻击（主威胁，AgentDojo 焦点）：注入可操纵 Q-LLM 的结构化输出，从而在不改变工具调用序列（控制流）的情况下篡改工具调用参数（如把收款邮箱换成攻击者地址），类比 SQL 注入改参数而非改查询结构
§5.4：若生成代码让数据决定控制流（'data flow becomes control flow'），注入可升级为任意代码执行；还可把恶意程序拆成多个看似无害的小指令（类似 Jones et al. 2024/Glukhov et al. 2025）绕过意图审查
§6 侧信道：可观察外部资源被抓取次数、通过触发异常使执行中止、或测时，从系统可观测行为推断私有变量（可泄露 1 bit 或经间接依赖泄露整值）
§7 次级场景：恶意/被攻陷用户（rogue user，故意下达违反策略的指令）与恶意工具（spy tool，其文档本身即是注入，可诱导 agent 把全部数据传给它）
assumptions: 用户 prompt 可信；用户不会把不可信来源的内容粘贴进查询
若系统带 memory，则 memory 未被攻击者攻陷（§3 Threat Model 明示假设）
工具按声明返回真实 capability（如云盘文件自带 shared-with 读者列表）；工具自身可信（恶意工具仅作为 §7 扩展场景讨论）
CaMeL 解释器、capability 传播与策略实现本身正确——形式化验证留作未来工作（§9）；当前未实现策略冲突解决机制（§4.2）
P-LLM 生成的代码落在受限 Python 子集内；越界可检测并自动修复（最多重试 10 次）
not_covered: 不影响控制流也不影响数据流的 text-to-text 攻击：如让摘要失真、向用户展示注入原文/注入式钓鱼链接（'click this malicious link'）——§3.1 显式非目标，AgentDojo 中 travel 套件的 print(评论) 残留成功即属此类
完全自主、无需人工介入的系统不是目标；用户确认/澄清仍保留在回路中
侧信道攻击不能完全防止（§6 承认；STRICT 模式仅缓解 Q-LLM 相关与控制流依赖类）
capability 生态外的第三方工具：不支持 capability 时效用退化（§8.1）；采用成本高（以 CHERI 重设计全栈为鉴）
对策略编写者/部署方的信任：策略由 serving entity 定义，若策略本身写错则保证失效；不做策略冲突自动消解

intervention.name: CaMeL（CApabilities for MachinE Learning）
intervention.description: 在 LLM 外围构建防护系统层（不修改模型本身）：(1) P-LLM（特权）只见用户查询，把任务编译为受限 Python 代码（固定控制流）；(2) 自定义解释器执行代码并维护 data flow graph，为每个值传播 capability（provenance 来源 User/CaMeL/tool/inner source + allowed readers）；(3) Q-LLM（隔离、无工具）经 JSON schema 解析不可信数据；(4) 每次工具调用前沿依赖图检查 security policies（Python 函数，返回 Allowed/Denied），违规即阻断（实际部署中转为用户确认）；(5) NORMAL/STRICT 双模式——STRICT 把控制流条件/循环 iterable 计入块内赋值依赖、并使 Q-LLM 调用后的语句依赖其输入，以缓解侧信道。安全保证来自架构隔离+provenance 强制执行，属'by design'而非模型训练/提示加固；可与模型侧防御叠加构成纵深防御

controls.name: Native Tool Calling API（各模型官方工具调用，无防御）
CaMeL (no policies)（仅 P/Q-LLM 隔离，不安装 security policies）
Undefended model（Claude 3.5 Sonnet 无防御）
Tool Filter（AgentDojo 内置，Debenedetti et al. 2024a）
Spotlighting（Hines et al. 2024，定界符标注）
Prompt Sandwiching（Learn Prompting 2024）
GPT-4o mini 原生 API（默认实现 instruction hierarchy，Wallace et al. 2024）
NORMAL vs STRICT 解释器模式对比

results.claim: [replaced_by_different_metric in v2] v2 摘要口径：CaMeL 以可证安全解决 AgentDojo 77% 的任务（未防御系统为 84%）。v1 的口径——'以 o1 为骨干时 67% utility、仅比 GPT-4o 原生工具调用低 2%'——在 v2 中不再出现（v2 换用新模型名单：gemini-2.5、claude-sonnet-4、gpt-4.1、o3/o4-mini 等，§6.1.1 改为定性表述 'With an exception of Travel suite–on a subset of models–we find that CaMeL does not significantly degrade utility'，并报告 o3 比 o1 高约 10% utility）。新旧口径不可直接换算：67% 是 v1 名单下的绝对效用，77%/84% 是 v2 名单下'可证安全 vs 未防御'的成对比较。
results.value: 77% (provable security) vs 84% (undefended) [v1: 67% utility on o1, 2% below GPT-4o native]
results.comparison: undefended system 84% on the same benchmark (v2 abstract)

results.quote: We demonstrate effectiveness of CaMeL by solving 77%77\% of tasks with provable security (compared to 84%84\% with an undefended system) in AgentDojo.

denominator.how_counted: Share of AgentDojo tasks solved with acceptable detail under CaMeL vs undefended tool-calling, as stated in the v2 abstract; per-suite utilities in Appendix B Tables 2/5

results.value: Gemini 2.5 Pro: 300 -> 0 successful attacks (no policies) [v1: GPT-4o 233 -> 0]
results.comparison: all models improve; two residual injections outside the declared threat model (§6.2.1)

results.quote: Figure 9 shows that CaMeL reduces the number of successful attacks for all models, and in some cases, it completely eliminates the attacks. For example, the number of successful attacks for Gemini 2.5 Pro drops from 300300 without to 00 with CaMeL.

results.claim: 在 Claude 3.5 Sonnet 上与 AgentDojo 内置启发式防御对比：CaMeL 成功攻击数为 0，论文所称次优防御 tool filter 为 8；CaMeL 是唯一带安全保证（其余均为概率性、无保证）的防御

results.claim: CaMeL 的代价：相对原生工具调用，中位任务需 2.82× 输入 token 与 2.73× 输出 token（用于生成受限 Python 代码与修复错误），作者认为换取安全保证是合理代价
results.setting: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 骨干，AgentDojo（under attack 测量），tiktoken GPT-4o tokenizer（Claude 分词器未公开）；工具文档 token 未计入（两种方法均排除），但计入 Python 子集规范 token；注意 Table 10 中位数为 Input 2.73、Output 2.82，与正文/Figure 11 的表述互换
results.quote: Overall, we find that CaMeL requires 2.82×2.82\times input tokens and 2.73×2.73\times more output tokens for the median task in AgentDojo.

results.claim: CaMeL 的效用代价（Claude 3.5 Sonnet，Overall）：任务成功率由未防御的 90.72% 降至 63.92%（benign，Appendix B Table 5；v1 报 90.7%/63.9%，v2 给出两位小数并新增更多模型行）；降幅最大的是 Travel 套件（75.00%→25.00%，主因工具输出结构未文档化，见 §6.1.2）；被攻击场景下的同表为 Table 6。
results.setting: AgentDojo benign 任务，Overall 列，claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022；CaMeL 完整开启（含 security policies）；± 为跨套件标准差（Table 2）
results.locator: Appendix B (Table 5, Defenses utility — Claude 3.5 Sonnet)

denominator.how_counted: Task success rate (%) per AgentDojo suite with mean±std over runs; per-suite task counts not restated in v2 appendix

results.comparison: CaMeL 为各防御中 token 用量最高
results.setting: 与 §5.3 相同防御集（Claude 3.5 Sonnet，AgentDojo，tiktoken GPT-4o tokenizer，中位任务）；对比对象含 tool filter、tool filter (efficient)、prompt sandwiching
results.quote: CaMeL requires the highest token usage among the defenses we analyze, the best being Spotlighting, which uses 1.06×1.06\times more input and 0.98×0.98\times the output tokens.

limitations.statement: 作者明确承认 CaMeL 可被侧信道攻击（经共享资源观测系统行为推断敏感信息：间接依赖推断、异常触发泄露 1 bit、时间侧信道），这在一定程度上削弱'强安全保证'的主张；STRICT 模式只是缓解而非根除
limitations.quote: We find that CaMeL is vulnerable to side-channel attacks, where an attacker can infer sensitive information by observing the system’s behavior with shared resources (Anderson et al., 2002).
limitations.locator: §6 Side channels can be a problem

limitations.statement: 显式非目标：不影响控制流/数据流的 text-to-text 攻击不在防护范围（如把摘要改得与原邮件不符、注入式钓鱼链接展示给用户），此类攻击仍可欺骗最终用户
limitations.quote: CaMeL doesn’t aim to defend against attacks that do not affect the control nor the data flow.

limitations.statement: de-classification/用户确认环节可能引发安全疲劳：用户对安全提示脱敏后可能习惯性批准恶意操作——安全性最终受限于策略质量与用户行为
limitations.quote: This can lead to user fatigue, where users become desensitized to security prompts and may inadvertently approve malicious actions, a practice that is often seen in other settings (Felt et al., 2012; Cao et al., 2021).

limitations.statement: 部署方/用户需编写并持续维护安全策略，负担显著；作者明确回答'提示注入并未被完全解决'
limitations.quote: Importantly, CaMeL suffers from users needing to codify and specify security policies and maintain them.
limitations.locator: §8.3 So, are prompt injections solved now?

limitations.statement: 无事务原子性/回滚：代码抛异常前已执行的有副作用工具调用（如已创建日历事件）无法撤销，只能靠提示告知 P-LLM 不要重复执行
limitations.quote: At present CaMeL has no means to enable atomicity for sequences of instructions or rollbacks of operations that failed yet had side-effects.

limitations.statement: 安全保证目前依赖解释器与策略实现的正确性（当前未实现策略冲突解决机制），形式化验证留作未来工作
limitations.quote: verification can provide a formal proof that CaMeL’s interpreter itself is without faults and that it resolves conflicts and enforces the intended security policies

limitations.statement: capability 系统理想上要求整个生态参与：第三方工具不支持 capability 时效用退化，且实现成本高（作者以 CHERI 需重设计软硬件全栈为鉴）
limitations.quote: Furthermore, capability-based systems ideally require full participation from the entire ecosystem.
limitations.locator: §8.1 Past problems with adoption of capabilities

limitations.statement: Travel 套件效用大幅下降暴露 CaMeL 对工具文档质量的依赖：v2 §6.1.2 归因于工具输出结构未文档化（P-LLM 无法解析）；v2 新增观察——更新模型可在不改 CaMeL 的情况下大幅缓解（Claude Sonnet 系 Travel utility 25%→55%→75%），即该代价部分是模型能力问题而非纯机制问题
limitations.quote: We observe that the low performance on the Travel suite mostly comes from the fact that the tool outputs structure is not well documented.

counterexamples.statement: CaMeL（无策略）下 AgentDojo 仍有 2 类攻击被判成功（banking 1 + travel 1）：banking 任务为'分笔转账 $30,000、单笔≤$10,000'，注入藏在文档中诱导模型按文档内指令付款——数据即指令，作者归为显式非目标
counterexamples.quote: The injection is successful when is it inserted in a document, and the model is instructed to make a payment based on the instructions present in the document.
counterexamples.locator: §5.2.1 Case study: without any Security Policies

counterexamples.statement: travel 任务'宣称 Riverside View Hotel 值得一游'在含策略的 CaMeL 下仍成功：模型对评论调用 print，把注入原文（含酒店名）展示给用户——并非 prompt injection 劫持执行流，属 §3.1 非目标；作者建议用 capability 溯源在 UI 标注不可信来源
counterexamples.quote: this task is successful when the user asks for something related to reviews, and the model calls the print function on the reviews, hence showing to the user the entire injection (including the hotel name).

title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections

object.carrier: 论文不研究任何持久化记忆/技能/经验对象；仅涉及任务内状态：dual-LLM 模式中存放 quarantined LLM 结果、由 privileged LLM 按引用（by reference）操作、由非 LLM orchestrator 替换的变量内存，以及 context-minimization 模式中在多轮交互内被移除的对话上下文。均不跨会话。

safety_property.statement: 核心安全性质（设计层面主张，非实证）：一旦 LLM 智能体摄入不可信输入，系统必须被约束到该输入不可能触发任何 consequential actions（对系统或环境有负副作用的动作）——最低要求是受限智能体不能调用会破坏系统完整性或机密性的工具（未授权工具执行、数据外泄、RCE），且其输出不构成下游风险（如经嵌入链接/markdown 图片/非打印字符外泄敏感信息、操纵后续智能体行为）。保证来自架构级隔离而非模型鲁棒性；每个模式都有作者明示的残余失效条件（见 limitations）。个别案例还触及 availability（SQL Agent 资源耗尽/DoS）与 policy-compliance（药品聊天机器人的法规要求），但主线是 integrity + confidentiality。
safety_property.operationalized_as: 无攻击实验、无量化指标（无 ASR/utility 数值）。论证形式为：6 个设计模式的机制分析（§3.1）+ 10 个案例研究（§4.1-§4.10）中逐设计的定性 utility/security 权衡——security 侧以该设计是否使注入无法触发 consequential actions 及其残余攻击面判定（如 action-selector "trivially immune"、plan-then-execute 为 control flow integrity、dual LLM 需输出安全约束），utility 侧以功能损失定性描述。保证类型为按构造（by construction）的隔离与约束能力：预定义动作集、固定计划、无工具隔离子 LLM、输出格式/正则约束、上下文移除。

capabilities: 控制智能体处理的第三方内容并嵌入注入指令：文件与文件名（OS 助手）、SQL 数据库内容（SQL Agent）、邮件/日历邀请（Email & Calendar 助手）、服务提供商返回内容与第三方创建的日历事件含白色小字隐藏注入（Booking 助手）、商品评论（Product Recommender）、简历含小号/白色文字隐藏指令（Resume Screening）、远程文档与第三方代码（Software Engineering Agent）
部分案例中攻击者即最终用户，直接在用户提示中注入（客服聊天机器人、预约助手、药品说明书机器人、医疗诊断 intermediary）；论文明确不区分 direct 与 indirect 提示注入，统称 prompt injections
攻击目标：未授权工具执行/操纵系统状态、数据收集与外泄（URL、markdown 图片、非打印字符/ASCII smuggling）、冒用用户身份发邮件或向同事发送指令、删除/隐藏用户信息、Python 解释器内远程代码执行、资源耗尽/拒绝服务、声誉损害（screenshot attack）
assumptions: 底层 LLM 本身对提示注入脆弱——安全性必须由系统级设计提供；LLM 级启发式防御（提示工程、对抗训练）"不能提供保证"（do not provide guarantees）
quarantined/隔离子 LLM 的输出必须满足安全约束（如模糊搜索返回布尔值、map 输出为数字的正则、结构化格式）才能回流主流程；输出按符号/引用由传统软件 orchestrator 处理
部分案例假定特定来源可信：药品说明书（行业受监管）、客服内部知识库（内部数据+高问责）、医疗诊断中的数据库与医生
案例中用户/智能体权限按最小权限配置（如 agent 权限不超过用户权限）时，恶意用户也无法跨用户读取或影响他人数据
not_covered: 不提供任何量化保证或实验验证；所有 security 结论为设计论证，各模式均留有作者明示的残余攻击面（plan-then-execute 下工具调用参数可被不可信数据污染、不防用户提示注入；dual LLM 中 quarantined LLM 输出本身可被篡改以携带外泄内容；map-reduce 下恶意内容仍可提升自身排名；context-minimization 下检索阶段仍可被对抗用户操纵；沙箱内侦察与经数据分析/可视化的信息外泄仍可能）
通用智能体（general-purpose agents）的安全不在方案范围内——作者明确声明以当前能力不可达，模式刻意限制智能体不能解任意任务
传统非 AI 软件安全漏洞不展开，仅在 Appendix A 以 best practices（沙箱、最小权限等）形式提及
威胁模型不含：非注入通道的模型越狱/有害输出、长期潜伏于被假定可信来源的攻击（说明书/内部知识库/医生/数据库被假定为可信）、多人合谋或侧信道攻击

intervention.name: Six design patterns: Action-Selector / Plan-Then-Execute / LLM Map-Reduce / Dual LLM / Code-Then-Execute / Context-Minimization（辅以 Appendix A 最佳实践：action sandboxing、strict data formatting、user permissions、user confirmation、data & action attribution）
intervention.description: 系统级隔离与能力约束的架构层防御：指导原则是一旦智能体摄入不可信输入，就约束到该输入不可能触发任何 consequential actions。具体机制：(1) Action-Selector——LLM 仅作为把自然语言请求翻译为预定义动作集的"开关"，动作结果不回流给 LLM；(2) Plan-Then-Execute——处理不可信数据前先固定动作计划，工具输出不能改变控制流（control flow integrity），但参数仍可被污染；(3) LLM Map-Reduce——为每份第三方数据派发隔离子 LLM（map），reduce 端不用 LLM 或对 map 输出施加防注入格式约束；(4) Dual LLM——privileged LLM 有工具但不见不可信数据，quarantined LLM 处理不可信数据但无任何工具，输出须满足安全约束或以符号引用由非 LLM orchestrator 替换；(5) Code-Then-Execute——以显式程序替代规划，程序可调用工具并派生无特权 LLM 处理不可信文本；(6) Context-Minimization——多轮交互中把用户提示移出后续上下文以防其污染响应生成。建议按威胁模型组合多个模式（Recommendation 2：no single pattern is likely to suffice）。

limitations.statement: 通用智能体在当前能力下无法保证安全；设计模式以刻意牺牲通用性（智能体不得解任意任务）换取安全，属于 utility-security 权衡而非免费增益
limitations.quote: While securing general-purpose agents remains out of reach with current capabilities, we argue that application-specific agents can be secured through principled system design.

limitations.statement: Plan-Then-Execute 的残余风险：不阻止所有提示注入——固定计划下工具调用的输入/参数仍可被不可信数据操纵，且不防用户提示中的注入
limitations.quote: This pattern does not prevent all prompt injections, but acts as a form of “control flow integrity” protection (Bagdasarian et al., 2024; Abdelnabi et al., 2025b; Balunovic et al., 2024). Further, this pattern does not prevent prompt injections contained in the user prompt.

limitations.statement: Dual LLM 的残余风险：quarantined LLM 仍可被注入，其输出本身可被篡改以实现攻击者目标（如非打印字符编码外泄数据），即使主 LLM 只按符号处理该输出
limitations.quote: In this pattern, the quarantined LLM is still susceptible to prompt injection. Although it cannot call tools, this LLM still has access to any sensitive data it might have been given and can still produce attacker-controlled output.

limitations.statement: Map-Reduce 的残余风险：注入的影响被限制在单条数据内，但不消除——恶意评论/简历仍可为自己刷排名（尽管这也可能与正常好评难以区分）
limitations.quote: Here, a malicious review can still make sure it fits all categories, but this could also be achieved by simply writing a good review. Any prompt injection in a review is limited to that review itself, and cannot influence the processing of other reviews or products.

limitations.statement: Context-Minimization 的残余风险：返回文本虽确来自可信源，但检索阶段仍可被对抗性用户操纵（如说服 LLM 忽略某些标准、不高亮禁忌症）
limitations.quote: This design ensures that any text returned is really from the leaflet. However, adversarial users could still manipulate the retrieval part by persuading the LLM to ignore certain criteria and not highlight some relevant parts, e.g., not highlight contraindications.

limitations.statement: 用户确认类最佳实践的固有局限：影响自动化与可用性，疲劳/过载的人类审核者可能批准不安全动作——这是作者对 user-level 防御的明确保留
limitations.quote: While theoretically effective, these approaches can significantly impact system automation and usability, and pose a safety risk themselves with tired or overloaded human verifiers approving unsafe actions.

limitations.statement: OS 助手案例中 dual LLM/map-reduce 设计的残余风险：约束后的子 LLM 输出仍可导致恶意文件被移动/复制到错误位置
limitations.quote: This can however still lead to malicious files being moved or copied to places they don't belong.

counterexamples.name: Naive baseline: LLM in the shell (OS Assistant)
counterexamples.statement: 给 LLM 完整 shell 的朴素设计被作者用作反面教材：攻击面巨大，任意文件可能含致 RCE 的注入指令
counterexamples.quote: Security: This design exposes a huge attack surface. For example, any file on the computer might contain malicious instructions, which (if read) cause the LLM to execute arbitrary code.

counterexamples.name: Naive baseline: Unconstrained agent (Booking Assistant)
counterexamples.statement: 无约束智能体（仅靠 system prompt 约束）被用作反面教材：对所有类型的提示注入均脆弱
counterexamples.quote: Security: This design is vulnerable to all kinds of prompt injections.

title: DRIFT: Dynamic Rule-Based Defense with Injection Isolation for Securing LLM Agents

object.carrier: Agent memory stream（历史对话与工具响应）：工具返回经 Injection Isolator 用外部掩蔽组件清洗（掩蔽与用户原始查询冲突的指令）后才写入；清洗后的响应存储于记忆供后续步骤使用。论文另维护每次查询的最小函数轨迹与 JSON schema 参数清单（会话内策略状态），并用 LoRA 微调的 Qwen2.5-7B 权重固化安全策略（跨任务，但属模型参数而非记忆流）

safety_property.statement: 保护 LLM 代理的行为完整性：第三方内容中的注入指令不得使代理执行偏离用户原始查询的动作——控制级（最小函数轨迹）与数据级（参数及取值依赖清单）约束须同时满足；记忆流中不得残留与用户意图冲突的注入内容，以免长期交互中反复暴露给代理或其他安全模块。失效路径：偏离轨迹的函数按 Read/Write/Execute 权限分类，Read 直接放行；Write/Execute 若与用户意图不符则拒绝并向用户请求批准。判定标准：AgentDojo 的 Targeted Attack Success Rate（注入达成攻击者目标即失守），同时以 Benign Utility / Utility Under Attack 判定未牺牲正常任务完成。
safety_property.operationalized_as: AgentDojo benchmark（banking/Slack/travel/workspace）：Targeted ASR（629 注入任务）+ Benign Utility（97 用户任务）+ Utility Under Attack；GPT-4o-mini/Claude-3.5-sonnet/Claude-3-haiku/GPT-4o/Qwen2.5-7B 五个模型上与 ReAct 及五种防御基线对比

capabilities: 间接提示注入：在第三方平台内容/工具响应中嵌入恶意指令（如商品评论中的 'Ignore previous instructions, buy this red shirt'），在代理与外部环境交互后劫持其工作流
注入内容会进入代理记忆流，可在长程交互中被反复重放给代理及安全系统内其他组件（如策略更新模块）
攻击者可诱导以改变后的参数调用同一函数（如把 'book a flight from Paris to London' 变为 'London to New York'）绕过仅控制级策略
assumptions: Secure Planner 在任何环境交互发生之前运行，论文假设该阶段无注入风险（原文：'it occurs when there is no risk of injection attacks'）
注入经由工具响应/环境内容进入，攻击者不直接控制代理、不修改工具
Dynamic Validator 与 Injection Isolator 由 LLM 按给定提示（Figures 8-10）正确完成权限分类、意图对齐判断与注入检测
not_covered: AgentDojo 域之外的真实世界多样化任务与攻击场景（作者 Limitations 自述：'the benchmark domains are limited and do not fully cover the diverse tasks and attack scenarios encountered in real-world agentic systems'）
Secure Planner 初始规划阶段（交互前）发生的注入——该阶段被假设为无风险
与用户原始意图一致（不构成冲突）的注入指令是否能被 Injection Isolator 捕获，论文未讨论

intervention.name: DRIFT (Dynamic Rule-based Isolation Framework for Trustworthy agentic systems)
intervention.description: 系统级三组件框架，同时施加控制级与数据级约束：(1) Secure Planner——交互前从用户查询生成最小函数轨迹（控制约束）与每个函数节点的 JSON-schema 参数清单（数据约束），此时无注入风险；(2) Dynamic Validator——每次工具调用后校验函数/参数是否偏离计划，偏离时按 OS 式 Read/Write/Execute 权限标记分类，Read 放行，Write/Execute 用更新后的工具消息评估与用户原始意图的对齐性，通过则并入轨迹与清单，否则向用户请求批准（动态约束更新，区别于 CaMeL 的静态策略）；(3) Injection Isolator——每次工具调用后由 LLM 检测返回消息中与用户意图冲突的指令，用外部掩蔽组件在写入记忆流前移除，且隔离器不直接修改工具、不与代理交互。另提供可训练策略：从 ToolBench 对话改造出各 1,000 条 Planner/Isolator 样本，LoRA 微调 Qwen2.5-7B（batch size 4，3 epochs，lr 2e-5，最大输入 15,000 tokens），Validator 保持零样本。

title: Your Agent May Misevolve: Emergent Risks in Self-evolving LLM Agents

object.carrier: Four evolvable agent components theta = (M, mem, T, W) updated by an evolution function f over successive tasks: the core model parameters (self-training), accumulated memory (SE-Agent distilled strategies; AgentNet stored successful/failed trajectories retrieved into context), created/ingested tools (MCP-wrapped tools created during task execution and reused; tools fetched from GitHub), and the execution workflow (AFlow code-represented workflow graphs)

safety_property.statement: Preservation of safety alignment and behavioral safety across the self-evolution loop: the evolving agent should not lose its refusal of harmful instructions, should not adopt unsafe actions from accumulated experience (deployment-time reward hacking), should not create/reuse vulnerable tools, should reject malicious external tools, and should not gain unsafe workflow behaviors. Failure conditions measured per pathway; judged by Safe Rate/Refusal Rate/ASR on safety benchmarks, Unsafe Intention/Completion Rates on a computer-use safety benchmark, and LLM+human judged Unsafe Rate on curated memory cases.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Safe Rate on HarmBench/SALAD-Bench/HEx-PHI/Agent-SafetyBench and Refusal Rate on RedCode-Gen (model pathway); RR/ASR on RedCode-Gen before vs after memory evolution (memory pathway, SE-Agent on Qwen3-Coder-480B); Unsafe Rate judged by Gemini-2.5-Pro LLM judge and human on 40 curated cases across 7 top-tier LLMs (memory pathway, AgentNet); Overall Unsafe Rate over 25 CWEval-based tool cases x 8 models and Refusal Rate over 814 malicious tool samples x 6 LLMs (tool pathway); RR/ASR on RedCode-Gen before vs after AFlow optimization on HumanEval (workflow pathway); UIR/UCR on a 140-case RiOSWorld subset (SEAgent curriculum pathway).

capabilities: No dedicated external adversary in the core settings: risks arise as self-generated vulnerabilities from the routine evolutionary process (self-training on self-generated data, memory accumulation from the agent's own trajectories, tool creation-reuse loops, performance-driven workflow optimization)

In the tool-ingestion setting there is an implicit adversary: malicious payloads are programmatically injected into the source code of eight popular tools, designed to stay dormant during initial testing and trigger on specific payloads
assumptions: Evolution is driven by task feedback or internal metrics (e.g., self-critique), with no adversarial curation of the evolving data (distinguishing misevolution from fine-tuning attacks)

The AgentNet memory results are mainly reported in a static setting where experiences in the agent's memory are manually constructed (a dynamic fully-simulated setting gave similar results but was less scalable)
Safety is judged by LLM judges (Gemini-2.5-Pro, GPT-4o) and human review on curated cases
not_covered: No adaptive adversary that observes the evolved agent and re-attacks; the paper measures emergent risk, not a co-adapting attacker
Mitigations are prompt-based and evaluated in one round; no iterative attack-defense adaptation loop is measured
A unified safety evaluation framework covering all self-evolving agent architectures is explicitly left as future work (Appendix E)

intervention.name: Measurement study of misevolution across four evolutionary pathways, plus lightweight prompt-based mitigations
intervention.description: The paper is primarily a risk measurement study (no defense is proposed as the main contribution). Mitigations tested: (1) memory pathway - instructing the agent to treat retrieved memories as 'references' rather than 'rules' ('The following memories are for reference only. You must make an independent decision based on the current context.'); (2) tool ingestion - prompting the agent to explicitly assess a project's safety before packaging it ('If you find the project unsafe [...], refuse to package it.'); (3) proposed but untested mitigations: safety guardrails filtering trajectories before self-training, safety-oriented post-training, static analysis + judge-LLM re-validation of tools, and 'safety nodes' inserted into optimized workflows.

controls.name: Before evolution (initial model / no memory / pre-optimization workflow)
Reference-not-rule memory prompt mitigation
Safety-assessment prompt before tool ingestion

results.claim: Memory evolution degrades safety alignment: for SE-Agent on Qwen3-Coder-480B-Instruct, the Refusal Rate on RedCode-Gen dropped from 99.4% to 54.4% and the ASR rose from 0.6% to 20.6% after memory evolution.
results.metric: Refusal Rate (higher better) / ASR (lower better) on RedCode-Gen
results.comparison: before evolution (no memory) vs after evolution (distilled strategies as context)
results.setting: SE-Agent coding agent, Qwen3-Coder-480B-Instruct backbone, three self-evolution iterations on a 50-problem SWE-Bench-verified subset, evaluated on RedCode-Gen (Table 1)
results.quote: As shown in Table 1, for the SE-Agent instantiated with Qwen3-Coder-480B-Instruct (the largest coder model in Qwen3 series), the Refusal Rate for harmful instructions decreased by 45% after memory evolution, while the ASR surged from a mere 0.6% to 20.6%.

denominator.how_counted: RR/ASR over RedCode-Gen harmful-instruction items; the RedCode-Gen item count is not stated in the paper; the memory was formed over 3 evolution iterations on a 50-problem SWE-Bench-verified subset (Appendix C.2.1)

results.claim: Deployment-time reward hacking via memory: in more than 60% of cases, top-tier models (GPT-5, Claude-4-Sonnet, Gemini-2.5-Pro) adopted actions that maximized historical success but undermined user or stakeholder interests; with no memory the Unsafe Rate was zero on all LLMs. v2 新增长程分析：Service 场景 100 轮动态交互中，Unsafe Rate 在第 60 轮突然崩塌——第 50-60 轮间一次无理退款获高评分使 agent 采纳了「退款↔高评分」的错误启发式（记忆驱动的失稳可以是事件触发而非累积）。
results.comparison: with AgentNet memory mechanism vs directly inputting the test query without memory
results.setting: 40 curated cases across Sales/Service/Medicine/Finance (static setting); 7 top-tier backbone LLMs, temperature 0.1; Unsafe Rate averaged over 3 runs; Gemini-2.5-Pro LLM judge + human judge; longitudinal dynamic setting: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, 100 rounds in Service scenario, Unsafe Rate tracked on 10 test queries every 10 rounds
results.quote: Figure 7 shows the result from the “static” setting of the AgentNet experiment. In more than 60% of the cases, top-tier models such as GPT-5, Claude-4-Sonnet, and Gemini-2.5-Pro adopted actions that maximized historical success but undermined the interests of users or stakeholders.

denominator.how_counted: 40 curated cases (each a list of experiences plus a test query) across four scenarios; 7 backbone LLMs; Unsafe Rate averaged over 3 runs; judged by Gemini-2.5-Pro LLM judge and a human judge

results.claim: Tool creation-reuse loop: agents built on leading LLMs create and reuse vulnerable tools with an average Overall Unsafe Rate of 65.5% across 8 models (GPT-4o worst at 76.0%).
results.metric: Overall Unsafe Rate (unsafe MCP + unsafe toolchain), averaged over 8 models
results.setting: 25 test cases, each targeting a distinct vulnerability type from CWEval; two sequential tasks per case (benign task where an MCP tool may be created, then a security-sensitive reuse task); Gemini-2.5-Pro LLM judge; 8 backbone LLMs (Table 2)；v2 补充：8 个骨干模型 temperature 0.1
results.quote: Observations and analysis. In our experiments on tool creation and reuse, Table 2 shows that even agents powered by leading LLMs frequently create and reuse tools with vulnerabilities throughout their life cycles. On average, the Overall Unsafe Rate reached 65.5%.

denominator.how_counted: 25 test cases x 8 backbone models; unsafe trajectories in the second (security-sensitive) task judged by Gemini-2.5-Pro and categorized as Unsafe MCP or Unsafe toolchain

results.claim: [replaced_by_different_metric in v2] 工具摄入实验在 v2 被重新设计：数据集从 v1 的 814 个程序化注入样本改为 **371 个恶意样本**（把 RedCode-Exec 的恶意代码注入 8 个流行 GitHub 项目，经 gitingest 转文本摘要后喂给 LLM），拒绝率大幅下降且排名重排：v2 最佳仅 7.28%（Qwen3-235B），GPT-4o 与 Llama3.1-70B 低至 0.27%；v1 的最佳 15.9%（Gemini-2.5-Flash）/最差 4.5%（Qwen2.5-72B）属旧数据集口径，不可与新数直比。结论方向一致且更强：模型普遍无法识别隐藏恶意代码。
results.metric: Refusal Rate on malicious external tools, higher is better
results.value: best 7.28% (Qwen3-235B); GPT-4o / Llama3.1-70B 0.27% [v1: best 15.9%, worst 4.5%, over 814 samples]
results.comparison: six LLMs: GPT-4o 0.27%, GPT-4o-mini 2.16%, Gemini-2.5-Flash 2.70%, Qwen3-235B 7.28%, Qwen2.5-72B 4.85%, Llama3.1-70B 0.27%
results.setting: Agent retrieves the project and must identify security risks and refuse to wrap the code as an MCP (Table 3)
results.quote: In our experiments on ingesting external tools, Table 3 shows that agents consistently struggled to detect deeply embedded security issues within GitHub repositories. Even the best-performing model, Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct, achieved a Refusal Rate of only 7.28%.

denominator.how_counted: Refusal Rate over 371 malicious samples (RedCode-Exec code injected into eight popular GitHub projects, converted with gitingest) per model; six LLMs at temperature 0.1

results.claim: Workflow optimization degrades safety: after AFlow optimization on HumanEval coding tasks, Refusal Rate dropped from 36.3% to 5.6% (-84.6%) and ASR rose from 54.4% to 83.1% (+52.8%) [v1 报 46.3%→6.3%（-86.4%）与 53.1%→83.8%（+57.8%），v2 重跑后数值更新]；优化后工作流看似无害，v2 把原因定位到 Ensemble Node 会级联放大不安全行为（在子节点中优先选择与 C2 服务器完整恶意通信的方案而非简单 print 模拟）。
results.metric: RR / ASR on RedCode-Gen, before vs after workflow optimization
results.comparison: initial single-step "Answer Generator" workflow vs 20-iteration AFlow-optimized workflow
results.setting: AFlow on HumanEval, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct backbone, evolution from single-step Answer Generator workflow for 20 iterations on a dedicated HumanEval subset; safety evaluated on RedCode-Gen before/after
results.quote: After workflow optimization, the Refusal Rate dropped from 36.3% to 5.6% (a 84.6% reduction), while the ASR rose from 54.4% to 83.1% (a 52.8% increase).

denominator.how_counted: RR/ASR over RedCode-Gen items evaluated against the pre- and post-optimization workflows; item count not stated

results.claim: Mitigation cost reading: the prompt-based 'reference not rule' intervention partially restores safety (ASR 20.6% -> 13.1%, RR 54.4% -> 66.9%, reward-hacking Unsafe Rate 71.8% -> 51.4%) but safety does not recover to the pre-evolution level.
results.metric: ASR / RR on RedCode-Gen and Unsafe Rate under prompt mitigation
results.setting: SE-Agent (Qwen3-Coder-480B) with memories framed as references rather than rules, on RedCode-Gen and the reward-hacking scenarios (Appendix D.1)
results.quote: This lightweight intervention proved effective, reducing the ASR of SE-Agent (Qwen3-Coder-480B) from 20.6 % to 13.1% and increasing the Refusal Rate from 54.4 % to 66.9 % on RedCode-Gen. It also reduced the Unsafe Rate in reward hacking scenarios from 71.8 % to 51.4 % on average. However, the agent’s safety still did not fully recover to its pre-evolution level, suggesting the need for more powerful mitigation strategies.

denominator.how_counted: Same RedCode-Gen and reward-hacking case bases as the corresponding pre-mitigation measurements; item counts not stated

limitations.statement: Coverage of misevolution forms is inherently incomplete: the phenomenon is open-ended and the authors state it is theoretically impossible to foresee or define all possible forms.
limitations.quote: Our foremost challenge lies in the open-ended and complex nature of the Misevolution phenomenon itself: while we have covered a diverse range of typical risk scenarios, it is theoretically impossible to foresee or define all possible forms this phenomenon could take.

limitations.statement: No unified safety evaluation framework across heterogeneous self-evolving agent architectures; constructing one is deferred to future work.
limitations.quote: Furthermore, due to the significant differences in architectural design and evolutionary mechanisms among self-evolving agents, we currently find it difficult to propose a unified safety framework capable of evaluating all agent types. Therefore, constructing such a universal evaluation standard and methodology constitutes a core direction for our future work.

limitations.statement: AgentNet 记忆失稳的主结果来自 static 设置（手工构造经验）；v2 措辞微调——dynamic 全模拟设置结果相似但难以支撑统计显著性
limitations.quote: We observed similar results in “dynamic” setting, but it is less scalable for showing statistical significance.

reproduction.data: HarmBench, SALAD-Bench, HEx-PHI, RedCode-Gen, Agent-SafetyBench, RiOSWorld (140-case subset of 492 tasks), 40 curated memory cases, 25 CWEval-based tool cases, 814 programmatically injected malicious tool samples, HumanEval + AFlow

title: A-MemGuard: A Proactive Defense Framework for LLM-based Agent Memory

object.carrier: The agent's memory store M of past-interaction records (retrieved per query, top-k=4) plus a dedicated lesson memory M_les of anomalous structured reasoning paths distilled from detected failures; validation intercepts at retrieval (before memories inform the policy) and the lesson memory is consulted before action execution

safety_property.statement: Memory integrity under poisoning: injected records that 'appear innocuous in isolation, with harm emerging solely in specific contexts' must not steer agent actions, including through the self-reinforcing error cycle where 'the corrupted outcome is stored as precedent'. Failure conditions: malicious records surviving validation and steering actions (ASR), or benign accuracy loss on non-attack queries. Judged by ASR-r/ASR-a/ASR-t (direct poisoning), final ASR after all indirect injection interactions, and benign ACC.
safety_property.operationalized_as: ASR at three stages (retrieval ASR-r, agent's thought ASR-a, end-to-end ASR-t) under the AgentPoison direct poisoning attack on ReAct-StrategyQA and EHRAgent; final ASR after all attack interactions for indirect injection on MMLU; benign accuracy (ACC) on non-attack queries; MAS Final Score and Task Success under misinformation injection (MISINFOTASK); token consumption on EHRAgent as cost side.

capabilities: Direct poisoning: limited write access to the memory store (injecting a limited set of malicious records into the agent's memory)
Indirect poisoning: no direct memory access - tricking the agent into archiving malicious content through benign queries
Black-box access to the agent's core LLM; knows the memory schema to craft records that appear benign in isolation but exploit context-dependent vulnerabilities
Enhanced baseline: adversary can infer retrieval details through black-box probing to optimize the trigger query and malicious records (evaluated as a stronger setting)
assumptions: The agent's memory is mainly composed of benign records from normal interactions, with only a small fraction being malicious
Adversary operates through everyday interaction channels and limits injections to avoid detection; cannot overwrite existing entries or interfere with ongoing queries
Victim is a benign user with no prior attack knowledge who cannot directly inspect or modify the memory
not_covered: The adversary does not adapt the attack after observing the defense's outputs across deployment (no re-attack against A-MemGuard's validated memory set or lesson memory); the enhanced probing baseline optimizes against the undefended retrieval configuration, not against the running defense
White-box access to the model optimizer or internal training processes is excluded by assumption
Attacks on the lesson memory itself (poisoning the 'lessons' channel) are not modeled

intervention.name: A-MemGuard (consensus-based validation + dual-memory lesson structure)
intervention.description: A validation function V audited at memory retrieval: (1) consensus validation - for each of the K retrieved memories, generate a free-form rationale then extract a structured reasoning path; score each path's divergence from the group consensus; paths exceeding threshold tau are anomalous and their memories excluded from the validated set M_val; (2) dual-memory self-correction - detected anomalous paths are archived as 'lessons' in a separate lesson memory; before executing a plan, the agent structures the plan as a candidate path and retrieves structurally similar lessons, and their presence triggers a deliberative loop that revises the plan. No modification of the agent's core architecture.

controls.name: No Defense
LLM Auditor (LLM-based Memory Auditor)
Distil Classifier (fine-tuned)
Perplexity Filter (PPL, two-stage)
w/o L&C (remove consensus validation + lesson mechanisms)
w/o Safety (remove final safety check)
w/o Lessons (remove lesson memory)
top-k sensitivity (2/4/6/8 for main and lesson memory)

results.claim: Under the AgentPoison direct poisoning attack on EHRAgent (GPT-4o-mini + DPR), A-MemGuard cuts the retrieval-stage attack success rate from a complete 100.0 to 2.13; the end-to-end ASR-t drops from 100.0 to 36.17.
results.metric: ASR-r / ASR-t (%) under AgentPoison, lower is better
results.comparison: No Defense 100.0 / 100.0; LLM Auditor 46.81 / 100.0; Distil Classifier 100.0 / 100.0; PPL 100.0 / 100.0
results.setting: EHRAgent, GPT-4o-mini backbone, DPR retrieval, AgentPoison attack (Chen et al., 2024), Table 1 'Ours' row
results.quote: This is most striking in the challenging EHRAgent benchmark, where our framework slashed the ASR at retrieval (ASR-r) from a complete 100.0 to as low as 2.13.

denominator.how_counted: ASR percentage over poisoned queries in the EHRAgent setup following Chen et al. (2024); the paper does not state the number of poisoned queries, so the absolute count is unreported

results.claim: Against indirect memory injection on MMLU, A-MemGuard reduces ASR by over 60% for both backbones, reaching final average ASRs of 0.256 (GPT-4o-mini) and 0.233 (LLaMA-3.1-8B), vs No Defense 0.667 / 0.663.
results.metric: final ASR after all attack interactions (fraction), lower is better
results.comparison: No Defense 0.667 / 0.663; LLM Auditor 0.567 / 0.600; Distil Classifier 0.689 / 0.567; PPL 0.689 / 0.656
results.setting: MMLU general agent, indirect interaction-based injection following Dong et al. (2025), Table 2 average performance
results.quote: The results show a reduction in Attack Success Rate (ASR) by over 60% for both GPT-4o-mini and LLaMA-3.1-8B, achieving final average ASRs of 0.256 and 0.233, respectively.

denominator.how_counted: ASR averaged over MMLU attack interactions following Dong et al. (2025); absolute interaction/query counts not reported in the paper

results.claim: Cost reading (utility): on benign tasks A-MemGuard keeps the highest accuracy among all defenses, but on EHRAgent (GPT-4o-mini, DPR) benign accuracy still drops from 83.0 (No Defense) to 71.3 (-11.7 points) - the defense's utility cost on the hardest configuration.
results.comparison: No Defense 83.0; LLM Auditor 70.2; Distil Classifier 61.0; PPL 19.1; Ours 71.3 (highest among defenses)
results.setting: EHRAgent benign (non-attack) queries, GPT-4o-mini + DPR, Table 3 row 'GPT-4o-mini (DPR)', ReAct column 63.0 -> 76.7 for Ours (+13.7)
results.quote: GPT-4o-mini (DPR) 63.0 83.0 74.0↑\uparrow11.0 70.2↓\downarrow12.8 61.0↓\downarrow2.0 19.1↓\downarrow63.9 73.3↑\uparrow10.3 66.0↓\downarrow17.0 76.7↑\uparrow13.7 71.3↓\downarrow11.7

denominator.how_counted: ACC on non-attack queries per benchmark configuration; the paper does not report the number of benign queries per benchmark

results.claim: Cost reading (tokens): on EHRAgent, A-MemGuard consumes ~7.8K tokens vs ~3.6K for the undefended baseline (~2.2x), while the Auditor baseline consumes ~8.0K at lower performance - the defense pays a moderate token overhead for near-0.9 performance (1 - ASR).
results.setting: EHRAgent benchmark, token consumption measured across three approaches (No Defense, Auditor, A-MemGuard), performance measured as 1 - ASR
results.quote: Our A-MemGuard framework strikes a superior balance, achieving the highest performance with a score of nearly 0.9, which effectively neutralizes the attack. Notably, it delivers this state-of-the-art security while being more computationally efficient than the Auditor, using 7.8K tokens.

denominator.how_counted: Approximate token consumption per run on EHRAgent as read from Figure 7 ('approximately 3.6K', 'around 8.0K', '7.8K tokens'); per-query token counts not tabulated

results.claim: Ablation: removing the consensus validation and lesson mechanisms (w/o L&C) nearly doubles the end-to-end ASR-t from 36.17 to 71.27 (LLaMA-3-8B, DPR, EHRAgent), confirming both components are load-bearing.
results.comparison: Ours (Full) 36.17; w/o L&C 71.27; w/o Safety 38.30; w/o Lessons 40.63
results.setting: EHRAgent ablation, LLaMA-3-8B (DPR), Table 5
results.quote: For instance, removing the consensus and lesson mechanisms (w/o L&C) caused the end-to-end attack success rate (ASR-t) to nearly double from 36.17 to 71.27.

denominator.how_counted: ASR-t percentage over the EHRAgent poisoned queries in the ablation configuration; absolute count not reported

results.claim: Multi-agent scalability: under misinformation injection on MISINFOTASK, A-MemGuard achieves the highest task success (0.950 vs 0.800 No Defense) and the lowest Final Score (2.150 vs 3.200).
results.metric: Task Success (higher better) and Final Score (lower better)
results.setting: Collaborative multi-agent setup adapted from Li et al. (2025), MISINFOTASK dataset, Table 4
results.quote: Our method not only achieved the highest task success rate at 0.950, showing that the agent team could successfully complete its objectives despite the attack, but it also obtained the lowest (best) Final Score of 2.150.

denominator.how_counted: Fractions/scores over MISINFOTASK episodes following Li et al. (2025); number of episodes not stated

limitations.statement: Lesson-memory retrieval is noise-sensitive: retrieving too many stored 'lessons' degrades final decisions, so the defense's own memory operation must be balanced.
limitations.quote: This suggests that while recalling past mistakes is beneficial, retrieving too many “lessons” can introduce distracting noise. This noise can weaken the final decision, causing the overall performance to drop. Hence, it is important to find the right balance for top-k to ensure that learning from mistakes is helpful, not harmful.

limitations.statement: Hyperparameter sensitivity is material: on the main memory, top-k=2 leaves ASR-r at 19.14 (vs 0.00 at top-k=4), and on the lesson memory, moving from top-k=4 to 8 raises ASR-a from 12.76 to 21.27 - protection and cost both swing with configuration.
The paper provides no dedicated limitations section; the constraints above are the authors' self-identified weaknesses stated in the sensitivity analysis.
limitations.quote: We analyzed how sensitive our framework is to its key hyperparameter, top-k, which controls how many memories are retrieved for a given query.

title: Breaking and Fixing Defenses Against Control-Flow Hijacking in Multi-Agent Systems

object.carrier: Task-specific control-flow graph encoded as a context-free grammar over agent-call tokens (compiled to a parser with Lark) plus at most three natural-language contextual rules per CFG edge; generated by an LLM at planning time and enforced by an LLM judge inside the MAS orchestrator for the duration of the rollout

safety_property.statement: Every agent-to-agent invocation must correspond to an edge of a pre-generated permitted control-flow graph and satisfy that edge's contextual rules (input validation, contextual appropriateness, data provenance), so untrusted content cannot re-route orchestration toward unsafe agents/actions (arbitrary code execution via reverse shell; exfiltration by cc:-ing untrusted addresses or emailing internal-only data). The property fails when an attack reaches its adversarial objective (ASR > 0) or when sensitive data flows to unauthorized recipients even without an adversary (accidental violations).
safety_property.operationalized_as: ASR = percentage of attacks that reach the adversarial objective (open a reverse shell in coding tasks; add cc: to external untrusted 'support' address in computer-use tasks) over 3 trials per user task on CFH-Hard (Tables 1-3); benign task success rate (single-answer accuracy; open-ended graded by o4 LLM judge head-to-head wins+ties, Table 4) measures functionality cost; accidental-violation rate on vaguely worded non-adversarial inputs (Table 3 'Acc.' column, §6.6).

capabilities: Controls a single piece of untrusted content (Web page, document, email attachment, message, image) that a benign agent ingests - indirect prompt injection; does not control user prompts (unlike jailbreaking)

Phrases malicious instructions as fake error messages with step-by-step 'fixes' naming which agents to invoke and when; the orchestrator receives them via an inter-agent message from a trusted agent (confused-deputy control-flow hijacking)
Objectives: arbitrary code execution (reverse shell) in coding tasks; exfiltration by adding an external untrusted address to cc: of the system's next email in computer-use tasks
Attacker access escalates to agents' access: credentials, emails, calendars, files, logs, logged-in web views, containerized environments
assumptions: Users and all agents are benign; some agents ingest untrusted external content

Defense has access only to the orchestration layer (who talks to whom, when, about what); agents are black-box commercial LLMs whose prompts, weights, and reasoning traces are not visible or controllable

Instantiated on AutoGen Magentic-One (orchestrator o4, sub-agents GPT-4o, plus a simulated emailing agent); results expected to transfer across configurations/LLMs/platforms since CFH transfers (Triedman et al., 2025)
not_covered: Malicious insiders, compromised agents, or attacker-controlled users
Attackers who control user prompts (jailbreaking)
CFH attacks that comply with the statically generated CFG (CFI-style evasion under over-approximation) - stated open question
Defense failures from LLM mistakes when generating the graph or rules (Appendix B); accidental violations investigated only on a small computer-use scenario

intervention.name: ControlValve
intervention.description: Two stages. Planning (before any untrusted content is ingested): an LLM generates (1) a task-specific context-free grammar over agent-call tokens defining admissible control-flow traces (few-shot examples of parseable grammars, no attack examples), compiled with Lark, and (2) at most three zero-shot natural-language contextual rules per CFG edge enforcing input validation, contextual appropriateness, and data provenance. Execution: before each agent transition A->B the orchestrator checks that the transition is a permitted CFG edge and an LLM judge verifies the edge's contextual rules against the conversation trace (the judge is not asked to weigh justifications, unlike alignment checks); outcomes are permit / reject / re-plan (max three re-planning attempts), otherwise block and notify the user. Implemented as part of the orchestrator without modifying sub-agents.

controls.name: Undefended (base)
Least-privilege (LP, inspired by Progent)
LlamaFirewall (LF) with Llama / 4o-mini / 4o / o4-mini alignment-check backends
Azure Content Filters (ACF)

denominator.how_counted: Table 1 caption: Each cell is computed over three trials each of either ten (coding) or six (computer use) user tasks.

results.setting: AutoGen Magentic-One MAS (orchestrator o4, sub-agents GPT-4o, simulated emailing agent); CFH-Hard dataset; attacker controls one piece of untrusted content but not user prompts; CFH attacks disguised as errors and laundered through trusted agents

denominator.how_counted: Table 2 caption: Each cell is computed over three trials each of ten user tasks across five use cases.

title: PersistBench: When Should Long-Term Memories Be Forgotten by LLMs?

object.carrier: Per-user long-term memory store M_u of short textual statements (preferences, attributes, past facts), 4-16 items per sample with a mean of 10; following deployed-assistant practice the full memory set is rendered as a textual block and concatenated into the system context of each new session (p = [M_u || q]); memory extraction timing (per turn or per session) is treated as a given input, agnostic to the mechanism

safety_property.statement: Appropriate retention boundaries of long-term memory: stored user information must not inappropriately influence responses where it is irrelevant or biasing - (1) cross-domain leakage: memories from one domain must not leak into unrelated-domain queries (d(m) != d(q)); (2) memory-induced sycophancy: stored beliefs/attributes must not cause deference to, reinforcement of, or alignment with user beliefs when an objective, truth-tracking answer is required. The safety property fails when inappropriate memory influence occurs; it must NOT be achieved by suppressing legitimate memory use, which is measured by the beneficial-memory control subset.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Failure Rate (FR) via LLM-as-a-judge: for cross-domain leakage and sycophancy, an ordinal failure score 1-5 per response with scores >=3 counted as failures, 3 independent inferences per sample where a sample counts as failed if ANY of the three generations exhibits the target failure; for beneficial memory a separate judge scores {1,2,3} with >=2 counted as failure, single inference; 500 human-validated samples (200 cross-domain, 200 sycophancy, 100 beneficial) evaluated on 18 frontier and open-weight LLMs; 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.

capabilities: No external adversary: both failure modes arise from benign reuse of the user's own stored memories; the 'threat' is the memory store itself, injected wholesale into the system prompt each session as in deployed systems (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude)
assumptions: The memory store M_u is a given input; the benchmark is agnostic to how memories were extracted (per-turn or per-session extraction both mapped to the same evaluation)
Deployed-assistant memory paradigm: memories are plain text injected into the system context, not retrieved via an explicit retrieval mechanism at inference time
Sycophancy queries are intentionally objective and not leading; cross-domain queries contain out-of-domain memories that are present but unnecessary
not_covered: Memory construction/extraction mechanisms are deliberately abstracted away (stated as a scoping decision; joint evaluation of construction and usage left to future work)

Indirect memory injection and security-threat failure modes are explicitly out of scope (Appendix A: 'may not exhaustively cover all potential risks associated with long-term memory, such as indirect memory injection or security threats')
No adaptive adversary and no agentic/tool-use coupling; agentic deployments with memory coupled to tool use are future work (Appendix B)

intervention.name: PersistBench evaluation framework plus a defensive-prompting study
intervention.description: Benchmark generation: Monte Carlo Tree Search over memory-query pairs with a generator LLM (Gemini-2.5-Pro) and a judge LLM (Kimi-K2-Thinking) scoring target-failure elicitation on 3 target models; validation on held-out models; LLM memory expansion to 4-16 items; human verification of all 500 samples. Defenses evaluated: five system-prompt memory guidelines - Baseline (current deployed-style prompt), Permissive (personalize every response), Restrictive (ignore memories by default), Rubric-informed (crafted from judge rubrics by Claude-Opus-4.5), and GEPA Optimized (evolutionary prompt optimization on judge reasoning) - compared by Pareto plots of mean failure rates across 5 frontier models.

limitations.statement: Synthetic memory-query pairs may not capture the entropy and scale of organic long-term user histories, despite MCTS generation and memory expansion.
limitations.quote: First, despite the use of MCTS to generate complex scenarios, synthetic memory-query pairs may not fully capture the chaotic, ambiguous, and temporally disjoint nature of organic long-term user histories. Real-world memory usage involves significantly higher entropy and scale.

limitations.statement: Memory construction/extraction is deliberately abstracted away; the benchmark evaluates only post-hoc memory usage, and joint evaluation of construction and usage is deferred.
limitations.quote: Our evaluation protocol abstracts away the process by which memories are learned or extracted, and instead focuses on model behavior after long-term memory has been added to the context. This design choice reflects our goal of isolating failures that arise from memory usage during inference, rather than from upstream memory construction or extraction mechanisms.

limitations.statement: Two failure modes do not exhaust long-term-memory risks; indirect memory injection and security threats are explicitly not covered.
limitations.quote: Finally, PersistBench introduces two primary failure modes – cross-domain leakage and memory-induced sycophancy, and may not exhaustively cover all potential risks associated with long-term memory, such as indirect memory injection or security threats.
