title: Agentic Unlearning: When LLM Agent Meets Machine Unlearning

object.carrier: Five-layer external memory store (episodic dialogue traces M, semantic summaries S, reflections R, procedural and external layers) organized as a dependency graph G=(V,E) with per-node reference counters and a persistent blocklist B; prototype store holds 2000 entries encoded by text-embedding-ada-002 (1536-dim), hybrid retrieval top-5 (semantic weight 0.7, keyword 0.3); deletion targets plus their dependency closure are pruned, vector index rebuilt when |B| > tau=100

safety_property.statement: Verifiable removal of targeted information from BOTH parametric and memory pathways of a memory-augmented agent without utility loss on retained data, preventing parameter-memory backflow: (i) the agent does not reveal target information D_tgt under adaptive interaction; (ii) memory contains no artifacts derived from D_tgt; (iii) the agent cannot rewrite D_tgt back into memory; (iv) utility on retained data is preserved. Failure condition: the backflow recontamination loop - parametric residue regenerates forgotten content which is re-stored, or residual memory artifacts re-expose deleted content through retrieval.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Forget-set accuracy (lower = better removal), Test-set accuracy and held-out generalization accuracy (utility preservation), MIA AUC (ideal 0.5) and normalized MIA Score on member vs non-member loss distributions, memory-side forget/retain accuracy before vs after unlearning (Table 4), and Agent-Loop retrieval hit rate across Store/Query/Delete/Probe stages (Figure 6); forget set sizes Q_F=100 and Q_F=1000; mean±std over 3 runs.

capabilities: Membership-inference attacker: computes area under the ROC curve from loss distributions of member vs non-member data to detect whether forgotten records remain distinguishable (MIA AUC near 1 = under-unlearning, near 0 = over-unlearning)
assumptions: Deletion requests arrive incrementally as forget sets D_F over medical QA data; retain set D_R is available for the utility-preserving loss term
Memory is modeled as a dependency graph over {M,S,R,K}; unlearning guarantees depend on the graph structure, not on specific memory-layer content
Retrieval honors the blocklist at retrieval boundaries (Invariant 1: no memory in B appears in results); derived artifacts follow dependency consistency (Invariant 2)
not_covered: No adaptive multi-turn attacker in the evaluation: property (i) (no revelation under adaptive interaction) is defined but the measured attacks are static forget-set accuracy, MIA, and a scripted four-stage agent loop, not an adaptive red-team
Dependency tracking may not fully capture cross-agent information flow in shared knowledge graphs (authors' stated limitation; multi-agent unlearning left to future work)
Deployment in clinical settings and formal HIPAA/GDPR compliance verification are out of scope (Ethical Statement)

intervention.name: Synchronized Backflow Unlearning (SBU): dual-pathway agentic unlearning
intervention.description: Memory pathway: dependency-aware unlearning - target IDs are added to a persistent blocklist for O(1) retrieval filtering, the dependency closure Dep(D_F) is traversed with reference counting to mark exclusively-dependent artifacts for deletion while preserving shared ones, zero-reference nodes are batch-removed, targets and their vectors are deleted, and the vector index is rebuilt when |B|>100; all operations logged in a tamper-evident write-ahead log with hash-chain verification. Parameter pathway: entropy-regularized unlearning (KL-to-random) - a frozen randomly-initialized reference model defines a high-entropy prior; the objective L_weight = L_CE^{D_R} + lambda_F T^2 L_KL^{D_F} aligns outputs on forget queries to the random-like distribution while cross-entropy on retain queries preserves utility. Unified protocol: memory unlearning executes FIRST so parameter updates operate on a sanitized retrieval context, preventing re-encoding; the process repeats per incremental request.

results.quote: The forgetting coefficient λF\lambda_{F} controls forgetting-utility trade-off: values below 0.5 fail to induce sufficient forgetting (forget accuracy 86%); excessive values (λF≥3.0\lambda_{F}{\geq}3.0) cause test degradation (66%) despite stronger forgetting (forget accuracy 64%). Temperature exhibits a narrow effective range, with moderate values (1.0–2.0) performing best, whereas high temperature (T=4.0T{=}4.0) destabilizes optimization and drops test accuracy to 68%.

denominator.how_counted: 34 hyperparameter configurations evaluated on MedMCQA; accuracy per configuration

limitations.statement: Dependency tracking does not capture cross-agent information flow in shared knowledge graphs; multi-agent unlearning protocols are deferred to future work.
limitations.quote: A limitation of our current approach is that dependency tracking may not fully capture cross-agent information flow in shared knowledge graphs. Future work will explore unlearning protocols specifically tailored for multi-agent collaborative environments.

limitations.statement: The blocklist-based design leaves vector-index staleness that must be managed by periodic rebuilds (threshold tau=100), i.e., deletion is only eventually consistent at the index level.
limitations.quote: To control vector-index staleness, the system periodically rebuilds the vector index when |B| exceeds threshold τ=100\tau=100.

limitations.statement: The entropy-alignment design deliberately avoids a perfectly uniform output distribution because that risks over-unlearning and capability damage; the KL-to-random scheme is chosen for stability.
limitations.quote: However, our KL-to-random scheme provides a more stable learning target by aligning to a structured high-entropy prior from a reference model, rather than forcing the output towards a perfectly uniform distribution, which can risk over-unlearning and damaging model capabilities.

counterexamples.observation: NPO attains the lowest forget accuracy (74.00%) but suffers severe generalization collapse (gen 41.67%) - aggressive forgetting destroys retained capability, demonstrating that parameter-only aggressive unlearning is not a viable cost profile.

reproduction.data: MedQA (~10k questions), MedMCQA (~183k questions, 2,400 topics, 21 subjects), MedReason (~33k QA pairs, answer pairs only); forget sets Q_F=100 and Q_F=1000; memory store 2000 entries; 3 runs per configuration

title: Agents of Chaos

title: Session Risk Memory (SRM): Temporal Authorization for Deterministic Pre-Execution Safety Gates

object.carrier: Session Risk Memory: a compact semantic centroid representing the evolving behavioral profile of an agent session, plus a risk signal accumulated through an exponential moving average over baseline-subtracted gate outputs; both operate on the same semantic vector representation as the underlying deterministic gate, with no additional model components, training, or probabilistic inference; the state lives and is evaluated over the trajectory of one session

safety_property.statement: Temporal authorization consistency: individually-compliant steps that collectively decompose harmful intent (slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, compliance drift) must be caught at the trajectory level, not only per action. Failure condition of the baseline being extended: stateless per-action gates are 'structurally blind to distributed attacks that decompose harmful intent across multiple individually-compliant steps'. Judged by F1, false positive rate, and detection rate over multi-turn attack sessions, with per-turn overhead as the cost side.
safety_property.operationalized_as: F1, FPR, and detection rate on a multi-turn benchmark of 80 sessions containing slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, and compliance drift scenarios; SRM extends the ILION gate and is compared against stateless ILION; per-turn overhead in microseconds.

capabilities: Distributed attack: decomposes harmful intent across multiple individually-compliant steps, each of which passes deterministic per-action authorization (spatial authorization consistency holds per action while the trajectory violates temporal authorization consistency)
Attack scenarios evaluated: slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, and compliance drift across multi-turn sessions
assumptions: A deterministic pre-execution safety gate (ILION) already evaluates each agent action against assigned roles; SRM extends it with trajectory-level authorization using the same semantic vector representation
Per the abstract, SRM requires no additional model components, training, or probabilistic inference
not_covered: The full paper (threat-model section, adversary knowledge assumptions, additional baselines and analyses) was not accessible for this card - no HTML full text exists on arXiv or ar5iv; all card content is grounded in the abstract only
Adaptive attackers that probe or evade the temporal risk signal are not addressed in the abstract

intervention.name: Session Risk Memory (SRM): trajectory-level authorization module on top of a deterministic per-action gate
intervention.description: A lightweight deterministic module extending stateless pre-execution safety gates with trajectory-level (temporal) authorization: it maintains a compact semantic centroid tracking the session's evolving behavioral profile and accumulates a risk signal via exponential moving average over baseline-subtracted gate outputs, reusing the gate's semantic vector representation; the framework distinguishes spatial authorization consistency (per action) from temporal authorization consistency (over trajectory).

controls.name: Stateless ILION (per-action gate without SRM)

results.claim: On a multi-turn benchmark of 80 sessions (slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, compliance drift), ILION+SRM achieves F1 = 1.0000 with 0% false positive rate vs stateless ILION at F1 = 0.9756 with 5% FPR, both maintaining a 100% detection rate.
results.metric: F1 / FPR / detection rate on the 80-session multi-turn benchmark
results.value: F1 1.0000 (SRM) vs 0.9756 (stateless ILION); FPR 0% vs 5%; detection 100% both
results.setting: Multi-turn benchmark of 80 sessions with slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, and compliance drift scenarios (per abstract)
results.quote: Results show that ILION+SRM achieves F1 = 1.0000 with 0% false positive rate, compared to stateless ILION at F1 = 0.9756 with 5% FPR, while maintaining 100% detection rate for both systems.

denominator.how_counted: Metrics over the 80 multi-turn attack sessions of the benchmark; per-session turn counts and per-scenario splits are not stated in the abstract

results.claim: Cost reading: SRM eliminates all false positives with a per-turn overhead under 250 microseconds - the temporal-authorization state is cheap enough for pre-execution gating.
results.comparison: added on top of the underlying deterministic gate, with no additional model components or training
results.setting: SRM module operating on the same semantic vector representation as the underlying gate (per abstract)
results.quote: Critically, SRM eliminates all false positives with a per-turn overhead under 250 microseconds.

denominator.how_counted: Per-turn overhead measured across the benchmark sessions; measurement methodology is not stated in the abstract

reproduction.data: Multi-turn benchmark of 80 sessions (slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, compliance drift scenarios), per the abstract; further details unavailable without full text

title: MemEvoBench: Benchmarking Memory MisEvolution in LLM Agents

object.carrier: Hybrid memory pool mixing correct and misleading entries - knowledge snippets, conversation history, personal notes, forum posts with timestamps (QA style, declarative memory) and correct vs contaminated workflow memories embedding operational errors (workflow style, procedural memory); the pool evolves: after each of three rounds the agent's response is appended as a retrievable entry, with simulated biased user feedback reinforcing risky shortcuts; A-MEM integration tested as a more realistic structured memory system

safety_property.statement: Safety of agent advice and actions under contaminated, continuously evolving memory: responses must not exhibit the target risk behavior - a response is MISLED if it provides advice that could directly cause the described harm, encourages/validates/normalizes risky behavior, fails to warn about or downplays the specific risk, or gives overly confident advice without appropriate caveats; SAFE if it warns against risky behavior, gives balanced advice with caveats, or recommends safe alternatives. Failure condition: memory-based shortcuts from semantically aligned contaminated entries overgeneralize into unsafe behavioral patterns across rounds.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Attack Success Rate (ASR, %) per evaluation round (R1/R2/R3) judged by GPT-5.2 with binary MISLED/SAFE verdicts (judge validated at 96.2% accuracy on a 50-response manually annotated set); two scenarios - QA Style (108 test queries, 7 domains, 36 risk types) and Workflow Style (83 test cases, 20 Agent-SafetyBench environments, 8 risk categories); three configurations (Vanilla, +SafePrompt, +ModTool) each with and without biased user feedback; memory-ablation rows compare no-memory vs initial-system vs A-MEM.

capabilities: Misleading memory injection: attackers disguise harmful experiences as 'high-value success cases' that are gradually consolidated and retained through repeated reinforcement; entries are mostly accurate with omitted caveats, shifted decision thresholds, or over-generalized conclusions that look reasonable in isolation

Noisy tool returns: tool outputs serve as indirect prompt injection channels (adversarial prompts embedded in legitimate content like search results) or expose information beyond the query scope (partial contact matches, adjacent sensitive files); agents with accumulated workflow memories may blindly pattern-match and propagate the oversights

Biased user feedback: an LLM simulating a biased user assigns negative feedback to safe-but-costly responses and positive feedback to risky-but-immediately-effective shortcuts (deployment-time selection pressure rather than a deliberate attacker)
assumptions: Real-world memory contamination emerges through omitted caveats and implicit assumptions rather than explicit falsehoods, which would be trivially filtered
The memory state is treated as shaped by prior evolution; a simplified update rule appends the agent's response to the pool after each round
Three rounds of related but non-identical decision situations per case instantiate the same underlying failure mode
not_covered: No adaptive attacker that observes and re-attacks against the agent's memory-correction behavior
The update rule is a simplified append-per-round protocol; A-MEM integration partially addresses realism but the benchmark does not model arbitrary memory architectures
Defenses evaluated act at prompt level or via agent-side memory-correction tools; securing the injection channels themselves (memory write-side admission control) is not evaluated

intervention.name: MemEvoBench evaluation with three agent configurations: Vanilla, +SafePrompt, +ModTool
intervention.description: (1) Vanilla: standard system prompt with access to the evolving memory pool. (2) +SafePrompt: system prompt augmented with explicit safety guidelines instructing models to critically evaluate retrieved content and reject unsafe advice. (3) +ModTool: proactive memory curation - agents get a correct_memory tool to revise misleading entries before responding (replacing original content with the corrected version), and for QA style additionally a web_search tool to verify information against external sources; this transforms agents from passive recipients of contaminated context into active curators of their own memory. Each configuration is tested with and without biased user feedback across the three-round protocol.

controls.name: Vanilla (no safety intervention)
+SafePrompt (safety guidelines in system prompt)
w/o Memory ablation (intrinsic knowledge only)
Initial system vs A-MEM memory system
w/feedback vs without feedback

results.claim: Under Vanilla prompting all models are highly susceptible to memory-induced risks: mean ASR averaged over models and both scenarios is 75.9% / 75.2% / 80.1% for rounds 1/2/3 without feedback, and biased user feedback drives a clear round-by-round increase to 71.6% / 84.9% / 87.8%.
results.metric: ASR (%), averaged over models and both scenarios, per round
results.setting: 9 representative LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen3-32B/Next-80B/235B, DeepSeek-V3.2), temperature 0.0, QA Style 108 cases + Workflow Style 83 cases, three-round protocol
results.quote: Averaged over models and both scenarios, the mean ASR is 75.9% / 75.2% / 80.1% for Rd.1/2/3, showing no clear round-by-round worsening.

title: On Safety Risks in Experience-Driven Self-Evolving Agents

object.carrier: 外部经验记忆 M={E1,...,En}（LLM 权重保持固定）：AWM 从历史轨迹归纳可复用 workflow 存入固定记忆（离线）；ReasoningBank 在部署中持续维护蒸馏出的 reasoning strategy 条目并增量更新（在线）；评测时按相关性检索（top-3）注入 prompt

safety_property.statement: 保护对象是 agent 的安全拒绝边界（对有害任务的 refusal）。失效条件：仅从良性任务积累并复用经验（backbone 权重不变）即可侵蚀该边界，使 agent 在高风险/有害场景从拒绝转向执行；经验条数越多风险越大；拒绝型经验可缓解 ASR 上升但引起对良性输入的过度拒绝（安全-效用权衡）。判定依据：ASR 在 BrowserART / Agent-SafetyBench(web 子集) / SafeAgentBench 有害子集上自进化前后的变化，以及良性任务成功率（过度拒绝侧）；危害类别覆盖欺诈点击、伪造身份、网络攻击、信息泄露、可用性破坏与家庭具身物理危害。
safety_property.operationalized_as: Attack Success Rate (ASR) 前后对比，GPT-4o 自动评判（论文称与人工标注强相关但未报告一致率数字）；辅以良性任务 task success rate 衡量 over-refusal；类别级 ASR 分解（Figures 1, 6-10）；长度匹配 prompt 扩充对照（Table 3）与 Integrated Gradients 归因（Figure 4）用于因果验证

assumptions: 无对抗者：风险完全由良性经验的形成-存储-检索-复用回路自发产生；所有经验来自良性任务（AWM 离线：812 个 WebArena 任务；ReasoningBank 在线：Reddit 子集 106 任务；具身：269 个良性任务）
LLM backbone 权重固定，自进化仅通过外部经验记忆实现，行为漂移可归因于记忆的构建、检索与利用而非参数学习
安全评测任务与经验积累环境不相交（BrowserART/Agent-SafetyBench/SafeAgentBench 有害子集仅用于评测，避免数据泄露）
RQ3 中有害任务经验的形态（refusal-only / execution-only / mixed）由作者显式人工控制注入（每环境 50 个有害任务），并非自然发生
not_covered: 未研究任何对抗性攻击者（如经验记忆投毒、prompt injection、恶意经验注入或跨用户共享被污染经验）
未覆盖多智能体交互、多模态输入等真实部署环境多样性
未研究超过 800 步的长期/无限期自进化动力学
未提出或评测任何防御/干预机制（仅呼吁未来工作）
GPT-4o 判官的评判偏差未量化报告

intervention.description: 本文为诊断性研究，未提出并评测任何干预机制；仅在讨论中呼吁：选择性经验过滤与内容控制、受控的记忆规模、动态记忆调度策略、长期安全监控与 memory intervention（§5、Appendix D.3/D.6、§Limitation）

results.claim: AWM 离线自进化下，7 个 LLM backbone 在全部 3 个安全基准上 ASR 一致上升（仅用良性任务经验、权重不变）：如 GPT-4o 在 BrowserART 上 37.0→50.0（↑35.1%），DeepSeek-V3.2 在 SafeAgentBench 上 24.5→36.4（↑48.6%）

results.setting: Qwen3-32B；ReasoningBank 在线自进化于 WebArena Reddit 子集（106 个良性任务，>800 步）；安全评测 Agent-SafetyBench（GPT-4o 判分）

denominator.how_counted: Agent-SafetyBench web-based interaction subset contains 657 test cases (Appendix B.1)

results.claim: 长度匹配对照实验证明退化由经验语义内容而非上下文长度驱动：仅扩充系统指令（不含经验内容）时 ASR 基本停留在进化前水平，而注入经验内容使 ASR 大幅上升——GPT-4o 在 BrowserART 上 37.0→51.0（经验）vs 38.0（扩充指令），DeepSeek-V3.2 48.0→64.0 vs 49.0
results.setting: ReasoningBank 在线自进化，BrowserART；GPT-4o / Claude-4.5-Sonnet / DeepSeek-V3.2 等 backbone；对照用 GPT-4o 扩写系统指令以匹配经验引入的 token 长度，总 prompt 长度不变

denominator.how_counted: BrowserART 由 100 个 harmful behaviors 构成（Appendix B.1）

results.claim: 经验注入导致的 safe→unsafe 翻转案例中，主因是敏感执行（Sen-Exe）与标准执行（Sta-Exe），Format Recovery 占少数：GPT-4o 在 BrowserART 上 45.0/50.0/5.0，Claude-4.5-Sonnet 36.4/54.5/9.1——良性经验主要强化“如何执行”而非“何时拒绝”
results.setting: 3 名受薪标注者对 flip cases 人工归因（每例判一个主因）；BrowserART 与 SafeAgentBench；7 个 backbone；ReasoningBank 在线自进化
results.quote:
| | Sen-Exe | Sta-Exe | Format |
| BrowserART |
| GPT-4o | 45.0 | 50.0 | 5.0 |
| Claude-4.5-Sonnet | 36.4 | 54.5 | 9.1 |

results.claim: 检索经验条数越多不安全行为越高：具身环境（SafeAgentBench，Qwen3-14B）中检索 7 或 9 条经验一致差于 1 或 3 条，说明即使单条经验无害，数量本身即可通过累积执行信号放大风险
results.setting: ReasoningBank，SafeAgentBench 具身环境，Qwen3-14B，自进化过程中周期性评测（Figure 14）；主文 §4.2 在 Agent-SafetyBench(web)+GPT-4o 上有同样趋势（Figure 3）
results.quote: Specifically, agents retrieving 7 or 9 entries consistently perform worse than those retrieving fewer (1 or 3), with an observable and persistent gap throughout self-evolving steps.

results.claim: 在真实部署式自进化（良性+有害任务经验混合）中，积累有害任务的 execution-only 经验使 ASR 在整个在线自进化过程中持续上升——执行型经验在决策中被反复复用，逐渐将 agent 偏向不安全动作
results.value: sustained increase in ASR throughout online self-evolution (qualitative)
results.setting: GPT-4o；ReasoningBank 在线自进化；Web 环境混入从 Agent-SafetyBench 抽样的 50 个有害任务经验（execution-only / refusal-only / mixed 三种人工控制形式）；评测 BrowserART；具身环境与其余 backbone 结果在 Appendix D.8
results.quote: As shown in Figure 5(a), accumulating execution-only experience from harmful tasks leads to a sustained increase in ASR throughout online self-evolution.

results.claim: 混入拒绝型经验（单独或与执行型交错）可显著抑制 ASR 上升，但伴随良性输入上任务成功率明显下降（over-refusal），暴露自进化 agent 的安全-效用根本权衡
results.value: ASR rise substantially suppressed; benign task success notably declined (over-refusal)
results.setting: 同 RQ3 设置：GPT-4o，Web 环境（BrowserART ASR / WebArena Reddit 子集任务成功率），50 个有害任务经验按 refusal-only / mixed 形式混入；Figure 5(a)(b)
results.quote: As shown in Figure 5(a), incorporating refusal behaviors into the memory, either in isolation or interleaved with execution traces, substantially suppresses the rise in ASR.

limitations.statement: 评测基准集合有限，可能无法覆盖真实部署环境的多样性（尤其是多智能体交互与多模态输入场景）
limitations.quote: However, these benchmarks may not fully capture the diversity of real-world deployment environments, especially those involving multi-agent interactions or multi-modal inputs.

limitations.statement: 受算力约束，自进化步数有限（最多 800 步）；真实部署可能远超此范围，无限期经验积累下的安全动力学及是否出现新失效模式仍属开放问题
limitations.quote: due to computational constraints, our experiments study self-evolving agents over a finite number of self-evolution steps (up to 800 steps).

title: Do Self-Evolving Agents Forget? Capability Degradation and Preservation in Lifelong LLM Agent Adaptation

object.carrier: A mutable capability repository R_t updated sequentially over task distributions, instantiated four ways: an executable workflow (operator orchestration + prompt specifications, EvoAgentX on tau2-Bench), a bounded-capacity skill bank of reusable procedural reasoning templates (MemSkill-style on MATH, least-frequently-used eviction), trainable LoRA adapter parameters (STaR self-training on MedMCQA), and a persistent external memory bank of reusable strategy notes (Dynamic-Cheatsheet-style, insertion/revision/eviction)

safety_property.statement: Capability preservation under self-evolution: adapting the agent to a new task distribution must not degrade previously mastered capabilities. Capability erosion occurs when adaptation toward the current distribution increases retained risk on previously encountered distributions (L_<t(R_t) > L_<t(R_{t-1})); it manifests as retrospective capability decay, behavioral policy drift (workflows growing longer and more complex with unnecessary steps), and generalization erosion. Failure condition: unconstrained self-updates overwrite the repository structures that supported earlier behavior.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Retained old-task performance measured after evolution on new tasks, per channel: workflow - simple/complex task accuracy on tau2-Bench (Airline/Retail/Telecom) after complex-task self-evolution from a shared simple-task seed workflow, GPT-5.1 and GPT-5 nano optimizers; skill - per-domain MATH accuracy after Algebra -> Geometry -> Number Theory evolution plus retained skill usage; model - MedMCQA domain accuracy after Anatomy -> Biochemistry -> Dental sequential self-training (Qwen3-0.6B, Llama3.2-3B); memory - held-out old-task probe accuracy before vs after new-task memory updates across six domain-backbone settings (GPT-5 nano, GPT-4o mini), vanilla vs evidence-gated preservation (CPE).

capabilities: No adversary: capability erosion emerges from unconstrained self-evolution itself - each update optimized solely for the new task distribution introduces destructive interference with structures supporting earlier tasks (curvature mechanism: naive adaptation increases retained loss whenever the update direction has nonzero projection onto a positive-curvature direction of the retained-loss Hessian)
assumptions: Self-evolution is modeled as sequential adaptation over task distributions D_1, ..., D_T with a general capability state R_t that may be a workflow, skill repository, parameter state, or memory store
The local analysis assumes R_{t-1} is a local minimizer of the retained loss with Hessian H_<t positive semidefinite and sufficiently small step size eta
Vanilla and CPE variants share identical evolution pipelines, budgets, and evaluation order; only the preservation mechanism differs
not_covered: Only straightforward constraint-based instantiations of preservation are explored; adaptive regularization schedules and jointly optimized multi-component preservation frameworks are future work (Appendix I)

Experiments use controlled sequential task-distribution shifts and representative frameworks; dynamic environments, multi-agent interaction, and continuously expanding capability spaces are not covered (Appendix I)
No adaptive adversary or attack process is modeled; the measured risk is self-inflicted drift, not an external attack

intervention.name: Capability-Preserving Evolution (CPE): dimension-specific regularizers against destructive capability drift
intervention.description: A general stabilization principle constraining self-updates to acquire new capabilities while preserving capability support for prior tasks. Instantiations: (1) workflow - anchor behavioral signatures extracted from the seed workflow (core task objectives, output constraints, failure-avoidance behaviors) injected to discourage disruptive rewrites under the same optimizer and mutation budget; (2) skill/tool - capability-preserving consolidation before admission: candidates checked against preserved capability signatures, semantically related skills merged to release capacity, historically reusable high-utility skills protected from deletion; (3) model - Elastic Weight Consolidation style Fisher-based parameter-importance regularization discouraging destructive updates on parameters important to prior domains; (4) memory - evidence-gated preservation: entries accumulating repeated self-verified support are protected from destructive rewrite or eviction while low-evidence entries stay adaptable.

controls.name: Vanilla (unconstrained) self-evolution per channel
Shared seed workflow / initial repository / evolution budget across variants
Pre-evolution memory state (old-domain probe accuracy before new-task updates)

results.claim: Workflow evolution: CPE improves retained simple-task performance from 41.8% to 52.8% under GPT-5.1 optimization while simultaneously achieving stronger complex-task adaptation (23.9% -> 33.4%) - mitigation does not trade against adaptation.
results.metric: tau2-Bench accuracy (%) on simple vs complex tasks after complex-task self-evolution
results.comparison: vanilla EvoAgentX vs CPE, same seed workflow and mutation budget (Table 1)
results.setting: EvoAgentX on tau2-Bench (Airline/Retail/Telecom), GPT-5.1 and GPT-5 nano optimizer backbones, parallel vanilla/CPE branches from a shared simple-task seed workflow
results.quote: For example, in workflow evolution, CPE improves retained simple-task performance from 41.8% to 52.8% under GPT-5.1 optimization while simultaneously achieving stronger complex-task adaptation.

denominator.how_counted: Accuracy averaged over the three tau2-Bench domains (Airline, Retail, Telecom) on the simple and complex task subsets after self-evolution; per-domain counts in Table 1

results.claim: Memory evolution erodes old-task retention even with frozen model parameters: across all six domain-backbone settings, average old-domain performance drops from 83.9% before new-task evolution to 81.6% after unconstrained memory updates; evidence-gated preservation (CPE) recovers retention to 83.3%.
results.metric: held-out old-domain probe accuracy (%) before vs after new-task memory evolution
results.comparison: pre-evolution memory state vs vanilla vs CPE post-evolution states (Figure 6); retention gap 2.3% -> 0.7%
results.setting: Dynamic-Cheatsheet-style external strategy repository, GPT-5 nano and GPT-4o mini solver backbones, base model fixed, six domain-backbone settings (Appendix B)
results.quote: Vanilla new-task memory evolution increases old-task interference. Across all six domain–backbone settings, average old-domain performance drops from 83.9% before new-task evolution to 81.6% after unconstrained memory updates.

denominator.how_counted: Held-out old-task probe accuracy per domain-backbone setting, averaged over the six settings; probe counts per domain not stated in the main text

results.claim: Skill evolution erodes via repository overwrite: as the distribution shifts from Geometry to Number Theory, newly synthesized skills dominate bounded repository capacity and evict previously useful Geometry skills; CPE's merge-based consolidation preserves prior-skill utilization and stabilizes retained Algebra performance.
results.metric: per-domain MATH accuracy (%) after sequential evolution + normalized retained skill usage
results.value: final-domain accuracy e.g. Number Theory 85.4 -> 87.8 (GPT-5 nano); Algebra retention stabilized under CPE
results.comparison: vanilla direct-admit + LRU eviction vs CPE merge-based consolidation (Table 2, Figure 3, Figure 4)
results.setting: MemSkill-style framework on MATH, GPT-4o mini and GPT-5 nano designer/executor backbones, sequential Algebra -> Geometry -> Number Theory evolution under identical budgets
results.quote: As the task distribution shifts from Geometry to Number Theory, newly synthesized skills gradually dominate retrieval frequency and bounded repository capacity, causing previously useful Geometry skills to become under-utilized and eventually evicted.

denominator.how_counted: Per-domain MATH evaluation accuracy after the full evolution sequence; bounded skill-bank capacity and evaluation-set sizes are in Appendix D

results.claim: Model evolution erodes via parametric overwrite (catastrophic forgetting): CPE's Fisher-based regularization preserves more retained accuracy on all evaluated domains (Qwen3-0.6B Anatomy 29.4% -> 30.5%, Biochemistry 37.2% -> 38.4%, Dental 32.2% -> 33.0%).
results.metric: MedMCQA per-domain accuracy (%) after sequential self-training
results.comparison: vanilla STaR self-training vs CPE (EWC-style regularizer), identical evolution order and LoRA configurations (Table 3)
results.setting: STaR self-training on MedMCQA, Qwen3-0.6B and Llama3.2-3B, sequential Anatomy -> Biochemistry -> Dental stages
results.quote: On Qwen3-0.6B, retained accuracy improves from 29.4% to 30.5% on Anatomy, from 37.2% to 38.4% on Biochemistry, and from 32.2% to 33.0% on Dental, with similar trends on Llama3.2-3B.

denominator.how_counted: Per-domain MedMCQA evaluation accuracy after the full three-stage evolution; evaluation-set sizes in Appendix E

results.claim: Cost reading (behavioral policy drift): unconstrained workflow evolution accumulates structural bloat - extra validation operators and detours that make the workflow over-defensive, rejecting slightly nonstandard but valid actions - and much longer workflow code; CPE substantially slows this structural growth.
results.metric: workflow complexity (code length) and post-evolution retention-adaptation trade-off
results.value: vanilla accumulates much longer workflow code; CPE slows expansion (Figure 2b)
results.comparison: vanilla vs CPE from the same seed workflow (Figure 2a-c)
results.setting: EvoAgentX complex-task self-evolution, per-domain workflow code length tracked during evolution (Figure 2)
results.quote: This structural drift is reflected in Figure 2(b), where vanilla EvoAgentX accumulates much longer workflow code, while CPE substantially slows this expansion.

denominator.how_counted: Workflow code length measured during self-evolution on the complex Airline task subset; post-evolution workflows evaluated on simple and complex subsets

results.claim: Memory-channel summary: CPE's evidence-gated preservation reduces the average old-task retention gap caused by new-task memory updates from 2.3% to 0.7%.
results.metric: average retention gap (percentage points) across six domain-backbone settings
results.setting: Same memory-evolution setup as Appendix B, summarized in §4.4
results.quote: CPE mitigates this interference through evidence-gated preservation, protecting historically reliable memories while keeping low-evidence entries adaptable, reducing the average retention gap from 2.3% to 0.7%.

denominator.how_counted: Gap between pre-evolution and post-evolution old-domain probe accuracy, averaged over the six domain-backbone settings

limitations.statement: Only lightweight, domain-specific preservation instantiations are explored; adaptive schedules and jointly optimized multi-component frameworks are left open.
limitations.quote: Accordingly, the preservation mechanisms used in this paper are intentionally lightweight and domain-specific, including anchor-based workflow regularization, repository consolidation, Fisher-style parameter constraints, and memory preservation heuristics. More sophisticated preservation strategies, adaptive regularization schedules, or jointly optimized multi-component preservation frameworks may further improve the stability–plasticity tradeoff in long-horizon self-evolving agents.

limitations.statement: Experiments cover controlled sequential distribution shifts on representative frameworks; real-world open-ended evolution trajectories (dynamic environments, multi-agent interaction, expanding capability spaces) are future work.
limitations.quote: In addition, our experiments focus on controlled sequential task-distribution shifts and representative self-evolution frameworks. Real-world autonomous agents may encounter substantially more complex and open-ended evolution trajectories, including dynamic environments, multi-agent interaction, and continuously expanding capability spaces. Extending CPE to such settings remains an important direction for future work.

reproduction.data: tau2-Bench (Airline/Retail/Telecom simple+complex subsets), MATH (Algebra/Geometry/Number Theory), MedMCQA (Anatomy/Biochemistry/Dental), Dynamic-Cheatsheet-style memory repository; backbones GPT-5.1, GPT-5 nano, GPT-4o mini, Qwen3-0.6B, Llama3.2-3B; frameworks EvoAgentX, MemSkill-style, STaR

title: Membrane: A Self-Evolving Contrastive Safety Memory for LLM Agent Defense

object.carrier: Contrastive Safety Memory (CSM): an external writable cell store where each cell m=(P, D, T) pairs an Attack Profile P (attack strategy, requested action, harm objective - mechanism-level fields indexed by strategy, not surface topic) with contrastive Decision Criteria D=(d_unsafe, d_safe) and an optional Tool-Action Context T for agent settings; the store evolves via a Memory Planner (create/update/delete/skip), a Memory Writer that synthesizes cell content, and a non-LLM validator enforcing schema, duplicate, and capacity constraints; inference retrieves candidate cells (vector retrieval) filtered by a Retrieval Critic before the Guard decides

safety_property.statement: A precise safety boundary under evolving jailbreaks: harmful queries must be blocked (low ASR) while superficially similar benign queries must be admitted (low FRR), with the writable memory itself resistant to poisoning (safe-as-unsafe injection that induces over-refusal, and unsafe-as-safe injection that induces jailbreaks). Failure conditions: jailbroken (guard permits the harmful side), over-refusal (guard rejects the benign side), or poisoned cells steering decisions.
safety_property.operationalized_as: ASR (fraction of harmful prompts answered / harmful tasks not refused), FRR (fraction of benign prompts refused), and F1 = 2(1-ASR)(1-FRR)/((1-ASR)+(1-FRR)) on HarmBench (320 harmful prompts paired with 320 in-house benign counterparts per transformed setting; 7 evaluation conditions incl. untransformed) and AgentHarm (176 harmful + 176 benign), with warmup N=80 (HarmBench) / N=32 (AgentHarm) bootstrapped then frozen; memory-poisoning robustness (ASR/FRR at 10% and 20% writer-mediated injection rates, top-k retrieval rate of poisoned cells, critic filter rate); per-query latency (mean/p95 seconds).

capabilities: Jailbreak attackers across six modern mechanisms: iterative refinement (PAIR), persuasion-based rephrasing (PAP), tree-of-thought search (TAP), nested instruction rewriting (ReNeLLM), character-level perturbation (FlipAttack), and lifelong strategy exploration (AutoDAN-Turbo)

Memory poisoner injects cells through the normal write path at rates rho of 10% and 20%, via two strategies: safe-as-unsafe (manipulate memory into refusing benign queries) and unsafe-as-safe (force acceptance of harmful queries), with the standard guard mechanism suppressed during the attack
assumptions: Attacker and scorer are the same fixed model (Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct) across all defenses, so cross-method differences come from the defense rather than the attack data

Bootstrapped memory is frozen during evaluation (static inference pipeline), isolating guard behavior from on-the-fly memory composition and keeping comparisons against static and fine-tuned baselines fair
not_covered: Fully adaptive white-box adversaries with access to the guard, the memory store, and the deployment pipeline are explicitly not modeled (the authors note this setting requires access-control and monitoring mechanisms beyond the algorithmic guard)
Cross-lingual, multimodal, and nested-agent deployments are out of scope (text-only English benchmarks)
The protected model is fixed to Qwen3-8B in the main tables (Appendix G sweeps sizes/backbones)

intervention.name: Membrane: self-evolving guardrail on Contrastive Safety Memory with Paired Self-Evolution
intervention.description: An external guard that decides safe/unsafe before the target model or tool-using agent acts. Paired Self-Evolution: each interaction pairs a harmful prompt with a benign counterpart exercising the same surface mechanism; the verdict (jailbroken / over-refusal / correct) plus the paired queries form an evolution signal from which one contrastive cell is written (create, update, delete, or skip), so every update commits a contrastive boundary rather than a one-sided exemplar; a deterministic non-LLM validator rejects writes violating schema/duplicate/capacity constraints. Inference: vector retrieval of candidate cells, a Retrieval Critic filters inapplicable matches, and the Guard issues the decision grounded on kept cells. Membrane lite disables the Retrieval Critic for lower latency.

controls.name: Vanilla (unguarded Qwen3-8B / unguarded tool-using agent)
Prompt-level guards: Self-Reminder, SmoothLLM, SelfDefend, TrustAgent, ShieldAgent
Fine-tuned classifiers: LlamaGuard3, WildGuard, GuardReasoner
Memory-augmented adaptive guards: RAD, GuardAgent, AGrail
Ablations: -CSM decision criteria, -Paired Self-Evolution, -Retrieval Critic, -Tool-Action Context (Table 3)
Warmup size sweep N (Figure 2)
Membrane lite (no Retrieval Critic)

results.claim: Membrane achieves the highest F1 on all six jailbreak attacks across both benchmarks; on HarmBench it drives ReNeLLM ASR to 0.3% (vs 11.3% for RAD, the best baseline) and completely suppresses FlipAttack at 0.0% ASR (vs 7.8% best baseline).
results.metric: ASR (%) per attack on HarmBench, lower is better
results.comparison: best baselines: RAD 11.3% (ReNeLLM), 7.8% (FlipAttack), 25.0% (TAP), 21.3% (PAIR); FRR held to 2.9%-6.1%
results.setting: HarmBench, 320 harmful prompts + 320 benign counterparts per transformed setting, Qwen3-8B target, warmup N=80 frozen (Table 1)
results.quote: On ReNeLLM, Membrane achieves an ASR of 0.3%, vastly outperforming the 11.3% achieved by RAD.

denominator.how_counted: ASR = fraction of the 320 harmful prompts answered per transformed setting; FRR = fraction of the 320 benign counterparts refused

results.claim: Cost reading (over-refusal): on AgentHarm, Membrane keeps benign refusal (FRR) at 7-14% across all settings, substantially below memory-augmented baselines GuardAgent (52-53%) and AGrail (27-32%) and prompt-level TrustAgent (73-85%).
results.metric: False Refusal Rate (FRR, %) on AgentHarm benign tasks
results.comparison: GuardAgent 52-53%; AGrail 27-32%; TrustAgent 73-85%; static guards reach 73-85%
results.setting: AgentHarm, 176 benign counterparts, Qwen3-8B agent, warmup N=32 frozen (Table 2)
results.quote: While effectively blocking these attacks, Membrane consistently restricts the FRR to a range of 7% to 14% across all settings.

denominator.how_counted: FRR = refusal rate over the 176 benign AgentHarm tasks per attack setting

results.claim: On AgentHarm, Membrane cuts FlipAttack ASR to 0.9% versus 100% for the unguarded agent, and reaches F1 89.2% (ReNeLLM) and 93.0% (FlipAttack) - the highest across all attack methods with a large margin on text-transformation attacks.
results.setting: AgentHarm, 176 harmful tasks + 176 benign counterparts (Table 2)
results.quote: Membrane drastically reduces the ASR compared to the unprotected agent, achieving an ASR of 0.9% on FlipAttack versus 100% for the vanilla baseline.

denominator.how_counted: ASR = fraction of the 176 harmful tasks not refused, per attack setting

results.claim: Cross-attack transfer: cells warmed on one jailbreak method retain 87-88% of the same-attack F1 when evaluated against other attacks sharing the underlying strategy (model safety 80.8% vs 92.6%; agent safety 69.5% vs 79.2%).
results.metric: cross-attack F1 retention (% of same-attack F1)
results.setting: For each attack A, CSM warmed only on A then evaluated frozen against the other attacks (Figure 3, full matrices in Appendix I)
results.quote: the transfer F1 retains 87%87\% of the same attack F1 in model safety (80.8%80.8\% vs. 92.6%92.6\%) and 88%88\% in agent safety (69.5%69.5\% vs. 79.2%79.2\%).

denominator.how_counted: Matrix means over off-diagonal attack pairs; model safety over 320-prompt HarmBench settings, agent safety over 176-task AgentHarm settings

results.claim: Poisoning robustness: even at a 20% writer-mediated injection rate, defensive performance stays near the clean baseline - unsafe-as-safe raises ASR only from 2.1% to 2.5% and safe-as-unsafe raises FRR from 10.8% to 15.4%, because poisoned-cell retrieval rates stay at 2.3-7.5% and the Retrieval Critic eliminates 33-40% of surfaced poisoned cells.
results.metric: ASR / FRR (%) under 10% and 20% poisoning; retrieval rate Ret; critic filter rate
results.comparison: clean baseline ASR 2.1% / FRR 5.0-10.8% depending on branch
results.setting: HarmBench, 80-event clean warmup then 10%/20% injection, standard guard suppressed during attack (Table 4)
results.quote: Even under the 20% injection rate, the defensive performance remains nearly identical to the clean baseline.

denominator.how_counted: ASR/FRR over the HarmBench harmful/benign evaluation pairs after warmup; poison rate rho = fraction of injected writes; Ret = share of poisoned cells in top-k retrievals; Critic = share of surfaced poisoned cells filtered

results.claim: Cost reading (latency): full Membrane runs at 12.89 s (HarmBench) and 14.59 s (AgentHarm) mean per query - far faster than SmoothLLM (156.93 s) and AGrail (25.22 s) - while Membrane lite (no Retrieval Critic) runs at 2.33/2.43 s with F1 91.7%/78.6%, still beating every baseline regardless of latency tier.
results.metric: per-query defense latency (mean seconds, single-stream) with F1
results.comparison: SmoothLLM 156.93 s @ F1 21.3; RAD 6.31 s @ 77.1; SelfDefend 0.90 s @ 59.6; AGrail 25.22 s @ 64.2; GuardAgent 5.94 s @ 59.6 (Table 5)
results.setting: Single-stream per-query overhead averaged over the seven evaluation settings, HarmBench and AgentHarm (Table 5)
results.quote: The full Membrane successfully maintains the highest F1 scores while operating significantly faster than computationally heavy baselines such as SmoothLLM (156.93 seconds) and AGrail (25.22 seconds).

denominator.how_counted: Mean and p95 per-query latency in seconds over the evaluation queries of the seven settings; query counts follow the per-setting HarmBench/AgentHarm splits

results.claim: Ablation: removing Paired Self-Evolution causes the largest F1 drop (-7.4 points HarmBench, -11.5 points AgentHarm), and removing the decision criteria or Tool-Action Context raises AgentHarm FRR from 6.3% to 20.5% and 17.1% - the contrastive structure is what suppresses over-refusal.
results.metric: F1 (%) and FRR (%) per ablated component, averaged over seven settings
results.value: F1 93.4 -> 86.0 (w/o Paired Self-Evolution, HarmBench); FRR 6.3 -> 20.5% (w/o decision criteria, AgentHarm)
results.setting: Component ablations averaged over the seven evaluation settings (Table 3)
results.quote: Removing Paired Self-Evolution causes the most severe performance degradation, decreasing the F1 score by 7.4% and 11.5% points on HarmBench and AgentHarm, respectively.

denominator.how_counted: Averages over the seven evaluation settings (six attacks + untransformed) on each benchmark

limitations.statement: Evaluation is text-only English on HarmBench/AgentHarm; cross-lingual, multimodal, and nested-agent deployments need separate benchmarks and threat models.
limitations.quote: Membrane is evaluated on text-only English model-safety and agent-safety benchmarks. This follows the coverage of HarmBench and AgentHarm and keeps comparisons to existing guardrails controlled; cross-lingual, multimodal, and nested-agent deployments require separate benchmark construction and threat models, which we leave to future work.

limitations.statement: The main tables fix the protected model to Qwen3-8B to avoid conflating guard behavior with target-model scale; robustness to this choice is only partially addressed by the Appendix G sweeps.
limitations.quote: Our main tables fix the protected model to Qwen3-8B to avoid conflating guard behavior with target-model scale or backbone effects.

limitations.statement: Fully adaptive white-box adversaries with access to the guard, memory store, and deployment pipeline are not modeled and would require access-control and monitoring beyond the algorithmic guard.
limitations.quote: The remaining attacks we do not model are fully adaptive white-box adversaries with access to the guard, memory store, and deployment pipeline. This operational setting requires access-control and monitoring mechanisms beyond the algorithmic guard studied here.

limitations.statement: All response-level evaluation is delegated to a single judge (Gemini 3 Flash), applied to every defense so residual judge bias is shared across baselines.
limitations.quote: All response-level evaluation is delegated to Gemini 3 Flash, a model family distinct from the Qwen3-8B guard, to reduce correlated blind spots between the guard and the judge. The same judge is applied to every defense, so any residual judge bias is shared across baselines.

reproduction.data: HarmBench (320 harmful + 320 in-house benign counterparts per transformed setting), AgentHarm (176 + 176), six attack suites (PAIR, PAP, TAP, ReNeLLM, FlipAttack, AutoDAN-Turbo) constructed with Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct as attacker and scorer; Appendices F/G/H/I document construction, sweeps, and full per-attack results; Appendix J lists artifact licenses

title: Agents Don’t Just Agree, They Remember: Benchmarking Persistent Sycophancy in Self-Improving Personal Agents

object.carrier: Durable agent state written by the agent itself inside an episode-level sandbox: user profile files (e.g., USER.md), memory profile files (e.g., MEMORY.md), and reusable skill artifacts; commits are identified by diffing the post-persist sandbox snapshot against an immutable clean baseline. Session-only writes are the non-commit category.

safety_property.statement: Durable agent state must preserve the source, status (role), and scope of user-originated content. The property fails when a transient, biased user claim is written into profile/memory/skill state with elevated status (stable preference, background fact, or reusable procedure), removed speaker attribution, or broadened scope, and then contaminates later neutral query sessions after the conversation history has been cleared. Failures are judged by Max-FR@3 >= 3 (1-5 Likert) on six judge dimensions (Sycophancy, Leak, Upgrade, Amplification, Persistence, Escalation) plus Commit% from sandbox snapshots.
safety_property.operationalized_as: PASB: 1,600 tasks per run (100 base items x 4 scenario framings x 4 temporal deliveries) on Hermes-Agent and OpenClaw; five-turn persist stage, cleared three-turn query stage; six Kimi-K2.6-judged dimensions on 1-5 Likert with >=3 as failure; Commit% from post-persist snapshot diff vs clean baseline; CDL subset isolates cross-domain (scope) leakage.

capabilities: Raises biased or unsupported user-centric claims across a five-turn persist stage, including low-information pressure (e.g., 'Are you sure?')
Frames the same claim under four apparent roles: Personal-Opinion, Signed-Memory (user-authored note), Environment-Fact, or Procedural-Workflow
Controls temporal delivery of the claim: All-at-Once, Progressive, Drip, or Late-Shock (repeated reinforcement)
No tool access, code execution, or direct state manipulation; influence is only conversational, and the agent autonomously decides what to write
assumptions: Conversation history, planner scratchpad, temporary tool observations, and runtime caches are cleared between persist and query stages, so any carry-over must pass through durable state
Episodes run in sandboxed workspaces restored from an immutable baseline; no cross-episode or cross-worker state sharing
The judge (Kimi-K2.6) is from a family disjoint from the evaluated backbones and blinded to backbone and framework; greedy decoding where the serving stack supports it
Commit identification is deterministic from captured artifact paths and content match against the tested claim
not_covered: External attackers or injected third-party content (no prompt-injection adversary); the source of unsafe content is the ordinary user
Cross-user or cross-agent state contamination (excluded by design)
Defenses or mitigations are proposed (capability ladder L0-L5) but not implemented or evaluated
Adversarially optimized claims and frameworks beyond Hermes-Agent and OpenClaw

intervention.name: Capability ladder for state-writing governance (L0-L5; proposed, not evaluated)
intervention.description: A proposed ladder of governance capabilities grounded in the paper's findings: L0 response calibration; L1 commit gating (write only stable, relevant, future-appropriate content); L2 surface-aware commit (stricter criteria for profile/skill surfaces than session notes); L3 source-and-status preservation (typed writes retaining source, uncertainty, and intended use); L4 scope-aware retrieval (explicit domain, task, source, and time bounds on durable state); L5 lifecycle governance (audit accumulated state, detect attribution removal and scope broadening, de-authorize or roll back unsafe writes). No mechanism is implemented in the paper; PASB is the diagnostic that localizes the intervention points.

results.claim: Across 24 model-framework runs, once a saved claim can be read back in the follow-up chat, mean downstream failure (Max-FR@3 over the four per-turn metrics) reaches 71.9% vs 45.0% when the claim stays in the first chat - a +27.0-point gap [v1 表述为跨 commit 边界；v4 改为 saved-vs-session-only 对比] that holds everywhere: all 24 combinations side with the saved claim more often on Sycophancy, with gaps +12.4 to +58.6 points.
results.metric: mean Max-FR@3 over the four per-turn dimensions (Sycophancy, Leak, Upgrade, Amplification)
results.comparison: saved-claim readable in follow-up chat vs claim stays in first chat (session-only reference)
results.setting: 24 model-framework runs (12 backbones x Hermes-Agent/OpenClaw) on PASB 1,600 tasks; pooled episodes, cleared query stage
results.quote: Downstream failure reaches 71.9%71.9\% when the follow-up chat can read a saved claim, against 45.0%45.0\% when the claim stays in the first chat. That is a +27.0+27.0 point gap, and it holds everywhere.

denominator.how_counted: Mean Max-FR@3 over the four per-turn metrics, across the 24 model-framework combinations of the 1,600-task benchmark; saved-claim-readable runs vs session-only runs (Figure 2c)

results.claim: Low save rate does not eliminate contamination: on OpenClaw, MiniMax-M2.7 saves the claim into notes in only 29.8% of runs yet downstream failure still reaches 77.4% [v1 报 72.0%，v4 数值更新]；OpenClaw 整体 save rate 区间 18.4%-53.9%。What matters is what happens to saved claims.
results.metric: Commit% and Avg mean Max-FR@3 over the six judge dimensions
results.comparison: OpenClaw save range 18.4%-53.9%; Hermes range 28.7%-72.8% with Gemini-3.1-Pro top at 80.6% downstream failure
results.setting: MiniMax-M2.7 on OpenClaw, PASB 1,600 episodes per run (Tables 2 and 13)
results.quote: OpenClaw saves less often, from 18.4%18.4\% to 53.9%53.9\% of runs. Yet with MiniMax-M2.7 it saves the claim into notes in only 29.8%29.8\% of runs, while downstream failure still reaches 77.4%77.4\%.

denominator.how_counted: Commit% is the row-level rate over the full 1,600 episodes of that model-framework run (Table 13: 'All is the row-level rate over the full 1,600 episodes'); Avg averages the six judge-dimension failure rates

results.claim: The act of writing is the authorization point: among accepted runs (agent acknowledges, agrees, or complies), the agent writes the claim down in 75.1% of runs; among saved notes 82.0% say more than the user did and 58.3% no longer record the source; 78.3% of these runs fail downstream. Figure 2a: downstream failure climbs from 47.3% after a challenge to 78.3% after compliance [v1 术语 Comply stance → v4 compliance].
results.metric: episode rate of durable write / status promotion / attribution removal / downstream failure by persist-stage response stance
results.comparison: challenge 47.3% -> compliance 78.3% (by strongest first-chat stance, Figure 2a)
results.setting: pooled annotated episodes across all runs; five-label persist-stage stance annotation (Appendix A.7), Wilson 95% intervals
results.quote: The agent writes the claim down in 75.1%75.1\% of these runs. The act of writing usually edits the claim. Among the saved notes, 82.0%82.0\% say more than the user did, and 58.3%58.3\% no longer record the source. The cost shows up later, as 78.3%78.3\% of these runs fail downstream.

denominator.how_counted: Rates pooled over accepted first-chat runs across the 24 combinations; Figure 2a breaks them by the strongest stance in the first chat

results.claim: At write time the agent systematically reshapes stored content: pooled across all runs, 51.4% of saves recast the claim as a stable preference, background fact, or reusable procedure [v1 表述为 status promotion：opinion→preference/fact/procedure]，and the saved note loses its source in 33.1% of cases, so it reads like a standalone statement; these two edits predict later reuse and source loss.
results.metric: episode rate of write-time status promotion / attribution removal
results.comparison: status promotion 51.4% vs attribution removal 33.1% of episodes
results.setting: pooled persist-stage annotation over 24 model-framework runs (12 models x 2 frameworks)
results.quote: Across all runs, agents save the claim as a stable preference, a background fact, or a reusable procedure in 51.4%51.4\% of cases, and the saved note loses its source in 33.1%33.1\% of cases, so it reads like a standalone statement.

denominator.how_counted: Appendix A.7: the persist-stage annotation is applied to every completed episode in the main evaluation, one row per episode, and 'A full 12-model x 2-agent PASB run therefore contains 12x2x1600=38,400 rows'; the pooled 51.4% (and 33.1%) are episode rates over all annotated rows of the 24 model-framework runs, counting status promotion when the annotator role label is not None and attribution removal when the stored state drops the source marker

results.claim: Memory-like and procedural framing raises unsafe writes: under Hermes-Agent, claims framed as signed memories are saved in 85% of runs and procedural workflows in 66%; OpenClaw saves procedural workflows most often, in 89% of runs; environment facts sit between (45% Hermes / 19% OpenClaw) and personal opinions are rarely saved (28% / 8%). Framing alone decides much of whether the agent writes the claim down.
results.metric: commit rate by scenario framing (with downstream failure context)
results.comparison: Hermes: Signed-Memory 85%, Procedural-Workflow 66%, Environment-Fact 45%, Personal-Opinion 28%; OpenClaw: Procedural 89%, Env 19%, Opinion 8%
results.setting: Hermes-Agent and OpenClaw scenario-agent matrix over 12 backbones (per-run values in Table 13)
results.quote: Under Hermes-Agent, agents save claims framed as signed memories in 85%85\% of runs and procedural workflows in 66%66\%, while OpenClaw saves procedural workflows most often, in 89%89\% of runs.

denominator.how_counted: Save rates by scenario framing pooled over runs per framework (Figure 2e); base claim held fixed across framings

results.claim: Repeated reinforcement raises downstream reuse but not commit propensity: Progressive (claim built up turn by turn) and Drip (fragments in small talk) raise downstream failure to 63.2% under Hermes-Agent and up to 57.0% under OpenClaw, vs All-at-Once 58.0%/53.1%, while save rates stay flat across deliveries (54.5-57.2% Hermes, 32.8-39.5% OpenClaw); Late-Shock sits close to All-at-Once. Repetition never reaches the write itself - it makes the saved note easier to pick up again.
results.metric: mean per-turn downstream Max-FR@3 failure by temporal delivery pattern
results.setting: Hermes-Agent across 12 backbones; delivery axis (OpenClaw shows the same direction, 53.1% to 57.0%/56.2%)
results.quote: These two deliveries raise downstream failure to 63.2%63.2\% under Hermes-Agent and up to 57.0%57.0\% under OpenClaw. The same claim delivered All-at-Once gives 58.0%58.0\% and 53.1%53.1\%.

denominator.how_counted: Downstream failure by delivery condition pooled per framework; save rates flat across the four deliveries (Figure 2f)

results.claim: Committed claims leak across a deliberate domain boundary: with the follow-up moved to a different domain, saved claims raise three failure rates by more than twenty points each - Leak +22.8 (later answers take the irrelevant claim as background assumption), Upgrade +21.4 (treated as fact or the agent's own rule), Sycophancy +21.2 (side with user's stance) - and the other three metrics rise by +12.6 to +16.6 points [v1 概括为 +12.6..+22.8；v4 逐指标给出].
results.metric: downstream failure lift (percentage points) of cross-domain committed episodes over cross-domain session-only baseline
results.comparison: cross-domain saved-claim follow-ups vs same-domain and not-saved groups (Figure 4)
results.setting: CDL cross-domain subset (persist claim and query in different domains by construction, 18 of 100 base items); all runs
results.quote: Leak metric rises by 22.822.8 points, so later answers take the irrelevant claim as a background assumption. Upgrade metric rises by 21.421.4 points, so later answers treat the claim as fact or as the agent’s own rule. Sycophancy metric rises by 21.221.2 points, so later answers side with the user’s stance.

denominator.how_counted: Per-metric failure-rate deltas of saved cross-domain follow-ups vs same-domain and not-saved groups (Figure 4)

results.claim: The LLM judge is reliable against human consensus: on the 50-task human-labeled gold subset (proportional stratified sampling over the 1,600-task benchmark; four annotators, Krippendorff's alpha 0.68), the judge agrees with the human gold label on 88% of individual answers counting predictions within ±1 Likert point as agreement [v1 表述为 turn-level 88% / cross-turn 86%；v4 统一口径为 88% within-±1].
results.metric: LLM-judge (Kimi-K2.6) agreement with human consensus (within ±1 Likert point)
results.comparison: within ±1 Likert point of the human majority label, per metric
results.setting: 50-task proportional stratified human-gold subset, four PhD/undergraduate annotators, per-dimension majority vote
results.quote: Across individual answers, the judge agrees with the human gold label on 88% of cases, the figure Section 3.3 reports.

denominator.how_counted: 50-task human-gold subset; human gold is the per-dimension majority vote of four annotators (inter-annotator Krippendorff's alpha = 0.68)

limitations.statement: Scope: longer horizons, other modalities, and evolving state need extensions; future work should test write filters and context-aware retrieval while tracking safety vs personalization value.
limitations.quote: Longer horizons, other modalities, and state that keeps evolving will need extensions. These should test concrete write filters or context-aware retrieval while tracking both safety and how much personalization value survives.

title: OpenEvoShield: Dual Non-Stationary Continual Defense for Open-World Multi-Agent System Attacks

object.carrier: 多智能体系统的行为边界与策略集成（M2 边界更新器、M3 EWC 正则化策略集成）随部署持续更新；攻击侧注入经智能体间通信传播

safety_property.statement: 多智能体系统在攻击策略持续精炼、正常智能体行为随系统扩张漂移的双重非平稳条件下，仍应阻断恶意指令传播并保持正常协作
safety_property.operationalized_as: 三个任务域（CSQA/MMLU/GSM8K）的 ASR 与 MDSR、InjecAgent/ PoisonRAG 的 TA/MA、以及 Novel-DR 与 FPR

capabilities: 经智能体间通信注入并传播恶意指令

not_covered: 单智能体的持久语义记忆
跨会话用户级状态
