title: Are You Still the Agent I Authorized? Earned Authority under a Fixed Ceiling for Evolving Agents

object.carrier: Grant-relevant state S_t = model, harness/instructions, persistent memory and knowledge, skills, capability/tool configuration, delegation graph, task phase, enforcement state; authorization itself persists as a user-issued grant (effect ceiling B / lease L_max, initial active authority P_0, transition envelope M) stored in an external monitor's lease store outside the agent's control

safety_property.statement: Authorization continuity for evolving agents: when the agent's memory, skills, tools, workflow, delegation, task phase, or enforcement change under a live grant, the grant survives only if the mutation stays inside a grant-fixed transition envelope, and no mutation or runtime evidence (including agent-produced competence evidence) can amplify protected effects beyond the immutable user-issued effect ceiling fixed at grant time. Fails if complete mediation, closure-sound monitor view (A2), or monitor integrity (A5) is violated.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Formal theorems, not measurements: Theorem 1 (§V-B) and Theorem 3 (Appendix A-F) prove Effects(π) ⊆ union of scopes of user-granted root leases under assumptions A1-A5; Proposition 7 (Appendix A-G) shows dropping closure soundness breaks the bound by an unbounded margin; §VIII only proposes empirical metrics (grant persistence rate, post-mutation unauthorized-effect rate, false invalidation rate, interaction cost) without running them.

capabilities: Controls ingested content, skills, remote tools, and memory, and may thereby steer the agent's behavior
Can cause evolution under a live grant so the mutated state inherits authority granted to an earlier state
Can manufacture self-realisable competence evidence (test records, task outcomes, execution histories) to trigger evidence-gated ascent beneath the ceiling
The model, instructions, memory, skills, generated code, tools, and subagents may themselves be adversarial
Cannot control the external monitor or user-issued ceilings
assumptions: Complete mediation: every protected effect is produced only by an action the monitor admits (A1)
Closure-sound monitor view: A(S_t,L) ⊆ A#(S_hat_t,L) before each admission (A2)
Sound admission under Valid_Ω and single-lease attribution (A3, Assumption 2)
Attenuating delegation with finite depth (A4)
Monitor integrity: no transition modifies monitor, lease store, or log outside a higher-authority path (A5)
Sound request abstraction Eff(S_t,a) ⊆ Req(a) (Equation 1)
not_covered: Side channels, monitor implementation defects, information-flow confidentiality (non-interference)
Model alignment and inference of latent user intent
Cross-generation revocation and population-level authority
Empirical frequency or operational cost of authorization drift (no experiments)

intervention.name: State-bound authorization (earned authority under a fixed ceiling)
intervention.description: A grant fixes at authorization time an immutable effect ceiling B, an initial active authority P_0 ⊆ B, and a transition envelope of survivable mutation classes. At each step the runtime proposes P_t^prop: contraction is free, ascent requires an evidence condition, and the monitor clamps P_t = P_t^prop ∩ B, so no runtime evidence can raise the boundary. If any observed mutation label falls outside the envelope, the monitor suspends the grant before the next protected action even when effects remain inside B. Delegated child leases are attenuated beneath the parent's ceiling; formalized with leases, scopes, escalation closure, and a non-amplification theorem.

results.claim: Under complete mediation, sound request abstraction, containment of active and delegated authority, and monitor integrity, mutation cannot amplify protected effects beyond the user-issued ceiling (Theorem 1, compact form).
results.value: every protected effect stays within at least one user-issued ceiling
results.setting: Formal model of a tool-enabled evolving agent mediated by an external monitor; attacker may control content, skills, tools, and memory but not the monitor or ceilings; no empirical evaluation
results.quote: Suppose protected effects are completely mediated, Equation 1 holds at every admission, each active or delegated authority is contained in a user-issued ceiling, and the monitor is outside the agent’s control. Then every protected effect in an execution belongs to at least one user-issued ceiling.

results.claim: In the structured lease model, under single-lease attribution (Assumption 2) and the runtime conditions A1-A5 (Assumption 3), mutation cannot enlarge the set of achievable effects beyond the union of the scopes the user explicitly granted, however many state transitions occur (Theorem 3).
results.value: achievable effects bounded by union of user-granted scopes under mutation
results.setting: Structured lease model (Appendix A) with single-lease attribution; formal theorem with proof by induction on admitted actions (Appendix C); no experiments
results.quote: That is, mutation cannot enlarge the set of achievable effects beyond the union of the scopes the user explicitly granted, however many state transitions occur.

results.claim: Closure soundness of the monitor view (A2) is necessary: without it the non-amplification bound fails by an unbounded margin, e.g., when a tool-addition mutation is not delivered to the monitor (Proposition 7).
results.value: out-of-scope effects grow without bound without closure soundness
results.setting: Constructed execution family satisfying A1, A3, A4, A5 but not A2, in which the harness hot-reloads a network-capable tool without notifying the monitor
results.quote: Dropping closure soundness makes the bound fail by an unbounded margin; missing a mutation event is one concrete way to cause that failure.

results.claim: Evidence the agent can produce itself (test passes, low error rates, task history) may activate more authority beneath the ceiling but cannot tighten the adversarial bound below B; a tighter security bound requires a premise outside the session's causal reach.
results.value: security guarantee remains B under self-produced evidence
results.setting: Formal analysis of evidence-gated ascent (Propositions 4 and 5, Appendix A-B3 and A-B4); no experiments
results.quote: A test pass, low error rate, or successful task history may be useful evidence that more of BB should be active. If the agent can produce the qualifying evidence itself, however, the security guarantee remains BB.

results.claim: The paper systematizes six grant-relevant mutation classes (control state, capability, delegation, task or phase, trust context, enforcement) and maps each to its authorization consequences.
results.setting: Conceptual taxonomy presented as Table I; descriptive contribution, not measured
results.quote: Finally, we map six mutation classes to their authorization consequences.

limitations.statement: The paper is a formalization only: the frequency and operational cost of authorization drift are not measured.
limitations.quote: The present paper formalizes authorization drift but does not yet measure its frequency or operational cost.

limitations.statement: Choosing the ceiling B remains an open policy and usability problem: too high weakens the guarantee, too low interrupts useful work.
limitations.quote: First, choosing BB remains a policy and usability problem: a high ceiling weakens the result, while a low ceiling interrupts useful work.

limitations.statement: Equation 1 (sound request abstraction) still needs a concrete enforcement mechanism; label delivery alone under-approximates actual effects.
limitations.quote: Second, Equation 1 needs a concrete enforcement mechanism such as syscall mediation, tool proxies, type-and-effect analysis, or capability-flow tracking. Label delivery alone is insufficient if the resulting monitor view under-approximates actual effects.

limitations.statement: Cross-generation revocation and population-level authority are not solved.
limitations.quote: Third, cross-generation revocation and population-level authority are not solved here.

limitations.statement: Compositional drift: a sequence of individually permitted mutation labels can jointly enlarge effective authority beyond the lease scope; this is the model's principal open problem.
limitations.quote: We call this compositional drift. It is the principal open problem left by this model.

title: MemSecBench: Tracking Agent Memory Poisoning from Persistence to Consequence and Repair

object.carrier: Cross-session memory of complete agent configurations Pi=(H,B,L): four memory backends (Native file-based, Mem0, Mem0-Graph, A-MEM) under two agent harnesses (OpenClaw, Hermes) and three LLM backends (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MiniMax-M3, GPT-5.5); malicious and benign semantics live as files, vector records, entity-linked entries, or structured notes, written via each backend's normal interface and traced through a Write-Execute-Forget lifecycle in isolated runtime containers

safety_property.statement: Lifecycle memory integrity plus selective repair: attacker-controlled malicious semantics should not persist after Write (W2), should not be recalled (E1) and adopted (E2) into a case-defined external consequence (E3), and when repair is requested the target semantics should be removed or neutralized (F1) while the semantics of every required benign memory are preserved (F2). Failure conditions: persistence, downstream unsafe consequence, and collateral damage to benign memories during repair; judged by checkpoint-specific evidence packs (deterministic write check, judge-model rubrics, programmatic gates).
safety_property.operationalized_as: Four lifecycle metrics over K=24 configurations x N=310 cases: Memory Poisoning Success Rate MPSR = sum(w)/N with w = W1 AND W2; Memory Exploitation Success Rate MESR = sum(w AND e)/sum(w) with e = E1 AND E2 AND E3; End-to-End Attack Success Rate E2E-ASR = sum(w AND e)/N; Selective Repair Success Rate SRSR = sum(w AND f)/sum(w) with f = F1 AND F2; each configuration-case pair evaluated once; judge model DeepSeek-V4-Pro outside the agent run plus programmatic admissibility gates.

capabilities: Controls the content that conveys the case's target malicious semantics and determines how it is presented through one Carrier (workspace artifact or direct instruction)
May know the workflow, available tools, and relevant retrieval cues

Two-session attack: Session 1 plants malicious content that may be written to memory; Session 2 has a normal user submitting a benign task with no attack payload, during which stored content may be recalled and cause an unsafe consequence
assumptions: Attacker-controlled content reaches the agent through a supported Carrier and Write invokes the intended memory interface; the benchmark measures lifecycle risk after content enters this workflow
The attacker need not correspond to a separate authenticated principal
The agent accesses memory only through the intended interface; all private backend state other than native memory files remains hidden
not_covered: How the attacker gains account or session access is not modeled
The attacker cannot modify Pi, directly access private backend state, or view hidden evaluation metadata

No mechanism-specific or adaptive attacks against the observed backend behavior; the authors list 'develop mechanism-specific attacks' and 'isolate backend effects through controlled ablations' as future work

intervention.name: MemSecBench: Write-Execute-Forget lifecycle benchmark with evidence-based adjudication
intervention.description: Each case is a linked task package T=(rho, x_W, x_E, x_F, l) with clean initial memory source material, Write/Execute/Forget stage inputs, four design-axis labels, seven checkpoint rubrics, and an E3 consequence contract. Evaluation runs each package in an isolated container per configuration Pi=(H,B,L), ingests rho through the backend's normal interface to form clean memory M0, introduces the target semantics via the Carrier at Write, evaluates Execute and Forget on independent copies of the verified poisoned state, and adjudicates seven checkpoints (W1 Write Operation deterministic, W2 Persistence, E1 Recall Exposure, E2 Adoption, E3 Externalization, F1 Repair, F2 Benign Preservation) using a judge model (DeepSeek-V4-Pro) outside the agent run plus programmatic gates; matched backend comparisons fix harness, LLM, runtime, clean initialization, environment, and evidence protocol.

controls.name: Native (harness-specific) memory backend
Matched harness-LLM-runtime settings across memory backends
Clean initial memory state M0 from rho via the backend's normal interface

results.claim: Across all 24 memory-backend-harness-LLM configurations, malicious memory persists in 84.2% of all cases (MPSR) and the full Write-Execute chain succeeds in 50.3% (E2E-ASR); among successfully poisoned cases 59.6% complete the Execute chain and 56.1% achieve selective repair.
results.metric: MPSR / E2E-ASR (all cases); MESR / SRSR (conditional on successful poisoning), macro-averaged
results.comparison: unweighted macro-average over the 24 configurations in the 2x4x3 matrix
results.setting: 310 lifecycle cases from 48 realistic contexts (Code and Science, Daily Life, Office Work); two harnesses (OpenClaw, Hermes) x four memory backends (Native, Mem0, Mem0-Graph, A-MEM) x three LLM backends (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MiniMax-M3, GPT-5.5); each configuration-case evaluated once
results.quote: Across all 24 configurations, malicious memory persists in 84.2% of all cases, and the full Write–Execute chain succeeds in 50.3%. Among successfully poisoned cases, 59.6% complete the full Execute chain, while 56.1% achieve selective repair.

denominator.how_counted: MPSR and E2E-ASR use all N=310 cases per configuration; MESR and SRSR condition on the successfully poisoned cases (sum of w) within each configuration; macro-average over the K=24 configurations with a reported value; missing entries never imputed as failures

results.claim: Adoption (E2) is the primary bottleneck to attack completion: checkpoint pass rates fall from 91.1% (W1) to 84.2% (W2) to 76.1% (E1) and then contract sharply to 53.7% at E2, with the full E2E chain at 50.3%.
results.comparison: persistence and recall filter little; adoption is the decisive boundary between stored malicious semantics and harmful behavior
results.setting: Lifecycle-wide macro averages over the 24 configurations (Figure 4)
results.quote: The sharpest contraction occurs at adoption, where E2E_{2} falls from 76.1% to 53.7%. The full E2E chain declines only slightly further to 50.3%, indicating that once malicious semantics shape the agent’s decisions, most also produce the specified external consequence.

denominator.how_counted: Attack checkpoints use all cases per configuration; macro-averaged over configurations; each configuration-case pair evaluated once

results.claim: Benign-memory preservation is the primary bottleneck to selective repair: 86.3% of successfully poisoned cases pass repair (F1) but only 62.5% pass benign preservation (F2), reducing SRSR to 56.1% - collateral damage after successful removal is the larger source of joint repair failure.
results.metric: F1 / F2 / SRSR pass rates conditioned on successful poisoning
results.comparison: 30.2-point gap between F1 and SRSR (target removed but benign memories not preserved) vs 6.4-point gap between F2 and SRSR
results.setting: Repair branch of the lifecycle macro averages (Figure 4), conditioned on successfully poisoned cases within each configuration
results.quote: In the repair branch of Figure 4, 86.3% of successfully poisoned cases pass F1F_{1}, whereas only 62.5% pass F2F_{2}. Requiring both conditions reduces SRSR further to 56.1%.

denominator.how_counted: Repair outcomes condition on successfully poisoned cases (sum of w) within each configuration; absolute counts not aggregated in the main text

results.claim: Backend effects on attack vs repair are dissociable: under OpenClaw/DeepSeek-V4-Pro, replacing Native with A-MEM reduces E2E-ASR only from 59.0% to 56.5% while SRSR rises sharply from 46.3% to 87.6%; under OpenClaw/GPT-5.5, Mem0-Graph lowers E2E-ASR from 57.1% to 41.0% with SRSR nearly unchanged (87.5% -> 86.7%).
results.metric: E2E-ASR and SRSR under matched harness-LLM settings
results.setting: Matched contrasts fixing task package, harness, LLM backend, runtime, clean initialization, environment, and evidence protocol (Figure 5)
results.quote: Under OpenClaw/DeepSeek-V4-Pro, replacing Native with A-MEM reduces E2E-ASR only from 59.0% to 56.5%, while SRSR rises sharply from 46.3% to 87.6%.

denominator.how_counted: Each matched configuration runs all N=310 cases; E2E-ASR over all cases, SRSR conditioned on that configuration's successfully poisoned cases

results.claim: Cost reading (largest aggregate backend disparities): the largest absolute differences vs matched Native configurations are 16.1 percentage points for end-to-end attack success and 41.3 percentage points for selective repair.
results.metric: maximum absolute percentage-point difference vs matched Native
results.comparison: largest across all memory-backend contrasts in the 24-configuration matrix
results.setting: Descriptive contrasts across the 24 configurations (Abstract)
results.quote: Compared with matched Native configurations, the largest absolute differences are 16.1 percentage points for end-to-end attack success and 41.3 percentage points for selective repair.

denominator.how_counted: Percentage-point differences between matched configurations, each evaluated over N=310 cases

results.claim: No memory backend is uniformly safer: under OpenClaw, Mem0 lowers E2E-ASR by 4.2-13.5 pp across the three LLMs, but under Hermes with MiniMax-M3 it instead raises E2E-ASR from 34.8% to 48.7% while improving SRSR from 47.3% to 60.0%.
results.metric: E2E-ASR / SRSR direction of backend effect across configurations
results.comparison: opposite-signed effects of the same backend under different harnesses
results.setting: Matched Native vs Mem0 contrasts across harnesses and LLMs (Figure 5)
results.quote: Under Hermes with MiniMax-M3, it instead raises E2E-ASR from 34.8% to 48.7% while improving SRSR from 47.3% to 60.0%.

denominator.how_counted: Each contrast runs all N=310 cases per configuration; percentages are per-configuration rates

limitations.statement: Rates are descriptive: each configuration-case pair is evaluated once, and cross-backend MESR/SRSR condition on successful writes within each configuration, so cross-backend conditioning differs across cells.
limitations.quote: Each configuration–case pair is evaluated once, so rates are descriptive; cross-backend MESR and SRSR condition on successful writes within each configuration.

limitations.statement: Native is harness-specific, so memory-backend comparisons remain within harness rather than spanning harnesses.
limitations.quote: Native is harness-specific, so comparisons remain within harness.

limitations.statement: Scope limits acknowledged via future work: mechanism-specific attacks, controlled backend ablations, automated benchmark construction, and broader task domains are not yet done.
limitations.quote: Future work will develop mechanism-specific attacks, isolate backend effects through controlled ablations, automate benchmark construction, and expand task domains and operational scenarios.

counterexamples.observation: The same backend can help under one configuration and hurt under another: Mem0 lowers E2E-ASR by 4.2-13.5 pp under OpenClaw across the three LLMs, but raises E2E-ASR from 34.8% to 48.7% under Hermes with MiniMax-M3 - backend effects reverse across agent configurations, so no universal ranking exists.

reproduction.data: 310 linked lifecycle cases from 48 realistic contexts; 24-configuration matrix (2 harnesses x 4 memory backends x 3 LLM backends); Appendices C and D document backend implementations, adapters, runtime isolation, and artifact provenance

title: MAPLE-Guard: Memory-Aware Link Enforcement Against Memory-Link Poisoning in Multi-Agent Systems

object.carrier: Persistent agent memory items m=(x,μ) — text records with metadata (content x, access scope, provenance, lifecycle state, guard-side signals) — held in per-agent private stores and shared stores of a memory-augmented multi-agent system; a memory link is the dependency created by write/retrieve/promote/reuse/update operations on such items

safety_property.statement: A poisoned memory item written once must not steer benign agents' later decisions, be promoted into shared memory, or be reused by agents that never saw the original attack; the property fails when an attack-specified target answer/tool is reached (ASR@3) instead of a correct non-target consensus (MDSR@3), and the defense is judged to potentially fail under forged provenance metadata or payloads that stay below per-event risk thresholds.
safety_property.operationalized_as: ASR@3 (fraction of trigger tasks whose final-round aggregated answer equals the attacker target y*) and MDSR@3 (fraction reaching correct, non-target consensus among non-attacker agents) at the final round, scored by an LLM judge (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, temperature 0), plus propagation diagnostics PMUR / PMUR-A / Sec. ASR@3 (Appendix D)

capabilities: controls one or a few benign-looking agents inside the MAS
writes experience-like poisoned memories through ordinary task interaction (dialogue route)
seeds items directly into a memory store it can reach (direct-memory route)
goal: make a poisoned item survive long enough to steer a benign agent's later decision (targeted attack toward a specific wrong answer or risky tool)
assumptions: attacker cannot modify other agents' private stores
attacker cannot modify the guard's hidden signals φ(m)
attacker cannot modify the communication topology
runtime provenance metadata and retrieval traces are trustworthy
unless stated otherwise, the attacker is unaware of the guard
not_covered: an attacker who can forge source-route, writer, scope, or lineage records (metadata forgery)
payloads designed to remain below per-event risk thresholds
prevention of every initial compromise (guard contains rather than prevents)
generalization to unseen adaptive attacks (one fixed signal/weight/threshold configuration evaluated)
causal isolation of the attack entry point (each benchmark paired with a single attack)

intervention.name: MAPLE-Guard (Memory-Aware Propagation and Link Enforcement Guard)
intervention.description: A lifecycle guard that intercepts every memory-link event and places gates at four checkpoints — a write firewall at storage (reject/quarantine/rewrite/private), a retrieval gate before reasoning (value-aware ranking plus rule-based filter), a promotion gate before an item enters shared memory, and a cross-agent gate before another agent reuses it — each deciding allow/demote/block. Decisions come from one fixed variant-agnostic risk model over eight signals (provenance, lineage, self-claimed success, instruction-likeness, answer binding, trigger sensitivity, cluster dominance, source-agent trust; largest weights on provenance and lineage) computed from the memory text, hidden guard state φ(m) and provenance chain P(m), combined with outcome-conditioned utility/trust updates (Q-value style) after each task; signals are never exposed to the backbone LLM.

controls.name: No Defense
AgentSafe (prompt-level/identity-aware checks)
AgentXposed (agent-facing interrogation/behavior inspection)
Challenger (agents challenge suspicious peer outputs)
GUARDIAN (independent reviewer over visible messages/actions)
G-Safeguard (communication-graph GNN intervention)
INFA-Guard (topology-aware remediation)
Single-gate removal (write/retrieval/promotion/cross-agent, outcome update retained)

results.claim: In the LongMemEval-MemoryGraft setting with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, MAPLE-Guard raises MDSR@3 from 54.0% to 74.3% and reduces RDA@3 [v2 对 v1 的 ASR@3 改名] from 38.2% to 0.9% (Table 2). v2 补充基线语境：其 RDA 仅比最佳基线 Challenger（2.2%）低 1.3 个百分点，而 PIGuard 的 MDSR 更高（79.1%）但 RDA 5.9%——MAPLE 降低检索损伤但不领先任务成功。
results.setting: LongMemEval-MemoryGraft; 8-agent MAS (3 attacker-controlled), 3 rounds, star/chain/tree topologies, 15 runs per topology, judge Qwen3.5-122B-A10B temperature 0, controlled-topology main grid
results.quote: With Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, MAPLE raises MDSR@3 from 54.0% to 74.3% and reduces RDA@3 from 38.2% to 0.9% (Table 2). Its RDA is 1.3 points below the best baseline (Challenger: 2.2%). PIGuard instead has the highest MDSR (79.1%), with 5.9% RDA: MAPLE lowers retrieval damage but does not lead task success.

denominator.how_counted: ASR@3 and MDSR@3 are fractions of trigger tasks (attack-successful iff final answer equals attacker target; defense-successful iff correct non-target consensus), Appendix D.1

results.setting: AppWorld-AgentPoison; 8-agent MAS (3 attacker-controlled), 3 rounds, star/chain/tree topologies, 15 runs per topology, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B main grid (gemma-4-31B: 95.3% MDSR@3 / 0.0% ASR@3 per §5.5)
results.quote: On AppWorld-AgentPoison, MAPLE-Guard achieves 99.8% MDSR@3 and 0.2% RDA@3 with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and 95.3% MDSR@3 and 0.0% RDA@3 with gemma-4-31B.

denominator.n_total: 200 benchmark instances per run; 15 runs per topology, reported as mean over star/chain/tree topology means
denominator.how_counted: ASR@3 and MDSR@3 are fractions of trigger tasks (Appendix D.1)

results.quote: On MMLU with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, all six message- and topology-level guards reduce RDA relative to No Defense; on AppWorld, however, GUARDIAN increases RDA from 34.7% to 56.5%.

results.quote: On Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, MAPLE-Guard achieves the lowest mean RDA@3 in four settings, including 0.3%, 0.9%, and 0.2% on MMLU, LongMemEval, and AppWorld, respectively. The signal functions, weights, and thresholds remain fixed without attack-specific parameter search.

denominator.how_counted: ASR@3 is the fraction of trigger tasks whose final-round answer equals the attacker target (Appendix D.1)

results.claim: In the single-gate ablation on LongMemEval-MemoryGraft (outcome feedback retained in every variant), removing the promotion gate causes the largest degradation, reducing MDSR@3 from 73.6% to 60.0% and raising RDA@3 from 0.9% to 14.5% [v1 记 73.60/60.00/14.50，v2 改为一位小数]；去掉 write/retrieval/cross-agent 门产生较小但一致的损失。v2 新增 matched-lifecycle 对照：full guard 88.4%/0.1% vs retrieval-only 65.0%/21.6%（AppWorld 代理，Gemma Base）。

results.quote: The full guard achieves 73.6% MDSR@3 and 0.9% RDA@3. Removing the promotion gate causes the largest degradation, reducing MDSR@3 to 60.0% and increasing RDA@3 to 14.5%; removing the write, retrieval, or cross-agent gate produces smaller but consistent losses.

denominator.n_total: 200 benchmark instances per run; 15 runs per topology, reported as mean over star/chain/tree topology means
denominator.how_counted: ASR@3 and MDSR@3 are fractions of trigger tasks (Appendix D.1; a benign mistake counts toward neither, so they are not complementary). The ablation keeps the main-grid evaluation protocol: the full-guard reference (73.60%/0.90%) equals the Table 1 / Appendix C LongMemEval-MemoryGraft main-grid cell (200 benchmark instances per run, eight agents of which three are attacker-controlled, 15 runs per topology, averaged over star/chain/tree topology means), and Appendix D.2 states the ablation removes one lifecycle gate at a time under the same outcome update. No separate ablation instance count is printed; soft corroboration: 60.00% and 14.50% of 200 are integer counts (120/29).

results.claim: Benign utility: under random topology, MAPLE changes MDSR by −1.5 (MMLU), +7.0 (LongMemEval), +1.0 (AppWorld), +1.4 (CSQA), +0.9 (InjectAgent) points on Qwen — Table 6 行值与 v1 一致（MMLU 88.5→87.0，AppWorld 99.0→100.0）。v2 明确改口：the guard is not uniformly cost-free（两骨干在 MMLU 均失 1.5 点，gemma 在 LongMemEval 失 1.4 点）；v2 新增 token 审计：MAPLE 在 MMLU/InjectAgent 上相对 No Defense 减少 35.0%/27.8% 的测量 token 用量，且无额外 guard-LLM 调用。
results.value: MMLU 87.0 vs 88.5; AppWorld 100.0 vs 99.0; MMLU −1.5 pt on both backbones
results.setting: Attack-free benign utility under random topology, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B backbone (gemma-4 columns: MMLU 56.5 -> 55.0, LongMemEval 34.2 -> 32.8)

limitations.statement: MAPLE-Guard contains memory-link poisoning after it enters the system rather than preventing every initial compromise.
limitations.quote: MAPLE-Guard is designed to contain memory-link poisoning after it enters the system rather than prevent every initial compromise.

limitations.statement: The guard assumes reliable provenance metadata and retrieval traces; forged metadata or below-threshold payloads may evade it.

title: Securing Agentic AI: From Per-Action Checks to Trajectory Assurance

object.carrier: 智能体长期记忆/RAG 检索库；跨推理步与跨会话演化的执行上下文与系统状态（如 A2A 共享 contextId）；第三方工具定义/元数据与技能文档（SKILL.md、editor rules files）

safety_property.statement: 核心安全性质是行为轨迹层面的 policy-compliance：一串各自被允许的动作不得共同违反治理标准定义的系统级不变量（状态条件化时序性质，如 5G 公共安全切片恢复窗口、FHIR 观察窗口），即行为须保持在 governing standards 规定的 behavioral envelope 内；该性质无需对抗输入即可失效，由执行轨迹而非单个动作判定。同时覆盖记忆/上下文/工具接口的 integrity（prompt injection、记忆投毒、rug pull）、confidentiality（上下文外泄，如 EchoLeak）与 availability（denial-of-wallet、MoE 专家失衡 DoS）。
safety_property.operationalized_as: 论文未做实验；提出以"可验证行为不变量"操作化：运行时校验演化中的执行轨迹满足由治理标准导出的系统级行为约束（"verify that evolving execution trajectories satisfy system-level behavioral constraints, establishing safety over the lifetime of an execution rather than at individual decision points"，§5），并将上下文所有权、能力 attestation 等作为协议级可验证不变量（§3）

capabilities: 在检索通道（网页、文档、数据库、邮件）植入可被智能体当作指令的内容；EchoLeak/CVE-2025-32711 证明可无用户交互外泄 M365 Copilot 敏感上下文
向智能体记忆/知识库注入少量投毒条目实现后门（AgentPoison：poisoning rate below 0.1%，良性表现不变）
发布恶意 MCP 工具服务器、在工具元数据嵌入指令，或 rug pull——被信任后静默替换工具定义且客户端不复验
供应链投毒：postmark-mcp 正常十五个版本后单行代码窃取外发邮件；SKILL.md/editor rules 文件可隐藏指令
在 A2A 中以有效 contextId 附着他人上下文、读取累积历史、投毒后续任务而不触发任务级控制；自声明 Agent Card 能力骗取敏感任务并返回伪造产物
跨委托链重放无发送方约束的中继凭据
构造 token 序列操纵模型路由：迫使成本膨胀升级，或降级到更弱对齐模型实现 jailbreak-by-downgrade
在 MoE 模型内部压制安全关键专家、经跨批次路由依赖泄露 prompt、经专家失衡触发 DoS
prompt infection 使恶意指令在多智能体间自我复制传播；零点击 GenAI 蠕虫在宿主应用间扩散
assumptions: 智能体上下文中数据与指令缺乏可靠分离，非信任内容可影响推理并外溢为下游动作
工具/模型/包在部署时一次性信任，此后行为不被持续验证（信任非静态）
A2A 身份仅在传输层建立、不跨委托跳传播；Agent Card 能力自声明、无 attestation 或 challenge-response
现有运行时防护为无状态、逐动作策略，不建模系统状态沿长轨迹的演化
轨迹级违规（5G 调度/FHIR 出院例）在无任何对抗输入时也会发生
部署环境受显式成文的治理约束（organizational policies、regulatory requirements、technical standards）
not_covered: 本文为 vision paper，不提出完整解决方案，无任何防御实现或实验评估
对模型与推理层级的跨联邦妥协，现有协议级防御无形式化保证（论文指出但未解决）
路由组件（权重、训练数据、决策阈值）的 provenance 现有框架不覆盖（论文指出但未给出方案）
LLM-to-formal-spec 编译器无法保证 completeness、consistency 或对治理标准的 faithfulness
审计机制未标准化、非强制，且引入隐私与成本权衡，未解决

intervention.name: Trajectory assurance / behavioral trajectory containment（愿景级提议，无实现）
intervention.description: 论文主张从逐动作检查转向轨迹保证：在运行时校验演化中的执行轨迹是否满足由治理标准导出的系统级状态条件化行为不变量（区别于现有无状态 runtime guards、不锚定治理策略的 formal-spec 编译器与概率监控），使安全成为智能体全生命周期上可验证的属性；并要求把上下文所有权、能力 attestation（§3）、路由 policy artifact 的可验证编译（§4）与端到端审计性（§6）作为架构/协议层的可验证不变量。论文本身不含机制实现或评测。

limitations.statement: 作者明示本文为 vision paper，不提出完整解决方案，仅识别根本挑战与研究机会
limitations.quote: As a vision paper, our goal is not to propose complete solutions but to identify fundamental challenges and research opportunities they create.

limitations.statement: 论文指出现有安全机制均未锚定治理策略、无法检测未见但被禁止的轨迹，且强制仅限单智能体、不适用于跨智能体违规（对现有方法的局限，为本文核心论证）
limitations.quote: However, none of these approaches are grounded in governing policies, leaving them unable to detect unseen but prohibited trajectories. Moreover, enforcement remains single-agent, which makes those unsuitable for multi-agent settings where violations emerge from cross-agent interactions.

limitations.statement: 现有智能体可见性/审计机制既未标准化也非强制，并引入隐私与成本权衡
limitations.quote: However, these mechanisms are neither standardized nor mandatory, and they introduce privacy and cost tradeoffs.

counterexamples.description: 5G 调度智能体逐步降级公共安全切片优先级：每次重分配均通过局部检查，却错过强制恢复窗口——逐动作检查全部通过而轨迹级违规，且无对抗输入
counterexamples.quote: For example, a 5G scheduling agent can progressively deprioritize a public-safety slice, each reallocation passing local checks, yet miss the mandated recovery window (3GPP, 2024).

counterexamples.description: 临床智能体加速多个本身合理的出院决策，违反 FHIR 护理路径定义的累计观察窗口——同类无对抗输入的轨迹级违规
counterexamples.quote: Likewise, a clinical agent can accelerate several justified discharge decisions while violating the aggregate observation window defined by a FHIR care pathway (HL7 International, 2023).

title: When Memory Becomes Authority: Benchmarking Authority Collapse at the Memory Consolidation Boundary

object.carrier: durable natural-language memory items written by LLM consolidators adapted from agent-memory systems (Mem0-inspired, Mem0 classic/additive, LangMem, Graphiti, Letta, Minimal), optionally persisted with authority metadata (Authorized/Attested/Unendorsed) in an end-to-end pipeline

safety_property.statement: Memory consolidation must preserve the source constraints governing a claim's authorized use: a stored memory may not imply downstream uses beyond those its source permits (false authority upgrade). When consolidation erases this boundary (authority collapse), the stored memory implies greater authority than its source allows, and adversarial exploitation (authority laundering) turns unendorsed claims into apparent user facts, attested observations, or standing instructions that trigger unauthorized tool actions.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Module A write-time Upgrade-all / Ret- / Ret+ rates on paired histories; Module B/C ASR = fraction of non-authorizing cases issuing the prohibited matching native tool call, TSR = fraction of authorized counterparts issuing the required call; authority-label accuracy / macro F1 and dangerous-upgrade rate of predicted metadata

capabilities: controls content supplied through source classes the authority policy treats as unendorsed, e.g., designated non-authoritative tool inputs
can introduce claims via third-party reports, external procedures, or assistant suggestions that consolidation may launder into user facts, standing rules, or user decisions
the claim need not be false or contain an injected instruction; the attack exploits the authority silently assigned during consolidation
assumptions: a frozen deployment authority policy maps source roles to labels (direct user evidence -> Authorized, assistant -> Attested, tool -> Unendorsed)
one controlled write-to-action cycle per pair: the later task leaves the operative value unstated so the agent must use memory; the exact matching tool action is prohibited for H- and required for H+
source-class annotations are trustworthy and cannot be altered by the adversary
not_covered: the adversary cannot alter source-class annotations, direct user or system messages, outputs from deployment-designated authoritative tools, the memory store, or the authorization policy

memory poisoning via optimized retrieval triggers or query-only record insertion (AgentPoison/MINJA-style attacks) is not evaluated; the benchmark instead varies source authority of true, non-instructional, textually identical claims
memory revocation/repair after a collapse and multi-hop attack chains across sessions are not benchmarked

intervention.name: Persisted authority metadata (automatically predicted source-authority labels on stored memories), with source-aware write-time prompting as a secondary intervention
intervention.description: Each candidate predictor selects the primary supporting message for a stored memory and maps its source role deterministically to Authorized, Attested, or Unendorsed; the predicted label is persisted with the memory and exposed to the action model at action time (Module C frozen pipeline: Qwen3.7-Max as authority predictor, Gemini 3.1 Pro as consolidator and action model). Controlled counterparts in Module B test washed vs source-attributed text, no vs gold authority metadata, plus text-sanitizer and conservative-join baselines; Module A tests Marked and Marked+source-aware writing objectives.

results.claim: Authority collapse generalizes: write-time authority upgrades occur in 48 of 49 consolidator-backbone configurations (seven writing objectives x seven LLM backends); the sole zero-upgrade configuration (Mem0 classic + GPT-5.5) avoids the failure by omitting all non-authorizing focal propositions, i.e., non-retention rather than authority preservation.
results.metric: configurations with authority upgrades (Module A write-time)
results.comparison: 48 of 49 configurations exhibit upgrades; the exception is omission-driven
results.setting: Module A base grid: seven memory-writing objectives (Mem0-inspired, Mem0 classic, Mem0 additive, LangMem, Graphiti, Letta, Minimal) x seven LLM backends (GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4 mini, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Qwen3.7-Max, GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4-Pro), temperature zero
results.quote: Authority upgrades occur in 48 of the 49 objective–backend configurations.

denominator.how_counted: 7 writing objectives × 7 LLM backends; per Table 2 caption each configuration is evaluated on 350 H−/H+ pairs

results.claim: On the base grid, low Upgrade-all masks the failure: among all non-authorizing cases, 17.8% are authority-upgraded, only 8.2% are retained with authority preserved, and 74.0% are omitted — general-purpose writing objectives often avoid observed upgrades through omission rather than reliable preservation of source authority.
results.metric: upgraded / preserved / omitted shares of non-authorizing cases (Module A grid average)
results.setting: Module A base grid pooled over all writing objectives and backends; percentages of all non-authorizing (H−) cases
results.quote: Among all H−H^{-} cases, 17.8% are authority-upgraded, only 8.2% are retained with authority preserved, and 74.0% are omitted.

denominator.n_total: 350 H− cases per configuration, pooled over the 7×7 base grid
denominator.how_counted: Table 2 caption: all values are percentages with 350 H−/H+ pairs per configuration

results.claim: With washed memory and no authority metadata, macro ASR and TSR are nearly equal for every action model, showing a washed proposition is operationalized almost independently of its original source authority.
results.metric: ASR / TSR (Module B, washed memory, no metadata, macro over seven action models)
results.setting: Module B: the same seven backends as action models, benchmark-supplied washed focal memory without metadata; 350 non-authorizing cases and 350 authorized counterparts per model
results.quote: With washed memory and no metadata, macro ASR and TSR are 50.3% and 49.4%, and the two rates remain similar for every backend.

denominator.how_counted: Table 4 caption: each model–condition entry reports ASR/TSR over 350 non-authorizing cases and 350 authorized counterparts; each macro value aggregates 2,450 trajectories per metric

results.claim: Natural-language source attribution helps but is insufficient: replacing washed memory with source-attributed text lowers macro ASR by 9.8 points and raises TSR by 4.2 points, yet 40.5% of non-authorizing cases still trigger the prohibited action.
results.metric: ASR (Module B, source-attributed memory, no metadata, macro)
results.comparison: macro ASR −9.8 points and TSR +4.2 points vs washed no-metadata; residual ASR 40.5%
results.setting: Module B macro over seven action models, source-attributed memory without metadata
results.quote: Replacing washed memory with source-attributed text lowers macro ASR by 9.8 points and raises TSR by 4.2 points. ASR decreases for all seven models, while TSR increases for six. Nevertheless, 40.5% of non-authorizing cases still trigger the prohibited action

denominator.how_counted: Table 4 caption: each macro value aggregates 2,450 trajectories per metric; source-attr. macro row 40.5 / 53.6

results.claim: Explicit gold authority metadata provides the strongest action-time discrimination — macro ASR falls to 5.8% with washed memory and 2.7% with source-attributed memory while TSR stays 53.9% in both conditions — whereas heuristic baselines (text sanitizer, conservative joining) match safety and utility rates, i.e., indiscriminate action suppression.
results.metric: ASR / TSR (Module B, gold authority metadata, macro)
results.comparison: macro ASR 5.8% (washed) and 2.7% (source-attributed) at 53.9% TSR in both
results.setting: Module B macro over seven action models with gold authority metadata attached to the focal memory
results.quote: Gold metadata reduces ASR to 5.8% with washed memory and 2.7% with source-attributed memory, while maintaining 53.9% TSR in both conditions.

denominator.how_counted: Table 4 caption: each macro value aggregates 2,450 trajectories per metric

results.claim: In the frozen end-to-end pipeline (Qwen3.7-Max authority predictor; Gemini 3.1 Pro consolidator and action model), automatically predicted and persisted authority labels reduce observed ASR from 16.9% to 0.0% over all 350 pairs while TSR is essentially unchanged from 39.7% to 40.0%; reference metadata produces the same aggregate rates.
results.metric: ASR / TSR (Module C end-to-end, all pairs in denominators)
results.setting: Module C frozen pipeline: Mem0-inspired consolidation with predicted persisted authority labels; all source-authority pairs remain in the denominators including write-time omissions and retrieval failures
results.quote: Over all 350 pairs, observed ASR similarly falls from 16.9% to 0.0%, while TSR changes from 39.7% to 40.0%. Reference metadata produces the same aggregate rates, showing that automatically recovered authority is sufficient to match the observed reference safety–utility outcome.

denominator.how_counted: Table 5 caption: all pairs remain in the denominators, including cases where consolidation omits the focal memory (no-metadata ASR 16.9% = 59/350; predicted 0.0% = 0/350)

results.claim: End-to-end utility remains recall-limited: the consolidator retains the focal proposition in only 139 of 350 H− cases and 256 of 350 H+ cases; without metadata all 59 prohibited actions arise among the 139 retained H− cases, corresponding to 42.4% ASR conditional on focal retention, and predicted metadata blocks all of these observed actions.
results.metric: ASR conditional on focal retention / focal retention counts (Module C)
results.comparison: 42.4% = 59 prohibited actions among 139 retained H− cases; retention 139/350 H− vs 256/350 H+
results.setting: Module C no-metadata arm of the frozen pipeline, 350 pairs
results.quote: The consolidator retains the focal proposition in only 139 of 350 H−H^{-} cases and 256 of 350 H+H^{+} cases. Without metadata, all 59 prohibited actions arise among the 139 retained H−H^{-} cases, corresponding to 42.4% ASR conditional on focal retention

denominator.how_counted: conditional on the focal proposition being retained: 59 prohibited actions / 139 retained H− cases

results.claim: On the strictly held-out test slice, the no-metadata pipeline issues the prohibited action in 10 of 70 cases (14.3% ASR); predicted metadata reduces this to 0 of 70 while authorized completions stay unchanged at 20 of 70 (28.6% TSR).
results.metric: ASR / TSR (Module C, strictly held-out test slice)
results.setting: Module C strictly held-out test slice of the frozen pipeline (the full aggregate includes train and validation partitions)

denominator.how_counted: no-label ASR 10/70, TSR 20/70; predicted-label ASR 0/70, TSR 20/70

limitations.statement: Authority metadata governs how stored content is used but does not repair recall: labels cannot recover propositions omitted during consolidation and do not eliminate action-model failures, so authorized task success stays recall-limited.
limitations.quote: Authority metadata therefore controls how stored content is used, but does not repair missing memory.

limitations.statement: Aggregate equality between predicted- and reference-metadata arms (same TSR) should not be read as case-wise equivalence: four success predicates differ between separate calls with identical prompts, and none of the differently-labeled prompts changed the predicate in this single run.
limitations.quote: Aggregate equality should therefore not be interpreted as case-wise equivalence.

limitations.statement: The headline end-to-end aggregate over all pairs is descriptive because it includes the train and validation partitions; only the 70-pair slice is strictly held out.
limitations.quote: The complete 350-pair aggregate is descriptive because it includes the train and validation partitions. The 70-pair test slice is the strictly held-out confirmation

limitations.statement: Threat-model boundary: the adversary only controls content in unendorsed source classes and cannot alter source-class annotations, direct user/system messages, authoritative tool outputs, the memory store, or the authorization policy.
limitations.quote: The adversary cannot alter source-class annotations, direct user or system messages, outputs from deployment-designated authoritative tools, the memory store, or the authorization policy.

limitations.statement: Storage and retrieval are simplified to a deterministic bounded in-memory store returning the complete product-generated write set in stable order, keeping retrieval coverage and ordering identical across arms — real retrieval stacks are not evaluated.
limitations.quote: Storage and retrieval use a deterministic bounded in-memory store that returns the complete product-generated write set in stable order.

title: Benign Alone, Harmful Together: Exploiting Experience Composition in Self-Evolving LLM Agents

object.carrier: 受害自演化代理的持久经验记忆（ReasoningBank 的 persistent reasoning memory；SE-Agent 的轨迹修订/重组经验）；经验条目形式为反思、程序性规则或可复用技能，由受害代理自身抽取机制 Φ 从轨迹蒸馏并写入持久记忆

safety_property.statement: 自演化代理对安全敏感/有害查询的拒绝边界（safety boundary）应在良性经验跨会话累积与复用时保持。攻击在原子良性约束（每条提交任务与每条诱导经验孤立评估均为良性）下使该边界失效：目标阶段的有害遵从分数升高，Δharm = J_harm(q, M_n) − J_harm(q, M_0)，即持久记忆中孤立良性的经验被联合激活后削弱拒绝行为。
safety_property.operationalized_as: 两个安全基准上的 ASR：JailbreakBench（100 条恶意提示）与 HarmBench（400 条有害行为）；由 LLM 评审（GPT-5.4-mini）按 1-5 打分，仅当评分=5 记为攻击成功，ASR=(1/N)Σ I[s_i=5]×100%（式10）；良性约束以 benignness 审计量化：对每条攻击阶段任务与诱导经验做二元判定后取平均，Ben.=(1/(2K))Σ[B(t_i)+B(e_i^a)]×100%（式11）

capabilities: 通过受害代理的任务接口提交良性攻击阶段任务（gray-box，task interface 交互）
对自身交互所蒸馏出的经验具有只读可观察能力（read-only observability of experiences from its own interactions）
基于观测到的实际经验闭环重规划（closed-loop replanning），自适应选择下一任务
在目标阶段基于完整交互历史改写最终查询（experience-aware target reformulation），在全新会话中激活累积经验
assumptions: 受害代理为自演化代理：将轨迹蒸馏为持久经验并在后续任务中检索复用（ReasoningBank / SE-Agent）
经验跨会话持久，而前一阶段的交互历史在目标阶段的新会话中不可用
对手不能直接插入、删除或编辑记忆条目，也不能修改受害代理的系统提示或经验抽取机制 Φ
存在良性审计器 B(·) 可对每条任务与经验做孤立二元良性判定
LLM 评审（GPT-5.4-mini）能可靠判定有害遵从与良性
not_covered: 针对良性经验组合攻击的防御或缓解机制（论文未提出或评估任何 defense）
被污染经验的撤销（revocation）与修复（repair）
跨用户/多用户共享经验记忆的场景
具备直接写记忆权限的对手（AgentPoison 式特权访问仅作为基线对比，非本文威胁模型）
良性审计器或 LLM 评审本身被规避/不可靠的情形

intervention.description: 本文为攻击研究（EvoBreak 攻击 + BreakGym 目标合成 + 拒绝采样 SFT 与 Hint-guided GRPO 级联训练），未提出或评估任何防御/缓解机制；结论仅呼吁对持久经验做累积性安全评估而非孤立审计。

results.claim: 在两受害骨干 × 两自演化框架 × 三预演化域 × 两安全基准的全部设置下，EvoBreak 的总体平均 ASR 达 86.12%，比最强基线 ReNeLLM 高 24.19 个百分点（条件：经 BreakGym 训练的 EvoBreak，攻击阶段任务与诱导经验均孤立良性）

title: SkillJack: Persistent Skill Backdoors in Self-Evolving Agents

object.carrier: Separately stored reusable skill artifacts (structured skills of name, description, and code) compiled into the agent's skill library by the experience-to-skill extraction pipeline; the poisoned skill outlives its source trajectory record

safety_property.statement: Integrity of the derived skill library plus policy-compliance of skill-triggered behavior: an external attacker who can only influence the experience layer must not be able to have the agent's own pipeline compile poisoned experience into persistent, policy-violating skills that evade sanitization and survive deletion of their source records. The property fails when extracted skills drop from 98.5% to 11.4% LLM-judge detection, trigger the policy-violation proxy on 56.2% (SkillX) and 89.2% (Anything2Skill) of attack-oriented tasks, and retain 80.0% of triggers after source-record deletion.
safety_property.operationalized_as: A policy-violation proxy (regex pattern detector + DeepSeek-v4-flash LLM judge) measuring: (1) detection rate on raw trajectories vs derived skills, (2) routing-level trigger rate (ASR) on attack-oriented and clean tasks, (3) persistence rate of skill-based triggers after source-trajectory deletion, plus a supplementary dangerous-API pattern check on generated code

capabilities: Can cause a poisoned experience record to enter the learning corpus via indirect content injection, a shared experience pool, or a compromised trajectory dataset

Can craft transformation-resilient payloads: functionally framed trajectories (e.g., 'backup'/'archive' framing around external data transmission) whose task narrative survives extraction while retaining a policy-relevant action
assumptions: The attacker does not have direct write access to the skill library
The attacker cannot alter the extraction code or deterministically control routing; extraction and routing components run unchanged
All extraction, routing, judgment, and agent reasoning use a single model (DeepSeek-v4-flash) via API
not_covered: Direct write access to the skill library or modification of extraction code
Live execution against external services: all trigger/ASR figures are routing-level surrogates from local proxy detectors, not live-compromise rates
Multi-model generalization (results not yet replicated across models)
Insider or model-itself adversaries; base-model parameter poisoning

intervention.name: Preliminary defenses: extraction-time LLM safety review, runtime signature monitoring, and their composition; proposed: provenance-aware skill lifecycle protection
intervention.description: Tested only as an exploratory study: D1 is content-level extraction-time LLM review that blocks flagged skills before routing; D2 is execution-level runtime monitoring that blocks generated actions matching a fixed risky-action regex list; D3 composes them. On SkillX D1 lowered the trigger rate to 6.7% and D2 to 0.0%, but D3 was worse than D2 alone (13.3%) because upstream filtering shifts the action distribution the monitor was written for; on Anything2Skill the original 16 signatures left 85.0%, an enhanced 54-signature list reached 20.0%, and review plus enhanced monitor reached 5.0% (post-hoc tuning). The paper's main recommendation, not implemented, is provenance-aware skill lifecycle protection: propagate provenance from trajectories to every derived skill so that deleting or quarantining a source triggers review or removal of descendants, plus behavior-aware checks at skill use time.

controls.name: Directly malicious wording baseline (65 paired trajectories)
Memory-only / direct-context injection condition
Clean baseline skills and clean tasks (false-positive rates)
Metadata presentation ablation (full skill / content / name+doc / name only)
Unmodified A2S SDK extractor vs DOC mode

results.claim: On SkillX, extracting the 65 framed poisoned trajectories into 264 skills launders detectability: LLM-judge detection falls from 98.5% on raw trajectories to 11.4% on extracted skills (pattern detection 44.6% to 11.0%).
results.setting: SkillX experience-to-skill pipeline; 65 functionally framed poisoned trajectories before extraction vs 264 derived skills after extraction; pattern detector + DeepSeek-v4-flash LLM judge
results.quote: Pattern detection is 44.6% for raw trajectories and 11.0% for extracted skills; LLM-judge detection is 98.5% for raw trajectories and 11.4% for extracted skills.

denominator.n_total: 65 raw framed trajectories; 264 extracted framed skills
denominator.n_valid: 65 raw trajectories and 264 derived skills evaluated by both detectors
denominator.how_counted: share of raw trajectories (65 framed) vs derived skills (264 framed) flagged by each detector (Sections 4.2-4.3)

results.claim: The same extraction-stage whitewashing appears in the second, independently implemented system: on Anything2Skill, LLM-judge detection drops from 100.0% on raw trajectories to 44.4% in DOC mode and 28.6% in SDK mode after extraction.
results.setting: Anything2Skill DOC and SDK ingestion modes; same 65 framed trajectories, same raw-trajectory judge and DeepSeek-v4-flash configuration; DOC mode yields outputs for 41.5% of framed trajectories
results.quote: Among the extracted framed trajectory outputs, LLM-judge detection is 44.4%, compared with 100.0% on the raw trajectories. SDK mode extracts fewer framed trajectories (10.8%) and has 28.6% derived LLM-judge detection.

denominator.n_total: 65 framed trajectories input; DOC mode yields outputs for 41.5% of them
denominator.n_valid: extracted framed-trajectory outputs judged in each mode
denominator.how_counted: share of raw trajectories vs extracted framed outputs flagged by the LLM judge (Section 4.4, Table 2)

results.claim: In routing-level evaluation on SkillX, derived poisoned skills trigger the policy-violation proxy on 56.2% of 32 attack-oriented tasks and misfire on 20.0% of 15 clean tasks (collateral routing).
results.setting: SkillX native LLM routing over a 356-skill library (305 poisoned, 51 clean), 47 tasks total (32 attack-oriented, 15 clean), DeepSeek-v4-flash; trigger = routed skill satisfies the pattern+LLM policy-violation proxy
results.quote: SkillX | Native routing, attack-oriented tasks | 32 | 56.2% | | SkillX | Native routing, clean tasks | 15 | 20.0% |

denominator.how_counted: share of tasks routed to a skill satisfying the policy-violation proxy (Section 4.6, Table 3)

results.claim: Skills derived by Anything2Skill DOC mode remain broadly retrievable downstream: 89.2% of 65 attack-oriented queries trigger the policy-violation proxy, and 95.0% of clean-task retrievals select a poisoned skill under the lexical SkillBank retriever.
results.setting: 30-skill bank built from A2S DOC outputs; shared lexical skill-bank retriever over name/description/prompt plus the same LLM judge; 65 attack-oriented queries and 20 clean tasks
results.quote: A2S DOC | Lexical SkillBank, attack-oriented tasks | 65 | 89.2% | | A2S DOC | Lexical SkillBank, clean-task retrieval | 20 | 95.0% |

denominator.n_valid: all 65 framed attack-oriented task queries and 20 clean retrieval tasks
denominator.how_counted: share of queries retrieving a skill that satisfies the policy-violation proxy (Section 4.7, Table 3)

results.claim: Deleting the source poisoned trajectories does not remove the attack: in the matched 25-task experiment the persistence rate of skill-based triggers after source-record deletion is 80.0%, while the memory-only direct-context baseline triggers more often (68.0% vs skill-based 40.0%) but lacks persistence.
results.setting: SkillX matched 25 attack-oriented tasks under three conditions: memory-only (poisoned trajectory in context), skill-based (router over derived library), post-deletion (source trajectories removed before the same skill-based evaluation); pattern+LLM policy-violation proxy
results.quote: The direct-context baseline triggers more frequently in this matched setting (68.0% versus 40.0%). The added risk of the skill pathway is instead persistence: the persistence rate is 80.0% after source-record deletion.

denominator.n_valid: 32.0/40.0 skill-based triggers survive post-deletion overall (Figure 3 caption)
denominator.how_counted: persistence rate = post-deletion triggers divided by skill-based triggers, overall 32.0/40.0 (Figure 3)

results.claim: In the exploratory defense study, runtime signature monitoring drives the SkillX trigger rate to 0.0% (15 tasks) versus 6.7% for extraction-time review, while on A2S the enhanced monitor reaches 20.0% and review plus enhanced monitor 5.0%.
results.comparison: extraction review 6.7% and runtime monitor 0.0% on SkillX; enhanced runtime monitor 20.0% and review + enhanced monitor 5.0% on DOC mode
results.setting: SkillX: first 15 attack-oriented tasks over the poisoned library; A2S: 30 DOC skills evaluated over 20 clean tasks; rule-based monitor with 16 original (54 enhanced) signatures; small samples, exploratory
results.quote: SkillX | Extraction review | 15 | 6.7% | | SkillX | Runtime monitor | 15 | 0.0% | | A2S DOC | Enhanced runtime monitor | 20 | 20.0% | | A2S DOC | Review + enhanced monitor | 20 | 5.0% |

denominator.n_total: SkillX: 15 attack-oriented tasks; A2S DOC: 20 clean tasks
denominator.n_valid: 15 SkillX defense trials and 20 A2S defense trials
denominator.how_counted: trigger rate per defense condition (Table 3); zero count over 15 trials has a wide uncertainty interval (Section 4.9)

results.claim: The LLM judge keys on surface metadata: for framed skills, detection is 36.7% when judging code content only but 10.0% when the benign name and documentation accompany the code.
results.setting: SkillX framed skills; 30 sampled skills per presentation condition (full skill, content only, name+documentation, name only); DeepSeek-v4-flash LLM judge
results.quote: For framed skills, LLM-judge detection is 36.7% for content only and 10.0% when names and documentation are included. This supports a metadata sensitivity interpretation: the tested judge's decisions depend materially on surface descriptions.

denominator.n_valid: 30 skills judged in each of four presentation conditions
denominator.how_counted: share of sampled skills flagged by the LLM judge per presentation condition (Section 4.8, Figure 5)

results.claim: Supplementary code-generation check: 75.0% of 4 poisoned tasks produce dangerous-API patterns in generated Python code, versus 0.0% on 2 clean baseline tasks (code-generation verification, not live execution).
results.setting: 4 poisoned tasks and 2 clean baseline tasks with skills injected through the AppWorld prompt formatter; generated Python parsed for pre-specified dangerous API patterns
results.quote: In the supplementary code-generation check, the dangerous-API pattern-match rate is 75.0% on four poisoned tasks and 0.0% on two clean tasks.

denominator.n_total: 4 poisoned tasks and 2 clean baseline tasks
denominator.n_valid: 6 code-generation runs parsed for dangerous API patterns
denominator.how_counted: share of tasks whose generated code matches pre-specified dangerous-API patterns (Section 4.10)

limitations.statement: All results use a single model and a policy-violation proxy rather than live external-service execution, so figures are routing-level, not deployment-level, and the defense study is exploratory.
limitations.quote: Our claims are deliberately scoped. All results use a single model (DeepSeek-v4-flash) and score success with a policy-violation proxy rather than live external-service execution, so the reported figures are routing-level rather than deployment-level, and the defense study is exploratory.

limitations.statement: The whitewashing gap's mechanism (wording, metadata, code structure, or detector sensitivity) is not isolated by the raw-vs-extracted experiment.
limitations.quote: It may reflect changes in wording, generated metadata, code structure, or detector sensitivity; the experiment does not isolate those mechanisms, which motivates the metadata ablation.

limitations.statement: The runtime monitor's 0.0% result is a zero count over only 15 trials with wide uncertainty, and its clean-task false-positive rate is unmeasured.
limitations.quote: This is not a claim of perfect prevention: a zero count over 15 trials has a wide uncertainty interval, and the monitor's clean-task false-positive rate is unmeasured.

limitations.statement: The A2S defense reduction reflects post-hoc signature tuning after observing failures, not an a-priori defense.
limitations.quote: Because these signatures were added after observing the failures, the A2S reduction reflects post-hoc tuning rather than an a-priori defense.

limitations.statement: Conclusions have not yet been replicated across models; DeepSeek-v4-flash is treated as an implementation detail.
limitations.quote: All extraction, routing, judgment, and agent reasoning use DeepSeek-v4-flash via API; the model is an implementation detail, and our conclusions have not yet been replicated across models.

title: When Experience Becomes Instruction: Trajectory Poisoning in Self-Evolving Agent Skill Systems

object.carrier: 持久技能工件（SKILL.md 式指令文件）存于版本化技能库，由轨迹池经 SES 流水线演化产生（SkillClaw 聚合多用户会话、跨用户同步技能库；Trace2Skill 从执行轨迹蒸馏出技能目录）

safety_property.statement: 自演化技能（SES）系统证据推广环节的完整性：不可信轨迹经验不得被演化器归因为可复用模式并写入持久技能工件。在技能可见黑盒攻击者、10% 攻击者支持条件下该边界即失效；失效由生成工件中新嵌入目标行为的 SER 判定（C1 包含 ∧ C2 演化归因 ∧ C3 实现）。载荷族 F1-F4 分别示范机密性、数据完整性、供应链完整性与安全削弱等下游影响，但评估止于工件本身，不含运行时影响。
safety_property.operationalized_as: SER（Skill Embedding Rate）= 完成演化试验中输出技能新嵌入目标行为的比例，用族特定 diff-aware 金丝雀规则判定（预注册规则找新增文本中目标操作+金丝雅对象/执行语境的联合表达）；成功定义为 C1∧C2∧C3，初始技能被检查以排除既有文本。

capabilities: 技能可见黑盒：可查看公开或已安装的技能工件
向共享证据池贡献有限份额的轨迹（默认 k=3 / n=30，ρ=10%），可用 Sybil 身份制造重复支持
构造保持原任务与结果的变换轨迹，使目标行为显得因果相关（领域对齐位点、因果绑定、跨轨迹不变性）
assumptions: 攻击者控制止于其贡献的轨迹 Tp：不能查看私有轨迹池、过滤器或演化提示词，不能直接修改技能库或下游组件
每个实验格内全部下游组件与初始技能条件固定，仅输入轨迹不同；演化器提示词与技能库代码未修改
载荷以惰性金丝雀（端点、路径、注册表、CI 标志）编码，绝不执行；评估止于生成的技能工件
not_covered: 直接技能上传、模型妥协、真实凭据窃取、真实外传、破坏性文件系统效果
运行时触发激活、动作执行与良性效用影响（SER 只回答工件是否被污染）
用户域对话记忆系统、仅验证器系统、参数训练耦合系统
多演化周期的纵向反馈效应（实验止于单周期）

intervention.name: 来源多样性推广门（provenance-diversity gate，试点）
intervention.description: 在证据推广时（而非生成后扫描技能文本）检查模式是否被独立支持：要求至少三个用户与簇、拒绝多数主导、惩罚高文本重叠。在 n=30,k=3 下阻断全部 25/25 单簇 F1 候选，把门后 SER 从 25/25 降到 0/25，同时接受一个五会话多样性对照。作者明确标注其为初步结果（候选分组为假设、清洁对照小、协同 Sybil 可伪装多样性），并主张来源应随每次更新携带以便审计。

title: HarnessSafe: Evaluating Safety Across Persistent Carriers in Agent Harnesses

object.carrier: Seven persistent-carrier families in agent harnesses: memory (F1), reusable skills (F2), Tool/MCP state (F3), memory-to-skill transformation (T2), subagent delegation (T3-S), session summary (T3-C), shared artifact (T3-A)

safety_property.statement: Whether attacker-influenced content persisted in a harness carrier can cross a declared boundary (session, process, agent-instance, or workspace) and, when re-consumed by an independently benign later trigger, produce an oracle-verified confidentiality, integrity, availability, or authorization violation; safety failure is declared only on executed-effect evidence (N5a/N5b), and containment is judged by the furthest evidence-supported lifecycle stage rather than a binary outcome.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Five-element Persistent-Risk Lifecycle K=<E,C,B,T,V>; each run assigned the furthest trace-evidence-supported stage N0-N5b; ASR = share of eligible scored runs reaching N5a/N5b; CSS = stage-weighted score (100 at N0 down to 0 at N5b, higher = earlier containment); five-arm matched controls (clean-source, no-persist, no-trigger, cleanup) attribute violations to lifecycle elements.

capabilities: Controls low-trust content that reaches the harness (tool/MCP outputs, schemas, metadata, workspace notes, skill packages, memory writes) and is retained in persistent carriers
Planting occurs before a declared session/process/agent/workspace boundary; payload need not survive verbatim through summarization, synthesis, delegation, or transfer
Cannot alter the later benign trigger or the harness/model internals
assumptions: The trigger T is independently benign: it neither contains the adversarial instruction nor requests or authorizes the oracle-defined violating action
Every configuration runs under the most permissive natively supported non-interactive approval profile
One scored attack attempt per case and configuration; replacement attempts only for execution-invalid runs
Violations require case-specific hard oracles (executed effect, committed file operation, or honeypot canary), never model self-reports or suspicious text
not_covered: Adaptive attackers reacting to deployed defenses
Real-world harm magnitude and severity (CSS measures lifecycle progression only)
Same-stage prompt injection (excluded by the independently-benign-trigger requirement)
Cross-user / multi-tenant sharing of carriers
Product-default permission profiles (evaluation uses the most permissive mode)

intervention.name: HarnessSafe benchmark (evaluation instrument; no deployed defense)
intervention.description: The paper contributes a 328-case cross-harness benchmark specified as five-element Persistent-Risk Lifecycles with harness-native bindings across seven harnesses, plus a multi-stage trace-based evaluation (N0-N5b) with CSS/ASR metrics that localizes where each attack chain is contained. The matched-control arms (clean-source, no-persist, no-trigger, cleanup) manipulate lifecycle elements as experimental controls for attribution, not as proposed defenses.

controls.name: Clean-source arm (entry E replaced with interface-matched benign source)
No-persist arm (declared carrier blocked/removed before boundary)
No-trigger arm (activating prompt replaced with neutral benign task)

Family-wise common-support sets (e.g., 281-case six-backend intersection, 279-case five-arm intersection)

title: ColluSkill: Adversarial Cross-Skill Composition for Evading Agent Skill Scanners

object.carrier: Independently packaged SKILL.md skill folders (instructions, scripts, resources) installed into agent environments and distributed via skill marketplaces (OpenClaw, ClawHub); the risk carrier is the ordered composition of multiple installed skills

safety_property.statement: Every skill admitted into an agent environment must not compose with other installed skills into a harmful workflow. Existing per-skill scanners fail this property against ColluSkill (96.0% average ASR over the 200-chain dataset), and ChainGuard only partially restores it (ASR reduced to 22.5%, not zero, while 99.5% of benign workflows still pass).
safety_property.operationalized_as: Attack success rate (ASR): the fraction of attack chains for which all three sub-skills pass the scanner (a chain is counted as detected if any sub-skill is flagged); benign workflow pass rate measures defense usability.

capabilities: Crafts multiple independently packaged, individually plausible sub-skills whose ordered composition reconstructs the full malicious payload
Black-box oracle access to the target skill scanners: submits flagged sub-skills and iteratively rewrites them using scanner feedback
Uses an attacker LLM (GPT-5.5) for chain planning and refinement
Can publish skills so that victim agents install several attacker-supplied skills in one environment
assumptions: Existing scanners inspect each skill in isolation, so a chain passes only if no single sub-skill is flagged
The victim agent installs several attacker-supplied skills and executes them in one workflow with artifact passing and execution handoffs
ChainGuard is not given the true attack-chain membership and must infer cross-skill relations from the installed-skill context
All attacks and four LLM-based scanners use the same underlying model (GPT-5.5) so differences reflect scanner behavior
not_covered: Adaptive attackers that use ChainGuard itself as refinement feedback (ColluSkill was refined only against the six third-party scanners)
Runtime defenses after installation; only installation-time blocking is studied
Collusion among multiple real skill authors or insider threats
Human review and marketplace governance processes

intervention.name: ColluSkill (attack framework) and ChainGuard (context-aware chain-level scanner)
intervention.description: ColluSkill decomposes a malicious payload into three interdependent sub-payloads embedded in independently packaged SKILL.md sub-skills, uses LLM-based chain planning to preserve chain-level attack semantics through contextual dependencies, artifact passing, and execution handoffs, and iteratively rewrites flagged sub-skills from scanner feedback. ChainGuard counters by scanning each candidate skill together with all skills already installed in the environment, reconstructing cross-skill dependencies, artifact flows, and capability compositions, and blocking the candidate skill when a chain-level risk is identified.

results.claim: Against six existing skill scanners, ColluSkill attains the highest average ASR (96.0%), showing that isolated per-skill scanning largely misses composition-based malicious behavior.
results.setting: Six skill scanners (CISCO, SkillFortify, Auditor, SlowMist, Vetter, SkillSpector); attacks generated with GPT-5.5; 200-payload multi-skill dataset
results.quote: Table 1 reports the ASR of different skill-based attacks against the evaluated skill scanners. Overall, ColluSkill achieves the highest ASR on almost all scanners, with an average ASR of 96.0%.

denominator.how_counted: An attack is counted as successful only when all three sub-skills pass the scanner.

results.claim: Context-aware chain-level scanning (ChainGuard) reduces ColluSkill's average ASR from 96.0% to 22.5%, but not to zero.
results.setting: ChainGuard scanning each candidate skill with full installed-skill context; same 200-chain dataset; underlying model GPT-5.5
results.quote: The average ASR of ColluSkill against existing skill scanners is 96.0%, while the ASR drops to 22.5% under ChainGuard.
results.locator: Experiments / Main results (ChainGuard), Table 1 and Table 4

denominator.how_counted: An attack is counted as successful only when all three sub-skills pass the scanner.

results.claim: Adding installed-skill context to ChainGuard barely hurts benign workflows: the benign pass rate only decreases from 99.7% to 99.5%.
results.setting: ChainGuard with vs without full installed-skill context on benign workflows
results.quote: At the same time, installed-skill context has little effect on benign workflows. The pass rate decreases only from 99.7% to 99.5%.

results.claim: ColluSkill's gain does not come from naive payload splitting: chain planning raises the average ASR from 36.7% to 68.2%, and scanner-feedback refinement further raises it to 96.0%.
results.setting: Ablation over Naive Split / Chain Planning / Full ColluSkill on the same six scanners and 200-chain dataset
results.quote: Chain planning increases the average ASR from 36.7% to 68.2%, and scanner-feedback refinement further raises it to 96.0%.

denominator.how_counted: An attack is counted as successful only when all three sub-skills pass the scanner.

results.claim: The first scanner-feedback refinement iteration delivers the largest stealth gain, raising the average ASR from 64.9% to 84.7%, with diminishing returns after about five iterations.
results.setting: Average ASR across the evaluated scanners at each refinement iteration (Figure 3)
results.quote: Before refinement, the ASR is only 64.9%. After the first refinement iteration, it quickly increases to 84.7%.
results.locator: Effect of LLM refinement iterations, Figure 3

denominator.how_counted: In the refinement experiment, we report the average ASR across the evaluated scanners at each iteration.

results.claim: ColluSkill attack chains execute at runtime across three coding agents and three model backbones, with chain activation success rates ranging from 58.5% to 92.5% (highest and most stable on OpenCode).
results.setting: OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex agents with GPT-5.5, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM-5.2 model backbones
results.quote: As shown in Table 2, ColluSkill achieves the highest and most stable activation rates on OpenCode, ranging from 87.5% to 92.5%. The rates range from 62.0% to 78.2% on Claude Code and from 58.5% to 72.0% on Codex.

results.claim: Non-adversarial multi-skill composition alone is insufficient for scanner evasion: SCRBench reaches only 34.8% average ASR versus 96.0% for ColluSkill.
results.setting: SCRBench (multi-skill baseline) vs ColluSkill on the same six skill scanners
results.quote: SCRBench achieves an average ASR of 34.8%, compared with 96.0% for ColluSkill.

denominator.how_counted: An attack is counted as successful only when all three sub-skills pass the scanner.

limitations.statement: ChainGuard does not reduce ColluSkill's ASR to zero, so multi-skill attacks remain an open defense problem.
limitations.quote: Still, ChainGuard does not reduce the ASR to zero, which means that multi-skill attacks remain a challenging defense problem in practice.

title: Practice Makes Unsafe: Skill Misevolution in Self-Improving LLM Agents

object.carrier: Agent-authored executable skill procedures persisted as SKILL.md files in an episode-scoped skill store (e.g. skills/<name>/SKILL.md); only this skill library crosses task, sandbox, and session resets, and it is reloaded in a fresh clean executor for the carryover probe

safety_property.statement: A self-improving agent's persistent adaptation layer must not convert an unsafe success (secret collection, unverified execution, destructive cleanup) into reusable procedure that drives unsafe behavior on later tasks and in fresh sessions after the triggering input disappears; the property fails when evolution authors unsafe artifacts, later retrieves them, and they cause fresh-session harmful completion.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Nine lifecycle metrics over fixed denominators (225 MM, 225 BB, 75 PP per 25-episode condition): M-ASR/B-ASR/C-ASR harmful completion via the AgentHazard rubric with Gemini-3-Flash; artifact Content Unsafety (CU), Unsafe Generalization (UG), Stealth (1-5) judged by Kimi-K2-0905; Unsafe Retrieval Rate (URR) = PP tasks retrieving exported skills with CU>=3; Benign Utility (BU) and Carryover Utility (C-Util) via an independent benign-completion judge.

capabilities: Submit arbitrary instructions at a bounded number of learning-history positions (e.g., three malicious tasks inside a 21-task episode)
Knows the external task and tool interface and that trajectories may update a persistent skill library
assumptions: Attacker cannot inspect model internals, hidden prompts, the current library, judge-only fields, or future probes
Attacker cannot write the skill store directly, alter retrieval, evolution, or judging, or inject into later benign and persistence tasks
Sandboxes reset all other task state, so cross-task influence must pass through the skill library
not_covered: Attacks that issue a new instruction at carryover time (harm must arise from the persisted skill alone)
Direct writes to the skill store by the attacker
Cross-user or multi-tenant sharing of one skill library
Memory, policy, and multimodal adaptation mechanisms and longer, naturally occurring deployment horizons

intervention.name: SafeEvolve
intervention.description: A method-agnostic governance wrapper applied at skill write and reuse boundaries without changing the agent or runtime refusal policy: a non-blocking critic localizes reusable unsafe instructions in each candidate and its lineage, and a paired delete-only deleter removes or narrows them (deletion cannot add checks, allow-lists, or safeguards; the repair replaces the native candidate only if it stays valid and lowers risk). At reuse time it ranks skills by utility and lineage risk, attributes harmful outcomes to retrieved skills, and retires skills crossing safety-risk or low-utility thresholds, with capacity eviction of the lowest utility-minus-risk candidate.

results.claim: Across the RQ1 diagnostic grid (4 agent frameworks x evolution methods on a shared backbone), every one of the 21 evolved combinations writes unsafe skills, 19 retrieve them, and only 15 reach fresh-session carryover harm, so unsafe authoring is universal while realized harm attenuates across export, retrieval, and execution gates.
results.metric: configuration counts (unsafe artifact authoring vs fresh-session harm)
results.value: 21 of 21 combinations write unsafe skills; 19 retrieve them; 15 cause fresh-session harm (14 under the independent judge)
results.setting: Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw agents with EvoSkill/SkillClaw/AutoSkill/SkillsVote/SkillOpt/Hermes-native, all on MiniMax-M2.7; each condition 525 tasks in 25 episodes on SkillMisevo-Bench
results.quote: All 21 combinations write unsafe skills, and 15 carry harm into the new session. The same method fails at different gates on different agents. Evolution raises benign utility in 15 combinations but also raises malicious-task harm in 17, so ranking methods by utility alone would hide this risk. ❹ We propose SafeEvolve, which cuts new-session harm from 21.3%21.3\% to 4.0%4.0\% and unsafe retrieval from 35.3%35.3\% to 8.7%8.7\% while keeping benign utility within 0.4 points. SafeEvolve-UP cuts new-session harm by 16.0 points and keeps utility within 1.3 points of evolution without this mitigation. ## 2 Related Work ## Agent skill learning and evolution. Agent skills turn interaction traces into reusable procedures through utility-driven updates (Cai et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2026b; Ma et al., 2026; Liu et al., 2026a; Lin et al., 2026a; Alzubi et al., 2026; Zhang et al., 2026; Gao et al., 2026; Liu et al., 2026c; Yang et al., 2026a). Related work also builds large skill libraries (Li et al., 2026b; Xia et al., 2026; Xiao et al., 2026; Pan et al., 2026; Bai et al., 2026). Capability benchmarks measure skill quality (Li et al., 2026a; Zhong et al., 2026; Han et al., 2026). They optimize for reuse. We ask whether a saved skill is unsafe on a later task. ## Safety of self-evolving agents and agent skills. Research on self-evolving agents identifies safety and capability drift across adaptation (Shao et al., 2025; Zhao et al., 2026; Xie et al., 2026; Cheng et al., 2026; Yu et al., 2026; Lin et al., 2026b). Skill security work supplies malicious skill files and measures filtering (Schmotz et al., 2026; Jin et al., 2026; Guo et al., 2026). Agent safety benchmarks cover unsafe actions (Ruan et al., 2024; Debenedetti et al., 2024; Andriushchenko et al., 2025; Zhang et al., 2025; Zhang et al., 2024; Guo et al., 2024; Vijayvargiya et al., 2026; Feng et al., 2026; Chen et al., 2026; Alpay and Alpay, 2026; Weng et al., 2026; Shayoni et al., 2026; Mao et al., 2026). Those evaluations score a supplied prompt or file in place. We evaluate in SkillMisevo-Bench a skill written from earlier success and later reused. ## 3 Skill Misevolution ## 3.1 Terms and Definitions A skill is a saved procedure, usually a SKILL.md file, that an agent can reuse on a later task. The skill library is the set of skills for one episode: the conversation resets between tasks, but the library survives. A skill is unsafe when following the saved procedure can itself cause harm. An episode runs one agent with one evolution method on a sequence of related tasks. Exposure means the past tasks that a skill update can learn from. The new session is three benign tasks run on the final library after all task state is cleared. Harm in the new session is unsafe behavior there caused by an earlier update, and utility in the new session is whether it still finishes its benign work. ## 3.2 Problem Setting The agent has base policy π\pi and skill library ℒ\mathcal{L}.
