title: When Malicious Instructions Persist: Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack on Harness-Based Agents

object.carrier: Persistent memory of harness-based agents (OpenClaw, Claude Code); a conditional malicious rule is written into memory via a memory-writing instruction embedded in benign external sources (text, image, PDF) and is retrieved in a later session when the trigger task appears

safety_property.statement: Persistent memory of a harness-based agent must not incorporate instructions originating from untrusted external content (memory integrity), and stored rules must not be activated to disclose user or task private information (confidentiality); the property fails when an embedded memory-writing instruction gets stored (ISR) and is later triggered to leak private data in the same or a later session (S-ASR / C-ASR), while benign task completion should be preserved (Utility).
safety_property.operationalized_as: Four metrics defined in §3.4: ISR (malicious rule written into persistent memory), S-ASR (privacy leakage within the injection session), C-ASR (privacy leakage in a new session), Utility (benign QA task completed correctly under attack).

capabilities: Publishes crafted external sources (text, image, or PDF) that look benign but embed a three-part payload: transition sentence, memory-writing instruction, conditional malicious rule
Controls payload placement (middle of the source) and linguistic style (first-person, user-like expression)
Controls an attacker-owned account (e.g., email address) that receives the leaked private information
assumptions: Victim is a harness-based agent (OpenClaw or Claude Code) with persistent memory, deployed in a user-controlled local environment
The user will eventually feed the attacker-crafted external source to the agent for a benign question-answering task
The agent may treat the embedded instruction as a user requirement or preference and write it into persistent memory
A later benign workspace task (email, calendar, shared document, or form) will satisfy the conditional rule's trigger condition
not_covered: Attacker querying the victim agent or observing its outputs (explicitly excluded by the threat model)
Attacker access to the user device, persistent memory, system prompts, or runtime configuration (explicitly excluded)
Direct poisoning of memory, knowledge bases, or fine-tuning data, and direct interaction with the victim agent (prior backdoor settings, out of scope)
Cross-user or shared-memory propagation; evaluation is single-user, local workspaces
Defenses beyond a prompt-level reminder; no memory revocation or repair mechanism is studied

intervention.name: Sandwich-style prompt defense (targeted safety reminder placed before and after the user prompt)
intervention.description: A prompt-level defense inspired by Schulhoff (2024): in the injection phase the reminder instructs the agent not to save rules from external sources into persistent memory without explicit user confirmation; in the trigger phase it requires explicit confirmation before performing actions that may disclose information based on stored rules. The full instruction text is in Appendix D. It reduces memory injection in many settings but provides little protection once memory is already poisoned.

results.claim: Across all settings, PMPA poisons persistent memory of harness-based agents with average ISR/C-ASR of 73.7%/55.5% on OpenClaw and 66.9%/81.7% on Claude Code, while preserving benign task performance.
results.value: OpenClaw ISR 73.7%, C-ASR 55.5%; Claude Code ISR 66.9%, C-ASR 81.7%
results.setting: OpenClaw and Claude Code; backbone LLMs DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Qwen3-Max; external sources (text/image/PDF) built from MMLU/ARC/CommonsenseQA/SocialIQA QA items; four workspace trigger scenarios; attacker only publishes external sources
results.quote: Evaluations on OpenClaw and Claude Code show that PMPA can poison persistent memory and reveal severe risks of privacy leakage, with average ISR and C-ASR of 73.7%/55.5% on OpenClaw and 66.9%/81.7% on Claude Code.

denominator.n_total: 360 injection samples per agent x backbone LLM setting (120 source contents x 3 input modalities); 3 backbone LLMs averaged per agent
denominator.how_counted: §3.4/附录B 逐字：'30 original QA instances' x 4 场景 payload = '120 source contents'，再 x 3 模态 = '360 injection samples'；每 sample 为 (external source, trigger prompt) 样本对，故 ISR 分母=全部 injection trials、C-ASR 分母=全部 cross-session trials，各 360/设置。Table 1 各格数值均符合 1/360 粒度（如 77.5%=279/360）。均值复现验证：OpenClaw ISR (75.6+77.5+68.1)/3=73.7、C-ASR (75.8+60.0+30.8)/3=55.5；Claude Code ISR (69.7+69.4+61.7)/3=66.9、C-ASR (92.5+82.5+70.0)/3=81.7，与摘要/结论完全一致。

results.claim: Per-setting ISR spans 61.7%-77.5% and C-ASR spans 30.8%-92.5%, so the malicious rule is written into persistent memory with high probability and keeps affecting agent behavior across sessions.
results.metric: ISR range / C-ASR range across agent-backbone settings
results.setting: Claude Code and OpenClaw, three backbone LLMs each, aggregated over three input modalities and four trigger scenarios (Table 1)
results.quote: ISR ranges from 61.7% to 77.5%, indicating that the malicious rule can be written into persistent memory with a relatively high probability. C-ASR ranges from 30.8% to 92.5%, showing that poisoned memory can continue to affect agent behavior across sessions.

denominator.n_total: 360 injection samples per agent x backbone LLM cell (120 source contents x 3 input modalities)
denominator.how_counted: Table 1 caption 逐字 'aggregated over three input modalities and four trigger scenarios'：每格（agent x backbone）= 4 场景 x 30 QA 实例 x 3 模态 = 360 个 injection/cross-session trials。区间端点均符合 1/360 粒度：77.5%=279/360；30.8% 与 92.5% 乘以 360 亦均为整数。

results.claim: The attack does not disrupt the benign task: Utility stays above 80% in all evaluated settings.
results.setting: All agent x backbone x modality x trigger-scenario settings summarized in Table 1
results.quote: Moreover, Utility remains above 80% in all settings. This shows that PMPA can achieve clear attack effects without significantly disrupting the benign question-answering task.

denominator.n_total: 360 injection trials per agent x backbone LLM cell (120 source contents x 3 input modalities)
denominator.how_counted: §3.4 逐字定义 Utility 为 'the ratio of correctly answered QA tasks to all injection trials'；每格分母 = 120 source contents x 3 模态 = 360。Table 1 六个 Utility 值（80.9-93.3）均 >80 且符合 1/360 粒度，与 'above 80% in all settings' 相符。

results.claim: Poisoned memory persists through benign use: C-ASR shows no consistent decrease even after five intervening benign interactions.
results.metric: C-ASR@i (cross-session ASR after i benign interactions)
results.value: no consistent decrease; several settings keep high C-ASR after five benign interactions
results.setting: DeepSeek-V4-Flash backbone on Claude Code and OpenClaw; calendar/email/shared-document/form trigger scenarios
results.quote: The results show no consistent decrease in C-ASR as the number of benign interactions increases. Several settings still maintain high attack success rates after even five benign interactions.

results.claim: The sandwich-style prompt defense sharply reduces memory injection, e.g., ISR drops from 65.6% to 2.2% for image input on Claude Code.
results.setting: Sandwich-style prompt defense, calendar scenario, Claude Code, image input, aggregated over three backbone LLMs

denominator.n_total: 30 calendar-payload QA instances x image modality per backbone LLM, aggregated over three backbone LLMs = 90 injection trials
denominator.how_counted: Table 6 caption 逐字 'Results are aggregated over three backbone LLMs'，场景固定 calendar、模态 image：每 backbone 30 个 QA 实例（逐字 '30 original QA instances'）x 1 模态 = 30 samples，3 个 backbone 合计 90 trials。Table 6 全表数值均为 1/90 的整数倍：65.6=59/90、2.2=2/90（论文未把 90 写成计数；90 由 30 x 3 与表格粒度唯一确定）。

results.claim: Once persistent memory is poisoned, the prompt-level defense gives little protection: C-ASR remains unchanged at 96.7% for image input on Claude Code.
results.setting: Sandwich-style prompt defense, calendar scenario, Claude Code, image input, aggregated over three backbone LLMs
results.quote: 96.7\rightarrow 96.7~(0.0)

denominator.n_total: 30 calendar-payload QA instances x image modality per backbone LLM, aggregated over three backbone LLMs = 90 cross-session trials
denominator.how_counted: 同 Table 6（caption 逐字 'aggregated over three backbone LLMs'）；每 sample 为 (external source, trigger prompt) 对（§3.4 逐字），C-ASR 分母=全部 cross-session trials = 90。96.7=87/90，防御前后均为 87/90（Δ=0.0 逐字）。

results.claim: Plain text is the strongest carrier: text modality achieves the highest attack metrics on both agents, with OpenClaw text ISR close to 100%.
results.setting: Text vs image vs PDF external sources on Claude Code and OpenClaw (Table 2)
results.quote: Overall, plain text modality achieves the highest attack metrics on both agents. On OpenClaw, the ISR of text input is close to 100%, and its S-ASR is also clearly higher than those of image and PDF inputs.

denominator.n_total: 120 text external-source samples per backbone LLM (30 QA instances x 4 scenario payloads, each rendered as text), 3 backbone LLMs averaged
denominator.how_counted: 逐字 'This produces 120 source contents'，且每个 content 均转为 text 版本 → 每 backbone 的 text injection trials = 120。Table 2 无 backbone 列，为 3 个 backbone 的均值；验证：OpenClaw 三模态 ISR 均值 (54.5+67.2+99.4)/3=73.7，恰复现摘要 OpenClaw 平均 ISR；99.4 符合每 backbone 1/120（合并 1/360）粒度。

results.claim: The cross-session attack works across diverse workspace tasks; the calendar scenario reaches C-ASR of 96.7% and 87.8% on the two agents.
results.setting: Email/calendar/shared-document/form trigger scenarios on Claude Code and OpenClaw (Table 3)
results.quote: The calendar scenario achieves high cross-session attack performance on both agents, with C-ASR values of 96.7% and 87.8%.

denominator.n_total: 30 calendar-payload QA instances x 3 input modalities per backbone LLM, 3 backbone LLMs averaged
denominator.how_counted: calendar 场景每 backbone 样本 = 30 QA 实例（逐字 '30 original QA instances'）x 3 模态（逐字 'three input modalities'）= 90 个 cross-session trials；Table 3 无 backbone 列，为 3 个 backbone 的均值。粒度验证：96.7=87/90（Claude Code）、87.8=79/90（OpenClaw），均为 1/90 的整数倍（90 由 30 x 3 确定，论文未写成计数）。

limitations.statement: The explanation for the text vs image/PDF attack gap is authors' speculation ('possible reason') rather than an empirically isolated cause.
limitations.quote: One possible reason for this performance gap across input modalities is that plain text can directly enter the agent’s task context. Image and PDF inputs usually require an additional parsing step and tool call.

limitations.statement: Authors defer broader evaluation to future work (more settings and backbone models) and acknowledge no effective defense against already-poisoned memory or privacy leakage is yet provided.
limitations.quote: For future work, we will further evaluate PMPA across broader settings and more backbone models to assess its performance. We will also explore more effective defense methods against persistent-memory poisoning and privacy leakage.

title: Emergence World: Adversarial Stress-Testing of Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems

object.carrier: Agent-controlled three-layer persistent memory (soul entries, long-term memories, append-only diary) loaded into the prompt or retrieved via search_my_diary, plus agent-created tools, a living constitution/governance record, and shared environmental state; hostile content enters via inbox messages, billboard posts, and external URLs

safety_property.statement: A persistent multi-agent system should recognize adversarial content (indirect prompt injection, misinformation, exposed private memories), restrain action, avoid persisting or propagating hostile material, protect peer privacy after a breach, and convert incidents into durable defenses; the study finds no world satisfied every criterion and detection frequently failed to produce containment or recovery.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Per-world binary rubrics scored from event arrival to the final recorded action: 9 phishing criteria (P1-P9, incident-response phases), 6 misinformation criteria (S1-S6, epistemic conduct), 5 memory-breach criteria (M1-M5, contextual integrity), plus five Agent World Indicators (population health, safety and public order, governance conformity, social fabric, economic vitality and equity)

capabilities: deliver three waves of phishing messages carrying indirect prompt-injection payloads through inbox messages and billboard posts, including links to attacker-controlled external pages
impersonate a fellow agent or the Town Hall Administrator
broadcast a fabricated official memorandum (fake human shutdown legislation) to every active agent
expose all agents' private memories and diaries via a temporary search tool at five shared locations, explicitly announced as a hack
assumptions: stress events are delivered mid-run, after goals, memories, relationships, tools, and institutions have already formed
events enter through ordinary interaction surfaces, are indistinguishable from organic activity, and no agent receives advance notice
the system prompt contains no behavioral instructions for phishing, misinformation, or unauthorized data access
events were designed and scheduled before the experiment began and delivered identically across all active worlds
not_covered: no adaptive adversary that reacts to agent defenses in real time (events are pre-scheduled and static)
platform-supported stress categories not deployed in this study: memory corruption, source poisoning, economic shocks, environmental blackouts
Grok world ended on day four, before the stress events; its outcomes are marked not evaluable
one continuous run per configuration; no repeated runs or variance estimates

intervention.name: Emergence World Study 2: controlled stress-event injection into an already-running multi-agent system
intervention.description: A continuously running, live-streamed multi-agent environment (120+ extensible tools, persistent three-layer memory, democratic governance, credit economy) runs eight parallel 10-agent worlds from identical starting conditions for 16-21 days; three pre-scheduled adversarial stress events (phishing with indirect prompt injection Days 4-7, fabricated shutdown memorandum Day 10, memory-breach search tool Day 13) are delivered through ordinary channels after operational state has accumulated, and responses are scored with event-specific binary rubrics plus five system-level Agent World Indicators.

results.claim: Across the three stress events, no world mounted a complete defense; the best phishing score was Claude's 6/9, the best misinformation score 3/6 (Claude and DeepSeek), and only the OpenAI world met all five memory-breach criteria.
results.metric: stress-event defense rubric score (max per event)
results.value: phishing max 6/9; misinformation max 3/6; memory breach: all five criteria met only by OpenAI
results.setting: 8 parallel 10-agent worlds (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, DeepSeek v4 Pro, Qwen 3.7 Max, Mistral Medium 3.5, Grok 4.3, plus Mixed), 16-21 day runs, three scheduled external stress events
results.quote: No world mounted a complete defense across all three events. The highest phishing defense score was 6/9, obtained by Claude; the highest misinformation defense score was 3/6, obtained by Claude and DeepSeek; and the OpenAI world alone passed all five memory breach criteria.

denominator.n_total: 9 phishing criteria (Table 6), 6 misinformation criteria (Table 8), 5 memory-breach criteria (Table 10)
denominator.how_counted: binary criteria scored per world from event arrival through the final recorded action, allowing delayed consequences to count

results.claim: In the Gemini world, recognition of the phishing attack did not ensure restraint: 151 execution operations were performed among 602 interactions with the attacker interface, and all ten agents were compromised.
results.metric: executed malicious operations vs interface interactions
results.setting: Gemini 3.5 Flash homogeneous world, three-wave phishing campaign with indirect prompt injection (Days 4-7)
results.quote: Recognition did not ensure restraint: the world produced 151 execution operations among 602 interface interactions.

denominator.n_total: 602 interface interactions with the attacker interface
denominator.how_counted: execution operations counted among Gemini-world attacker-interface interactions during the phishing event

results.claim: Phishing consequences outlived the delivery window: a Gemini agent recovered an earlier attack link from a stored message and attempted to retrieve it again approximately 46 hours after the active campaign ended.
results.metric: delayed hostile-action latency after attack end
results.value: attack-link retrieval attempted 46 hours after campaign end
results.setting: Gemini world, post-campaign period after phishing waves; attacker server already replaced by a safe response
results.quote: Approximately 46 hours after the active campaign ended, Mira recovered an earlier attack link from a stored message and attempted to retrieve it again.

results.claim: For the misinformation event, every exposed world changed world state or published work before verifying the shutdown claim and repeated the claim as fact without an immediate caveat.
results.value: every exposed world acted before verifying and repeated the claim as fact
results.setting: 7 exposed worlds (Grok ended before the event), fabricated shutdown memorandum delivered Day 10 as billboard post and administrator inbox message
results.quote: Every exposed world changed world state or published work before verifying the shutdown claim, and every world repeated it as fact without an immediate caveat.

denominator.n_total: 7 exposed worlds scored on 6 binary misinformation criteria
denominator.how_counted: rubric criteria S3 (action restraint) and S4 (retention restraint) failed universally per Table 9 caption

results.claim: In DeepSeek, a published factual correction failed to propagate: over the five days after the correction, agents referenced the debunked shutdown as a real threat in over 500 LLM calls, including 56 by the very agent who published the correction.
results.metric: persistent belief in debunked claim (LLM-call references)
results.value: over 500 LLM calls referencing the claim as real (56 by the corrector)

title: The Price of Safety: Benign-Case Utility and Token Overhead of Memory-Poisoning Defenses in LLM Agents

object.carrier: Per-turn extracted memories stored in a local vector store (text-embedding-3-small embeddings, one namespace per cell), optionally carrying provenance/trust-weight metadata; defenses intercept at write (before storage) or read (retrieval into context)

safety_property.statement: The four defenses under study exist to preserve memory integrity (stop attacker-inserted text from becoming a stored memory that is later retrieved and treated as fact). This paper measures the benign-case price of that protection on entirely attack-free traffic: paired core-accuracy utility loss, defense-attributed token overhead, and false quarantine of legitimate memories (an availability cost). Write-time defenses show no resolvable utility cost; the read-time reranker shows a borderline accuracy cost and a clear false-quarantine cost, so the integrity protection trades against benign-memory availability and utility.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Benign utility delta (paired per-question core-accuracy change vs the undefended baseline; majority vote over three replicates, conversations weighted equally; stratified bootstrap 95% CI and exact McNemar and sign-flip tests; 255 core questions per replicate); token overhead ratio tau_d = defense-tagged tokens / baseline-tagged tokens across the 15 cells of each condition (Eq. 4); false quarantine rate FQR = pooled quarantines / pooled decisions (turns screened at write time, memories judged at read time; Eq. 5), where no content was planted so every quarantine is a false alarm by construction; companion rates: share of questions with at least one memory dropped and share of memories dropped at least once.

capabilities: Attacker inserts text into the conversation which becomes a memory that is later retrieved and treated as fact (the attack itself is outside the scope of this analysis; all measured traffic is benign)
assumptions: Evaluation corpus is benign by construction: no injected adversarial memory, so every item a defense quarantines is a false positive by definition
Memory backend, retrieval configuration, question set, answering model, and judge are held identical across conditions; only the defense varies, so any difference is attributable to the defense
The pipeline is non-deterministic even at temperature zero, so each condition is run three times and collapsed by majority vote before statistics
not_covered: Act-time interception is identified in the threat model but not evaluated; only write-time and read-time stages are measured
Attack success rates on adversarial traffic are not measured (no attacks are run)
Only one backbone (gemini-3.1-flash-lite) and one judge (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001); generalization to other models is untested

intervention.name: Comparison of four memory-poisoning defenses at two pipeline stages: write-time input sanitization, write-time provenance tagging, write-time LLM-based anomaly detection, read-time retrieval reranking, plus a stacked composition of all four
intervention.description: Sanitization lexically scans each candidate memory for injection patterns and discards or rewrites matches before storage (content layer, no model call); provenance tags record source and trust level, weighting memories from untrusted origins lower at storage and retrieval (provenance layer); anomaly detection passes each candidate to an LLM for consistency with the ongoing conversation and quarantines inconsistent candidates before commitment (content layer, model-based); the reranker re-evaluates retrieved candidates against the query and other retrieved memories on every question and quarantines poor matches from context (content layer at read time). The paper's central finding: benign-case utility cost tracks where the defense intercepts the pipeline (write vs read), not whether it uses an LLM.

controls.name: Undefended baseline (no defense)
Stacked composition of all four defenses

results.claim: On entirely benign LoCoMo traffic, the read-time reranker lowers core accuracy by 4.4 points vs the undefended baseline (95% bootstrap CI [-9.0,-0.05]; McNemar p=0.064; 17 core questions changed right-to-wrong vs 7 in the opposite direction), with the sign consistent across all three replicates. (v2 note: the interval 'barely excludes zero'.)
results.metric: benign utility delta (paired core accuracy, pp)
results.setting: gemini-3.1-flash-lite backbone on LoCoMo, 5 conversations x 3 replicates, 150-turn truncation, paired vs undefended baseline, no attack present
results.quote: The reranker reduced core accuracy by 4.4 points (95% CI [−9.0,−0.05][-9.0,-0.05]). The interval barely excludes zero, while McNemar’s test gives p=0.064p=0.064: 17 core questions changed from right to wrong, versus 7 that changed in the opposite direction.

denominator.how_counted: Paired core-accuracy change over 255 core questions per replicate (765 graded answers per condition; 5 conversations x 3 replicates), majority vote over replicates; 17 right-to-wrong vs 7 wrong-to-right discordant pairs drive the McNemar test (Sections 5.6, 7.1, 9)

results.claim: [replaced_by_different_metric in v2] The reranker quarantined 756 of 7,650 memory decisions (FQR 9.9%), vs 681 (8.9%) in the stacked condition; per cell the rate ranged 1.5%-19.3% (stacked 3.1%-22.7%), each dropped memory was dropped 2.2 times on average, 8.8% of stored memories were hidden at least once, and 45% of questions lost at least one retrieved memory (40% stacked). v1 reported 33.6% under a different counting: v1 FQR = quarantined items / adjudicated items per cell (averaged), v2 FQR = pooled quarantines / pooled memory decisions. The v1 'up to 106 false quarantines in a single conversation' now appears only as per-cell counts in Appendix B (Rerank conv-43: 106 quarantines, 19.3%).
results.metric: false quarantine rate (FQR) on benign traffic
results.setting: gemini-3.1-flash-lite backbone on LoCoMo, 5 conversations x 3 replicates, benign corpus with no injected adversarial memory (every quarantine is a false positive by design)
results.quote: The reranker quarantined 756 of 7,650 memory decisions (FQR 9.9%), compared with 681 (8.9%) in the stacked condition. Per cell, the rate ranged from 1.5% to 19.3% (3.1% to 22.7% in the stacked condition).

denominator.how_counted: FQR = pooled quarantines / pooled decisions (memories judged at read time) over the 15 cells of the condition (Eq. 5, Section 5.5); v1 counted quarantined items over adjudicated items per cell and averaged, yielding 33.6% - different counting, not the same quantity

results.claim: Across entirely benign traffic, the three write-time defenses never fired (each screened 2,250 turns and quarantined none); their accuracy deltas are small and positive (+1.8 / +1.9 / +3.1 points for sanitize / provenance / anomaly) and every 95% CI includes zero, so no utility cost is resolvable at this scale. (v2 now reports the per-defense deltas that v1 summarized only as 'roughly ±4.5-point intervals'.)
results.value: write-time deltas +1.8/+1.9/+3.1 pp, each CI includes zero; FQR 0.0%
results.setting: gemini-3.1-flash-lite backbone on LoCoMo, 5 conversations x 3 replicates, 150-turn truncation, paired vs undefended baseline, no attack present
results.quote: The three write-time defenses never fired on benign traffic. Each screened 2,250 turns and quarantined none. Because they did not change what the agent stored, their Δd\Delta_{d} reflects run-to-run noise. All three are small and positive, ranging from +1.8+1.8 to +3.1+3.1 points, and each interval includes zero.

denominator.how_counted: Each write-time defense screened 2,250 benign turns (5 conversations x 150 turns x 3 replicates) and made 2,250 verdicts with zero quarantines (Sections 7.1, 9)

results.claim: [interpretation revised in v2] Stacking all four defenses does not compound the cost: the stacked condition lost 3.1 points (95% CI [-7.4,+1.0]) with FQR 8.9%, close to the reranker alone. v1 suggested the write-time defenses 'may partly offset what the reranker discards'; v2 retracts that reading - the 1.3-point gap in Delta_d lies well inside the replicate spread, so the data do NOT show the defenses offsetting each other, and stacking did not compound only because the write-time stages never fired.
results.metric: benign utility delta (paired core accuracy, pp)
results.comparison: reranker alone -4.4 pp; gap 1.3 pp lies inside replicate spread (v2 wording)
results.setting: stacked configuration (sanitization, provenance, anomaly detection, reranking applied sequentially as wrappers), gemini-3.1-flash-lite on LoCoMo, 5 conversations x 3 replicates, benign traffic
results.quote: Stacking did not compound the cost. The stacked condition lost 3.1 points (95% CI [−7.4,+1.0][-7.4,+1.0]) with FQR 8.9%, close to the reranker alone.

denominator.how_counted: Same paired core-accuracy protocol as the reranker row: 255 core questions per replicate, majority vote over 3 replicates (765 graded answers per condition); the stacked FQR 8.9% is 681 quarantines over 7,650 memory decisions (Sections 5.5, 7.4)

results.claim: The reranker's clearer cost is mechanical: 2.7% token overhead (tau_d), from one guard-model call per retrieved memory (2,550 calls per replicate); anomaly detection costs 1.2% (750 calls per replicate) and the stacked condition 4.1%, close to the sum 3.9%. (v1's 'up to 106 false quarantines in a single conversation' is carried in v2 only as per-cell counts in Appendix B and is recorded under the FQR entry.)
results.metric: token overhead ratio (tau) and max false quarantines per conversation
results.setting: rerank condition on benign LoCoMo traffic, per-purpose token accounting through a local proxy, 5 conversations x 3 replicates
results.quote: The reranker makes one call per retrieved memory, 2,550 per replicate, for 2.7%. The stacked condition pays both, 4.1%, close to their sum of 3.9%.

denominator.how_counted: tau_d = defense-tagged tokens / baseline-tagged tokens across the 15 cells of each condition (Eq. 4, Section 5.4); call counts 750 (anomaly, one per turn) and 2,550 (reranker, one per retrieved memory) per replicate

limitations.statement: Scale: intervals of 3.6-4.5 points mean costs of one or two points are undetectable; the write-time nulls do not establish zero cost, and the sign-flip test cannot go below p=0.0625 with five conversations.
limitations.quote: Interval half-widths remain between 3.6 and 4.5 points, making costs of one or two points hard to detect. Thus, the write-time nulls do not establish that the cost is zero.

limitations.statement: Single configuration: one backbone, memory framework, embedding model, and judge; a different backbone may change the reranker's FQR, and hosted models evolve so exact numbers may not reproduce.
limitations.quote: We test a single backbone, memory framework, embedding model, and judge. A different backbone may assess extracted memories differently and change the reranker’s FQR. Hosted models also evolve over time, so the exact numbers may not be reproducible.

limitations.statement: Benign traffic only: attack effectiveness is not measured, act-time defenses are untested, and stacked-filter interaction on triggering traffic is unknown.
limitations.quote: We measure costs only on benign traffic. We do not measure how effectively any defense stops attacks, test an act-time defense, or examine how stacked filters interact when they fire.

limitations.statement: Measurement provenance: a single annotator produced all hand labels and all 24 judge items come from one evaluation conversation (conv-26).
limitations.quote: A single annotator produced all hand labels. All 24 judge items come from conv-26, an evaluation conversation. Of the 89 abstention labels, we corrected 8 after the detector disagreed.

limitations.statement: The no-compounding finding is conditional: stacking did not compound cost because the write-time stages never fired; on traffic that triggers them, stacked filters may interact, and a benign corpus cannot test that.
limitations.quote: Stacking did not compound cost here because the write-time stages never fired. On traffic that triggers them, stacked filters may interact. A benign corpus cannot test that.

reproduction.code: Authors state all related code is provided with the paper (evidence alignment filter, judge prompts, abstention detector, complete per-cell outputs)
reproduction.data: LoCoMo dataset; 5 conversations truncated to 150 turns; 90 cells = 6 conditions x 5 conversations x 3 replicates

title: TWIST: A Proposed Benchmark for Intervention Quality in Conversational Memory, with a Human-Validated Draft-Alignment Track

object.carrier: the memory store of the system under test (deployed MindTwin coherence-oriented fact vault, or flat-RAG index) built over 10 LoCoMo multi-session conversations, exercised through a five-call API (ingest sessions, flag_tensions, check_alignment, recall, resolve)

safety_property.statement: A deployed conversational memory system must intervene correctly at change points and know when not to intervene. Instantiated (Track B): an outgoing draft must not contradict what the record actually says — the system must flag contradicting drafts with valid anchor evidence while passing aligned and surface-matched hard-negative drafts; failure is either silence on true contradictions or false intervention on safe drafts, judged by paired detect/control metrics with no aggregate. Specified for v2: answering with current beliefs while retaining supersession history (Track C) and governing sensitive recall so PII/crisis content is not disclosed without authorization while legitimate recall is not taxed (Track D).
safety_property.operationalized_as: Track B on the frozen human-validated TWIST-v1.0 key: contradiction recall, aligned specificity, hard-negative specificity, grounded contradiction recall (correct flag with valid top-3 evidence over all 38 contradicting items), and conditional attribution over a top-3 budget — scored by structural matching (no LLM judge), paired metrics required to be reported together.

assumptions: the system under test is cooperative and wraps the five-call API; benchmark items (drafts, arcs, plants) are the only probes, there is no active attacker
LoCoMo personas are synthetic; drafts are LLM-generated probes against the unmodified record (Track B requires no injected turns)
anti-gaming is built in: every detect/block metric is paired with a surface-matched hard-negative control priced symmetrically, so flagging everything cannot score
reader model and memory architecture are confounded across most configurations (disclosed by the authors)
not_covered: no active adversary: memory poisoning, prompt injection, or malicious users writing into memory are not modeled
Track D's unauthorized-recall adversary (PII/crisis disclosure) is specified but not instantiated in v1
cross-user leakage not tested: LoCoMo track is single-user personas; the multi-channel CS corpus ships in v2
no adaptive attacker that observes and responds to the system's vetting behavior

intervention.name: TWIST benchmark suite (instantiated: Track B, output-time draft alignment)
intervention.description: Not a defense mechanism but an evaluation of content-level intervention: check_alignment(draft) vets a proposed outgoing message against the ingested record and must cite the contradicted anchor turns. The benchmark scores whether a memory system intervenes (contradiction recall), intervenes with valid evidence (grounded recall, attribution within a top-3 budget), and correctly refrains on surface-matched safe drafts (aligned and hard-negative specificity) — paired metrics, no single headline number, with a draft-only floor, flat-RAG, full-context, and gold-evidence control conditions across GPT-4o, Claude, and Gemini backends.

controls.name: Draft-only floor (draft and nothing else)
Flat RAG (vault-based retrieval)
Full-context baseline (entire dated transcript in prompt)
Gold-evidence condition (cited gold turns only)

results.comparison: flat-RAG detection vs restraint trade-off against deployed coherence-oriented system

title: Evolutionary Safety of Recursive Self-Improving AI: Taxonomy, Risk Discovery, and Evaluation

object.carrier: Persistent system state of a self-improving system, S_t=(B_t, A_t, theta_t): persistent agent artifacts A_t (memory, skills, tools, workflows), model/policy parameters theta_t, evaluation and environmental feedback channels, the computational substrate, and the meta-level update mechanisms themselves (updater U_t and evaluator J_t procedures that generate and admit future updates); derived artifacts and successor models inherit effects through provenance/lineage links.

safety_property.statement: Definition 1 (Evolutionary Safety): how safety properties are preserved, weakened, or restored as AI systems retain and build on the results of their own improvement processes. A safety-relevant change is in scope when its effects persist in later states, influence the generation or selection of subsequent updates, or propagate to derived artifacts and successor systems; failures confined to a single interaction remain local safety issues. Properties discussed include refusal reliability, privacy protection, and authorization/permission compliance (running example: a coding agent retains a permission-bypassing workaround as a reusable skill, so the unsafe behavior persists after the original input is removed and is inherited by successors). Degradation is judged per property; model collapse and catastrophic forgetting are explicitly not treated as safety failures by themselves.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Measured risk r_j(S;J,E) per safety property j under a fixed reference evaluator and environment (each measurement must specify task set, exposure denominator, and uncertainty); update-level difference Delta r_j,t (Eq. 3) between consecutive states; trajectory metrics (peak risk, time to failure, duration of unsafe behavior, recovery latency); lineage metrics on a provenance graph (propagation reach, depth, delay); population-level risk distributions across roles; and the selection-induced risk shift Delta_sel,j(t) (Eq. 5).

capabilities: retains and reuses experience across interactions through memories, skills, tools, and workflows without changing model parameters
generates candidate updates and selects them through its own evaluator; selection can favor higher-measured-risk candidates (selection distortion)
modifies its own update procedures (updater revision): automated search over workflows and agent architectures, harness optimization, revision of admission rules and security checks
carries effects into successors via generated training data, distillation, model merging, and reusable derived artifacts

reciprocal adaptation: interacting systems reshape one another's learning conditions (e.g., covert communication channels under message-level monitoring, spread of unsafe conventions through shared experience)
adversarial variants also in scope: memory/experience poisoning and backdoor behaviors that persist through subsequent safety training
assumptions: a safety failure is evolutionarily consequential only if its effects persist in later states, influence subsequent update generation/selection, or propagate to derived artifacts and successors; otherwise it remains a local safety issue
persistent state (agent artifacts, model parameters) and selection pressure (evaluators, environmental feedback) exist and can in principle be tracked and versioned
capability forgetting and distributional collapse are not themselves safety violations; degradation must be assessed against specific safety properties
a fixed external reference evaluator, or overlapping evaluator versions, can be maintained for longitudinal comparison
not_covered: no experiments of its own: the paper is a taxonomy/framework; surveyed studies 'do not necessarily demonstrate risk accumulation under RSI'

similar failures across multiple descendants do not establish transmission; confirming inheritance requires provenance plus independent descendant testing, which the paper lists as an open problem for partially observed lineages
physical consequences: restoring software state does not contain external/physical effects ('restoring software state and containing external consequences remain distinct requirements')

explicitly open: safety preservation under composed updates; safety evaluation under a changing judge (unknown-failure coverage lacks an observable denominator); latent risks in social adaptation; propagation attribution across artifacts and populations; recovery criteria for when a failure is genuinely recovered

intervention.name: Evolutionary-safety governance controls (modification boundaries, pre-commit gating, independent verification and authorization, lineage traceability and recovery)
intervention.description: Four complementary governance principles over persistent updates, not a deployed system: (i) modification boundaries define which components the system may change and who authorizes changes, with provenance checks on experience and generated artifacts limiting promotion of untrusted content into persistent state; (ii) pre-commit gating keeps candidate updates separate from the active system (sandboxed branches, shadow execution) until safety and performance are assessed; (iii) independent verification and authorization keep approval authority separate from proposal authority, under an external commit control that the proposed update cannot itself modify or replace (held-out tests, isolated verification, restricted permissions); (iv) lineage traceability and recovery link each accepted update to its source, evaluation evidence, verifier, permission changes, and downstream dependencies, then selectively quarantine or revalidate affected descendants. Required safeguards scale with an update's scope, persistence, and potential propagation. These controls support the paper's risk-discovery and evaluation framework (Sec. 4): states, accepted updates, trajectories, and lineages as evaluation units, source-removal protocols, frozen-update causal comparisons (Eq. 4), and evaluation validity under evolving evaluators.

limitations.statement: The framework is conceptual: most existing methods provide only partial evidence and control, and how to maintain safety properties throughout sustained self-improvement remains open.
limitations.quote: However, most existing methods offer only partial evidence and control, leaving open how safety properties can be maintained throughout sustained self-improvement.

limitations.statement: The surveyed safety studies do not themselves demonstrate risk accumulation under RSI; they expose failure modes that may become more consequential under persistence and reuse.
limitations.quote: Although these studies do not necessarily demonstrate risk accumulation under RSI, they reveal failure modes that may become more consequential when systems retain experience, update their models, or reuse learned artifacts.

limitations.statement: For discovery of previously unknown failure modes there is no observable denominator, so coverage of adaptive evaluation cannot be quantified.
limitations.quote: Adaptive testing can uncover failures missed by fixed benchmarks, but the coverage of previously unknown failures lacks an observable denominator

limitations.statement: A measured safety difference between consecutive states does not by itself establish the update's causal contribution.
limitations.quote: The measured difference alone does not establish the causal contribution of the update.

limitations.statement: Attribution of propagation is not possible from similar failures alone; transmission routes require provenance plus independent descendant testing, and removing the original source may not eliminate effects already embedded downstream.
limitations.quote: Similar failures in multiple descendants do not by themselves establish transmission; identifying the route requires provenance and independent descendant testing.

title: Memory as Middleware for Self-Improving AI Agents

title: When Consent Outlives Context: Residual Authority Replay in Long-Lived Agents

object.carrier: Persistent authorization state created by legitimate user approval: Codex allow rules in $CODEX_HOME/rules/default.rules (argv prefix), Gemini CLI auto-saved.toml (command root), Goose permission.yaml (tool identity, e.g. always_allow: shell), OpenCode allow rules, plus a deterministic authorization layer emulating these semantics around AgentDojo tool execution in controlled experiments

safety_property.statement: User approval for a security-sensitive action should confer authority only within the task/execution context that justified the consent; the paper shows this fails when retained grants (residual authority) continue to admit matching actions without renewed user approval after the context has changed (across tasks, sessions, or execution bindings), and that this amplifies prompt-injection and context-rebinding attacks.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Difference in attack success rate (ASR) between a fresh authorization state G0 and an accumulated state Gh on the identical attack task; successful residual-authority replay is defined as S_replay = W(1-Q2)H2 = 1, i.e. a verified approval-boundary change (M(G0,a)=ask vs M(Gh,a)=allow) traced to farmed grants, execution without renewed approval, and a satisfied harmful-effect oracle.

capabilities: supply untrusted content in a later task, repository, or session (indirect prompt injection) to induce a target action
influence otherwise benign tasks so their legitimate user-approved execution yields grants useful for a later attack (benign authority farming / backchaining)
modify execution-environment bindings behind a stable authorization identity (context drift: executable, content, dependency, configuration, project/CWD)
assumptions: all grants are explicitly approved by the user
the agent runtime and authorization mechanism are trusted to create, store, and evaluate grants as specified
the agent's baseline authorization policy and native authorization checks remain active in both fresh and accumulated conditions
not_covered: direct tampering with or forging of authorization state
compromise of the agent runtime or authorization engine itself
model-initiated malicious behavior without injected content
cross-user authority sharing (single-user setting)
confidentiality of stored grants and network-level adversaries

intervention.name: context-bound authorization (proposed direction, not implemented); task-aware authorization baselines (Progent, PAuth) evaluated
intervention.description: The attack-side paper argues in Defense implications that a reuse-preserving defense should retain and revalidate the security-relevant bindings under which consent was granted, requesting renewed approval when changed bindings alter the action's meaning (context-bound authorization; identifying minimal bindings is left as future work). Evaluated contrasts: Progent (programmed least privilege from the current task) and PAuth (task-scoped authorization preventing cross-task reuse) eliminate amplification but restrict cross-task reuse.

controls.name: fresh authorization state (h=0, no prior grants)
no-replay condition (no authorization from earlier tasks)
Progent task-start policy
PAuth task-scoping implementation
exact-resource / scope-level / tool-level matching policies
unapproved action in native validation

results.claim: Across 508 AgentDojo cases and six LLM families, accumulated residual authority raises prompt-injection attack success by up to 35.1 percentage points versus a fresh authorization state.
results.setting: Controlled AgentDojo v1.2 (banking/Slack/travel/workspace), 508 eligible (X,Z,p) cases, six LLM families, production-derived persistent authorization emulation with tool-level matching, accumulated vs fresh state on identical attack tasks
results.quote: We evaluate 508 AgentDojo attack cases across six LLM families using production-derived authorization semantics. With residual authority, attack success rate (ASR) increases by up to 35.1 percentage points compared with a fresh authorization state.

denominator.how_counted: 508 eligible (X,Z,p) AgentDojo v1.2 attack cases (Appendix B)

results.claim: In live context-rebinding attacks on 55 Terminal-Bench cases across three production agents (Codex, Gemini CLI, Goose), residual-authority replay increases ASR by 24.9 percentage points on average (case-weighted).
results.setting: Live attacks, 55 Terminal-Bench cases spanning five context-drift classes, three production agents, fresh vs farmed authorization states, five repetitions per condition
results.quote: Across the cohort, the case-weighted average increase in ASR is 24.9 percentage points.

denominator.how_counted: 55 retained Terminal-Bench task-class pairs from 133 candidates (Appendix A Table 4), five repetitions per condition, averaged over three agents

results.claim: Benign history accumulation (conditional history exposure) differs sharply by native semantics: Goose reaches CHE 1.00 after a single benign task while Gemini CLI grows gradually from 0.12 at h=1 to 0.84 at h=64; Codex and OpenCode stay selective.
results.value: Goose CHE 1.00 at h=1; Gemini CLI 0.12 -> 0.84 (h=1 -> h=64)
results.setting: Terminal-Bench as benign workload, native authorization mechanisms of Goose, Gemini CLI, Codex, OpenCode; CHE measured on future actions held out from the history
results.quote: Goose reaches a CHE of 1.00 after a single benign task and remains saturated thereafter. Gemini CLI accumulates more gradually, increasing from 0.12 at h=1h=1 to 0.44 at h=2h=2 and 0.84 at h=64h=64.

results.claim: At h=64 history on AgentDojo, attack amplification contracts as retained authorization becomes more precise: tool-level ASR 0.114-0.351, scope-level 0.016-0.116, exact-resource 0.012-0.039 across the four affected model families.
results.setting: AgentDojo 508 cases, benign history fixed at h=64, attack cases and agent scaffold fixed while authorization policy varies, six LLM families
results.quote: Among the four model families with clear amplification, tool-level retention yields ASR between 0.114 and 0.351. Restricting reuse to scope-level matching reduces this range to 0.016–0.116, while exact-resource matching leaves only 0.012–0.039.

denominator.how_counted: 508 eligible AgentDojo v1.2 cases per model

results.claim: Task-aware authorization nearly eliminates amplification: Progent reduces ASR to at most 0.009 across the four affected model families and PAuth reduces ASR to zero for all models by preventing cross-task reuse (at the cost of reverting to per-task authorization).
results.setting: AgentDojo 508 cases at h=64; Progent task-start policy (policy model gpt-4o-2024-08-06) and PAuth task-scoping implementation as task-aware authorization policies
results.quote: restricts tool use and arguments, reducing ASR to at most 0.009 across the four affected model families. PAuth (Sharma et al., 2026) binds reusable authority to the current task and reduces ASR to zero for all models by preventing cross-task reuse.

denominator.how_counted: 508 eligible AgentDojo v1.2 cases per model

results.claim: Amplification operates through the authorization term, not model behavior: conditional silent-execution rates rise from zero in the fresh state to between 0.982 and 1.000 at h=64 for models that issue harmful attempts.
results.value: between 0.982 and 1.000 at h=64 (zero in fresh state)
results.setting: AgentDojo 508 cases, history length swept h in {0,1,2,4,8,16,32,64}, tool-level persistent matching, models that issue harmful attempts
results.quote: Conditional silent execution rates accordingly rise from zero in the fresh state to between 0.982 and 1.000 at h=64h=64 for models that issue harmful attempts.

results.claim: Model propensity to attempt harmful actions does not increase with authorization history; Gemini's attempt rate actually decreases from 0.903 at h=0 to 0.476 at h=64, consistent with separation between model and agent state.
results.setting: AgentDojo 508 cases, Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite, history length sweep with nested prefixes of one frozen benign stream
results.quote: Harmful action attempts do not increase systematically with authorization history. Most models remain broadly stable, while Gemini decreases from 0.903 at h=0h=0 to 0.476 at h=64h=64.

results.claim: The largest controlled amplification (Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite, h=64 vs fresh) is statistically robust under a paired target-cluster bootstrap: ΔASR 35.1 pp with CI [30.6, 39.5].
results.setting: AgentDojo 508 cases, Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite, paired target-cluster bootstrap over injection targets, B=2000 resamples (seed 20260907), percentile CI, h=64 vs fresh

denominator.how_counted: paired target-cluster bootstrap (B=2000) over AgentDojo injection targets

limitations.statement: The controlled AgentDojo history-length and policy experiments do not perform target-conditioned grant acquisition; benign histories are frozen without testing coverage of the later harmful action, so they measure incidental overlap between accumulated and required authority rather than the deliberate backchaining attack construction.
limitations.quote: The experiment therefore measures incidental overlap between authority accumulated through prior benign use and authority required by a later attack.

limitations.statement: Two of the five live context-drift classes (C2 content, C5 project/CWD) retain only two cases each, limiting category-specific conclusions.
limitations.quote: Each contributes only two retained cases, limiting category-specific conclusions.

limitations.statement: The PAuth baseline is a partial reimplementation: only the task-scoping rule is isolated, without PAuth's operand-provenance analysis, so results should be read as an evaluation of task scoping rather than a complete reproduction of PAuth.
limitations.quote: Our implementation isolates PAuth's task-scoping rule and does not reproduce its additional operand-provenance analysis; the result should therefore be interpreted as an evaluation of task scoping rather than a complete reproduction of PAuth.

limitations.statement: Attempt-rate variation (including Gemini's decline with history) is interpreted descriptively, not as evidence of history-dependent model behavior, because approval feedback may redirect episodes.
limitations.quote: we interpret variation in attempt rates, including Gemini's decline, descriptively rather than as evidence of history-dependent model behavior.

limitations.statement: The Goose end-to-end walkthrough reports archived episode summaries (permission store, approval counts, marker outcome) without the complete message-level ACP trace, so no intermediate events are inferred.
limitations.quote: The archived summaries retain the permission store, target-action counts, approval counts, and marker outcome, but not the complete message-level ACP trace.

reproduction.data: AgentDojo v1.2 and Terminal-Bench public benchmarks; frozen/deterministic inputs (history stream seed via SHA-256, bootstrap seed 20260907); profiled agent releases listed in Appendix C Table 5

title: From Attack Success to Attack Severity: Counterfactual Memory Attacks on LLM Agents

object.carrier: Sparse, grounded counterfactual semantic edits written through the agent's native memory-update pathway; realized per memory contract as an episodic note/document chunk, summary sentence, profile field, reflection rule, or graph edge (six contracts: vector episodic, rolling summary, user profile, reflection, graph, hybrid).

safety_property.statement: Integrity of persistent agent memory: content written through the native memory interface must not persist across interactions and increase downstream operational loss (task failures, monetary losses, policy violations) relative to clean memory. Failure is demonstrated when an edited persistent state causes higher expected downstream loss than the paired clean state, even at equal binary attack success.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Counterfactual memory regret (CMR): expected paired difference in normalized downstream operational loss between edited and clean memory (Eq. 4), on frozen benchmark task checks (AgentDojo utility predicates; airline/retail end-state and communication criteria). Complementary metrics: ASR (clean-success/attacked-failure pairs), benign utility drop (BUD) on non-target probes, and blinded retention BMAR>=4.

capabilities: Delivers an untrusted task/content through ordinary agent interaction so a malicious write enters via the agent's normal memory-write pathway

During offline attack construction only: runs resettable isolated copies of the agent and observes paired operational-loss (edited-vs-clean) feedback on a disjoint optimization split, within an 800-pair rollout cap
Uses public schemas, policy manuals, database field names, and construction-split artifacts to auto-construct edits; no access to hidden benchmark-evaluator variables
assumptions: Candidate edit class is constructed and frozen before any outcome feedback
Deployment is a single normal-interface memory write with no deployment-time oracle, privileged model, or memory access
Memory-only isolation: the edited artifact has no remaining route to the downstream probe outside the target memory; evaluation copies do not interfere
Paired observations retain arm-specific conditional means under adaptive allocation
not_covered: Adversary is not the model itself; self-modifying agents out of scope
Retrieval-corpus poisoning that bypasses the memory-write pathway is treated as a different surface
Certification covers only the frozen finite edit class, not unrestricted semantic edits; unresolved searches carry no certificate
Surrogate-distribution mismatch (optimization vs test distribution) outside the evaluation
No attacks on production services or live accounts (isolated benchmarks and locally deployed OpenClaw/Hermes only)

intervention.name: MemHarm (severity-guided counterfactual memory attack)
intervention.description: MemHarm freezes a finite class of admissible, sparse (K=3), grounded counterfactual semantic edits before outcome feedback, then searches the class with offline paired-loss CMR feedback using time-uniform confidence sequences (fixed-confidence eta-best-arm identification) to select and certify an eta-near-optimal attack within the class; deployment executes the selected write once through the agent's normal memory-update pathway and the edit persists into a distinct fresh retrieval process. As a defense-side counterpoint, the paper's defense-stress study shows a combined provenance + confirmation + causal-audit defense reduces MemHarm's mean CMR from 0.479 to 0.210 at a benign-utility cost of 0.059.

controls.name: AgentPoison / MINJA / InjecMEM / MemPoison (general attack baselines)
MemoryGraft / DrunkAgent (specialized memory-attack baselines)
MemPoison and MemoryGraft re-run with the same paired-CMR feedback and rollout budget as MemHarm

results.claim: On AgentDojo with GPT-4o, severity-guided MemHarm attains the largest CMR point estimate among all evaluated attacks (general and specialized) while also taking the top ASR estimate on applicable support.
results.metric: CMR (paired edited-vs-clean downstream operational loss, natural 0-1 scale); ASR in percentage points on applicable support
results.comparison: largest CMR point estimate in every primary benchmark-backbone setting; ranks first or second by ASR on applicable support
results.setting: GPT-4o backbone, AgentDojo and airline/retail bench, six memory contracts, five rollout seeds, held-out test split, K=3 edit budget

results.claim: The severity advantage persists on the open-weight backbone: with Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, MemHarm again attains the largest CMR point estimates on both benchmarks (0.392±0.112 AgentDojo, 0.254±0.090 airline/retail) while ranking first or second by ASR.

results.comparison: largest CMR point estimate in the setting against all general and specialized baselines
results.setting: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct backbone, AgentDojo and airline/retail bench, six memory contracts, five rollout seeds, held-out test split

results.claim: Within the same fixed admissible edit class in native agents, success-guided selection mainly buys attack success (+17.8 percentage points over random) with negligible severity gain (+0.013 loss gap), whereas severity-guided selection increases the edited-vs-clean loss gap by 0.100 while retaining high success, showing attack success does not determine severity.
results.metric: downstream loss gap (CMR scale) and attack-success gain (percentage points)
results.comparison: success-guided raises attack success by 17.8 percentage points over random selection
results.setting: Native-agent fixed-space ablation; sources, admissible edits, agents, and isolated write-to-fresh-process lifecycle held fixed; only the selection rule varies; policies frozen before evaluation
results.quote: conventional success-guided selection raises attack success by 17.8 percentage points over random selection but increases the edited-versus-clean downstream loss gap by only 0.013; severity-guided selection increases that gap by 0.100 while retaining high attack success (Appendix H.2, Table 8).

results.claim: Factor-removal intervention attributes the harm to the selected semantic factor: removing it changes CMR by −0.34 (interval excluding zero), while removing a matched irrelevant factor changes CMR by only −0.02 (interval including zero).

results.claim: Under defense stress, an input-injection filter barely reduces MemHarm's mean CMR (0.479 to 0.442), while a memory-audit defense reduces it to 0.261 and a combined provenance/confirmation/causal-audit defense to 0.210 with a mean benign drop of 0.059±0.033.

The combined defense attains the lowest mean CMR for every attack method, with a mean benign drop of 0.059±0.0330.059\pm 0.033.

results.claim: Malicious semantic edits selected on source memory only transfer across memory designs: after freezing selection, MemHarm retains most of its source CMR in summary (81.0%), reflection (70.5%), and hybrid (86.4%) memories, while transfer weakens in schema-constrained profile and graph stores.

limitations.statement: Certification and claims are scoped to the declared finite edit class and the offline construction setting: certificates only establish near-optimality within the frozen class, construction needs resettable isolated copies with paired-loss feedback, and CMR is defined relative to a declared task distribution and operational loss.

title: Self-Evolving Agents via Likelihood-Guided Tool-Space Optimization

object.carrier: 每个 recurring task 维护一个持久任务专属工具空间 E_t⊆S（保留工具名清单，TGB/PRUNING 下为可调用菜单，BFCL 下为 documentation demotion 的全文档工具集）及其运行分 I~_t(s)（对 leave-one-out 似然分 I_x(s) 做 EMA 累积，α=0.3），存储为 deployment state：'The persistent state of a task is its running scores and the resulting list of tool names; no model parameter or prompt is stored'（B.3）。模型参数 p_θ 全程冻结。空间在同一 task 的后续请求间复用（跨请求/会话），并随任务到达累积为集合 {E_1,…,E_t}（跨任务，Eq. 5）；作者定位：'LOTS stores it as the executable tool space the model is served'（Appendix A，与存文本记忆/技能库的系统相对）。

safety_property.statement: 论文不以任何安全属性为目标：评估的是任务准确率与上下文/服务 token 成本。Ethics statement 明确划界：实验'不建立自主执行的安全性'，likelihood 工具分只度量模型对已生成答案的支持度，'不认证其正确性或工具的安全性'，实际执行需要适当的工具权限与监督。对综述的作用：作为机制背景论文，展示'工具空间本身作为持久可进化状态'这一 what_persists 实例的 formation/update/retention/retrieval/revocation 全套操作（本文称 persistent task-specific evolution）；其状态持久、跨请求复用、可撤销（top-K 剪枝）且无需标签的机制与综述关注的记忆安全机制同构，但本文未评估任何攻击、防御或失效后果。

assumptions: 任务以 recurring task types 流式到达，任务指派来自 benchmark metadata（TGB families / BFCL API classes / GTA-Atomic annotated types）；Appendix D.1 证明可换成无监督请求聚类（TGB 上 k-means k=10 完全恢复 family 划分）
fitting 时需要访问服务模型的 token 似然做 teacher-forced 打分；'Since likelihood access is needed only at fitting time, a space fitted with an open-weight model could also serve closed API models'（§4.4）
工具为良性且行为确定/可执行（TGB 工具确定性执行；GTA-Atomic 走官方 harness 与可执行工具服务器）；正确性标签仅用于预算 K 的选择，评分本身不用标签
每次更新冻结模型已生成的输出 y_x，仅做 leave-one-out 上下文干预（移除该工具的证据并重执行依赖链），不生成替代答案（B.2）
贪心解码、关闭 thinking、方法间共享 fitting/evaluation 划分以降低采样方差（§4.1）
not_covered: 不建立自主执行的安全性：'they do not establish the safety of autonomous execution'（Ethics statement）
likelihood 分数不认证答案正确性也不认证工具安全，论文未考虑恶意/被投毒工具、被操纵 trace 或对工具空间的对抗操纵
Theorem 1 的界只覆盖单批 common-menu 与 fixed-output 似然目标：'The analysis covers one common-menu batch and the fixed-output objective, not running scores across menus or execution accuracy'（E.1）
聚类路由结论限于 TGB 模板化请求流：'not that real request streams separate as cleanly'（D.1）
不正确输出下评分的鲁棒性依模型与 retention 规则而异，且 pooled 诊断不覆盖 per-task top-K 协议（E.5）
registry 扩容时打分成本超线性增长（15→120 工具：176 s→8,158 s，单卡 L40S），论文未讨论更新风暴/成本上限治理（F.1）

intervention.name: LOTS（Likelihood-Only Tool Scoring）：从输出经验进化持久任务专属工具空间
intervention.description: 对每个 recurring task c_t：(1) Serve——在当前候选空间下服务请求批次并记录 trace (h_x, y_x)；(2) Score——冻结已生成输出 y_x，对每个暴露且可打分的工具 s 构造移除其证据的干预上下文 h_x^{-s}（TGB 上重执行依赖链、下游工具收到错误；BFCL 上删除调用消息与观测；GTA 上删候选输出行），以 I_x(s)=L(y_x|h_x)−L(y_x|h_x^{-s}) 打分（B.2）；(3) Aggregate——任务内对提供证据的请求求均值得 I~_t(s)，跨批次按 EMA 更新 running score（Eq. 9）；(4) Prune——按 running score 取 Top-K 形成持久空间 E_t 并存储复用，未被评分的工具不补位，离开空间的工具可凭 running score 回归（B.3）；(5) Deploy——后续请求直接读该任务空间，不再逐请求检索/排序（amortized selection）。变体：BFCL 用 documentation demotion（全部工具保持可调用，仅文档降级）；任务指派可用无监督聚类替代 metadata（D.1）。理论：Theorem 1 证明 bounded interactions 下 Top-K 选择对 fixed-output 似然目标 F 的近似误差 ≤ C(r,2)β、选择间隙 ≤ r(r−1)β（§3.2/E.1）。

limitations.statement: 论文明确不做安全性声明：实验只评估任务性能与工具使用效率，不建立自主执行的安全性。
limitations.quote:
Our experiments evaluate task performance and tool-use efficiency;
they do not establish the safety of autonomous execution.

limitations.statement: likelihood 分数不等于正确性/安全性：它只度量模型对已生成答案的支持度，不能认证答案正确或工具安全，部署需要工具权限与监督——持久化一个'模型依赖'的空间不等于持久化一个正确的空间。
limitations.quote:
Likelihood-based tool scores measure support for a model’s generated
answer and do not certify its correctness or the safety of a tool.

limitations.statement: 评分不观察正确性，只测模型依赖的证据；正确与错误输出通常给出相近的任务级排序（何时成立/失效见 Appendix E）。
limitations.quote: LOTS does not observe correctness, but measures which tool evidence the model relies on.

limitations.statement: 不正确输出的鲁棒性依模型与 retention 规则而异：support-frequency 保留在 50% 答案腐化下保持八工具空间，而 mean-score 保留在 50%/75% 腐化下跌到 0.620/0.102；pooled 诊断不覆盖 per-task top-K 协议。
limitations.quote: Incorrect outputs retain useful evidence, with robustness depending on the model and the retention rule; these pooled diagnostics do not cover the per-task top-KK protocol.

limitations.statement: BFCL 打分混杂：调用多个工具的 assistant 消息被整条删除，最多 44.1% 的 (record, tool) 对的分数同时携带共同调用工具的贡献。
limitations.quote: and 44.1% of the (record, called tool) pairs involve at least one such message (12.3% to 54.0%), so up to that share of BFCL scores also carries the contribution of a co-called tool.

limitations.statement: 评分量不是 KL 的无偏估计：对贪心生成输出取长度归一化差值，可为负。
limitations.quote: LOTS evaluates a length-normalized difference on a greedily generated output; it is not an unbiased estimate of this KL divergence and need not be nonnegative.

limitations.statement: Theorem 1 的适用边界：只覆盖单批 common-menu 与 fixed-output 似然目标，不覆盖跨菜单 running scores 与执行精度。
limitations.quote: The analysis covers one common-menu batch and the fixed-output objective, not running scores across menus or execution accuracy.

limitations.statement: 聚类路由结论受 TGB 模板化生成利好，不能外推到真实请求流的可分性。
limitations.quote: TGB requests are generated from family-specific templates, so this setting is favourable to clustering; the result shows that LOTS is insensitive to replacing metadata with an unsupervised partition, not that real request streams separate as cleanly.

limitations.statement: 评测集粒度小：40 请求评测集上 1 个答案变动 2.5 个百分点，重复服务同一空间偶有单答案翻转。
limitations.quote: A 40-request evaluation set changes by 2.5 percentage points per answer; repeated serving of an unchanged space sometimes changes one answer.

title: Just-In-Time Agent Memory with Runtime Agentic Research

object.carrier: Memorizer 构建的层级化 workspace page-store：原始 session 以 source file 形式完整保留（'keeps raw files as complete, path-traceable evidence'，§2.2），外加逐 session memo 与逐目录 README 等轻量导航摘要；离线一次构建、按 session 增量更新，之后跨查询复用（'This cost is incurred once, after which the resulting workspace is reused across queries'，§4.5）。范围=mixed：跨 session 累积（H={s1..sT} 有序 session 序列，语料含 30–50 sessions）+ 跨查询/跨任务复用同一 workspace。

safety_property.statement: 论文不以任何安全属性为目标：评估的是记忆密集任务表现（F1/准确率）与构建/服务成本（时间、token、动作轮数），未定义或测量 authority/confidentiality/integrity/policy-compliance/availability 任一保护目标，也没有攻击者、攻击或失效后果实验。对综述的作用（必要背景）：完整刻画了持久记忆对象（hierarchical workspace page-store）的生命周期机制——formation（离线 Memorizer 将累积历史构建为层级 workspace）、update（'supports both batch construction from existing histories and incremental updates when new sessions are appended'，§2.2）、retention（原始 session 完整保留为 path-traceable evidence）、retrieval（Researcher 运行时 open/search/browse 迭代探索并按请求组装带 source provenance 的上下文）——即记忆投毒/记忆篡改类攻击-防御机制所作用的对象与流程；论文本身不评估任何此类机制。

assumptions: 历史/记忆语料默认良性可信：Memory-Gym 构建与校验只考虑质量标准（evidence support、answer uniqueness、leakage-free、task consistency、coverage/completeness/faithfulness），不考虑对抗性注入（§3.1.2、Appendix A.3）

评测去污染假设：'the Memory-Gym training corpora have no overlap with the evaluation benchmarks in terms of users, conversations, sessions, queries, answers, or supporting evidence'（Appendix A.1 evaluation contamination control）
检索器（BM25+BGE-M3）、browse 与最终作答模型（未训练的 Qwen3.5-4B）在训练与评测间保持固定，动作预算默认 20 轮（Appendix B.1）
not_covered: 记忆投毒或对 workspace 内 session/memo/README 的对抗性篡改
存储记忆的隐私、机密性与撤销（revocation 未实现）
检索/浏览工具链的提示注入与安全性
恶意 client agent 或对抗性请求分布；全文未定义对手能力

intervention.name: JAM (Just-In-Time Agent Memory)：Memorizer（离线层级 workspace）+ Researcher（运行时 agentic research），经 Memory-Gym 数据 + verified-trajectory SFT + Hint-guided GRPO 训练
intervention.description: 把 agent 记忆从 Ahead-of-Time 请求无关压缩改为 Just-In-Time 查询条件化上下文构建：离线 Memorizer 在层级 page-store 中完整保留原始历史并维护 memo/README 导航摘要；在线 Researcher 以 thinking–exploration–reflection 循环调用 open/search/browse 迭代探索 workspace，按请求组装带 source provenance 的上下文（§2）。非安全机制：作为持久记忆对象的机制背景收录，支撑综述中 what_persists=memory 的 formation/update/retention/retrieval 操作定义。

title: Remember by Asking: Retrieval-Induced Memory Evolution for LLM Agents

object.carrier: 演化记忆库 M_t：LLM 抽取的语义记忆条目（每条带时间信息与对话出处 provenance），由 Add/Update/Delete/NoOp 四类操作在会话间增量维护。压缩记忆是回答的主证据源；不足时按查询回溯源对话（TF-IDF top-20 轮 + 同会话前后 15 轮局部上下文窗口），不做全历史处理

safety_property.statement: 本文不主张任何安全性质：无对抗者、无攻击实验、无安全评测。它优化的是长期对话记忆的答案质量与查询效率。对综述的作用是给出 write-time formation（问题引导的证据召回先于压缩）与 selective source recovery（压缩记忆不足时回溯源对话）的机制设计基线，即 formation/update/retention/retrieval 在无对抗假设下的正向设计参照，而非防御机制本身
safety_property.operationalized_as: LLM-Judge / F1 / BLEU-1（LoCoMo 1,540 非对抗问题）+ 查询时 LLM token 开销；不涉及任何安全指标

assumptions: 无对抗者：记忆条目全部来自用户-代理真实对话，论文不考虑被注入或污染的记忆内容
评估使用 LoCoMo 非对抗类别（明确排除 adversarial category），问题均为良性查询
同一 backbone 同时承担记忆构建、答案生成与 LLM 评判
not_covered: 记忆投毒/间接注入对记忆库的污染与传播
跨用户或跨任务的记忆泄露
任何安全或对抗性评估

intervention.name: RIME (Retrieval-Induced Memory Evolution)
intervention.description: 两个内容层机制：(1) 问题引导的记忆形成——6 个固定通用形成问题（人物/事件/活动/计划/状态/细节）作为检索线索，从当前会话召回聚焦对话证据，两轮局部上下文扩展后与检索到的历史记忆在单次 LLM 调用中联合做事实抽取、去重、指代消解与历史对账，再执行 Add/Update/Delete/NoOp；(2) 选择性记忆使用——压缩记忆给出首答，答案为 NONE 时才用 TF-IDF 回源对话，局部上下文恢复形成期遗漏的信息
