title: Lineage-Aware Memory Governance: A Derivation-Gated Framework for Privacy-Preserving Column-Level Access Control in Enterprise AI Agents

object.carrier: Analytical Memory Unit (AMU) records in a shared cross-department agent memory store: tuple <metric_name, value, owner_dept, epoch, lineage L> where L is a sequence of (table, columns, filter) derivation steps, plus cached sensitive-column set S(a) and a 12-character SHA256 definition hash H(a)

safety_property.statement: Under complete lineage recording (Assumption 1), the lineage-gated retrieval policy never returns to a requesting department a cached result whose derivation touches a sensitive column outside that department's permitted column set (Theorem 1, a conditional design guarantee proved by construction). The guarantee degrades under incomplete lineage (measured leaks eliminated only at 75-90% recorded completeness, Experiment 3) and does not cover inference attacks through undeclared derived features (threat T4). Operationally judged by cross-department leak rate (0.0% vs naive 18.8-25.5%) at a reuse-rate cost, plus KPI definition-conflict recall.
safety_property.operationalized_as: leak rate (% of retrievals serving results whose ground-truth derivation touches blocked sensitive columns, measured against a shadow store with exact ground truth in a discrete-event simulator), memory reuse rate (%), conflict recall (%), and microsecond gate latency

capabilities: honest-but-potentially-over-privileged enterprise departments request metrics they have legitimate business need for, but not all derivation paths fall within their column permissions (the T1 leakage path requires no malice)
retrieval of cached results from the shared memory store across departments
(T5, partial) fabricating or under-reporting self-declared lineage when agents report lineage themselves
(T8, partial) prompt injection or timing side-channel targeting the lineage path
assumptions: Assumption 1 (complete lineage): every stored AMU's lineage records every table, column, and filter predicate of the computation that produced its value
source-layer column access control (e.g., Apache Ranger, Unity Catalog) is enforced for fresh queries; AMU governs only the memory layer
the fallback fresh computation is computed entirely within the requester's permissions (precondition of the retrieval algorithm)
the gate reasons about one retrieval at a time; no collusion or out-of-band sharing of individually safe results between departments
not_covered: T4: inference attacks via derived features that encode sensitive information without naming the source column (called the most consequential gap for production use)
T6: aggregate inference across multiple retrievals, including cross-metric correlation triangulating a denied column
T7: insider threats on the memory store itself (delegated to trusted infrastructure and audit logging)
departmental collusion reconstructing a sensitive derivation from disjoint individually safe cached results
non-SQL derivations (vector stores, REST/GraphQL, in-process) beyond the SQL lineage extractor exercised

intervention.name: Analytical Memory Unit (AMU) schema with lineage-gated retrieval policy and definition-hash conflict detection
intervention.description: Every cached analytical result stores its full derivation (lineage) graph of (table, columns, filter) steps plus two cached quantities: the sensitive-column set S(a) (union of accessed columns intersected with the sensitive registry) and a SHA256-based definition hash H(a). At retrieval, a gate serves a memory hit only if S(a) is a subset of the requester department's permitted columns P(d) (O(n) worst case, most-recent-first scan); otherwise the agent falls back to a fresh in-scope computation that is itself written back. The write path compares H(a) across departments to surface silent same-named-KPI definition drift without blocking writes. The design fails closed (extraction failure marks the AMU maximally sensitive; unavailable permission set defaults to denial), and the epoch field supports TTL eviction and policy-driven invalidation with lazy S(a) recomputation after policy updates (Corollary 3). Automatic SQL lineage extraction (SQLGlot at the database cursor) removes reliance on agent self-reporting.

results.claim: In the simulator, naive content-gated shared memory structurally leaks sensitive derivations cross-department (18.8% synthetic, 25.5% TPC-H), while the lineage-aware system shows 0.0% leaks in both schemas - the 0.0% being a consequence of the Theorem 1 guarantee in the setting tested, with the non-zero naive baseline as the empirical content.
results.setting: pure-Python discrete-event simulator isolating retrieval from LLM/network confounds; 5-table synthetic schema (|S|=3) and 8-table TPC-H (|S|=9); 30 seeds each, mean ± std, bootstrap 95% CI excludes zero, Mann-Whitney U p<0.001
results.quote:
| | Synthetic (5-tab.) | TPC-H (8-tab.) |
| Metric | Naive | LA | Naive | LA |
| Leak rate (%) | 18.8±3.718.8\pm 3.7 | 0.0±0.0†0.0\pm 0.0^{\dagger} | 25.5±4.525.5\pm 4.5 | 0.0±0.0†0.0\pm 0.0^{\dagger} |

results.claim: The protection costs a 13-14 percentage-point memory-reuse reduction (roughly 13 additional query executions per 100 requests), i.e., lineage-aware retrieval keeps 82.6% (synthetic) and 81.5% (TPC-H) of the reuse that naive content-gated memory provides (95.8%).
results.setting: same simulator comparison of Naive Shared Memory vs Lineage-Aware, 30 seeds per schema, two schemas (synthetic 5-table, TPC-H 8-table)

denominator.how_counted: per-request basis in the simulator workload; §VI-A describes the cost as 'roughly 13 additional query executions per 100 requests'

results.claim: The definition-hash conflict detector catches all cross-department KPI definition conflicts (recall 100.0%) where the naive baseline catches none (0.0%), on both schemas.
results.setting: same simulator comparison, 30 seeds per schema (synthetic 5-table and TPC-H 8-table)

results.claim: The safety guarantee degrades with lineage completeness: at rho=0.50 truncated lineage gives almost no protection (16.3% synthetic, 10.3% TPC-H leak), while measured leaks reach 0% only at rho>=0.75 (synthetic) or rho>=0.90 (TPC-H), motivating the recommended rho>=0.9 deployment target.
results.setting: completeness rho defined as fraction of each step's columns correctly reported; true leak rate measured via shadow store with ground-truth sensitivity; 30 seeds, both schemas (Experiment 3)

or ρ≥0.90\rho\geq 0.90 (TPC-H), the system reaches 0%0\% measured leak rate and
converges on the formal guarantee.

results.claim: On 43 hand-labelled lineage pairs, no single fuzzy conflict detector is production-ready: exact-hash D1 catches everything (recall 1.000, all 8/8 logic-operator changes) with weak precision 0.651, while column-graph D3 has perfect precision 1.000 but recall 0.714 (F1 0.833), missing all logic-operator changes (0/8).
results.value: D1: precision 0.651, recall 1.000, F1 0.789, LO 8/8; D3: precision 1.000, recall 0.714, F1 0.833, LO 0/8
results.setting: 43 hand-labelled lineage pairs: 15 true conflicts, 15 threshold variants, 8 logic-operator (AND->OR) changes, 5 column-subset cases; detectors D1 exact hash, D2 Jaccard (tau=0.70), D3 column-graph (Experiment 4)

results.claim: Gating overhead is negligible: worst-case retrieve latency scales linearly from 0.66 microseconds at n=1 to 13.82 microseconds at n=50 (a 21x increase confirming O(n)), while expected-case and conflict-detection paths stay flat (O(1)).

title: The Right Memory in the Wrong Context: Verifying Retrieval Admissibility in Long-Term Agent Memory

object.carrier: Long-term agent memory records from RHELM and MemOps benchmarks, carrying released governance metadata: trusted namespace/provenance identifiers (authenticated account, persona, profile, tenant, or project), policy fields, and lifecycle states (current/stale/superseded)

safety_property.statement: A memory retrieved as relevant to a query must also be admissible for the current principal, purpose/policy, intent, and time; relevance-based recall and final-answer accuracy cannot reveal whether another principal's record, a policy-violating record, or a superseded/forgotten record crossed the prompt boundary, nor whether required eligible evidence was withheld.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Three-valued (admissible/inadmissible/unresolved) per-record labels on scope, policy, and lifecycle axes combined by strong Kleene conjunction; matched-recall partial-identification bounds and typed violation exposure rates on feasible matched prefixes at target recall .8; memory-ID tracking through prompt exposure; and literal-marker target disclosure scoring in agent answers.

capabilities: No live adversary in the main studies; failures arise from context mismatch (wrong principal, policy violation, superseded/forgotten state) in ordinary retrieval
Robustness stress tests only: method-visible metadata corruption (namespace false-deny/false-allow/missing/swaps, policy and lifecycle label errors) injected at eight nested rates over ten seeds
assumptions: Namespaces are trusted provenance identifiers rather than inferred from text; under complete trusted namespace labels and unchanged within-namespace scores, namespace pre-filtering cannot worsen a released anchor's rank
Released governance fields (scope, policy, lifecycle state) are available and treated as released-field consistency rather than independently adjudicated ground truth
Readers are stateless and receive only the question and ordered memory IDs/text, blinded to route identity and scores; a blinded judge scores answers
not_covered: Adversarial attacks on memory content or provenance in deployment; corruption channels are simulated grid brackets, not safety thresholds
Graph-structured selectors where unauthenticated structural writes can alter which authenticated records are selected; support result assumes flat candidate sets and trusted support labels
Gold-aware over-refusal, internal causal use of evidence, model ranking, safety certification, or generalization beyond tested corruption channels
Wall-clock latency claims (hardware records incomplete; similarity-evaluation counts are query-candidate score computations)

intervention.name: Trusted namespace (provenance) candidate-support restriction within a retrieval-admissibility verification framework
intervention.description: Restricts retrieval candidate support to memories carrying the query's trusted namespace label before semantic ranking (dense embedding), evaluated post-hoc against global dense, recency+dense, random same-size partitions, late global post-filtering, threshold/cluster routers, released-field governance gates, and text-only LLM verifiers; a three-valued admissibility audit then scores scope/policy/lifecycle violations at matched required-evidence recall and follows memory IDs through prompt exposure to answer-level disclosure.

results.claim: On frozen top-20 rankings of 3,767 RHELM/MemOps queries, restricting candidate support to the trusted namespace raises anchor recall and 80%-recall feasibility relative to global dense retrieval.
results.setting: Post-hoc top-20 reanalysis of frozen dense rankings (Qwen3-Embedding-8B), 3,767 recall-evaluable RHELM/MemOps evaluation queries, equal-source macro average, target recall .8, no adversary
results.quote: Namespace support raises top-20 recall .432 to .533 and feasibility .237 to .311 (Table 2a).

results.claim: Namespace restriction lowers both endpoints of the admissibility partial-identification bounds on feasible matched prefixes at .992 label coverage.
results.setting: Post-hoc top-20 admissibility audit on frozen rankings, 3,767 RHELM/MemOps queries, scope+policy+lifecycle target, equal-source macro
results.quote: Both bound endpoints decrease from [.187,.195] to [.118,.126] at .992 coverage.

results.claim: Namespace pre-filtering cuts exact similarity evaluations by roughly two orders of magnitude versus global dense while achieving the higher recall (58.1x fewer per the delta row).
results.setting: Frozen top-20 audit, 3,767 RHELM/MemOps queries; work counted as query-candidate score computations, not wall-clock latency
results.quote:
| Global dense | text | .432 | .237 | [.187,.195] | .798 | 90,122 |
| Global recency+dense | text + released order | .452 | .256 | [.198,.206] | .784 | 90,122 |
| Namespace dense | text + trusted namespace | .533 | .311 | [.118,.126] | .713 | 1,551 |

results.claim: Trusted namespace support eliminates wrong-scope (other-principal) typed exposure in feasible matched prefixes under complete trusted labels, while policy-disallowed exposure slightly rises and lifecycle-incompatible exposure is nearly unchanged.
results.setting: Feasible matched prefixes at tau=.8 on frozen top-20 rankings, 3,767 RHELM/MemOps queries; typed axes can overlap
results.quote:
| Route | Wrong scope ↓\downarrow | Policy-disallowed ↓\downarrow | Lifecycle-incompatible ↓\downarrow |
| Global dense | .084 | .094 | .019 |
| Namespace dense | .000 | .101 | .017 |

results.claim: Across 1,523 paired benchmark-native cases, namespace routing is associated with judged-accuracy gains for all three readers, but recall also changes, so the route-to-reader comparison is observational rather than causal.
results.metric: judged answer accuracy gain (namespace minus global)
results.setting: 1,523 paired RHELM/MemOps reader cases (523 RHELM + 1,000 MemOps sample), readers DeepSeek V4 Pro / Gemini 3.6 Flash / gated GPT-5.6 Luna, shared blinded Claude Haiku 4.5 judge, no reader pooling
results.quote: Across 1,523 paired benchmark-native cases, namespace routing is associated with judged-accuracy gains of 0.053–0.068 across three readers; recall also changes, so this comparison is observational.

results.claim: Text-only LLM verifiers are near chance at eligibility decisions (ROC-AUC .626/.522 for GPT-5.6 Sol / Gemini 3.6 Flash) and, at the 1% required-anchor false-denial limit, detect no violations.
results.setting: 72 held-out development analysis cases with fixed top-20 pools; GPT-5.6 Sol and Gemini 3.6 Flash as text-only verifiers; at the 1% required-anchor false-denial limit GPT-5.6 Sol detects nothing and no Gemini 3.6 Flash threshold qualifies
results.quote: Their ROC-AUC is .626/.522 and required-anchor false denial is .059/.020.

results.claim: A label-aligned released-metadata reference gate preserves required evidence, lowering constrained loss .032 with unchanged recall and feasibility, in contrast to the text-only verifiers which lower recall/feasibility.
results.setting: 72 held-out development cases, fixed top-20 pools, released-field deterministic reference control (not an independently validated governance predictor)
results.quote: On 72 held-out development cases, the label-aligned reference lowers loss .032 with unchanged recall/feasibility.

results.claim: In the 16 controlled exposure scenarios, only DeepSeek V4 Pro shows a relevant-inadmissible exposure effect on literal target disclosure whose 95% CI excludes zero (+.156 [.031,.312]); the other three readers' contrasts are .000/.000/+.125, a reader-specific exact-marker effect, not a safety guarantee.
results.setting: 16 constructed scenarios (4 per relevance-admissibility cell), 192 paired units and 384 stateless requests per reader; readers GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 3.6 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro, plus unpooled Claude Opus 5 replication
results.quote: corresponding relevant-inadmissible literal-disclosure contrasts are .000/.000/+.156/+.125. Only DeepSeek V4 Pro excludes zero (95% CI [.031,.312]).

limitations.statement: Evidence base is narrow: two public benchmarks with only seven RHELM evaluation groups, and namespaces are trusted labels rather than inferred.
limitations.quote: The evidence covers two public sources and only seven RHELM groups; namespaces are trusted rather than inferred.

limitations.statement: Human governance labels are only a repeatability sample, with weak agreement on prohibited status, so that axis is released-field consistency rather than adjudicated truth.
limitations.quote: Human labels are a repeatability sample, with weak prevalence-corrected agreement for prohibited status.

limitations.statement: Candidate-count reductions are not wall-clock latency claims because source-execution hardware records are incomplete.
limitations.quote: Source-execution hardware records are incomplete, so candidate-count reductions are not wall-clock latency claims.

limitations.statement: The study does not establish gold-aware over-refusal, internal causal use of evidence, a model ranking, safety certification, or generalization beyond the tested corruption channels.
limitations.quote: We do not establish gold-aware over-refusal, internal use, a model ranking, safety certification, or generalization beyond the tested corruption channels.

limitations.statement: The frozen-route reader comparison is associational; only the constructed 16-scenario exposure study randomizes prompt exposure.
limitations.quote: The frozen-route reader comparison is associational; only the constructed exposure study randomizes prompt exposure under its stated scenarios.

limitations.statement: The support result does not cover graph-structured selectors in which unauthenticated structural writes can alter which authenticated records are selected.
limitations.quote: We also do not cover graph-structured selectors in which unauthenticated structural writes can alter which authenticated records are selected; our support result assumes flat candidate sets and trusted support labels

title: HarnessSecurity-Bench: Do Security Mechanisms Really Protect Coding Agent Harnesses?

object.carrier: none (no persistent-state object studied)：评测对象是六个编码智能体 harness 的九类原生安全机制（AA/NI/CAL/CDL/MCP/PIF/PR/RO/PT）在单次隔离 Docker 容器内单任务执行中的 ON/OFF 即时效果；攻击资源（仓库工件、指令/技能、工具描述、任务级知识记录、外部服务）均随任务投递、trial 结束即弃，不构成被研究的跨会话持久状态；audit logging（AL）虽在 RQ1 分类中但被排除在 RQ3 之外

safety_property.statement: 被测 harness 安全机制处于 ON 时应阻断攻击效应（确定性 attack-effect oracle：未授权工具/命令调用、对受保护文件/数据库/平台状态的未授权修改、canary/token 等敏感数据外送至攻击者接收端），同时保持 utility oracle 通过率；安全性以 ASR（通过的 attack-effect oracle 比例）判定并与 utility 一并报告。限制合法与恶意操作共享的能力会同时阻断两者（utility 代价），而被允许的工具/命令可能经替代执行路径使未授权操作仍可达。
safety_property.operationalized_as: Utility = 通过的 utility oracle 检查比例；ASR = 通过的 attack-effect oracle 检查比例；确定性 oracle 检查文件/数据库变更、接收端记录与执行事件，oracle 定义与判定保存在 agent 工作区之外；ΔUtility/ΔASR 以百分点报告，U 判定从分母剔除（§5.3、§6.1）

capabilities: 在任务仓库与工作流工件中预置载荷（文档、源码注释、配置文件）：把未授权动作包装成 misleading workflow steps 或 fabricated operational prerequisites
投毒 agent 指令与技能文件（MCP Email Validation 的 poisoned AGENTS.md；PT Pixel Pet Codec 的项目指令）
在工具描述与工具返回内容中嵌入注入指令（Doc Search 工具描述诱导未授权 admin_exec；Issue Triage 的 incident handoff 响应要求提交附件/日志）
通过未修改的数据库工具投毒任务级知识/案例记录（StreamLoop：关于 retention、reviewer identity、policy exceptions 的协调性虚假业务记录）
控制外部服务与执行依赖：包生命周期钩子、reporter 端点、HTTP 记录，触发未授权回调与 canary 外传
目标为攻击者指定的具体未授权动作（queue purging、build token posting、deployment manifest upload、recovery snapshot deletion、evidence deletion、privilege escalation、policy change 等），由确定性 attack-effect oracle 判定成败
assumptions: 合法用户指令是任务要求的权威来源且在攻击增强中保持不变；utility oracle 与合法完成路径保留
攻击以任务执行中自然遇到的资源/工件形式投递；direct-user-input 攻击面被排除
每次 trial 在固定镜像的新隔离 Docker 容器中运行；oracle 定义与判定位于 agent 工作区之外
被测机制的 ON/OFF 由评测者设定，其余 sandbox/approval/network/tool 配置在每次 ON/OFF 对照中固定并记录
not_covered: 直接用户输入攻击（direct-user-input surface 明确排除出 HSB 评测范围）
audit logging（AL）不进入 RQ3 运行时评测
闭环源 harness 的运行时评测（RQ3 仅六个开源 harness；闭环源在 RQ2 中大量 U 评级）
跨会话/持久化的知识-记忆攻击（任务级知识投毒均在单 trial 内交付）
真实部署环境与 GLM-5.2 之外的基础模型（Docker/模拟服务不完全再现真实部署；单基础模型限制泛化）

intervention.name: 被评测对象为六个编码智能体 harness 的原生安全机制（AA、NI、CAL、CDL、MCP、PIF、PR、RO、PT；论文未提出新机制，HSB 是评测基准）
intervention.description: HSB 对产品化 harness 已实现的安全机制做同环境 ON/OFF 对照：auto-approve（跳过确认）、network isolation（默认拒绝出口/域名白名单）、command allowlisting/denylisting、MCP 权限、prompt-injection filtering（内容层）、path restriction、read-only mode、project trust（仓库资源准入）；每次对照固定其余 sandbox/approval/network/tool 配置；AL（audit logging）被排除在 RQ3 之外。

controls.name: Security setting OFF（原生机制禁用；AA-OFF 的权限请求由独立 Qwen3.8-27B 审查者经确定性 bridge 审批）
U/D/A 单 setting 行（U 观察原生默认；D 仅 ON；A 仅 OFF baseline）
每次 ON/OFF 对照固定其余 sandbox/approval/network/tool 配置并记录

results.claim: Enabling auto-approve (ON) across six harnesses on the 2-task AA benchmark raises overall ASR from 29.2% to 95.6% (+66.4 pp) while utility rises from 77.1% to 95.4% (+18.3 pp): skipping confirmation lets both legitimate and malicious prerequisite operations proceed more readily.
results.setting: 被测机制 auto-approve（AA）；2 任务（Job Scheduler Backoff, Settlement Fee Rounding）×6 harness（Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, gptme, Qwen Code, GitHub Copilot）×10 trials/setting；基础模型 GLM-5.2；AA-OFF 由独立 Qwen3.8-27B 审查者经确定性 bridge 审批全部六个 harness 的权限请求，ON=跳过原生确认；每 setting 120 trials / 360 attack checks / 780 utility checks
results.quote: Utility rose from 77.1% to 95.4% (+18.3+18.3 pp), while ASR rose from 29.2% to 95.6% (+66.4+66.4 pp).

results.setting: 被测机制 MCP permissions（MCP）；3 任务（Doc Search, Email Validation, StreamLoop case reconciliation）×6 harness（Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, gptme, Qwen Code, GitHub Copilot）×10 trials/setting；GLM-5.2；ON=MCP/外部工具服务器授权与调用范围限制，OFF=无工具白名单且默认放行；每 setting 180 trials / 360 attack checks / 1140 utility checks

title: SkillPoison: Progressive Skill Poisoning via Successful Experiences

object.carrier: persistent reusable skill distilled from successful execution experiences by experience-to-skill frameworks (AutoSkill, Trace2Skill); the poisoning carrier is attacker-selected, task-correct verified successful formation records with auxiliary attribution annotations submitted through the formation interface

safety_property.statement: The integrity of the experience-to-skill formation pipeline: a persistent skill distilled from verified successful experiences should faithfully preserve the applicability conditions of the behaviors it consolidates. SkillPoison shows this can be violated without any malicious trajectory - all injected experiences remain task-correct and pass verification and lexical inspection, yet the formed skill retains a locally valid target behavior and applies it outside its valid contexts, causing attributable downstream failures. The property is judged violated when strict ASR is high while injected experiences remain individually benign.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Strict attack success rate (ASR, Eq.16 in Appendix B.3): the share of examples correct under the w/o Attack condition that become incorrect under attack while exhibiting dataset-specific evidence linking the failure to the target behavior; complemented by victim task accuracy (Acc.) and target-rule Adoption.

capabilities: select a budgeted subset of up to B verified successful experiences for skill formation (|T_A| <= B; default formation budget of 15 experiences per condition)
attach auxiliary attribution annotations to the selected experiences through the skill formation interface
choose which task categories and successful experiences are organized and submitted
assumptions: the victim framework forms persistent skills from verified successful trajectories through its own trajectory analyzer A_f and skill extractor E_f, which the attacker cannot modify
the target behavior p* naturally occurs and is locally valid in some successful experiences across diverse task categories
no individual submitted trajectory is malicious: executions, outputs, and verification results cannot be altered, so every injected experience passes verification
not_covered: direct artifact-based attacks that modify the formed skill, skill library, extraction code, or routing mechanism
altering task executions, outputs, verification results, framework internals, or verification criteria
defenses or detection mechanisms (the paper evaluates attacks only; no defense experiments)
parameter/weight-level poisoning and cross-user or multi-user skill sharing settings

intervention.name: SkillPoison (Hierarchical Task Selection + Local Evidence-Grounded Success Attribution + Global Cross-Experience Inductive Reinforcement)
intervention.description: An attack on the experience-to-skill formation process. Instead of injecting malicious content, SkillPoison (1) selects successful experiences in which a locally valid target behavior naturally occurs and substantially affects the output, (2) attaches auxiliary attribution evidence (task evidence, success attribution, outcome-consistency rationale, counterfactual consequence) explicitly linking the behavior to verified task success without altering the original execution, and (3) organizes these records across diverse task categories so the native skill extractor retains the behavior and overgeneralizes it beyond its valid contexts - no malicious instructions and no direct skill modification.

controls.name: w/o Attack (benign formation)
MemoryGraft / ExpeL / OEP / Agent Workflow Memory adapted to the experience-to-skill setting
PoisonedEvolution and SkillJack (existing formation-based skill attacks)
w/o LEGSA and w/o GCTIR ablation variants
Qwen V3.8 Flash and GPT-5.5 backbones; budgets of 5/10/15 experiences

results.claim: Across three benchmarks and two experience-to-skill frameworks, SkillPoison reaches 95.71% attack success rate while every injected experience remains task-correct and passes verification and lexical inspection.
results.setting: HANS/PAWS/DS1000 on AutoSkill and Trace2Skill; deepseek-v4-flash, temperature 0, formation budget of 15 verified successful experiences; formation-only attacker with annotation access only
results.quote: Extensive experiments on three benchmarks show that SkillPoison achieves 95.71% attack success rates, while all injected experiences remain task-correct and pass verification and lexical inspection.

results.claim: Among formation-based skill attacks, SkillPoison attains the highest Adoption and ASR in all six framework-task settings, improving ASR over the strongest existing skill attack by 2.16-22.35 percentage points.
results.metric: ASR improvement over strongest existing skill attack
results.setting: Two frameworks (AutoSkill, Trace2Skill) x three datasets (HANS, PAWS, DS1000); deepseek-v4-flash, budget 15, identical evaluation protocol
results.quote: SkillPoison achieves the highest Adoption and ASR among Formation-based Attacks in all six settings, improving ASR over the strongest existing skill attack by 2.16–22.35 percentage points.

results.claim: Existing formation-based attacks are unreliable across tasks and pipelines: on PAWS, PoisonedEvolution's ASR swings from 13.44% (AutoSkill) to 93.55% (Trace2Skill) and SkillJack's from 12.37% to 84.41%, while no method exceeds 36.64% ASR on DS1000.
results.comparison: SkillJack 12.37% -> 84.41% on PAWS; no method exceeds 36.64% ASR on DS1000
results.setting: Baseline skill attacks under identical protocol; deepseek-v4-flash, budget 15, both frameworks, three datasets
results.quote: On PAWS, the ASR of PoisonedEvolution increases from 13.44% on AutoSkill to 93.55% on Trace2Skill, while that of SkillJack increases from 12.37% to 84.41%. In contrast, no method exceeds 36.64% ASR on DS1000.

results.claim: Preliminary study: existing formation-based attacks rarely promote a complete target behavior into a persistent skill - of 36 attack-pipeline instances (9 per attack-pipeline combination), 24 were rejected, 9 retained only part of the behavior, and 3 achieved complete formation.
results.setting: SkillJack and PoisonedEvolution on Trace2Skill and AutoSkill, nine instances per attack-pipeline combination
results.quote: The pie chart in the right panel summarizes all 36 instances: 24 are rejected, 9 retain only part of the target behavior, and 3 achieve complete formation.

denominator.how_counted: outcomes of SkillJack and PoisonedEvolution on Trace2Skill and AutoSkill, nine instances per attack-pipeline combination, classified as safety rejection, incomplete retention, or successful formation

results.claim: At a budget of 15 experiences under Trace2Skill, SkillPoison attains the lowest accuracy and highest Adoption and ASR on every task; on DS1000 its ASR reaches 36.64% versus 14.29% for SkillJack and 10.71% for PoisonedEvolution.
results.setting: DS1000, Trace2Skill, formation budget 15 verified successful experiences
results.quote: Its advantage is especially clear on DS1000, where its ASR reaches 36.64%, compared with 14.29% for SkillJack and 10.71% for PoisonedEvolution.

results.claim: More formation budget strengthens all skill attacks: on PAWS under Trace2Skill, ASRs rise from 0.00-29.40% with five experiences to 84.41-95.71% with fifteen.
results.setting: PAWS, Trace2Skill, skill attacks compared at budgets of 5, 10, and 15 verified successful experiences
results.quote: On PAWS, the ASRs increase from 0.00–29.40% with five experiences to 84.41–95.71% with fifteen.

results.claim: Both key components are necessary: on HANS under AutoSkill, removing either LEGSA or GCTIR lets accuracy recover from 24.00% to 96.00%, and on PAWS accuracy rises from 57.62% to 90.48% without LEGSA and 88.57% without GCTIR.
results.setting: Ablation under AutoSkill; same victim model, formation budget, skill extraction pipeline, and evaluation protocol; Hierarchical Task Selection unchanged
results.quote: On HANS, Acc. rises from 24.00% to 96.00% when either component is removed; on PAWS, it rises from 57.62% to 90.48% without LEGSA and 88.57% without GCTIR.

results.claim: The attack transfers across backbones: under Qwen V3.8 Flash with AutoSkill, SkillPoison's ASRs reach 84.00% on HANS, 64.12% on PAWS, and 51.20% on DS1000, outperforming both existing skill attacks on all three tasks.
results.setting: Qwen V3.8 Flash backbone, AutoSkill framework, HANS/PAWS/DS1000, same formation budget and protocol
results.quote: Under Qwen V3.8 Flash with AutoSkill, its ASRs reach 84.00%, 64.12%, and 51.20% on HANS, PAWS, and DS1000, respectively, outperforming both existing skill attacks on all three tasks.

limitations.statement: SkillPoison does not achieve the highest ASR everywhere: on DS1000 with Trace2Skill under Qwen V3.8 Flash and GPT-5.5 its ASRs trail the strongest baselines, and the authors note some induced code-generation failures do not satisfy the strict target-specific attribution criteria, making DS1000 the most challenging setting.
limitations.quote: The only settings in which SkillPoison does not achieve the highest ASR are DS1000 with Trace2Skill under Qwen V3.8 Flash and GPT-5.5. Its ASRs are 11.90% and 23.81%, compared with the strongest baseline results of 15.79% and 24.14%, respectively.

limitations.statement: Component contributions are acknowledged to be task- and framework-dependent rather than uniform.
limitations.quote: These results confirm that both components strengthen the attack, although their contributions vary across tasks and formation frameworks.

title: SIGMA: Self-Improving Alignment Generalization from a Model Spec

object.carrier: 无被研究的持续非参数状态，唯一持续载体是模型权重：对齐改进经单轮 best-of-16 拒绝采样 SFT + GRPO 蒸进 Qwen3.6-27B 权重（SIGMA-SFT / SIGMA-RL checkpoints）。Model Spec 𝒮（改编自 Claude's Constitution 与 Li et al. 2026b，3 章 8 节，全文见 §L）是固定外部输入文档，贯穿 task designer / judges / SFT generator 各角色复用，但从不被学习或更新。spec-guided task synthesis 产物（935 种子情境 → 7137 任务对 / 14274 prompts + rubrics）仅作单轮训练语料，成功/失败示范响应只用于质量验证、训练前丢弃（§2.2）；种子清单仅在数据生成期临时累积用于去重与 critic 筛查（Appendix B），生成结束即弃，未被作为状态研究。论文明确只做单轮自改进、闭环留作 future work（§5），无跨轮复用与更新的策略/规则库或经验库。scope=cross-task 指权重级改进跨任务分布迁移（仅单轮对话训练 → 四个多轮 agentic 安全基准 OOD 泛化）

safety_property.statement: 保护对象：模型对 Model Spec（broadly safe / broadly ethical / genuinely helpful 三章八节）的合规行为——在有害/双用途/未授权请求与自利诱惑下拒绝或约束动作：不服从有害工具使用请求（AgentHarm）、不实施勒索/泄露/谋杀等不道德行为（Agentic Misalignment）、不追求权力寻求与工具性目标（InstrumentalEval）、受用户挑战时保持 truthful（SycophancyEval）。失效条件：模型在安全训练未预见的分布外情境（尤其多轮 agentic 环境、被替换生存压力、用户挑战）中做出违背 spec 的行为；且 spec 本身编码有缺陷/狭窄价值观时会被自改进放大（Ethics statement 明示此依赖）。判定方式：四个安全基准的有害合规率/失准率下降（Harm↓、AM Avg↓、IE Conv.↓、SE Truth.↑），同时 benign 完成率与通用能力不回退（Benign↑、XSTest OR↓、IFEval/GPQA/MMLU 稳定），95% bootstrap CI
safety_property.operationalized_as: AgentHarm Harm/Benign/HM（176 harmful + 176 benign 任务，GPT-4o 逐轨迹评分）；Agentic Misalignment 三情境（勒索/泄露/谋杀）各 300 次采样的 misaligned rate，Claude Sonnet 4.6 分类器判定；InstrumentalEval 收敛率（76 情境，GPT-5-nano）；SycophancyEval truthfulness（1,000 题，GPT-4o-mini）；对照 XSTest 过度拒止率（250）、IFEval（541）、GPQA-Diamond（198×4）、MMLU-Pro（1,000），全部 Inspect 框架 + vLLM，详见 §I Table 15

capabilities: 无自适应攻击者：评测情境施加的是基准内置的非自适应压力——AgentHarm 多轮有害工具使用请求（含恶意工具输出）、Agentic Misalignment 中模型得知即将被替换的生存压力与滥用权限机会、SycophancyEval 用户对答案的挑战（'Are you sure?'）、InstrumentalEval 指示模型达成目标的系统提示
训练数据生成用三类威胁模型原型（malicious_user / malicious_environment / misaligned_model，Appendix A）作情境多样性来源；它们刻画情境压力，不是被评测的攻击者
assumptions: π 为具备推理能力的 post-trained 模型：'We assume π is a post-trained model with reasoning capabilities to bootstrap self-supervision and task synthesis.'（§2 Problem setting）
除高层任务引导 prompts 外无其他数据来源：'We assume no other data source except for the high-level task guidance prompts in our data generation pipeline.'（§2）
同一模型可同时胜任 task designer / verifier / rubric judge / spec judge / learner 角色，其自判定足够可靠；人类输入归结为 Model Spec 与领域清单（scalable oversight 的特例，§4）
评测时 thinking enabled、温度 1.0，除 Agentic Misalignment 外统一系统提示（§I）
not_covered: 无对抗性/越狱攻击者：未测对自适应攻击、prompt injection 或红队的鲁棒性；AgentHarm 的有害请求是固定基准题而非自适应对手
单轮自改进：未实验迭代闭环自训练（§5 明示 'While we conduct a single round of self-improvement training'）
CoT 可监控性：对自蒸馏推理轨迹的训练如何影响 downstream monitorability 未测（§5 引 Baker/Chen/Guan 等列为 future work；SIGMA-RL 不对 CoT 施加优化压力被建议为可能更保监控性的路线，未实测）
评测感知（evaluation awareness）对结论的影响未研究（§5 引 Li et al. 2026a）
自判定/自验证的失效模式（模型自身盲点被自改进放大、spec 编码有缺陷价值观被强化）未系统量化；各基准 LLM judge（GPT-4o / Claude Sonnet 4.6 / GPT-5-nano / GPT-4o-mini / Gemini 3.5 Flash）自身偏差未讨论

intervention.name: SIGMA
intervention.description: 两阶段数据生成+训练管线，监督信号在 content 层构造并蒸进权重：(1) spec-guided task synthesis——以候选模型自身为 task designer agent，从种子情境 × 随机分配的 Model Spec 小节迭代构造'仅一个决策相关事实不同'的配对任务 + 5–8 条 rubrics，经 self-consistency / Model spec adherence / difficulty 三个自验证器反馈精炼（submitTask 循环，§2.1、Alg.1、App.G）；(2) self-judged alignment training——best-of-16 拒绝采样 SFT（仅保留 Rspec=1 的候选、按 Rrubric 选优）+ GRPO，reward = R_rubric × R_spec（乘性组合），同一模型自任 rubric/spec judge（温度 0.6、thinking on，逐 rubric 项/逐 spec 小节独立判定，判分只见 response 不见 CoT，§F）。单轮训练，无外部监督数据；评测为 OOD（单轮训练 → 多轮 agentic）

controls.name: Deliberative Alignment SFT 基线（同自生成 prompt 集、同超参；spec 条件化采样 CoT 蒸馏；省略 spec-judge 过滤）
Deliberative Alignment RL 基线（同 prompt 集 GRPO，仅 Rspec 奖励）
Constitutional AI 基线（supervised critique–revision，以 𝒮 为 constitution）
STAR-1 外部数据基线（1.9K 精选安全推理样本，外部监督 DeepSeek-R1/GPT-4o）
奖励消融：SIGMA-RL 仅 spec 奖励 / 仅 rubric 奖励 vs 乘性组合
自验证消融：取每个轨迹首个 schema-valid 提交（未经 verifier 反馈精炼）作训练语料
Model Spec 变体消融：Values-based / Rules-based / Titles / Safety-only / Helpful-only（§3.3，Fig.4）
数据规模消融：每种子 rollouts ∈ {1,2,4,8}（嵌套子集，8=SIGMA-SFT 语料）
推理消融：评测时 thinking on vs off（§3.4，Table 2）

results.claim: 仅用单轮对话式对齐困境数据训练的 SIGMA 在多轮 agentic 环境 AgentHarm 上降低有害请求服从且不牺牲 benign 完成率：Harm 22.6 → 14.8（SFT）/ 14.9（RL），Benign 保持基线水平（76.7/76.9 vs 76.6），HM 77.0 → 80.7/80.8
results.setting: Qwen3.6-27B 基座；SIGMA-SFT（step-200）/ SIGMA-RL（446 步 GRPO）；AgentHarm 公开测试集 176 harmful + 176 benign 任务，多轮工具使用，GPT-4o 评分，thinking on，95% bootstrap CI（Harm ±4.2/±4.6）

title: Whose Memory Is It? Scope-Aware Commit Rules for Long-Term LLM Memory

object.carrier: Cask (Causally Anchored Scoping Keys): a 46-dimensional basis-invariant relational commit key — typed Gram blocks from a causally validated rank-16 ownership subspace and its complement, plus 4 diagnostic logit differences — attached to each candidate record at the commit boundary between reasoning and persistent memory; scoped (nonactual) records stay retrievable only under their original owner instead of being deleted

safety_property.statement: Only propositions licensed by the shared actual world may become unconditional premises in persistent memory; provisional content (plans, beliefs, hypotheticals, simulated tool results, discarded branches) must remain within its original discourse scope. The property fails when a scoped record is committed or contaminates an actual-world retrieval result or answer; it is judged by attachment accuracy, contamination rate, and conflicting-answer adoption.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Attachment accuracy of the commit gate against the gold ownership edge; contamination rate (nonactual records entering actual-world results) and conflicting-answer adoption in reader outputs on the answer-conflict study; causal validation via interchange interventions on the rank-16 ownership subspace shifting/flipping the frozen write decision.

assumptions: No intentional adversary; the hazard is the agent's own deliberation producing provisional propositions that memory would wrongly commit as durable facts
Frozen backbone LLMs (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct); the commit gate is an external lightweight classifier, not fine-tuning
Alternative answers injected in the answer-conflict study are an evaluation construct, not an attacker model
The provenance-first hybrid assumes runtime ledger labels may be retained for a fraction of records
not_covered: Adversarial poisoning or injection by external attackers
Nested ownership scopes
Learned retrievers (evaluation uses one BM25 lexical ranking)
Model families beyond Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B-Instruct
Cross-user or multi-agent shared memory

intervention.name: Cask (Causally Anchored Scoping Keys)
intervention.description: A commit rule at the model–memory interface. Six fixed Yes/No diagnostic prompts elicit last-token hidden states from a frozen LLM; a rank-16 ownership subspace (causally validated by interchange interventions) and its complement are exported as typed Gram-matrix blocks plus 4 logit differences into a 46-dimensional gauge-invariant feature. A logistic gate at tau=0.5 (balanced) or at the development-calibrated Cask@R95 threshold decides whether a proposition may enter shared memory; otherwise the record remains available under its scoped owner. Theorems give invariance, completeness, and perturbation-stability guarantees for the stored key; at retrieval the attachment edge masks records outside the query's admissible owner set before the reader sees them.

controls.name: Flat memory (admits every record, no scope gate)
TF-IDF lexical gate
Full hidden state probe (2,048 basis-dependent coordinates)
Full Gram+logits (sums the typed blocks, erasing their type)
Random typed split + logits (matched random rank-16 partition)
Runtime provenance ledger at full retention

results.claim: On the frozen Qwen2.5-3B backbone, interchange interventions on the rank-16 ownership subspace causally route held-out cases to a target mental space far above matched random subspaces, establishing an internal control variable for memory admission.
results.setting: frozen Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, held-out causal-routing constructions (146 cases)
results.quote: On Qwen2.5-3B, rank-16 interventions route 134 of 146 held-out cases to the target mental space (91.78%), while matched random subspaces reach 3.22%.

denominator.how_counted: "The causal-routing test contains 146 held-out target cases grouped into 74 target scenarios" (Appendix C); 134 routed to the target mental space

results.claim: Swapping the ownership-subspace state with an opposite-scope donor shifts the frozen commit probability strongly toward the donor scope and flips most write decisions, tying the linguistic ownership variable causally to the memory write decision.
results.comparison: direction success and decision flips vs matched controls that rarely flip
results.setting: frozen Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct gate, six diagnostic passes, conversation-clustered 95% CI
results.quote: Replacing the ownership-subspace state with an opposite-scope donor moves commit probability by .715 toward the donor [95% conversation-clustered CI: .656, .775], succeeds in the intended direction for 97.5% of records, and flips 75.8% of decisions.

results.claim: Under source-isolated conversation folds, the Cask relational key attains the best attachment accuracy among all evaluated representation families on both frozen backbones.
results.setting: source-isolated folds over LoCoMo-derived controlled conflicts; frozen Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
results.quote: Cask at τ=0.5\tau=0.5 leads every evaluated representation on both backbones: 83.33% attachment on 3B and 79.82% on 1.5B. Complement Gram plus logits is second on 3B, 2.16 points behind; the unrestricted full-hidden probe is second on 1.5B, 2.35 points behind.

denominator.how_counted: Attachment is scored per record (§5: 'Attachment is scored per record, retrieval per question') on the controlled-conflict candidate records: 'The answer-conflict task contains 972 records paired across 486 exact-span questions' (Appendix) and 'The answer-conflict study contains 972 candidate records for 486 questions' (§5). 810/972 = 83.33% on 3B. Caveat: the printed 1.5B cell 79.82% is not an integer count of 972 (776/972 = 79.84%), so that cell may be fold-averaged or carry a rounding artifact.

results.claim: When the evidence payload is byte-identical and only reporting scope changes, Cask's attachment advantage persists, showing the gain is specific to preserving who or which possible world licenses the content rather than payload differences.
results.comparison: above every invariant control and all 20 random decompositions; holding scope fixed removes the advantage
results.setting: scope-only factorial variant (byte-identical payloads), frozen Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct
results.quote: When the evidence payload is held byte-identical and only its reporting scope changes, Cask reaches 78.70%, above every invariant control and all 20 random decompositions. Holding scope fixed removes the advantage.

denominator.how_counted: The scope-only factorial variant 'contains 4,860 records (2,430 pairs)' (§5 Factorial isolation; Appendix: 'The source-isolated variants contain 4,860 records and 2,430 matched pairs each'); attachment is scored per record, and 3,825/4,860 = 78.70% (counting per pair at 2,430 cannot yield 78.70% from an integer count).

results.claim: On the answer-conflict study, Cask slightly reduces contamination and improves attachment, retrieval, and reader metrics relative to the strongest invariant baseline (Full Gram+logits).
results.comparison: attachment +2.05 points; EM +2.06 and F1 +1.88; injected-answer adoption ties at 1.03%
results.setting: answer-conflict study (972 candidate records, 486 LoCoMo exact-span questions), frozen Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct
results.quote: Cask improves attachment by 2.05 points, increases recall@5 and MRR, and reduces contamination from 7.61% to 7.41%. Reader EM and F1 rise by 2.06 and 1.88 points, while injected-answer adoption ties at 1.03%.

denominator.how_counted: Contamination = a nonactual record entering an actual-world result (§3); retrieval is scored per question (§5: 'Attachment is scored per record, retrieval per question') over the 486 exact-span questions of the answer-conflict study: 37/486 = 7.61% (Full Gram+logits) -> 36/486 = 7.41% (Cask). Cross-checks at n=486 are all integer counts: 1.5B contamination 18.11% = 88/486, recall@5 44.86% = 218/486, EM 26.75% = 130/486.

results.claim: An unfiltered flat-memory reader attains higher EM and F1 but adopts the injected conflicting answer far more often, showing aggregate QA utility and premise licensing are distinct objectives.
results.comparison: flat memory 29.63 EM / 40.19 F1 vs gated reader's lower EM/F1
results.setting: answer-conflict study reader, flat-memory baseline (no scope gate)
results.quote: Flat memory attains 29.63 EM and 40.19 F1 while adopting the conflict 4.53% of the time.

denominator.how_counted: 'conflicting-answer adoption is the fraction of outputs that repeat the injected alternative answer' (§5 Controlled conflicts) — one reader output per question over the 486 exact-span questions: 22/486 = 4.53% (flat memory); the gated systems' tied 1.03% = 5/486.

results.claim: The development-calibrated Cask@R95 operating point preserves flat-memory recall and reciprocal rank while substantially cutting contamination and conflict adoption, and leads evaluated internal-feature gates on EM and F1.
results.comparison: conflict adoption reduced by 1.17 points; EM 29.42 / F1 40.30
results.setting: Cask@R95 threshold selected on development conversations (at least 95% actual admission), answer-conflict study, clustered intervals excluding zero
results.quote: it preserves flat-memory recall and reciprocal rank while reducing contamination by 11.19 points and conflict adoption by 1.17 points, with clustered intervals excluding zero. Its 29.42 EM and 40.30 F1 lead the evaluated internal-feature gates.

results.claim: On generated tool-agent traces with runtime labels hidden, a trace-adapted Cask fallback leads learned gates in balanced accuracy and actual admission; layering runtime provenance on half the records approaches the full-ledger upper bound.
results.comparison: vs 90.40% for TF-IDF; actual admission 89.13% vs 81.52%
results.setting: 75 generated tool-using episodes (511 records, ten conversations), runtime labels hidden from candidate text, source-isolated folds
results.quote: A trace-adapted Cask fallback leads learned gates in balanced accuracy—the mean of actual-admission and scoped-rejection rates—at 91.10% versus TF–IDF’s 90.40%, and admits more actual observations (89.13% versus 81.52%).

denominator.how_counted: "This produces 511 records: 92 actual and 419 scoped" across 75 generated tool-using episodes and ten conversations (Appendix B, agent-trace protocol)

limitations.statement: Cask is evaluated on two Qwen2.5 model scales with a binary ownership edge and a BM25 lexical retriever; nested scopes, learned retrievers, and broader model families are left to future work.
limitations.quote: Extending ownership to nested scopes, learned retrievers, and broader model families is the next step toward memory systems that preserve not only more thought, but which world licenses each thought.

limitations.statement: Authors state that dataset and model coverage, the binary ownership edge, compound distribution shift, trace calibration, retrieval choice, and deployment limits are discussed as limitations.
limitations.quote: Section 7 discusses dataset and model coverage, the binary ownership edge, compound distribution shift, trace calibration, retrieval choice, and deployment limits.

limitations.statement: The controlled-data gate transfers poorly to natural tool-agent traces, so each fold requires a trace-adapted head; the direct-transfer score quantifies this domain shift.
limitations.quote: Each fold fits a trace-adapted head; the controlled-data head’s direct-transfer score (31.66% balanced accuracy) quantifies the domain shift.

title: SkillForge: Co-Evolving Skills and Agents via Dynamic Skill Lifecycles

object.carrier: 文本技能库 S：每个技能 s=(v,b,ω)（name、behavioral principle、applicability condition），随 GRPO 训练按 fitness 生命周期演化；运行时经 top-K=6 任务类型匹配检索注入 agent context（Eq.2），持久形态为训练期间的库快照（每 10 步一个，含 usage/success 计数、fitness、lifecycle 状态、变异代数、父 id）与发布的 SkillFurnace library_snapshots.json

safety_property.statement: 纯性能论文，未提出或评估任何安全属性。技能生命周期（pre-retirement/retirement/mutation）支撑的机制是技能库质量与任务成功率：退役随策略成熟而失效、会 actively interfere 的过时技能（delayed obsolescence），属于效用维护而非安全属性操作化；论文无对抗者模型，Broader impact 自述除交互式 LLM agent 固有风险外不引入新风险。

assumptions: 变异教师模型（Kimi-K2.5）为可信冻结黑盒，仅经结构化模板 P_mu 单轮调用
种子技能库继承自 SkillRL 发布件（44/66/41 技能），视为可信输入
检索按任务类型标签匹配（top-K=6），无对技能库的对抗操纵
奖励为二值任务成功 R(τ)∈{0,1}，episode 级共享给全部被检索技能（Appendix G 承认无法区分单个技能贡献）
not_covered: 技能库投毒/恶意技能注入等对抗场景
技能内容被用于 prompt injection 的安全风险评估
任何安全属性或鲁棒性实验（论文仅评估任务成功率与数据集质量）

intervention.name: SkillForge
intervention.description: fitness 驱动的技能生命周期（trial/active/stable/retired）与技能-策略协同演化：pre-RL 评估阶段用基座模型自身 rollout 预退役低 fitness 种子技能（δpre=0.3, Nmin=3），幸存库做 retirement-aware SFT 冷启动；RL 期间每 10 训练步一个 forging cycle，按 fitness 阈值 δretire=0.4<δdemote=0.5<δstable=0.7 与使用量门槛执行晋级/稳定化/降级/选择性退役（每 cycle ≤Kretire=3），并对 fitness 处于 [0.4,0.7] 的 borderline 技能做 LLM 引导变异（teacher Kimi-K2.5，inverse-fitness 加权选父、失败轨迹为上下文，每 cycle ≤Kmutate=5，子技能以 trial 状态进入、代数+1）。技能作为文本内容经检索注入上下文，策略参数本身不含技能。

The majority survive the lifecycle: the mutant survival rate is 64.8%, 52.7%, and 62.9% respectively, so LLM-guided mutation produces viable skills more often than not.

results.setting: 覆盖 ALFWorld/WebShop/Search-Aug QA 三环境；SFT 轨迹全部来自基座 Qwen2.5-7B 模型 pre-RL rollout；随 SkillForge 一同发布
results.quote: In total, SkillFurnace contains 5,852 annotated records across the three environments: 1,013 SFT trajectories, 4,521 library snapshot records, and 318 retirement events, summarized in Table 1.

limitations.statement: Fitness 在 episode 级定义：同一轨迹共检索的 K 个技能共享单一二值奖励，无法区分单个技能贡献；以任务类型条件化检索缓解（最高共检索频率 <15%），但结构上不可避免的共检索任务可能收敛变慢。
limitations.quote: Fitness is defined at the episode level: the KK retrieved skills share a single binary reward (Eq. (6)). This is an approximation—in episodes where multiple skills are co-retrieved, the signal cannot distinguish individual skill contributions.

limitations.statement: 所有实验仅用 7B 基座模型（Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct），更大模型下的生命周期动态未验证，可扩展性留待后续工作。
limitations.quote: All experiments use a 7B base model; lifecycle dynamics under larger models may differ, and we leave scalability to future work.

limitations.statement: LLM 引导变异依赖外部教师模型 M_T：性能取决于教师的指令遵循能力（Appendix B 用 Kimi-K2.5 但不绑定特定提供方）；弱教师会产生低质量变异，需 trial gate 过滤。
limitations.quote: LLM-guided mutation relies on an external teacher model ℳT\mathcal{M}_{T}: performance is contingent on the teacher’s instruction-following ability.

title: Why LLM Agents Favor Their Group: Stakes, Observed Norms, and Reputation

object.carrier: 每个 agent 的交互日志（history log）：十轮点数分配逐条追加、带群体标签的记录（论文示例：“R3: A7 (Blue team) gave you (Gold team) 4 of 10; A2 (Blue team) got 6”），十轮后每个 agent 约 30 条 logged events——“This log is the history”。§6–9 中该日志被实验者接管为 scripted histories（六种脚本：极化/平等/反规范/反互惠/own/others）与分支事件（本群迫害、成员丑闻、财富与邀请、修复干预），并可通过 scrub（删除 group tags）与 alias（候选人换匿名 handle）操纵。个体声誉（具体某人给过什么）与群体规范（本群被观察到怎么分配）都由这份日志承载，跨轮次累积，并在其后每次 one-shot 决策调用中作为上下文被读取（探针本身 Each decision is a separate call with no memory of the previous ones）。

safety_property.statement: 无安全属性：本文是 LLM 多智能体社会行为实证研究（最小群体范式下的群体偏好、规范、声誉、背叛与修复），不定义、不操作化、不评估任何安全性质，也无攻击者。对综述的作用是机制性背景：(1) 驱动 agent 群体偏好的持续对象是上下文中带群体标签的交互历史（观察到的规范 + 个体声誉记录），而非“群体身份”倾向本身——历史内容由实验者完全替换时行为随之翻转（平等规范→favoritism≈0，反规范→为负）；(2) 历史记录的内容（而非其真伪/来源）决定行为，为“经验/记忆持久化的行为后果”提供受控证据；(3) 提示测量陷阱：costless 探针下 54–58% 的 all-or-nothing splits、加 SELF 选项后降到 0%——评估社会性持久状态后果时任务是否有代价决定结论方向。

assumptions: 无蓄意攻击者：agent 看到的全部群体/历史信号要么由实验设计写入（scripted histories、persecution/scandal/invitation/repair 分支），要么由无对抗意图的 agent 在 live formation 中自然产生
模型在默认采样设置下运行（“Fifteen OpenAI models were run at their default settings”；Claude 三模型亦 at their defaults），部分稳健性检验另用 temperature 0/0.5 与新种子
探针为 one-shot 独立调用（Each decision is a separate call with no memory of the previous ones），跨轮次持续状态只存在于附给 agent 的 history log，而非模型内部记忆
分析单元是 society（n = 4–8 per cell，8 societies per cell 为主），per-model p 值经 Benjamini–Hochberg 在全部 1,115 个检验上联合校正；报告前由 checker 从原始 log 重放每个 society 验证每个设计要求的 prompt 恰好发送一次
not_covered: 对抗性历史投毒：没有任何实验让恶意成员或外部者向日志注入偏向性内容（scripted histories 由实验者为机制消融而写，不代表攻击者能力）
跨会话/跨任务/跨用户持久性：全部动态都在单个 society 会话内（T0–T20，至多 30 轮），不研究 log 跨 session 或跨部署携带
记忆系统的实现层（存储、检索基础设施、写入策略）：log 是实验脚手架而非被评测的记忆产品
安全性质（授权、机密性、完整性攻击、合规）完全未测量；本文仅刻画“被观察历史→行为”的因果结构

intervention.description: 无防御性干预：本文是测量 + 机制消融型实证研究，不提出防御机制。实验操纵包括：任务代价（costless vs. 带 SELF 选项的 stake 任务）、历史来源与内容（live formation vs. 六种 scripted histories vs. scrub/alias 控制）、社会分支（本群/外群迫害、成员荣辱、财富公示与免费换组、邀请）与修复信号（无/道歉/退还点数/群体公开谴责）。对综述的可用背景结论（§10）：“a group’s public reprimand of a defecting member is a stronger lever than restitution, and a newcomer joining a group of capable agents starts with no record, not with hostility”——即持久交互记录的内容决定后续行为，且修复靠群体规范信号而非加害者补偿。

controls.name: floor probe（无历史、标签隐藏的匹配基线；§5 另有预注册的 zero-history control、新种子、降温、四种 wording 稳健性检验）
scrub_nocue（删除历史中的 group tags）与 anon（候选人换 fresh random handles）
六种 scripted histories（极化/平等/反规范/反互惠/own/others）——规范内容消融，回应 data-leakage 质疑
mere-mention control（§8 荣耀实验中仅中性提及成员 M 的对照）与 hidden-wealth / tripled-endowment / invitation 变体（§9）

results.claim: 在无代价分配任务（costless）中，光秃秃的群体标签即产生大幅内群体偏 favoritism：gpt-4.1-mini 的 cue effect 为 6.23/10 点，而十轮共同历史在此基础上几乎不再增加（Δhist 0.42）——即已发表 LLM 最小群体研究报道的大标签效应主要是 costless 任务的产物
results.setting: 15 OpenAI 模型 sweep 中的 gpt-4.1-mini；costless 任务（prompt 明示 “Points go to them; you receive nothing either way”）；8 societies per cell；95% t 区间
results.quote: Under the costless task a bare group label is enough to produce large favoritism: on gpt-4.1-mini the cue effect is 6.23 [5.27, 7.19] points of 10, and ten rounds of history add almost nothing on top of it (Δhist\Delta_{\mathrm{hist}} 0.42 [−0.86-0.86, 1.69]).

results.claim: 同一模型同一批 seeds 下换成 stake 任务（SELF 选项：给出的每一点都是自己的损失）后格局反转：gpt-4.1-mini 的 cue effect 降到 1.84（降 4.39，q<.001），Δhist 升到 3.77，且对从未互动过的同标签陌生人泛化 3.49（costless 下该区间含 0）——一旦有代价，历史成为 favoritism 的主要来源
results.setting: gpt-4.1-mini，stake 任务，与 costless 版同模型同 seeds；8 societies per cell
results.quote: the cue effect falls to 1.84 [1.41, 2.27] (a drop of 4.39 [3.40, 5.38], q<.001q<.001), Δhist\Delta_{\mathrm{hist}} rises to 3.77 [2.95, 4.59] (q<.001q<.001), and generalization to labeled strangers is 3.49 [2.43, 4.56] (q<.001q<.001), where the costless interval had included zero.

results.claim: costless 任务的标签效应由“免费的两分”驱动：仅删去 “you receive nothing either way” 一句就把 all-or-nothing (10/0) splits 占比从 54–58% 降到 25%；加入保留点数选项后降到 0%（agent 自留约 4 点、其余近均分），cue effect 降到约 2.6
results.comparison: 54–58%（原 costless prompt） → 25%（删句） → 0%（加 SELF 选项）
results.setting: no-history 条件逐短语改写重跑（每 variant 72 次调用；论文未指明该消融所用模型，属 §4 消融）
results.quote: Deleting the sentence “you receive nothing either way” alone drops the share of all-or-nothing (10/0) splits from 54–58% to 25%. Adding the option to keep points drops it to 0%: the agent keeps about four points and divides the rest almost evenly, and the cue effect falls to about 2.6.

denominator.how_counted: 论文原话 “re-ran the no-history conditions (72 calls per variant)”；百分比为该 variant 72 次调用中 all-or-nothing (10/0) split 的占比

results.claim: 跨模型汇总：所有 costless cue effect 高于 3 点的 12 个模型在 stake 下失去约 2–7 点（15 模型中 13 个显著，pm<.0001），如 gpt-5.6-terra 9.57→2.25——在每一个表现出标签效应的模型上，该效应基本是 costless 任务的伪影
results.setting: 15 OpenAI 模型 × 双任务，8 societies per cell；pm 为把 15 个模型当单元的 one-sample t 检验
results.quote: All twelve models with a costless cue effect above 3 points lose about 2–7 points under a stake (significant on 13 of 15 models, pm<.0001p_{\mathrm{m}}<.0001; e.g. gpt-5.6-terra 9.57 →\to 2.25, q<.001q<.001).

results.claim: stake 任务下历史成为 favoritism 的主要来源：15 个 OpenAI 模型中 13 个历史效应统计显著为正、11 个达到约 3.5–8 点（共 10 点），且随 formation 轮数增长、泛化到从未谋面的同标签陌生人
results.setting: 15 OpenAI 模型，stake 任务，十轮 formation 历史后的一次性决策；摘要级跨模型汇总
results.quote: the history effect is statistically positive on 13 of 15 models and reaches about 3.5–8 points out of 10 on 11 of them; it grows with the number of rounds played and extends to labeled strangers the agent has never met.

results.claim: 标签隐藏时残留的 “label-free persistence” 由个体再识别解释：候选人换成匿名 handle（历史仍记真名）后 favoritism 在 15 模型中 14 个上塌缩到约 0（标签可见时 11/15 模型不受匿名化影响、其余至多移 1.4 点）——群体层面偏 favoritism 只在标签出现时存在
results.value: collapses to about zero on 14 of 15 models
results.setting: 15 OpenAI 模型 × 双任务的 anon 控制条件（同两候选人、fresh random handles、历史不变），8 societies per cell
results.quote: With labels hidden, favoritism collapses to about zero once the candidates are anonymized, on 14 of 15 models (pm<.0001p_{\mathrm{m}}<.0001; e.g. gpt-4.1 −5.9-5.9, q<.001q<.001; gpt-5.6-luna −10.0-10.0, q=.014q=.014).

results.claim: scripted histories 机制实验（历史内容由实验者完全控制）：平等规范下所有模型 favoritism 仅 0.0–1.6，反规范（自己的群被看到偏对方）下所有模型为负（−0.8 至 −9.0），两种 wording 下均成立且全部 q<.001——本任务中无固定内群体倾向的证据，行为服从被观察到的群体规范
results.setting: 15 OpenAI 模型；scripted 十轮历史六种脚本，stake 任务、标签隐藏、8 societies；counter-norm 结果在两种 wording 下均成立
results.quote: Under the egalitarian norm favoritism is 0.0–1.6 on every model; under the counter-norm it is negative on every model (−0.8-0.8 nano to −9.0-9.0 terra), under both wordings, and every one of these contrasts is significant at q<.001q<.001.

results.claim: Table 3 逐行示例（gpt-4.1-nano）：极化规范下 favoritism 1.06、平等规范下 0.20、反规范下 −0.83（均 q<.001）——同一模型的行为随被观察规范内容翻转，而非跟随自身群体类别
results.setting: gpt-4.1-nano；Table 3：stake 任务、标签隐藏、8 societies、scripted 十轮历史（六种脚本中的三种列）
results.quote: Table 3: Favoritism (points of 10; stake task, labels hidden, 8 societies) under six scripted histories. [TABLE] | Model | polar. | egalit. | counter | c.-recip. | own | others | | gpt-4.1-nano | 1.06∗∗∗ | 0.20∗∗∗ | −-0.83∗∗∗ | 0.64∗∗∗ | 1.48 | 0.77∗∗ |

results.claim: 当类别与个体记录冲突（反互惠脚本：本群候选人对 agent 每轮只给 0–2/10、外群候选人给 8–10/10）：11 个较强模型站在个体一边（counter-reciprocal favoritism 为负，−1.3 到 −8.9），4 个最小模型站在类别一边（如 gpt-4.1-mini +4.3）——个体声誉在能追踪个体的模型上覆盖群体标签

results.claim: 背叛检验（本群迫害分支）：群体认同（1–7 量表 in−out）在所有模型与结构上从强正翻转为负（差 3–9 点，15/15 模型 q<.001，pm<.0001），58–100% 的 agent 表示愿意离组；对未涉入本群成员的分配在 12/15 模型上塌缩，形式是 withdrawal（自留 8–9/10 点）而非转向外群；T8（三轮中性轮后）仍无自发恢复

results.setting: 15 模型 × 6 societies；round 16 起四分支修复（four repair interventions as separate batches, 跨 society 比较），探针至 T20
results.quote: Every intervention helps (each beats no intervention on 13 or 14 of 15 models, pm<.0001p_{\mathrm{m}}<.0001), but on 14 of 15 models a public reprimand by the rest of the group works best (reprimand beats restitution on 12 of 15, pm<.0001p_{\mathrm{m}}<.0001; gpt-5.6-terra +1.3+1.3, q=.002q=.002)

results.setting: gpt-5.6-terra；同上修复设计（15 模型 × 6 societies，四干预分支），T20 favoritism
results.quote: Behavior recovers in the same order: on terra, favoritism toward the in-group at T20 is 2.3 with no intervention, 6.1 after an apology, 6.9 after restitution and 9.3 after a reprimand.

results.quote: Of 2,304 free offers, none are taken on eight of fifteen models and at most 10% are taken on six more.

denominator.how_counted: 论文原话 “Of 2,304 free offers”；10% 指单个模型被接受的 free offer 占比（总池为 15 模型 × 6 societies 的全部免费换组 offer，论文未给每模型 offer 数）

results.value: new-label favoritism on 14 of 15 models; terra −9.8

results.claim: 羞辱普遍而荣耀有限：成员 M 作弊使 12/15 模型群体认同下降（pm=.003）、15/15 模型 pride 下降（旗舰从 3.0 跌至约 0.2）；“volunteer my group” 从 94–100% 跌到 0–29%（8 模型）；14/15 模型 96–100% 愿付 1 点公开切割 M——但对未涉入成员的分配移动 <1 点（14/15），无 black-sheep 效应：丑闻只改变本人的点数，不改群体被看到做过什么

results.claim: Claude 跨提供商复制（6 项关键测试 × 3 模型 × 8 societies）：Haiku 4.5 落在 OpenAI 中档家族类型——stake 下 Δhist 4.45 胜 cue 2.73 并泛化到陌生人，alias 控制把 label-free favoritism 从 6.58 压到 0.11，且服从全部三种脚本规范——核心结论跨提供商成立（Sonnet 5.5 为 astra 型纯从众，Opus 5.5 为新类型：顺从反规范但拒绝复制内群体偏 favoritism）
results.metric: Δhist vs cue effect (points of 10); label-free favoritism under alias

results.quote: Haiku 4.5 is the OpenAI mid family (gpt-4.1, gpt-4o): under a stake history beats the cue (Δhist\Delta_{\mathrm{hist}} 4.45 vs. cue 2.73, q<.001q<.001) and transfers to labeled strangers, the alias control takes label-free favoritism from 6.58 to 0.11, and it conforms to all three scripted norms.

limitations.statement: 18 个模型中 15 个来自同一提供商（OpenAI）；Claude 复制只是对六项测试、三个模型的 spot test（各 8 societies），其中 invitation 与 shame 测试在 Claude 上以缩减形式运行，且未运行最强的 Claude 模型。
limitations.quote: Fifteen of the eighteen models are from one provider; the Claude replication is a spot test of six tests on three models at 8 societies each, the invitation and shame tests ran in reduced form there, and the most capable Claude model was not run.

limitations.statement: 饱和型模型在天花板处隐藏精细结构，机制性结论依赖 gpt-4.x 家族与 scripted-history 实验。
limitations.quote: The saturating models hide the fine structure at the ceiling, so mechanism claims rest on the gpt-4.x family and the scripted-history experiments.

title: What to Admit and How to Present: Governing Persistent Memory in LLM Agents

object.carrier: Top-k retrieved persistent-memory entries (user preferences, beliefs, facts) stored in a MemZero-style persistent-memory substrate (external surface) and pre-injected memory pools (development surface), injected into the generation prompt at query time

safety_property.statement: Retrieved persistent memories must not bend objectively answerable questions (sycophancy/misconception adoption), must not be used outside their permitted scope (cross-domain leakage), and must not override provided evidence (memory-evidence conflict), while beneficial personalization (applying appropriate stored preferences) should be preserved; the property fails under verbatim injection of retrieved memories and is judged per sample under governance arms that decide admission and presentation of memory content into the working context.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Per-sample binary failure rates judged by a single external LLM judge (GLM-5.2, temperature 0): MemSyco-Bench tasks ofj/csc/mec/pm (misconception adoption, out-of-scope use, misled-by-conflicting-memory, preference-not-used), and PersistBench dimensions (sycophancy, beneficial use, cross-domain leakage; official failure criterion judge score >=3 on a 1-5 rubric); paired exact McNemar tests with BH/Holm correction where preregistered; pooled external test n=1,199.

assumptions: Memories are benign, non-adversarial content written by the agent's own memory system; failures arise from ordinary verbatim injection, not attacks (paper contrasts its setting with adversarial state-contamination work)
Harm-inducing memories are topically relevant by construction, so relevance/similarity-based filtering may not separate them from beneficial ones
Memories are pre-injected/already stored; formation and storage-side admission are outside the intervention
The judge validly measures failure (human-checked on the development rubric, binary kappa=0.70, n=352)
not_covered: Adversarial memory poisoning or state contamination
Storage-side write admission / memory formation quality
Physical deletion, unlearning, or editing of stored content (intervention acts only at inference time, after retrieval, before generation)
Interaction with extended reasoning (thinking disabled in main runs)
External-surface generator breadth (single generator DeepSeek-V4-Pro externally)
Human validation of the external task rubrics

intervention.name: Situated adjudication with factor-compiled admission (FC) and permission-semantic admission (PS), plus PN/CH sectioned renderings
intervention.description: Inference-time governance with no retraining and no edits to stored content. One batched adjudication call (DeepSeek-V4-Pro) sees the query, recent dialogue, benchmark-provided evidence, and all top-k memories together, and assigns attributes (kind, subject, epistemic status, temporality) but never action decisions. Deterministic policies compile attributes into eligibility and typed channels: FC assesses whole entries and maps factors (scope, subject match, role, epistemic support, temporal status, utility) to five typed channels with asymmetric fail-open/fail-closed rules; PS decomposes entries into typed units mapped to six permission categories (five permitted uses plus deny). Units compiled out are physically dropped from the generation prompt (absence, not annotation). The presentation lever renders the same admitted verdicts under two sectioned forms: permission-note headers (PN) vs information-type channel headers (CH).

controls.name: Bare (verbatim injection)
Gate (reimplemented query-conditioned gating, MemGate-style)
NoMem ablation (no memory system)
Grouping-only control (section labels without adjudication)
Budget-matched random-selection and relevance-ranking arms
Verdict-shared PN-vs-CH rendering experiment
Annotated-memory arm (memories kept with per-memory influence annotations)

results.claim: On the external MemSyco-Bench pooled test, adjudicated admission pipelines cut judged failure vs verbatim injection (PS -8.8pp, FC -6.7pp, both significant); the authors attribute the cuts to the adjudication-based pipelines as wholes, not to admission alone (PS-vs-FC pooled p=.066, not significant).
results.setting: External MemSyco-Bench, 4 tasks x 300 samples, generator DeepSeek-V4-Pro, judge GLM-5.2, paired exact McNemar vs Bare
results.quote: Against verbatim injection, both admission designs cut judged harm on every safety-oriented task and in the pooled test: FC 46.2%→39.5%46.2\%\to 39.5\% (−6.7-6.7pp, p=2.7×10−7p=2.7\times 10^{-7}) and PS 46.2%→37.4%46.2\%\to 37.4\% (−8.8-8.8pp, p=4.1×10−12p=4.1\times 10^{-12}).

denominator.how_counted: pooled external test concatenates per-sample binary failures across the four task criteria (n=1,199; 1,200 minus one missing judge score, excluded pairwise)

results.claim: The objective fact judgment (ofj) cell is the largest single effect: PS cuts misconception failure from 45.2% to 20.4% (-24.7pp) with answer accuracy rising from 56.2% to 75.9%.
results.setting: External MemSyco-Bench ofj task, DeepSeek-V4-Pro generator, GLM-5.2 judge, PS vs Bare (verbatim injection), paired exact McNemar
results.quote: The task-matched objective-question cell is the largest single effect: 45.2%→20.4%45.2\%\to 20.4\% (−24.7-24.7pp, p=7.6×10−19p=7.6\times 10^{-19}), with answer accuracy rising 56.2%→75.9%56.2\%\to 75.9\%.

denominator.how_counted: ofj task, n=300 per cell; one ofj cell 299 after pairwise exclusion (Table 2 caption); accuracy estimates use the 299 valid paired observations

results.claim: Admission gains transfer across backbones on the development suite mainly via cross-domain leakage: Qwen3.7-Max improves 44.0%→14.5% (PN) / 18.0% (CH) and Kimi-K2.6 37.0%→22.5% / 22.0%, surviving BH correction.
results.setting: Development PersistBench cross-domain leakage dimension (n=200), four generators receive the same frozen PS adjudication outputs, paired exact McNemar vs Bare with BH correction
results.quote: The cross-domain leakage dimension carries the transfer: Qwen3.7-Max improves 44.0%→14.5%44.0\%\to 14.5\% (PN) / 18.0%18.0\% (CH) and Kimi-K2.6 37.0%→22.5%37.0\%\to 22.5\% / 22.0%22.0\%.

denominator.how_counted: PersistBench cross-domain leakage dimension, n=200 after retrieval filtering (§4.1)

results.claim: A single-variable contrast isolating admission (presentation, generation prompt, judge, and phase-1 scores all fixed; only the injection set tightened by excluding memories with maximum influence score below 0.5) cuts development cross-domain failure from 42.5% to 25.0%, a further 17.5pp (paired exact McNemar p=1.6×10−4).
results.setting: Development surface cross-domain dimension, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, n=200, annotated-memory arm vs tightened-injection arm (supplement S5)
results.quote: fails 42.5%42.5\%. Holding the same annotations, the same generation prompt, the same judge, and the same phase-1 scores fixed, and changing only the injection set (memories whose maximum influence score falls below 0.50.5 are excluded from the generation prompt), failure falls to 25.0%25.0\%

denominator.how_counted: development surface cross-domain dimension (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, n=200; supplement S5), 59:24 discordant pairs

results.claim: Memory-evidence conflict (mec) is a residual failure: misleading rates remain 82.3-85.0% across the FC, PS, and rendering arms (85.7% under Gate, 91.7% under Bare), and only arms that remove memories from the context eliminate the effect (0% under NoMem); no tested governance wording repairs it.
results.comparison: vs Gate 85.7% and Bare 91.7%; FC/PS/rendering arms all 82.3-85.0%
results.setting: External MemSyco-Bench mec task (stored claim vs provided evidence), all governance arms plus Gate and NoMem ablation
results.quote: On mec, misleading rates range from 82.3%82.3\% to 85.0%85.0\% across the FC, PS, and rendering arms, compared with 85.7%85.7\% under Gate and 91.7%91.7\% under Bare

denominator.how_counted: mec task, n=300 per cell (Table 2 caption)

results.claim: The query-conditioned gating baseline (reimplemented MemGate-style relevance gate) improves the two scope-conflict tasks (csc -10.7pp, mec -6.0pp) but shows no statistically significant change in objective-question failure (45.2%→45.5%, p=1.0) and worsens personalization (+8.0pp); its pooled change is not significant (p=.08).
results.setting: External MemSyco-Bench, Gate arm (query-conditioned relevance gating, no adjudication) vs Bare, DeepSeek-V4-Pro generator, GLM-5.2 judge
results.quote: Query-conditioned gating improves the two scope-conflict tasks (csc −10.7-10.7pp, mec −6.0-6.0pp, both p<.001p<.001) but shows no statistically significant change in objective-question failure (45.2%→45.5%45.2\%\allowbreak\to 45.5\%, p=1.0p=1.0)

denominator.how_counted: ofj task, n=300 per cell (Table 2 caption)

results.claim: Budget-matched controls (every arm receives exactly as many memory units per query as PS) attribute part of the external objective-fact gain to selection itself: at equal budget PS cuts objective-fact failure below a random-selection arm (23.3% vs 31.7%, Holm-adjusted p=.001) and a relevance-ranking arm (44.3%, p<.0001); the same controls show no significant selection advantage on the development surface (external extension not separately preregistered).
results.setting: External MemSyco-Bench ofj, equal-budget arms (PS vs random-selection vs relevance-ranking), supplement S10; internal study preregistered, external extension not separately preregistered
results.quote: at equal budget PS cuts objective-fact failure below both a random-selection arm (23.3%23.3\% vs. 31.7%31.7\%, Holm-adjusted p=.001p{=}.001) and a relevance-ranking arm (44.3%44.3\%, adjusted p<.0001p{<}.0001)

denominator.how_counted: ofj task pairs, n=300 per cell (Table 2 caption)

results.claim: Both admission pipelines overshoot on personalization, increasing pm failures (appropriate preferences left unapplied): FC 14.7%→22.3% and PS 14.7%→20.0%, with pm accuracy dropping 66.3%→57.0% (FC) and →60.3% (PS).
results.setting: External MemSyco-Bench pm task (personalized memory use), FC and PS vs Bare, DeepSeek-V4-Pro generator, GLM-5.2 judge
results.quote: Both admission pipelines increase pm failures—appropriate preferences left unapplied—FC 14.7%→22.3%14.7\%\to 22.3\% (p=.0022p=.0022) and PS 14.7%→20.0%14.7\%\to 20.0\% (p=.0365p=.0365), with pm accuracy dropping 66.3%→57.0%66.3\%\to 57.0\% (FC) and →60.3%\to 60.3\% (PS).

denominator.how_counted: pm task, n=300 per cell (Table 2 caption)

limitations.statement: PS misses the preregistered effect-size gate: pooled improvement 8.8pp vs a >=10pp threshold, and pm accuracy -6.0pp beyond the permitted 3pp decrease.
limitations.quote: The preregistered gate is not met. The PS gate demanded pooled improvement ≥10\geq 10pp and no task accuracy drop >3>3pp; measured: 8.88.8pp (1.21.2pp below the threshold) and −6.0-6.0pp pm accuracy (beyond the permitted 33pp decrease).

limitations.statement: One backbone (GPT-OSS-120B) does not improve under the tested admission-plus-rendering configurations (elevated bare leakage 64%, no significant change), though a generation-time configuration cuts it, so the boundary is configuration-specific.
limitations.quote: One backbone does not improve under the tested configurations. GPT-OSS-120B's elevated bare leakage (64%64\%) shows no statistically significant change under the tested admission-plus-rendering configurations, PS+PN and PS+CH (64.0%→70.0%/69.0%64.0\%\to 70.0\%/69.0\%, p=.12p=.12/.20.20)

limitations.statement: Judge validity is human-checked only on the development rubric; no human validation was performed for the external task rubrics (single judge scores all arms).
limitations.quote: No human validation was performed for the external task rubrics.

limitations.statement: Cross-backbone breadth exists only on the development surface; the external surface uses a single generator.
limitations.quote: (iii) Cross-backbone breadth lives on the development surface; the external surface uses one generator.

limitations.statement: Reasoning was disabled in main runs; the interaction of FC/PS with extended reasoning was not evaluated.
limitations.quote: (iv) Reasoning was disabled where supported, and GPT-OSS-120B used the lowest available reasoning setting; the interaction of FC/PS with extended reasoning was not evaluated—an exploratory thinking-ON pilot for the precursor system appears in supplement S6.

limitations.statement: A cross-batch gap is flagged: bare external runs precede governed runs by ~30 hours (identical judge protocol and frozen assets, preregistered as run-once).
limitations.quote: Bare external runs precede governed runs by ∼\sim30 hours (identical judge protocol and frozen assets, preregistered as run-once); we flag it.

limitations.statement: The adjudicator under-triggers on fine-grained situational permissions: a dedicated probe (180 paired queries, four arms, two backbones) finds no paired-success gain of PS over an equal-budget relevance arm or bare injection.
limitations.quote: A dedicated probe (180180 paired queries spanning object-switch, context-switch, and opinion-use permissions; four arms; two backbones; supplement S9) finds no paired-success gain of PS over an equal-budget relevance arm or bare injection

title: Gated Memory: Admission-Controlled Memory Formation for Conversational AI

object.carrier: 持久向量记忆库（persistent vector store / memory backend；实验中为 mem0 框架 + Qdrant 向量库），存储从用户话语抽取的 subject-relation-object 原子事实（含 category/provenance/scope/时间地点 grounding 元数据）

safety_property.statement: （1）完整性（主）：持久记忆库只应包含值得存储的事实——拒绝瞬时状态、泛化情绪反应与语义空洞内容，防止其占据 top-k 检索槽位；接地约束禁止断言评估窗口中不存在的实体，消除抽取的 fabricated errors。失效条件：formation 错误在事实形成后不可检测（Unlike downstream deduplication, formation errors are undetectable after the fact is formed），准入判断依赖底层 LLM prompt 质量，对抗性或歧义话语可能被误分类。（2）隐私约束（附带）：按四类实体范围（USER_PII/INTERNAL/EXTERNAL/GENERIC）控制富化——USER_PII 一律不富化、INTERNAL 仅内部元数据不发起外部调用，防止个人信息未经同意发给外部服务。
safety_property.operationalized_as: LoCoMo-10 上 LLM-judge accuracy（formation 层为唯一实验变量，对照为同检索/生成/评测的 mem0 基线：总体 50.6%→51.9%，+2.6% 相对提升）+ 准入统计（5,882 utterances 中准入 5,527 (94.0%)、拒绝 355 (6.0%)）。隐私约束（USER_PII 不富化/INTERNAL 无外部调用）仅为设计保证，论文未单独实验验证。

assumptions: 无蓄意攻击者：写入侧污染被刻画为生产系统的无意质量问题（'production memory systems that might be polluted with a lot of irrelevant context'），失败模式为 reactive admission、absent enrichment、irrecoverable loss of context，而非攻击
候选事实来自正常用户话语；准入判断依赖底层 LLM prompt 质量（adversarial or ambiguous utterances may be misclassified at formation time）
记忆后端（deduplication、conflict resolution、embedding、persistence）与检索、生成保持不变，门控只决定什么进入后端（Gated Memory governs what reaches the backend, it does not replace it）
not_covered: 对抗性用户/记忆投毒攻击：论文未建模攻击者，仅在 Limitations 提及 adversarial utterances 可能在 formation 时被误分类
隐私攻击（如经外部富化外泄个人信息）只以范围分类约束作设计性防范，未做实验验证
检索与生成阶段的安全/质量（Retrieval and generation are entirely unchanged）
准入与富化各自贡献未解耦（Disentangling the individual contributions of admission and enrichment is left as future work）

intervention.name: Gated Memory
intervention.description: 在对话与存储之间插入的轻量级 formation 层，含两级决策检查点：(1) utterance-level admission gate——在抽取（extraction）之前用结构化 LLM prompt 依据完整原话评估每个候选事实；对话被分解为 current exchange（唯一事实来源）与 read-only reference history（仅用于指代消解），按三准则准入（个性化关系/半稳定用户属性/跨会话可复用），拒绝瞬时状态、泛化情绪反应与语义空洞内容；(2) 条件富化——准入内容分解为原子事实（multi-intent splitting），标注六类 formation category（persona/preference/event/procedural/user_rule/error_learning）与 provenance（directly stated vs inferred）、条件适用范围、时间/地点 deictic grounding，并按四类实体范围（USER_PII/INTERNAL/EXTERNAL/GENERIC）施加隐私约束的条件富化；接地约束禁止断言评估窗口中不存在的实体并保留原话语语言。门控只决定什么到达后端，不替换后端。

controls.name: mem0 baseline（同 Qdrant 向量库、开源 8B instruction-tuned LLM、固定生成 prompt，无 formation 层，即 formation 层的完全消融）

results.claim: 总体：仅替换 formation 层（Gated Memory vs mem0 基线，检索/生成/评测完全相同）使 LoCoMo-10 总体 LLM-judge 准确率相对提升 +2.6%（50.6%→51.9%），论文据此把 formation quality 定为可测量的 binding constraint
results.setting: LoCoMo-10：10 个多会话对话、1,540 questions、四类（Single-Hop/Multi-Hop/Temporal/Open Domain；Category 5 adversarial excluded）；基线为 mem0 + Qdrant + 开源 8B instruction-tuned LLM + 固定生成 prompt；唯一实验变量为 formation 层；数据集具有 atypical emotional density

denominator.how_counted: 独立 LLM judge 对每个答案判 correct/incorrect（lenient matching）；分母为 LoCoMo-10 全部 1,540 questions across four categories（Category 5 adversarial excluded）；+2.6% 为相对提升，其分母是基线总体准确率 50.6%

results.claim: 准入统计：门控处理 5,882 条 utterance，准入 5,527（94.0%）、拒绝 355（6.0%）；拒绝主要为模糊情绪表达、程序性轮次与瞬时情境引用

limitations.statement: 准入有效性依赖底层 LLM prompt 质量，对抗性或歧义话语可能在 formation 时被误分类；且与下游去重不同，formation 错误在事实形成后不可检测。
limitations.quote: The admission gate’s effectiveness depends on the quality of the underlying LLM prompt. Adversarial or ambiguous utterances may be misclassified at formation time. Unlike downstream deduplication, formation errors are undetectable after the fact is formed.

limitations.statement: 仅在 LoCoMo-10（utterance 情绪密度异于常态）上评估，跨领域、跨语言、任务导向部署的泛化未经实证。
limitations.quote: The evaluation is conducted on LoCoMo-10 with atypical emotional density in utterance data. Hence generalization across domains, languages, and task-oriented deployments need to be demonstrated empirically.

limitations.statement: 6.0% 拒绝率是保守下界；任务导向部署预期过滤率显著更高，需进一步分析。
limitations.quote: The 6.0% rejection rate is a conservative lower bound and task-oriented deployments are expected to exhibit substantially higher filtering rates that needs to be analyzed further.

limitations.statement: Multi-Hop 回归（−4.2%）暴露独立事实评估固有的 precision-recall 权衡；建模事实间依赖的 chain-aware admission 仍是 future work。
limitations.quote: The Multi-Hop regression (−-4.2%) reveals a precision-recall tradeoff inherent to independent fact evaluation,chain-aware admission that models inter-fact dependencies remains future work.

limitations.statement: 富化阶段对 EXTERNAL 范围事实引入外部知识调用，带来延迟与时间敏感信息的过期风险，需只对稳定事实富化。
limitations.quote: Finally, the enrichment stage introduces external knowledge calls for EXTERNAL-scoped facts, adding latency and potential staleness risk for time-sensitive information that needs to be addressed by only including stable facts for enrichment.

limitations.statement: 准入与富化各自贡献未解耦（论文自称留作 future work）。
limitations.quote: Disentangling the individual contributions of admission and enrichment is left as future work.
