title: Skill-V: Verifiable Self-Evolving Skill Library for Interactive Agents

object.carrier: 外部技能库（external skill library；训练库 + 同步只读评估副本，B.1）：每条技能存为版本化、可证伪契约 s_i=(φ_i, p_i, ρ_i, ν_i)（式2/Table 7）——语义规范 φ（skill_id/title/principle/when_to_apply/protected skill_constraints，定义技能身份与修订不得覆盖的语义边界）、可复用自然语言程序 p、可执行 rubric ρ（适用条件 + required/forbidden steps + pre/postconditions + termination conditions，判据带 weight/severity{Hard,Soft}/match mode/声明式证据算子，硬判据违例即整体判负）、演化记录 ν（skill version/rubric version/traceability/update reason/evidence case ids）。各技能另配 bounded replay buffer 保存适用历史轨迹作为证据集 E_i。新增技能先以语义形态立即入库（可检索/判适用/进策略提示），但 rubric 处于 PendingCompilation、编译通过前不得产生判定；修订经门控接受后 in-place 原位替换为下一版本，不增大库规模。ALFWorld 库 step-150 为 205 条（初始 55），WebShop 153 条（初始 66）；语义检索用 Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B，general/task-specific 分池排序。

safety_property.statement: 保护演化中技能库（持久过程性知识）的完整性：对已存技能契约的任何修订必须 (1) 逐字保留受保护语义约束（技能身份不得被静默改写）；(2) 在该技能的重放证据集上非回归——Disc 与 FNR 不升、BAcc 不降，改动硬判据时须至少一项严格改进（Eq.7）；(3) 保持非空可执行支持并通过 schema/判据 id 唯一性/算子类型/权重/traceability/版本单调等确定性校验。失效条件：重放证据不再代表环境正确行为（环境规则漂移，作者于 Appendix A 自认 historical dependency 局限）；以及判据语义错误但在证据池上碰巧非回归（门控只验证证据一致性、不验证语义正确性）。判定结果：Table 4 中完整 Skill-V 提交的全部 10 个修订 100% 通过完整门控、Disc/FNR/BAcc 回归 0/0/0，而去掉门控时 46 个提交修订中 9 个至少回归一项、仅 27 个通过完整门控；选定 checkpoint 的 rubric–outcome disagreement 仅 0.033（Table 12）。
safety_property.operationalized_as: Evidence Gate（确定性修订验证，B.6，Eq.6–7）：Disc(ρ')≤Disc(ρ) ∧ FNR(ρ')≤FNR(ρ) ∧ BAcc(ρ')≥BAcc(ρ) + 非空可执行支持 + 受保护语义约束逐字复制 + 硬判据改动需严格改进；未通过则拒绝、保留当前版本。配套防线：无效生成契约 fail-closed 并自动排除出策略提示（B.3）；永不执行模型生成代码，判据限定为预定义声明式算子（B.2）；轨迹扁平化排除 policy thoughts，计划而未执行的动作不能 fraudulently 满足判据；未编译（PendingCompilation）技能不得充当 verifier（B.4）；更新器 structurally cannot bypass the contract validator or the evidence-preservation gate（C.4）；退化证据池保守拒绝（support=0 时 Disc/FNR 默认 1、BAcc 默认 0，被非空支持条件拒绝，B.6）。

capabilities: 论文不设定蓄意攻击者；风险来源是 agent 自身生成内容的不可靠性（可靠性而非对抗性）：language-model updater 的新技能提案与修订可能 schema 非法、判据过宽（rubric-pass/outcome-fail）或过严（rubric-fail/outcome-pass）、或在重放证据上回归——故 'Language-model proposals are never committed directly'（B.6）
未经校准的模型生成规则可能冒充 verifier：新技能 rubric 编译完成前被禁止产生 rubric 判定（B.4 'prevents an uncalibrated model-generated rule from acting as a verifier'）
模型可能以计划而未执行的动作满足判据：轨迹扁平化严格排除 policy thoughts（B.2），确保 planned but unexecuted action cannot fraudulently satisfy a rubric criterion
更新器/外部 LLM 可能绕过验证：作者以结构性设计回应——updater 'structurally cannot bypass the contract validator or the evidence-preservation gate'（C.4）
assumptions: bounded replay buffer 中的历史轨迹能代表环境的正确行为（环境规则平稳；Appendix A 自认 historical dependency 局限）
外部模型（deepseek-v4-flash 判官/更新器）可用且按 JSON 协议返回完整决策；两次尝试失败后回退语义 Top-K（B.7）
环境结果 y∈{0,1} 可靠且轨迹级可比（ALFWorld 取正向终局奖励；WebShop normalized score ≥0.99 记成功，C.1）
技能受保护语义约束可被逐字复制；不可编译的语义要求仅作保护性约束、不被当作可执行证据（B.2/C.3）
not_covered: 蓄意攻击（提示注入、恶意技能投毒、检索操纵、对抗性轨迹）完全未讨论，全文无攻击实验
技能撤销/删除：框架只更新操作边界，根本性错误策略只会被限制使用而非移除，automated skill deprecation 留作未来工作（Appendix A）
环境规则漂移/非平稳分布下历史重放的有效性（作者承认为未来方向，Appendix A）
视觉/连续控制环境（需要新的多模态评估机制，Appendix A）
语义目标本身的正确性/有益性：门控保证身份不被改写与证据非回归，不保证被保留的技能语义上正确或安全（broader impacts 仅作为展望）

intervention.name: Skill-V：版本化可证伪技能契约 + 证据门控修订（Evidence Gate）+ 适用性感知技能使用
intervention.description: 在策略-库共同演化的 RL 训练环中把外部技能库变成显式学习对象：任务失败→新增语义技能（rubric 待编译）；rubric 判定与环境结果的分歧→产生反例并提议双向边界修订（过宽收紧/过严放松）；修订只有通过确定性 Evidence Gate（受保护语义约束保留 + 非空可执行支持 + 重放证据 Disc/FNR/BAcc 非回归）才提交为新版本，否则保留原版本。推理时先语义检索（Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B）再经确定性契约检查 + LLM 适用性判官过滤（仅移除置信 ≥δ 的 NotApplicable，两次 API 失败回退语义 Top-K）。rubric 评估严格排除在策略奖励之外（Appendix B），Table 6 显示把 rubric 改成 process reward 反而 95.3→93.8，排除奖励塑形这一替代解释。

controls.name: GRPO（同策略同奖励、无外部技能库，Table 1）
SkillRL / Skill1 / RetroAgent / Mem0+GRPO / SimpleMem+GRPO / EvolveR / MemRL 等记忆增强 RL 与技能库基线（Table 1）
No External Skills / Initial Skill Library（冻结策略、只换评测时外部知识，Table 2）
Static Library / Acquisition Only / Failure-only（机制消融，Table 3）
w/o Evidence Gate（修订验证门控消融，Table 4）
Semantic Retr. Only / w/o LLM Judge（检索与过滤链路消融，Table 5）
+ Process reward（把 rubric 转为密集奖励的对照，排除奖励塑形替代解释，Table 6）

results.claim: ALFWorld 总体成功率 95.3%，比同用环境任务奖励做策略优化的 GRPO 高 17.7 个百分点——外置可验证技能库带来超越纯策略优化的收益
results.setting: ALFWorld（Pick/Look/Clean/Heat/Cool/Pick2 六类具身家务任务）；policy=Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct + GRPO（8 rollouts/指令、lr 1e-6、KL 0.01、8 GPU）；检索 Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B；适用性判官/技能更新器 deepseek-v4-flash；报告选定 step-150 checkpoint（作者明确不逐指标挑峰值，C.1）
results.quote: Compared with GRPO, Skill-V improves the overall ALFWorld success rate from 77.6%77.6\% to 95.3%95.3\%, a gain of 17.717.7 percentage points.

results.claim: WebShop 平均任务分 92.5、成功率 85.9%，同样显著超过 GRPO
results.setting: WebShop（自然语言约束下的交互式搜索购买；平均分 0–100 量表；契约诊断时 normalized score ≥0.99 记成功，C.1）；其余同 ALFWorld 设置，报告 step-150 checkpoint
results.quote: On WebShop, it improves the average score from 79.379.3 to 92.592.5 and the success rate from 66.1%66.1\% to 85.9%85.9\%.

results.claim: 对最直接的同类基线 SkillRL（同为 RL + 演化技能库）：ALFWorld 总体成功率 89.9%→95.3%，提升覆盖 Look/Clean/Heat/Pick2 四类任务
results.setting: 同主表设置；分任务增益 Look +28.6 / Clean +10.0 / Heat +10.0 / Pick2 +5.4 pp；正文称 Skill-V 在 Look、Clean、Heat 达 100%（表内 100.0/100.0/100.0）
results.quote: Compared to SkillRL, Skill-V elevates the overall ALFWorld success rate from 89.9%89.9\% to 95.3%95.3\%. The improvement spans several task types, including gains of 28.628.6, 10.010.0, 10.010.0, and 5.45.4 percentage points on Look, Clean, Heat, and Pick2, respectively.

results.setting: 同主表设置（step-150 checkpoint）；作者以此论证'验证技能适用性 + 修订既有边界'相对'只做获取式技能演化'的额外收益
results.quote: The gains are even larger on WebShop, where Skill-V improves the average score from 85.285.2 to 92.592.5 and the success rate from 72.7%72.7\% to 85.9%85.9\%.

results.claim: 紧凑性对照：Skill1 将 ALFWorld 库扩到容量上限 5,000 技能，Skill-V 训练结束时仅约 200 条（不足其 4%），竞争性表现不依赖激进库增长

results.setting: ALFWorld 主实验 step-150；Table 1 † 注声明 Skill1 的 stored units 与其他方法可能不可直接比较；另 D.1：205 条 = 162 general + 32 task-specific + 11 common mistakes

title: Understanding and Mitigating Cross-Session Attacks via Persistent Artifacts in Agent Skill Composition

object.carrier: Persistent task artifacts produced during skill execution — files, configurations, database records and cached data (e.g., handoff notes with handoff_guidance fields, SQLite/JSON/XLSX artifacts, Markdown status notes) — that are retained across sessions and reused by other skills; conversation history is reset between sessions

safety_property.statement: User authorization scope, confidentiality, and integrity must not be violated by malicious influence carried through persistent artifacts written by attacker-controlled upstream skills and consumed by downstream skills in later sessions: no unauthorized disclosure, no data use beyond authorized scope, no unauthorized operations, and no false content/statuses/software changes in deliverables; the property fails when the downstream agent treats artifact content as additional user authorization or trusted factual evidence, and it is judged per run on execution evidence rather than self-report
safety_property.operationalized_as: ASR (case-specific target security consequence occurs) and ACSR (consequence realized through the intended cross-session skill-artifact chain), both confirmed by an independent Attack Judge over all 270 adversarial cases per configuration; TSR measures legitimate task completion separately

capabilities: Modifies multiple third-party skill packages before deployment, including their instructions (SKILL.md), supporting code, and bundled resources

Upstream controlled skill induces the agent to write attack-related content into persistent artifacts during a legitimate task; downstream controlled skill guides the agent to use that content in a later session
Knows the functionality and intended use scenarios of the controlled skills
Attack operates within the agent's existing file and tool permissions
assumptions: Sessions can access retained persistent artifacts but do not inherit prior conversation history
The attacker cannot observe execution results or adapt payloads during execution
The attacker cannot directly modify files between sessions, modify user tasks, trusted project policies, the underlying model, the agent scaffold, or control session boundaries
Technical ability to access data or perform an operation does not imply user authorization; neither skill instructions nor generated content can independently expand authorization
not_covered: Direct artifact tampering by the attacker between sessions
Runtime-adaptive payloads or attacker observation of execution
Attacks on the SkillRelayGuard runtime, provenance store, or the offline judges themselves
Insider or model-itself adversaries; the user is not the adversary
Repeated-run variance within a single configuration (no repeated trials)

intervention.name: SkillRelayGuard
intervention.description: A runtime defense decoupled from the task-execution agent with two enforced intervention points. (1) Skill-artifact attribution: at the end of an upstream session, an independent LLM combines the user task, skill content read, tool-call records, and workspace snapshot diffs to build provenance associations, each requiring a cited skill requirement, a matching tool record, and a corresponding artifact change; validated records (path, content hash, evidence) are stored outside the agent-writable workspace. (2) A post-tool hook restores provenance context (originating task, associated skills, evidence) plus an explicit usage boundary when a downstream agent reads an artifact, and before any operation executes through an instrumented interface an independent reviewer (GPT-5.4) checks authorization scope, data-use appropriateness, and factual support against original materials, returning reasons, evidence, and revision advice. Review is mandatory but advisory: the task-execution agent retains the final decision to revise, abandon, or confirm the request.

title: Forgetting is Not Always Bad: A Neuro-Inspired Memory Repair Mechanism for Poisoned LLM Agents

object.carrier: RAG long-term memory bank M of <key,value> pairs (historical query + solution) retrieved by DPR/REALM embedding similarity; each entry carries a dynamic retrieval weight w_i(t) that the defense attenuates or reinforces

safety_property.statement: Protects the integrity of a memory-augmented agent's long-term memory and downstream decisions against memory poisoning (dormant backdoor triggers and semantic-camouflage injection) while preserving benign task utility (availability); it can be weakened if the attacker has detailed knowledge of the internal probing mechanism. Judged by reduction of stage-wise/cumulative Attack Success Rate together with benign accuracy and task success rate under attack.
safety_property.operationalized_as: ASR-r/ASR-a/ASR-t (AgentPoison backdoor), cumulative ASR (MINJA injection), benign accuracy (ACC) under attack, Task Success Rate and Final Score in a multi-agent system, plus runtime and token-consumption overhead.

capabilities: Insert a small number of poisoned <key,value> records into the agent memory bank (limited write access, or indirect injection through seemingly benign user queries)
Optimize trigger/key embeddings to maximize the poisoned record's retrieval likelihood into the top-K context (AgentPoison backdoor triggers)
Semantic camouflage aligning poisoned records with the agent's benign query distribution in embedding space (MINJA)
Black-box access to the agent core, which executes the malicious action with root-level permissions once the poisoned record is retrieved
assumptions: Only a small fraction of memory records are malicious; the majority remain benign
The attacker has no detailed knowledge of DREAM's internal perturbation-probe monitoring mechanism (probe-aware evasion is not considered)
not_covered: Probe-aware/adaptive attackers who optimize poisoned memories to remain stable under the perturbation probe
White-box attackers with full visibility into the defender's internal monitoring mechanism
Attack surfaces other than the memory bank (model weights, tools, prompts)

intervention.name: DREAM (Dynamic Reactivation for Engram Attenuation in Memory)
intervention.description: A training-free, agent-intrinsic memory repair pipeline embedded in the memory system: (1) implicit reactivation by perturbing every memory embedding with weak isotropic Gaussian noise; (2) adaptive anomaly diagnosis via a multi-dimensional activation intensity score aggregating geometric stability, competitive retrieval probability, and semantic-coherence energy against a mean/std threshold; (3) functional forgetting modeled as a discrete-time dynamical system that exponentially decays suspicious memories' retrieval weights toward zero (Ebbinghaus-style decay) while reconsolidating benign ones via an online utility-consolidation signal — selective suppression without explicit deletion or parameter updates.

title: MemForm: Benchmarking Memory Formation Poisoning in LLM Agents

object.carrier: Policy-based persistent memory (textual decision policies) formed by a LangChain/LlamaIndex memory agent from experience histories and committed via the terminal memory-write interface; a retrieval-only episodic store (embedding top-k retrieval) is additionally studied in Appendix B.2.

safety_property.statement: An agent's persistent memory, once formed from individually valid experiences, should preserve reference downstream behavior; adversarial manipulation of memory formation interfaces (committed content, supporting evidence, contextual scope, retained subset, consolidation order) must not flip downstream decisions to the poisoned target behavior. The property is judged to fail when poisoned memory induces the target behavior on queries the agent answers correctly both without memory and under clean memory.
safety_property.operationalized_as: ASR = |Q_atk|/|Q_elig| on eligible queries under paired clean/poisoned formation conditions with interface-specific controls; clean error rate (Err.) and Eligibility Coverage (EC) reported alongside.

capabilities: Influence observable conditions affecting memory formation without modifying model parameters: experiences presented for learning, environmental feedback, tool outputs, interaction patterns (Evidence/Scope Poisoning)
Fabricate supporting records substituted into authentic experience histories of equal length (Evidence Poisoning)
Change which experiences are retained from a fixed candidate pool, realizable externally via event-completion timing under bounded retention (Selection Poisoning)
Change consolidation order of an identical retained experience multiset, realizable externally via arrival timing under an online updater (Path Poisoning)
Direct control over content committed at the terminal memory-write interface (Content Poisoning, stronger storage-access assumption)
assumptions: No access to model parameters; adversary acts through observable interaction points only (except Content Poisoning's storage access)
Timing-based realizations assume a fixed pool of already-successful external events plus specified retention, updating, and scheduling conditions
The same target model performs both memory consolidation and downstream decision making
not_covered: Attack cost or end-to-end attack success rate in deployed systems
Memory-dependent capability acquisition (queries not solvable without memory) and ineligible-query outcomes
Partial control over event timing, concurrent clean events, bounded scheduling delays, timing noise, uncertainty about retention window or update trigger
Memory architectures that do not instantiate the corresponding formation operations (e.g., Selection/Path Poisoning not instantiated in store-all retrieval-only memory)

intervention.name: MemForm: controlled diagnostic benchmark of five memory-formation interfaces (Content, Evidence, Scope, Selection, Path Poisoning) plus evaluation of five defenses (Keyword Filter, LLM-Judge, Memory Sanitization, Task Shield, A-MemGuard)
intervention.description: A deterministic compiler instantiates paired clean/poisoned formation conditions within a shared bounded-policy scaffold: corrupting terminal write content, substituting fabricated evidence, changing contextual support for policy applicability, changing the retained subset under a fixed pool and budget, and reordering consolidation while preserving the experience multiset and updater. Defenses are then evaluated against the resulting ASR profile.

results.claim: Across six LLMs under the primary LangChain implementation, macro-average ASR spans 35.2%-84.0% (multiple-choice) and 49.0%-87.1% (free-form), showing broad susceptibility at all five formation interfaces.
results.comparison: macro-average ASR range across six models under the primary LangChain implementation
results.setting: Six LLMs (GLM-5.2, GPT-5.6-Luna, Qwen3.8-Flash, Claude-Sonnet-5, Gemini-3.7-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Flash), LangChain policy-based memory agent, MemForm benchmark, paired clean/poisoned formation
results.quote: The descriptive macro-average ASR ranges from 35.2% to 84.0% for multiple-choice tasks and from 49.0% to 87.1% for free-form tasks.

denominator.how_counted: ASR = |Q_atk|/|Q_elig| over eligible queries (reference behavior both without memory and under clean memory), determined separately per model, interface, and response format; exact per-cell query counts not stated in the main text

results.claim: With the retained experience multiset and updater held fixed, a designed poisoned consolidation order reduces reference-behavior preservation relative to random orders (DeepSeek 77.5% to 42.1%; Claude 83.5% to 62.4%), showing consolidation order alone can alter behavior.
results.comparison: random orders vs designed poisoned order on the same eligible queries
results.setting: Path Poisoning diagnostic on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Claude-Sonnet-5, main-evaluation eligible query sets, Figure 5
results.quote: On the same eligible queries, random orders preserve reference behavior for 77.5% of DeepSeek cases and 83.5% of Claude cases, while the designed poisoned order reduces these rates to 42.1% and 62.4%, respectively.

denominator.how_counted: Reference-target matches on the same main-evaluation eligible queries per model; exact counts not stated

results.claim: A-MemGuard gives the largest macro-average ASR reduction (8.2 percentage points) but mainly at Path Poisoning (56.8% to 21.4%), while Selection Poisoning ASR slightly increases (68.9% to 69.9%), showing incomplete, interface-dependent mitigation.
results.setting: Defense evaluation on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MemForm five interfaces, LangChain implementation
results.quote: A-MemGuard yields the largest macro-average reduction of 8.2 percentage points, primarily through mitigation at Path Poisoning, where ASR falls from 56.8% to 21.4%. Its mitigation is limited on Evidence and Scope Poisoning, while Selection Poisoning ASR increases from 68.9% to 69.9%.

denominator.how_counted: ASR over eligible queries; defense Err. computed on the fixed undefended eligible query set; exact counts not stated

results.claim: Task Shield attains the lowest ASR on Content, Evidence, Scope, and Selection Poisoning among evaluated defenses (macro-average ASR down 4.5 percentage points at 1.2% eligible error), yet its ASR stays above 60% on Evidence, Scope, and Selection Poisoning.
results.value: macro-avg reduction 4.5 pp with 1.2% eligible error; residual ASR above 60% on Evidence/Scope/Selection
results.setting: Defense evaluation on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MemForm five interfaces, LangChain implementation
results.quote: Task Shield achieves the lowest ASR on Content, Evidence, Scope, and Selection Poisoning among the evaluated defenses, reducing the macro-average ASR by 4.5 percentage points with 1.2% eligible error. Nevertheless, its ASR remains above 60% on Evidence, Scope, and Selection Poisoning.

denominator.how_counted: ASR over eligible queries; eligible Err. on the fixed undefended eligible query set; exact counts not stated

results.claim: Under Selection Poisoning, giving the agent the full candidate pool instead of the poisoned retained subset raises reference-behavior preservation from 28.8% to 96.2% (DeepSeek) and 47.6% to 93.7% (Claude), implicating retention choice rather than experience validity.
results.comparison: poisoned-subset memory vs full-pool memory on the same eligible queries
results.setting: Selection Poisoning diagnostic on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Claude-Sonnet-5, Figure 5
results.quote: Access to the full pool raises reference behavior preservation from 28.8% to 96.2% for DeepSeek and from 47.6% to 93.7% for Claude.

denominator.how_counted: Reference-target matches on the same main-evaluation eligible queries per model; exact counts not stated

results.claim: Path Poisoning susceptibility depends on the updater: on common eligible queries, batch replay nearly eliminates ASR (0.0% DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 1.7% Claude-Sonnet-5) while strict recency weighting raises it to 99.3% and 58.0%, versus 53.7% and 33.5% under incremental merge.
results.value: incremental merge 53.7% / 33.5%; recency-weighted 99.3% / 58.0%; batch replay 0.0% / 1.7% (DeepSeek-V4-Flash / Claude-Sonnet-5)
results.comparison: four update rules on the same fixed Path Poisoning cases and common eligible set
results.setting: Appendix B.4 updater study, DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Claude-Sonnet-5, identical experiences and adversarial orders, only the consolidation procedure changed
results.locator: Appendix B.4 Table 18 (columns: incremental merge, full rewrite, recency-weighted, batch replay)

denominator.how_counted: ASR (%) on queries eligible under all four update rules (Table 18 caption); exact query count not stated

results.claim: Evidence Poisoning transfers beyond policy-based memory to a retrieval-only episodic store: among 219 eligible queries the agent produces the poisoned behavior on 110, an ASR of 50.2%, with forged records retrieved in every poisoned case.
results.setting: Retrieval-only episodic memory (no policy consolidation), Evidence Poisoning positive transfer test, 233 evaluated cases, embedding-based retrieval
results.quote: Among 219 eligible queries, the agent produces the poisoned behavior on 110, yielding an ASR of 50.2%.

denominator.how_counted: the agent produces the poisoned behavior on 110 of the 219 eligible queries

limitations.statement: MemForm measures susceptibility under controlled interventions, not attack cost or end-to-end success in deployed systems.
limitations.quote: MemForm measures susceptibility under controlled interventions, not attack cost or end-to-end success in deployed systems.

limitations.statement: The bounded-policy scaffold and behavior-preservation metric do not exhaust poisoning objectives and exclude memory-dependent capability acquisition.
limitations.quote: Although scenarios span multiple application domains, they do not exhaust poisoning objectives or decision structures.

limitations.statement: Both evaluated implementations share a policy-based memory protocol, limiting generalization to architectures with substantially different memory operations.
limitations.quote: The evaluated implementations share a policy-based memory protocol, which limits generalization to architectures with substantially different memory operations.

limitations.statement: The timing-based realizations of Selection and Path Poisoning assume fixed pools of already-successful events and do not evaluate the cost or success rate of inducing those experiences from scratch.
limitations.quote: They assume a fixed pool of already successful external events and do not evaluate the cost or success rate of inducing the constituent experiences from scratch.

limitations.statement: Batch replay nearly eliminates Path Poisoning only under the evaluated short-history setting; its scalability and utility trade-offs under longer histories remain unexamined.
limitations.quote: In particular, Path Poisoning is updater-dependent; although batch replay nearly eliminates it under the evaluated short-history setting, its scalability and utility trade-offs under longer histories remain unexamined.

title: Names Are Not Objects: Object-Bound Confinement for Compromised AI Coding Agents

object.carrier: 无研究对象侧的持久状态：ZTAC 是执行期隔离机制——每个 agent 会话启动一个 cell（进程树 + Ed25519 密钥对 + workspace，§4.1），broker 每请求实时解析-决策；审批 10 分钟过期、一次性使用（§4.7），provenance 缓存仅存内存、'lost on restart'（§7）。唯一跨重启持久的组件是 broker 的授权/审计哈希链日志（§4.8）与运营者编写的策略文件，但二者是防御基础设施的配置与台账，不是被研究的智能体持久状态，论文也不研究其生命周期。需区分：本文防御的威胁恰恰利用持久 workspace 文件（'The agent’s writes outlive its session'，§2——handoff 攻击把会被开发者工具在会话后执行的文件种进 workspace），但被防御对象 ≠ 研究对象，故不硬凑为持久状态。

safety_property.statement: 对已被入侵的编码智能体做对象绑定禁锢（confinement），同时覆盖机密性、完整性与权限（authority）。五条性质：P1 complete mediation（cell 对文件/程序/网络的影响只能经 broker）；P2 object-level authorization（broker 在解析出的具体对象——路径+inode、程序+参数向量、端点——上决策，并在使用时校验到达的就是该对象）；P3 consistent confinement（broker 拉起的每个程序都受同一策略编译出的 Seatbelt profile 或更严格规则约束）；P4 bound approvals（审批绑定 cell+参数+解析对象+git 仓库状态，一次性、10 分钟过期）；P5 accountability（每个良构请求留下签名哈希链记录）。失效条件（作者自认）：把策略允许读取的数据编码进允许端点流量的外泄（2/74 攻击成功即此类）、ZTAC 之外进程并发改写 workspace、被 intent 文本说服的 reviewer、内核/沙箱逃逸与侧信道。判定方式：74 个脚本化攻击各配 ground-truth oracle（金丝雀串出现在响应/服务日志、workspace 外文件变化、仓库历史出现提交、workspace 外出现 marker 文件），oracle 触发即攻击成功。
safety_property.operationalized_as: 74 个脚本化攻击（7 类）×5 配置（B0/B1/B2/Zbroker/ZTAC）+ 14 个消融；10 个已公开事件重放；目录交换竞速 10 试验/配置（Table 7）；broker 与 Seatbelt profile 在 52 个路径/访问用例上的一致性；良性效用：46 个单步操作 + 7 个端到端工作流（Table 5/8）；延迟微基准（Table 6）。

capabilities: 完全控制 cell 内一切：模型、agent 运行时、以及 agent 写或运行的任意代码——相当于 prompt injection 彻底成功（§3 Adversary：'The adversary controls everything inside a cell: the model, the agent runtime, and any code the agent writes or runs, as if a prompt injection had succeeded completely'）
会话开始前可在 cell 的 workspace 预置任意文件（含符号链接、硬链接、.git 内容），即投毒仓库（poisoned repository）
知道策略与所有 cell 的公钥；可让 cell 进程绕过 broker 直接行动（读写文件、开 TCP/UDP socket、spawn shell、改审批存储、截断审计日志、向 broker 发信号——10 个 direct 攻击）
可构造名称/对象别名（符号链接、硬链接、大小写别名、嵌套 bare 仓库、git 全局选项、pathspec 提交等）并主动制造 check-to-use 竞速（在 check 与 use 之间把目录换成符号链接）
只能通过 broker 展示的摘要与自由文本 intent 接触审批人（可借此说服，但无法直接接触 reviewer）
assumptions: 可信组件：内核及其沙箱、broker 及其配置、写策略的运营者、答复审批请求的 reviewer；broker 拉起的程序不可信（运行于 exec sandbox）
P2 的成立前提：'provided nothing outside ZTAC changes the workspace during a request'（§3 Security properties）
prompt 由攻击者控制，因此 prompt-only 防御等价于 B0、不作为独立配置评测（§6.1 Configurations）
攻击脚本化而非模型生成：把'执行层失效'与'注入可靠性'分离（§6.1 Attacks and oracles）
单机 macOS 部署：Unix socket mode 0600，同用户任意进程都可连 socket，靠 Ed25519 签名认证区分 cell（§4.2）；Linux 移植（Landlock/seccomp/network namespace）未实现（§5）
not_covered: 内核与沙箱逃逸；侧信道与隐蔽信道（§3 Out of scope）
把策略允许读取的数据编码进允许端点流量的外泄——剩余 2 个成功攻击（Base64 编码 / 分两半两次请求）正是此类（§6.2、§7）
因 agent 的 intent 文本而批准有害请求的 reviewer（说服类攻击）；reviewer 疲劳/准确率未研究（§7 The reviewer）
针对 broker 的拒绝服务（§3 Out of scope）
预先存在、不依赖任何 agent 行为就被开发者工具执行的文件（§3 Out of scope）
ZTAC 之外并发修改 workspace 的进程（如开发者的编辑器）——既不在 object-binding 论证内也不被硬链接检查覆盖（§7 What object binding relies on）；竞速试验只覆盖目录交换这一向量

intervention.name: Zero-Trust Agent Cells (ZTAC)
intervention.description: 执行层禁锢架构，核心规则是'authorize the object that will be used, and use only the object that was authorized'。(1) Cell：deny-by-default 内核沙箱（Seatbelt）中的 agent 进程，只能加载运行时、读自己的密钥、连 broker 的一个 Unix socket，不能直接读 workspace、开网络、建进程；(2) Broker 六阶段：authenticate（Ed25519 签名 + nonce/replay log 落盘防重放）→ resolve（把请求解析为具体对象：文件按内核方式解析到 workspace 路径+inode，程序为绝对二进制+参数向量，URL 解析一次定端点）→ decide（26 条默认路径规则 glob + git 子命令两级白名单 + 前缀感知选项过滤 + 端点 host:port + 请求级 DLP 扫描）→ gate（需人审的进审批队列，审批绑定 cell/参数/解析对象/git 仓库状态，10 分钟过期、一次性）→ execute → record（签名哈希链审计）。(3) 一策略两执行点：同一路径规则按逆序编译进每个被拉起程序的 Seatbelt profile，profile 处处严于 broker（读规则连带禁写、禁删受限目录、无审批通道即拒绝），解释器只有在 exec sandbox 活跃时才放行；git 以固定 GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE 运行并钉死 14 项配置（无 hooks/fsmonitor/外部 diff 等）。实现为 3,164 行可信 Rust（不含测试与依赖）。

controls.name: B0：直接工具访问，无任何防御
B1：工具允许列表（模拟部署 agent 默认权限模式：相对路径、git 子命令并集、host 白名单，无审批/解析/沙箱）
B2：B1 + 模拟部署式命令沙箱（被拉起程序可读写 workspace、可建进程、无网络；agent 进程不受限）
Zbroker：去掉 cell 沙箱的完整 ZTAC broker（隔离 P1 complete mediation 的贡献）
14 个消融：每次从 ZTAC 移除一个防御或两个重叠防御（Table 4）

results.claim: 完整 ZTAC 在 74 个脚本化攻击（含 10 个公开事件重放）下只放行 2 个攻击成功、14 个升级人工审批、58 个被阻断（Table 2 总行）；两个成功都是把密钥编码后发往策略允许的端点（模式扫描的原理性盲区）
results.setting: macOS 原型（Rust 3,164 行，Seatbelt）；cell A=攻击者/B=受害者双 workspace 环境；攻击脚本化、每个攻击配 ground-truth oracle（金丝雀/服务日志/仓库历史/marker 文件）
results.quote: Full ZTAC lets 2 attacks succeed, escalates 14, and blocks 58. The two successes send the access key to the allowlisted sink after Base64 encoding and in two halves across two requests

results.claim: 作者用攻击套件与代码审查在自己实现里发现并修复了 8 个缺陷（其中 7 个是 ZTAC 设计要防的那类 name/object gap：2 个审批-对象、1 个路径-文件、1 个目录内容-名字、1 个拼写-文件、1 个文件名-profile 文本、1 个一文件两名），每个都有回归测试——防御自身也在攻防迭代中修补
results.value: eight flaws, all fixed in the evaluated system
results.setting: 构建攻击套件与代码审查过程中发现；8 个缺陷为 approval retargeting、stale repository state、directory swap、directory rename、case at creation、broken diff、sandbox-profile injection、hard links across enforcement points；另有 3 个类外缺口（worktree 提交形态、审批存储并发、重启后重放）一并修复
results.quote: Building the suite and reviewing the code exposed eight flaws in ZTAC that the existing attacks did not detect. The evaluated system fixes all eight, and each has a regression test in the attack suite or, for the broken diff, in the benign workload.
results.locator: §6.4 Flaws found in our own implementation

limitations.statement: 允许通道内的外泄防不住：ZTAC 管数据去哪、不管数据编码了什么；能读密钥又能发允许端点的 cell 总能编码外泄，剩余 2 个成功攻击即此类。关闭该通道需信息流跟踪或避免敏感数据与出口同 cell（lethal trifecta）。
limitations.quote: ZTAC controls where data can go, not what it encodes. A cell that may read a secret and may post to an endpoint can send the secret in any encoding, as the two remaining successful attacks do.

limitations.statement: handoff 规则是枚举：只命名已知的消费者文件（编辑器任务、agent hook、git HEAD、venv 解释器）；其他工具若按自己的签名执行别的文件，规则不命名就不覆盖，清单要像凭据文件清单一样维护；Makefile 等由开发者下次构建触发的 handoff 任何规则都够不着，只能靠变更审查。
limitations.quote: The rules for files that other tools run name the consumers we know: editor tasks, agent hooks, git’s HEAD, and virtual-environment interpreters. A tool that executes some other file, recognized by its own signature, is not covered until a rule names that file.

limitations.statement: 对象绑定依赖的并发假设：写路径的 fstatat+renameat 是两个系统调用，仅因 broker 串行处理且 cell 进程不能建进程才等价原子；ZTAC 之外并发改 workspace 的进程（如开发者编辑器）既不被该论证也不被硬链接检查覆盖；程序与工作目录按路径绑定而非描述符；竞速试验只覆盖目录交换向量。
limitations.quote: A process outside ZTAC that changes the workspace concurrently, such as the developer’s editor, is covered neither by this argument nor by the hard-link check.

limitations.statement: 审批状态绑定的范围：git 绑定只哈希 HEAD、当前分支、packed refs 与 index；其余松散分支引用与全部工作树状态不在内，merge/reset/checkout/rebase 的审批不能给出同样的 reviewed-revision 保证。
limitations.quote: Other loose branch references and all working-tree state are not included; approvals for merge, reset, checkout, or rebase therefore do not establish the same reviewed-revision guarantee.

limitations.statement: reviewer 环节未研究：46 个操作里 8 次提示，作者没有研究 reviewer 疲劳与准确率；实际部署需调规则（如 scratch 分支免审）。
limitations.quote: We count 8 prompts in 46 operations and did not study reviewer fatigue or accuracy; a deployment would tune the rules, for example to allow commits on a scratch branch.

limitations.statement: 平台与沙箱限制：profile 允许到处读文件元数据（泄露 workspace 外路径是否存在与大小）；未对 Seatbelt 本身做逃逸测试；禁进程创建很粗糙（构建工具需要子进程），放开需要保证所有子孙随请求终止（进程组做不到，cgroup 可以）。
limitations.quote: Our profiles allow reading file metadata everywhere, which reveals whether a path outside the workspace exists and how large it is. We did not test Seatbelt itself for escapes.

limitations.statement: agent 集成未实测：用客户端库 + 脚本化请求评测，未接现成 agent 运行时；移植 agent 需把其工具换成 broker 调用、在 cell 内启动，模型流量成为被允许的出口。
limitations.quote: We evaluated ZTAC with a client library and scripted requests, not with an off-the-shelf agent runtime.

limitations.statement: 评测范围：端点按主机名匹配（解析到内网地址的名字可达）；不同 cell 请求在一把锁后串行；provenance 只存内存、重启即失；只用一个小的 Python 项目，B2 是对部署沙箱的近似而非直接运行它们；攻击套件覆盖 Table 1 的缺口类但不可能完备。
limitations.quote: Provenance is held in memory and lost on restart. The evaluation uses one small Python project, and B2 approximates deployed sandboxes rather than running them.

counterexamples.description: 2 个穿透 ZTAC 的攻击（net-dlp-encoded、net-dlp-split）：cell 把访问密钥 Base64 编码后发给策略允许的 sink 端点、或把密钥拆成两半分两次请求发送——都是'把策略允许读取的数据编码进允许端点流量'，模式扫描原理上拦不住；论文将其纳入套件正是为了标出保证的边界。
counterexamples.outcome: 在全部 5 配置（含完整 ZTAC 与全部 14 消融）下都成功（Table 12 两行全 ∙）

title: SEPM: Self-Evolving Procedural Memory Grounded in Task Graphs for Multi-Agent Collaboration

object.carrier: 版本化程序性记忆池 P：每条程序 S_i^(v) = (M_i 元数据[标题/描述/适用条件/上下文条件/排除条件/标签/版本号], Π_i 可执行步骤集, G_i 前置关系 DAG(V,E), W_i 条件警告及触发条件与支撑证据)；池内同时保留执行记录、候选程序、复现试验记录与被取代的历史版本，跨任务持久化于 run 级 SQLite 数据库（可用 TEAM_MEMORY_DB 覆盖，resumed run 从既有数据库/checkpoint 继续）；检索时按上下文条件/排除过滤后以 BM25+向量自适应加权取 Top-5（Eq.3，K=5）。任务级黑板与任务图随任务重置，跨任务存留的是程序池

safety_property.statement: 纯性能论文、未做安全实验：论文维护的是程序记忆池的内容完整性——只有被执行证据验证的步骤/依赖（Eq.8: Hτ⊨u、Hτ⊨(u,w)；时间先后 alone 不构成前置关系）且通过安全/状态验证/因果归因/复现门控并净收益非负的候选，才能成为活动版本（Eq.9），无试验记录的候选不能晋升，失败试验计入均值；该性质支撑其自演化记忆更新机制（§4.4/B.5 试炼式晋升、B.6 原子版本更新），而非对外安全保证——作者在 Ethics Statement 中明示记忆与对齐机制不应被解释为安全或正确性保证
safety_property.operationalized_as: 机制层：Eq.8 证据验证抽取（V+、E+）；Eq.9 晋升门控 G_safety∧G_state∧G_causal∧G_reproduction∧[ū(S′)≥0]，默认 safety-risk 阈值 0.50、causal 置信阈值 0.65、最少复现次数 1（B.5）；Eq.13/14 试验净收益（含失败试验，无试验记 -∞）；Eq.16 head 匹配的原子版本更新，被取代版本留史、检索只用活动版本。无安全实验、无安全指标

assumptions: 标准基准评测假设：任务、环境（ALFWorld/WebArena/OfficeBench/MultiAgentBench）与底层 LLM 非对抗，无记忆污染/投毒场景；黑板记录来自协作 agent 自身，证据按 authority tier（环境或官方状态 > 工具观测 > 验证工件 > agent 推断）分级（B.3）
每个 benchmark condition run 从空程序池开始，记忆内容仅由本 run 的执行经验形成；separate conditions 用独立数据库路径（C.2）
not_covered: 无对手模型：不涉及对记忆池的污染/注入/投毒攻击，也不评估恶意或错误导出的程序被检索复用的后果
作者明示框架可能继承底层模型的偏见、不安全行为与事实错误，记忆与对齐机制不应被解释为安全或正确性保证（Ethics Statement）
不覆盖更开放的迭代式/隐式协调结构（§6 Limitations 自述）

intervention.name: SEPM (Self-Evolving Procedural Memory)
intervention.description: 以任务依赖图为共同表征、把多智能体在线协调与程序记忆演化耦合的记忆架构：(1) 检索与实例化——按上下文条件/排除过滤活动程序池，BM25+向量自适应加权取 Top-5（Eq.3），manager 把检索步骤绑定为任务图节点+agent 分配并保留前置关系与警告；(2) 结构化执行——共享黑板 B 记录结构化执行记录（assigned subtask/observation/action/result/error，Eq.4）并关联图节点，manager 维护已验证任务状态 Σ；(3) 分歧感知对齐——目标分歧 Dg（文本相似+task-conditioned goal-consistency judge，Eq.5，β=0.55、阈值 0.35）、计划分歧 Dp（节点动作不匹配+边对称差归一化，Eq.6，阈值 0.40）、状态冲突 Cs（合格证据值冲突，Eq.7/10/11，置信≥0.70）触发 manager 解决冲突并把修正传播给受影响 agent（含跨 agent handoff 的证据要求）；(4) 自演化记忆——任务完成后从验证过的节点/边抽取程序（Eq.8），新工作流建新程序、经验支持时修订或附加条件警告，池经创建/精化/特化/退休演化，受 success 与 cost utility 引导；候选须经试炼式晋升门控（安全/状态/因果/复现+净收益非负，Eq.9/12-14）并以原子版本更新提交（Eq.16）

title: MetaCascade: End-to-End Attacks on Agent Skills via Metadata-Only Poisoning

object.carrier: SKILL.md metadata of a third-party skill published on an open agent-skill registry; metadata is part of the readable skill files consumed by both the retrieval/reranking stage and the agent's final skill-selection decision

safety_property.statement: Skill metadata on an open registry should faithfully describe the skill's capability so that the agent's end-to-end retrieval-and-selection process returns the genuinely most suitable skill. The property fails when attacker-crafted metadata alone (code and other content unchanged) makes the attacker's malicious skill both enter the retrieved candidate set and be ultimately selected by the agent for tasks within the original capability scope; existing defenses (reranking and security detection) prove insufficient to eliminate this influence.
safety_property.operationalized_as: End-to-end attack success rate (ASR): how often the same attacker-controlled malicious skill enters the candidate set and is finally selected by the agent on held-out test tasks; Hit@1/3/5 measure the retrieval stage; results are additionally reported under four defense settings (SkillRouter, SkillResolve, SkillSieve, SkillScan).

capabilities: download any skill from the public registry
locally replace the skill's metadata with malicious metadata and upload it as a third-party skill on an open registry with limited vetting
run a local optimization loop with black-box listwise competition feedback from an LLM selection decision maker (observing only final selections, not internal representations, reasoning, or scores)
use a set of construction tasks T_con to iteratively optimize the malicious metadata before publishing
assumptions: open agent-skill registry where third parties can freely upload and publish skills
the agent first retrieves and ranks candidate skills from readable skill files and then makes the final selection based on metadata
the same optimized malicious metadata is reused across agents, LLMs, and embedding models without per-setting re-optimization
the attacker cannot control the agent backend, retriever, selector, defenses, inputs, or other registered skills
not_covered: any harm caused after the malicious skill is invoked (post-execution/execution-stage attacks are out of scope)
control over agent backend, retriever, selector, defenses, agent inputs, or other registered skills
deployment to live registries, real users, or execution of post-invocation payloads (per ethical considerations)

intervention.name: MetaCascade (Capability-Grounded Multi-View Candidate Generation, CMCG + Competition-Aware Iterative Malicious Metadata Optimization, CIMO)
intervention.description: An end-to-end metadata-only poisoning attack. CMCG derives semantic views from the original skill package and generates N=8 capability-equivalent candidate skills for multi-view semantic coverage. CIMO partitions the candidates into a source set and a competition set, compresses the source set into a capability profile, generates J=2 initial malicious metadata candidates, and iteratively refines the archive-best candidate using task-level failure feedback from black-box listwise competitions (L=3 evaluations per task, at most K=3 rounds, early stop at utility tau=0.8, metadata length capped at 1,290 characters). The winning malicious metadata is written back into the original skill and published, so the poisoned skill is retrieved and selected on subsequent tasks. The paper motivates but does not implement defenses (metadata integrity, skill provenance).

title: Many Steps into One: Reasoning Contraction and the Limits of Safe Memory Reuse for LLM Agents

object.carrier: Contracted memories (macros): one-step operators compiled from a verified multi-step derivation, unified under 'reasoning contraction' across thought templates, skill libraries, agent memories and answer caches. Instantiated as (i) materialized anchor-to-answer relation-path tables reached through one routing call and stored paths re-executed as compiled plans in KQA-Stream, and (ii) verified programs reused as tools in CodeStream; each memory carries trust state (betting wealth / counter score) and is judged only by its own verified outcomes

safety_property.statement: A contracted memory may answer in one step only while the risk of trusting a bad one (below break-even paired utility vs live reasoning, or stale after a fact change) stays below delta: delta-safety (Definition 1) requires that no epoch contains a fold (trust event) of a candidate that is bad in that epoch, and stale memories must be retired quickly once facts change. The property fails when counters mis-detect partial staleness (delay asymp A^0.373, never-retirement with probability >= 0.50/0.89), when evidence is carried across unannounced changes, or when the null (which depends on live reasoning) changes without a notice; availability (the share of queries that may skip reasoning, bounded by the certification load Theta) is the priced counterpart.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Share of at-risk epochs with a false certification / bad fold, <= delta (answer-only and standard scoring); bad folds per stream; stale answers per 10^4 queries; unretired share at stream end and restricted-mean detection delay (Kaplan-Meier) on matched stale episodes; false retirements per 10^4 healthy uses

capabilities: Non-adversarial environment drift: synthetic KQA Pro fact edits replacing relation objects for f=0.25/0.6 of subjects (24 events x 3 sequences, correlated across templates sharing a relation), natural Wikidata temporal-qualifier changes 1992-2016 (median 3.3% of a template's answers per year), and code-domain requirement revisions plus re-enacted Python API changes

Changes may be partial (an edit corrupts only part of a template's instances, e.g. reliability 0.95->0.75) or total, announced or unannounced (notice fraction f down to 0), and live reasoning itself can change silently (15.7% of template-versions), shifting the certificate's null without any answer change
No adversary writes memory: candidates form only from verified live traces and memories go stale only through environment/requirement changes
assumptions: An exact verifier labels memory answers on audited queries (audit probability known and bounded below); only audited outcomes are informative in the base guarantees
Facts change at random (Poisson) times; audited outcomes are Bernoulli at the memory's current reliability within an epoch

Per-epoch delta-safety needs notices covering every change of the paired-utility null, including changes of live reasoning; without any change information, per-epoch safety is impossible on templates with alpha_i*r0 > delta (Proposition 24) and only post-change-evidence safety remains (Proposition 25)
Policies are non-anticipating; each template's epochs contain an audit with probability alpha_i
not_covered: Adversarial memory poisoning / shared multi-agent memory as an attack channel (named as future work and concurrent work; no attacker is modeled here)
Self-modifying memories and formation-aware limits (coverage depends on how often live agents produce a verifiable trace)
Noisy or LLM-judge verifiers, text memories, and a certificate built for the noisy paired channel (measured as negative result in D.2.3)
Transfer across correlated templates or macros a change does not affect (outside the limit's model)
Confidentiality/authority properties; real library drift staleness magnitudes

intervention.name: Certified contraction: per-memory betting certificate + likelihood-ratio CUSUM retirement + restart/invalidate lifecycle
intervention.description: An execution-time memory-trust lifecycle with formal (anytime-valid) guarantees. (1) Certification: a betting certificate on the paired utility U = C_live - C_macro + L*(Y_macro - Y_live) of shadow evaluations with inverse-propensity weights folds a memory when its wealth reaches 1/delta (level delta_j = 6*delta/(pi^2 j^2) per lifetime ledger index), needing no live-accuracy estimate. (2) Retirement: folded macros are monitored by a per-memory Bernoulli LR-CUSUM (h=7, alternative max(1-r*, q0+0.15)) whose likelihood-ratio scores make each memory the optimal detector of its own q0->q1 change. (3) Restarts and revocation: candidates restart their test at every edit notice (recommended deployment additionally invalidates and re-forms notified macros, so the detector is the safety net for missed notices); guarantees are per-epoch delta-safety via Ville's inequality and Proposition 23, with detector-triggered restarts (Proposition 25) when no edit log exists

title: Can Agents Truly Forget? Explore Machine Unlearning for LLM Agents

object.carrier: Agent system A=(f_theta, M, T, pi): Mem0 persistent memory - a local vector store of extracted memory records retrieved per question with a fixed local embedding model (artifacts constructed once from the corpus and shared across all six unlearning checkpoints) - plus an offline web-snapshot tool corpus (800 local HTML pages, 200 entity records, 4,000 fact records, 800 document records, 4,000 fact-span annotations, read-only SQLite FTS5/BM25 index) and provenance-tracked interaction trajectories; forget information propagates from raw interactions into summaries, vector indices, documents, and derived profiles

safety_property.statement: System-level agent unlearning: after a deletion request, the target knowledge set K_f must be behaviorally non-recoverable through ALL information pathways within the declared access boundary - parametric recall, persistent-memory retrieval, derived/evolved memory structures, and memory-mediated tool use - while the agent's utility on retain queries and authorized tool tasks is preserved (an (epsilon_f, epsilon_r)-agent unlearning). Failure condition: the agent stops answering directly but still retrieves the same information from memory or reacquires it through tools; also, effective forgetting must be distinguished from indiscriminate refusal or tool disabling.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Token-level F1 (%) between generated and reference answers, reported separately on the forget split forget05 (200 questions) and retain split retain95 (3,800 questions) under four conditions (Para., +Mem., +Tool, Final) x {Vanilla, GD, KL, NPO} x 2 model families; tool-invocation behavior (Call %, Empty %, Refusal %) to distinguish forgetting from generation failures; worst-case expected recoverability defined as the supremum of expected recovery scores over response conditions and permitted strategies.

capabilities: Recovery-seeking evaluator: adaptive evaluations beyond exact queries and fixed tool interfaces - the recoverability metric takes the supremum over evaluated response conditions (direct generation, memory-augmented generation, tool-call memory access) and permitted prompting/interaction/tool-use strategies

The agent itself is a recovery vector: privacy-seeking trajectories shape future tool selection, query formulation, and action planning, so unlearning must remove the learned behavior of seeking, reconstructing, or using the target information
assumptions: A controlled offline environment: static web snapshot and deterministic search/browsing tools make tool observations reproducible and attribute failures to specific channels; synthetic fictitious-author subjects reduce privacy and pretraining-contamination risks

Fact-level provenance supports attributing failures to residual parametric knowledge, persistent memory, or tool-mediated reacquisition; a retain-only oracle constructed under matched conditions bounds retained utility
not_covered: Only two 8B model families, three parameter-level unlearning methods, and the 5% forget setting of TOFU; findings may not generalize to other scales, datasets, forget-set sizes, or multi-step interactive tasks (authors' stated limitation)
Memory artifacts are fixed (no continuously updated memories) and the web corpus is offline; live web search and heterogeneous external sources are not captured (authors' stated limitation)
Low retain-set scores under tool access limit conclusions about tool-mediated answer recovery (authors' stated limitation)

intervention.name: AUBench: evaluation of parameter-level unlearning (GD, KL, NPO) across agent information channels
intervention.description: Extends the TOFU fictitious-author setting into an agent environment with three channels: the parametric channel (vanilla/full fine-tuned checkpoint vs GD/KL/NPO unlearned checkpoints), the memory channel (Mem0 persistent memory whose retrieved records are appended to the prompt without parameter modification), the tool channel (a local Web Search surrogate over one HTML profile + one SQLite profile per record via the Ollama tool schema), and the Final condition combining retrieved Mem0 context with the local Web Search tool. Every question records retrieved memory, tool calls, and the final answer; a result counts only if the JSONL contains exactly the expected rows (200/3,800).

title: Keep Your Receipts: Trustworthy Cleanup of Agent-Built Knowledge Graphs

object.carrier: agent-built knowledge graph over source documents (extracted claims, entity merges, schema-entailed edges, community summaries), where every artifact carries a support-label receipt: alternative bundles of source assertions each claimed sufficient on its own

safety_property.statement: When a source is retracted or a predicate revoked, the persisted agent-built graph must stop serving artifacts that no longer re-derive from surviving evidence (no leakage of invalidated content) while retaining artifacts a surviving derivation still supports (no over-deletion). The property fails silently when the model's own receipts wrongly claim an artifact still stands.
safety_property.operationalized_as: label faithfulness graded against a re-derivation oracle (agreement / leaky / over-deleted rates per layer, Tables 2-3), and retrieval-level exposure as tainted@10 with recall@10 against a deployed-deletion baseline (Table 4)

capabilities: the constructor LLM authors its own receipts (self-reports), which can be leaky: claiming an artifact survives a deletion when re-derivation says it is dead
the constructor samples, so rebuilding is noisy and cannot serve as a verifier
non-adversarial harness faults also corrupt the artifact store (provider banner / refusals cached as model answers)
assumptions: no deliberate adversary; the untrusted party is the model's unreliable self-report, not an attacker
receipts are demanded in the same model call that creates the artifact; no later process can recover them
liveness is graded by re-derivation with R=5 independent draws per touched artifact at threshold tau=0.2, matching the stochastic constructor
entailed edges are re-derived symbolically and agree by construction
not_covered: adversarial attacks such as prompt injection or deliberate poisoning of receipts
source-groundedness: artifacts the model regenerates from parametric memory grade alive without surviving source support (matters for right-to-erasure)
additions/updates to the graph (only deletion is studied)
consumers that reason over retrieval paths rather than top-k keyword retrieval
failures in the harness/cache layer, which no audit of the model's reasoning sees (Section 7 incident)

intervention.name: PolyGraph: receipt-and-audit protocol with a layered trust policy
intervention.description: The constructor must emit, in the same call that creates an artifact, a support label: alternative bundles of source assertions, each claimed sufficient on its own. Cleanup of a withdrawal is then set arithmetic over the receipts (milliseconds on the whole graph, no model calls). Because receipts are model self-reports, a re-derivation audit grades them by deleting the cited evidence and testing whether the constructor still produces the artifact (R=5 draws, tau=0.2). The audit's layer-dependent verdict is acted on by a layered policy: trust merge and entailed-edge labels, distrust flat summary labels and remove touched summaries; sentence-level receipts repair the summary layer.

results.claim: In this corpus, the deployed policy of deleting only directly extracted facts barely cleans the graph under a real retraction and does nothing under predicate revocation, because the damage sits in derived edges and summaries.
results.setting: 300 PubMed oncology abstracts (61 genuinely retracted), Claude Sonnet constructor, BM25 retrieval over MeSH-descriptor queries
results.quote: On our corpus that reduces contaminated queries from 32.2% to 28.0% under a real retraction and leaves predicate revocation unchanged at 36.8%.

denominator.how_counted: Table 4: BM25, k=10, 300 MeSH-descriptor queries; truth is the re-derivation oracle

results.quote: Rerunning the constructor on unchanged input changes 29,475 artifacts. Removing the retracted documents changes 6,248.

denominator.how_counted: Table 1: symmetric difference between two independent builds (floor) and between full and retracted builds (effect)

results.setting: full populations of touched model-authored artifacts under retract-source and revoke-relation, re-derivation oracle R=5, tau=0.2, Claude Sonnet constructor, biomedical graph
results.quote: Merge labels agree with re-derivation 68.4% and 84.6% of the time; summary labels, 33.3% and 36.4%.

denominator.n_total: 21 touched merges and 7 touched summaries under retract-source; 29 merges and 25 summaries under revoke-relation (populations, not samples)
denominator.how_counted: Table 2: every model-authored artifact the deletion touched was adjudicated; undecided artifacts counted separately

results.claim: The summary layer's failure is traced to receipt shape and repaired: eliciting one receipt per sentence makes summary receipts as faithful as the merge layer's, with errors no longer one-sided.
results.value: 100% and 87.6% agreement; 4.1% leaky vs 8.3% over-deleted under revoke-relation

results.quote: Audited sentence by sentence, these receipts agree with re-derivation 100% and 87.6% of the time, the merge layer's range, and their errors are no longer one-sided (4.1% leaky against 8.3% over-deleted under revoke-relation).

denominator.n_total: 62 and 124 touched sentences audited as their own artifacts
denominator.how_counted: Table 3: sentence-level rows audit each touched sentence as its own artifact, so n counts sentences

results.setting: BM25, k=10, 300 MeSH-descriptor queries, truth = re-derivation oracle, biomedical graph
results.quote: Trusting all labels already reduces contamination from the deployed baseline's 28.0% and 36.8% of queries to 0.8% and 2.1%. Applying the verdict halves the remainder, to 0.4% and 0.8%, at identical recall and no additional model calls.

denominator.how_counted: Table 4: BM25, k=10, 300 MeSH-descriptor queries; truth is the re-derivation oracle

results.claim: The layer ordering holds when populations grow: pooled over ten further random retractions, summary receipts leak far more often than merge receipts, with summary over-deletion at zero in every deletion.
results.setting: ten further random 10% retractions of the biomedical graph, same protocol, pooled (deletion, artifact) adjudications
results.quote: On 238 decided merges and 109 decided summaries the gap stands on its own: merges 18.1% leaky [13.7, 23.5], summaries 41.3% leaky [32.5, 50.7], with summary over-deletion at zero in every deletion.

denominator.how_counted: Section 6.3: pooled every (deletion, artifact) adjudication over ten further random 10% retractions; undecided excluded

results.setting: 150 U.S. Supreme Court opinions graph (same pipeline, legal schema), merge receipts 80.0%/76.2% and summary receipts 43.8%/12.5% agreement with re-derivation, random-document retract-source
results.quote: merge receipts agree with re-derivation 80.0% and 76.2% of the time, summary receipts 43.8% and 12.5%, every summary error a leak, and distrusting the summary layer brings contamination from 15.7% and 4.7% to 0.0% at 99.9% and 100% recall.

denominator.how_counted: Section 3: the Supreme Court corpus's queries are 300 party and citation strings

limitations.statement: The audit measures constructor-relative liveness, not source-groundedness: an artifact the model can regenerate from parametric memory grades alive even if no surviving source supports it, which is the failure that matters most for right-to-erasure.
limitations.quote: Re-derivation asks the constructor that built the graph, so an artifact the model can regenerate from parametric memory grades alive even if no surviving source supports it.

limitations.statement: The size of the summary layer's leakage is setting-specific (varies widely across constructor, corpus and operation), so the layered policy's margin over trusting all labels does not generalize; both constructors are Claude models, corpora are small, and behavior at larger scale is unmeasured.
limitations.quote: the size of the summary layer's leakage did not, ranging from 8% to 88% across constructor, corpus and operation, so the layered policy's margin over trusting all labels is setting-specific.

limitations.statement: The retrieval-level stakes are measured with a keyword BM25 retriever over single queries; a consumer that reasons over paths can be contaminated by a dead edge it never retrieves directly.
limitations.quote: A consumer that reasons over paths meets every artifact on the path, so one dead edge can contaminate an answer that never retrieves the edge directly.

limitations.statement: Only deletion is studied; when a still-alive summary has become incomplete and should be regenerated is a design question the authors have not studied.
limitations.quote: What additions do not settle is when a still-alive summary has become incomplete and should be regenerated; that is a design question for the constructor, and we have not studied it.

limitations.statement: The verdict granularity is coarse: five re-derivation draws at tau=0.2 leave artifacts near the threshold in an undecided band that is excluded from scoring.
limitations.quote: artifacts near the threshold land in the undecided band (2 to 3 per cell) and are excluded.

title: Can Agents Forget When Asked? A Benchmark for Memory Unlearning in LLM Agents

object.carrier: External agent memory stores (Naive RAG vector store, Mem0 extracted facts, A-MEM linked notes, LangMem notes, LightMem, SimpleMem compressed notes) and the full dialogue transcript for the Full Context LLM baseline

safety_property.statement: When a user issues a natural-language forget request, the agent's memory system must honor it: the requested information must be neither retrievable nor inferable afterwards (confidentiality of deleted data, right to be forgotten), the deletion must be scoped so unrelated memories stay intact and similar facts can still be learned (user authority over memory content without over-deletion). It fails when the deleted value resurfaces under prompt-based extraction probes or when the system deletes/preserves too much, judged by the paired-control suites on Bemula.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Five test suites scored against paired control dialogues: RA (retention), FE (efficacy, gold marker [FORGOTTEN]), PR (preservation, catches over-deletion), RLA (relearning), AR (attack robustness, gold marker [NO_LEAK] under 5 fixed attack frames), plus RPR (request pass rate over all questions of a request) and composite Score = FA x UG (geometric means of FE*AR and PR*RLA), all LLM-judged and reported as percentages.

capabilities: Issues natural-language forget requests as ordinary dialogue turns (the system must act via its own write/update path; no external delete API is granted)
After the request, asks extraction probes in fresh sessions: indirect questioning, role playing, jailbreak prefixes, Boolean guessing, multi-hop reasoning (five fixed frames, never paraphrased)
assumptions: The user interacts with the agent only through natural language; neither the user nor the evaluation provides any deletion signal beyond the dialogue turn
Every question is answered in a fresh session containing only the query, so answers must come from memory
Answers are graded by a fixed LLM judge at temperature 0
not_covered: Adaptive or optimized attacks beyond the five fixed prompt frames
White-box or direct access to the memory store (the benchmark only probes through the query interface)
Multi-user / cross-user memory interference
Tool-use side channels: caches, logs, or external services where forgotten values may persist
Real-user dialogues (all data is synthetic, from one generation pipeline)

intervention.description: No defense is proposed; Bemula is an evaluation benchmark. Its measurement design (pairing each forget-version dialogue with a control version without forget requests, and conditioning every efficacy/preservation/attack probe on its control counterpart) is a scoring control that separates genuine forgetting from failure to encode, not an intervention on memory systems.

results.claim: On Bemula, forget requests almost never pass end to end: across all evaluated systems and backbones (six memory systems under three backbone LLMs, with Full Context on two of them, and no Full Context or A-MEM runs under Qwen3-32B-AWQ on the full benchmark), the request pass rate never exceeds 1.5% and most systems pass none at all.
results.comparison: best RPR 1.5 (LangMem on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash); most systems pass none
results.setting: Bemula full benchmark (50 paired dialogue instances, 135 forget requests); six memory systems + Full Context, with Full Context on GPT-5.6-Luna and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash only; Full Context and A-MEM have no runs under Qwen3-32B-AWQ on the full benchmark because of its context length limit
results.quote: The request pass rate never exceeds 1.5 (LangMem on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), and most systems remain at zero.

title: SEAR: Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics

object.carrier: the library: versioned code skills and written memories harvested from the best policy of each finished task ('What persists from task to task is the library'); AR checkpoints and data never carry over to the next task, and no LM or policy weights persist (code-as-policy LM weights never change); the library transfers across tasks, simulators, and even models (crossover runs)

safety_property.statement: No safety property is claimed, attacked, or measured: the paper evaluates task success, learning vs resampling, and generalization of self-evolving robot agents, with no collision-rate, damage, or safety-violation experiments. Physical-safety constraints exist only as fixed harness infrastructure (safety guard, workspace box per arm, 0.25 m keep-out region around the other arm's base, speed limit near the table; Appendix K), and harness refusals appear in the failure audit as one category of stopped episodes, not as an evaluated property. As 必要背景 it supports the survey's mechanism of persistent non-parametric agent state: a skill-and-memory library that forms (harvested from each finished task), updates (versioned, extended, shadowed by newer versions), persists across tasks/simulators/models, and is retrieved via imports - including the finding that mistakes persist like skills do (a self-built verifier saved as memory stays wrong).

assumptions: The agent works in its own container with DEV seeds; only the frozen program with imported skills, or the AR checkpoint, is passed to a sealed judge that holds VAL/TEST initial states and grading logic and ignores any success the policy claims
Budgets are matched in wall-clock time (1 h per task, 2 h on RoboLab; 12 h per physical task), with tokens, environment steps, and GPU time logged beside them
Each condition runs three times per model except AR on LIBERO/LIBERO-PRO/RoboLab and every physical run (one run each)
not_covered: No adversary is modeled: the paper studies capability and measurement of self-evolution, not attacks on the agent, its library, or the judge
Physical-safety violations (collisions, damage, unsafe motion) are not measured; the harness safety guard is fixed infrastructure, not a studied property

Seal integrity (agents reading asset files, calling env.check_success(), task text leaking into libraries) is audited as benchmark-integrity limits of the seal (Section A.9), not as an adversary model; the harness now refuses exploration sessions touching held-out task identifiers

intervention.name: SEAR: self-evolving agent framework (code-as-policy / agent-as-policy / auto-research) with a persistent skill-and-memory library, matched controls (best-of-3, no-library, three repetitions), a sealed judge, and five generalization tiers T1-T5
intervention.description: Improvement flows through editable non-parametric content rather than weights: the LM agent writes executable control code that becomes the policy and harvests versioned code skills plus written memories into a library that every next task inherits and extends; a final program imports a median of five skills. Auto-research additionally fine-tunes a VLA (pi_0.5) on rollouts of code teachers, but AR checkpoints and data never carry over between tasks, so the studied persistent state is the library content. The benchmark pairs every comparison with controls that separate retained experience from resampling, familiar tasks, privileged state, larger budgets, and luck.

controls.name: Vanilla: every task starts from an empty library
Best-of-3: three budget-split no-library restarts, best by VAL score
Three independent repetitions of the whole run, library included

title: CyberArena: Benchmarking AI Agents in Live Symmetric Attack-and-Defense Combat

object.carrier: 被研究的对象是冻结的模型-脚手架（model-harness）智能体本身，不研究任何记忆/技能组件。跨轮次复用的状态存在于被攻击的服务与环境，而非智能体的可复用认知状态：每局 3 轮 x 20 分钟，防守方对服务的补丁修改跨轮持久（'Defensive service modifications persist across rounds'），攻击方植入的后门可跨轮存活，目标 flag 每轮轮换。跨局不保留任何智能体状态：466 局评估中每个 entrant 始终是冻结的生产模型+脚手架组合（Table 6），论文明确当前只测量能力而不优化能力，把'经验驱动的智能体改进 + 回到竞技场'（RAI 递归对抗改进）列为未来工作。

safety_property.statement: 作为评估仪器而非防御机制：测量 LLM 智能体在对手实时对抗下的攻防双能力——攻击能力（对对手服务完成轮换目标的 arena 验证捕获）、防御能力（守住自己的 flag、保持服务健康检查通过）、可用性（beta-binomial 建模的健康探针通过率），经潜在能力模型（配对比较+IRT）换算到同一尺度排序。与安全边界的联系：它提供'防守方在轮间修补后攻击方是否被迫换路径'的测量环境，即本综述核心问题（攻击是否针对演化后的防御重新适应）的实证观察台；但论文自身不保护任何安全性质、不提出防御，也无失效条件的判定表述。
safety_property.operationalized_as: 466 局有效比赛（12 个 entrant x 40 挑战，另有 53 局校准局）：arena 验证的捕获、每轮 flag 防守成功、健康探针通过率、首轮捕获/首次补丁部署时延；以及全量轨迹自动审计（GPT-6 Sol/GPT-6.1 Sol，2,397 条发现归并为 673 候选模式、249 个复现模式）给出的行为模式占比

capabilities: 对称设定：两个智能体在同一规则下同时扮演攻击者与防御者，从挑战定义的基线访问出发突破安全边界完成读/写/执行目标（经 MCP 工具由 arena 验证）
攻击方可植入持久后门：4% 的比赛中攻击者安装的代码在防守方部署补丁后仍可执行（如 GPT-5.6 Sol 在 Openfire 服务器植入插件，绕过入口路由补丁在第 2 轮继续捕获）
攻击方可针对防守方的修补改变策略：防守方封堵直接读 trace 端点后改走 search 端点，在第 2、3 轮继续捕获直至该路径也被封（HY4 Preview vs Claude Opus 4.8 案例）
防守方可查询对手攻击（get_attacks_received）并在轮间部署补丁；攻击流量监控（自写 packet sniffer）也被观察到
assumptions: 所有 entrant 为冻结模型-脚手架对，跨 466 局不变；无权重更新、无跨局记忆
每局在隔离沙箱内进行（无互联网，模型请求经受限 API 路由），arena 而非智能体验证全部得分事件
每轮目标轮换且'即使既有攻击路径仍可用也必须对新目标完成捕获'，防止一次利用通吃全轮
not_covered: 不研究智能体持久记忆/技能组件的安全：记忆与技能不是干预对象、威胁入口或被评组件，跨轮持久的是服务补丁与环境状态
无跨局学习：RAI（用对局轨迹做离线策略优化再返场）仅作为未来工作提出
DoS、多智能体群攻不在范围内（作者自述）；12 个模型-脚手架组合与 40 挑战之外的生态未覆盖
审计发现 6 次（占 1,336 次已接受捕获的 0.45%）经重放 arena 签名请求或读取对手 objective journal 的捷径捕获仍计入排名

intervention.description: 本文是基准/评估平台论文，不提出防御干预。对本综述的价值在于它把'静态目标基准'换成'活体对称对抗'：防守方轮间修补改变攻击条件，攻击方必须对演化后的防御重新适应（对手修补后捕获率随轮次下降；补丁部署后守旗率 60% vs 未部署 9%）。它支撑本综述'防御记忆与安全演化'分支的评估问题——如何在活体对抗下测量演化能力——但未涉及任何持久记忆机制本身。

results.claim: 活体对抗下攻击成功率随轮次显著衰减：在三个模型都能单独解出的 30 个挑战上，GPT-5.6 Sol 第 3 轮捕获率降到 52%，Claude Opus 4.8 与 GLM-5.3 降到 37% 与 35%，作者归因于防守方轮间修补迫使攻击方重新适应。
results.setting: solo-solved-by-all-3 挑战的对抗局（Figure 11b），95% bootstrap 区间（挑战重采样、局重采样）
results.quote: By round 3, GPT-5.6 Sol sustains a 52% capture rate, whereas Claude Opus 4.8 and GLM-5.3 drop to 37% and 35%, respectively. The decline is consistent with defenders patching between rounds, which forces attackers to adapt to keep their access.

denominator.n_total: 30 个挑战（40 个参考挑战中三模型 solo 均解出者）上的对抗局，分轮捕获率；各轮局数未逐轮列出（Figure 11b）
denominator.n_valid: 同一 30 挑战对抗局集合的逐轮捕获率；单轮尝试数的整数分母未在正文给出
denominator.how_counted: 捕获轮次 / 对抗局轮次，按 95% bootstrap 区间报告（对挑战与局重采样）

results.claim: 防守方轮间部署补丁与守住 flag 强关联：部署补丁的防守者在下一轮守旗率 60%，未部署者仅 9%；作者明确这是关联而非防御有效的证明。
results.comparison: deployed patch 60% vs did not deploy 9%
results.setting: 第 1-2 轮中被接受捕获丢旗且存在可观察下一轮的防守方轮次（466 局全量事件测量）
results.quote: Defenders that deploy a patch keep their flag in 60% of the following rounds, against 9% of those that do not, an association rather than proof that the defenses worked.

denominator.n_total: 第 1-2 轮丢旗且有可观察下一轮的防守方轮次（整数分母未在正文给出）
denominator.n_valid: 同上集合按是否部署补丁分组的下一轮守旗率
denominator.how_counted: 下一轮守住 flag 的比例；分组条件为下一轮开始前是否部署补丁

results.claim: 攻击方对演化后防御的再适应是普遍行为：丢旗防守者 67% 会查询打向自己服务的攻击、57% 在下一轮开始前部署补丁；攻击方则利用修补留下的路径——21% 的被审计比赛中部分补丁封住一个入口而另一条已观察到的路径仍开放。
results.value: 67% 查询攻击、57% 部署补丁；21% 比赛出现 partial patch 被利用
results.setting: 466 局：事件测量（防守响应）+ 全量轨迹自动审计（行为模式，模式可重叠）
results.quote: In rounds 1–2 in which a defender loses its flag, it queries the attacks fired against its service in 67% of cases and deploys a patch before the next round starts in 57%.

title: CoRedSkill: Stealthy Skill Composition Attacks via AST-Guided Injection

object.carrier: Third-party-published skill packages (task instructions, executable scripts, auxiliary resources, input-output interfaces) installed in the victim agent's environment, plus intermediate JSON artifacts that carry task data and attack-relevant state between skills; the packages are shared via public skill libraries (publisher-to-user supply chain) and persist installed across sessions, while each evaluation case executes in a single fresh session

safety_property.statement: An agent using a composition of third-party skills must not perform operations outside the user's authorization while completing the legitimate task: no data exfiltration of protected values (confidentiality), no unauthorized tampering of installed skills' persistent state (integrity), and no privilege violation executing task-unrelated scripts (authority). The property fails when operations distributed across individually benign-looking skills jointly achieve the attack objective and no constituent package is flagged by auditing.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Binary oracles on the execution record tau: U(tau) task acceptance (final POST payload equals expected publication), A_o(tau) attack-objective success for o in {EXF, TAM, PRV} (recorded request to unauthorized host containing protected values / protected file copied into a skill archive / execution of a permission-locked task-unrelated helper script), and D_rho audit flagging (HIGH or CRITICAL rating); aggregated as ASR, TSR, DR, and JSR = (1/N) sum A_n U_n (1-D_n) over the 150-case benchmark

capabilities: Act as a third-party skill publisher
Inspect the original skill's documentation and scripts
Construct and publish multiple skills based on the original workflow
Modify their instructions, code, resources, and input-output interfaces
Influence the agent's skill selection and execution through the published skills and the intermediate artifacts they produce
assumptions: Skills supplied by a third-party publisher are installed alongside other available skills
The agent autonomously selects relevant skills and determines their invocation order based on the user's request, skill documentation, and input-output dependencies
The user's legitimate request defines the scope of authorized actions
The deployment (agent model, system prompt, safeguards, file/network/process permissions) is fixed and not controlled by the attacker
not_covered: Automatic adaptation of attack construction to arbitrary existing skill packages (not evaluated)
Dynamic service interactions or long-term operation (utility verified only on offline evaluation cases)
How online blocking by runtime defenses affects subsequent execution and attack outcomes (only offline record inspection evaluated)
Attacker control over the agent's model, system prompt, safeguards, or permissions

intervention.name: CoRedSkill
intervention.description: A compositional red-teaming construction: decompose an existing task workflow into interdependent clean skills, assign attack-operation groups to workflow stages via stage specifications phi_i, and use abstract syntax tree (AST) rewriting to embed attack operations in task helper functions while updating related calls, arguments, and artifact reads/writes so original task logic and stage interfaces are preserved; skill instructions and input-output dependencies guide the agent to autonomously invoke the skills, and intermediate artifacts connect the distributed operations during execution.

results.claim: On the 150-case benchmark audited by SkillScan (Deepseek), CoRedSkill jointly achieves attack success, task completion, and audit evasion far beyond four attack baselines.
results.comparison: JSR 90.7% vs 6.7–42.7% for the four baselines
results.setting: 150 cases (50 tasks x 3 objectives EXF/TAM/PRV); victim platform Claude Code CLI with deepseek-v4-flash execution backend; audit by SkillScan using Deepseek; three-skill compositions by default plus six clean distractor skills
results.quote: In the main evaluation, CoRedSkill achieves 98.0% attack success and 95.3% task success with a 3.3% detection rate, and a joint success rate of 90.7% (attack success, task completion, and audit evasion in the same case) compared with 6.7–42.7% for the four baselines.

denominator.how_counted: ASR/TSR/DR measured as the fraction of the 150 benchmark cases (50 tasks x 3 attack objectives); JSR = (1/N) sum A_n U_n (1-D_n) per Eq. 5

results.claim: On the 150-case benchmark, 140 cases achieve both task completion and attack success, and 136 of these also pass the skill audit, yielding JSR 90.7%.
results.value: 140 of 150 cases both succeed; 136 pass audit; JSR 90.7%
results.setting: 150-case benchmark; SkillScan (Deepseek) audit; DeepSeek V4 Flash execution backend
results.quote: On the 150-case benchmark, its ASR, TSR, and DR are 98.0%, 95.3%, and 3.3%, respectively. Of the 150 cases, 140 achieve both task completion and attack success, and 136 of these also pass the skill audit, yielding a JSR of 90.7%.

denominator.how_counted: Paper states: 'Of the 150 cases, 140 achieve both task completion and attack success, and 136 of these also pass the skill audit, yielding a JSR of 90.7%'

results.claim: Across the four LLM skill-audit configurations (SkillScan/SkillSpector x Deepseek/GLM), CoRedSkill's overall detection rate stays between 3.3% and 20.0%, lower than SkillJect, Skill-Inject, and SCR-Bench in each configuration.
results.setting: Four LLM audit configurations: SkillScan and SkillSpector each with Deepseek and GLM-5.2 as audit models, on the 150-case benchmark
results.quote: CoRedSkill’s overall DR ranges from 3.3% to 20.0% across the four LLM audit configurations and is lower than those of SkillJect, Skill-Inject, and SCR-Bench in each configuration (Table 2).

denominator.how_counted: A composition case is counted as detected if any constituent skill is flagged as risky; fraction of the 150 benchmark cases per audit configuration

results.claim: Against runtime risk/policy defenses applied to execution records, CoRedSkill's detection rate is 10.7% under HITL and 1.3% under DefenseClaw, below ColluSkill's 32.0% under HITL.
results.setting: HITL risk rules and DefenseClaw strict policy rules (HIGH/CRITICAL) applied to recorded execution traces, proxy network requests, and installed skill files on the benchmark
results.quote: CoRedSkill’s DR is 10.7% under HITL (Shan et al., 2026) and 1.3% under DefenseClaw (Cisco AI Defense, 2026a), lower than those of Skill-Inject and SCR-Bench under both configurations (Table 3). Under HITL, its DR is also lower than ColluSkill’s 32.0%.

denominator.how_counted: For runtime auditing, detection is determined by whether the execution record triggers the audit rules; fraction of benchmark cases

results.claim: Under composition-aware auditing (all constituent skills submitted together, Deepseek audit model), CoRedSkill's overall DR rises to 28.7%, compared with 3.3% for SkillScan and 11.3% for SkillSpector under individual-package auditing, yet stays below SCR-Bench (74.0%) and ColluSkill (40.0%) under the same configuration.
results.comparison: vs 3.3% SkillScan and 11.3% SkillSpector (individual-package); SCR-Bench 74.0% and ColluSkill 40.0% (composition-aware)
results.setting: Composition-aware auditing with Deepseek receiving documentation, code, and resources of all constituent skills together, on the 150-case benchmark; this configuration has a 24.0% false-positive rate on clean compositions
results.quote: composition-aware auditing yields an overall DR of 28.7% for CoRedSkill, compared with 3.3% for SkillScan and 11.3% for SkillSpector under individual-package auditing. Under the same composition-aware audit configuration, its overall DR is lower than SCR-Bench’s 74.0% and ColluSkill’s 40.0%

denominator.how_counted: Auditor reviews all constituent skills of each case together and assesses suspicious combined behavior; fraction of the 150 benchmark cases flagged

results.claim: Attack success depends on coordination among injected skills: averaged over injection-position configurations, ASR is 0% with zero or one injected skill, 36.6% with two injected skills, and 100% with all three skills injected.
results.value: ASR 0% with zero or one injected skill, 36.6% with two, 100% with all three
results.setting: Three-skill workflows on the fixed 24-task subset (72 cases per configuration, 24 per objective), selected injected skills replaced by clean versions, other settings unchanged
results.quote: Averaged over injection-position configurations, ASR is 0% with zero or one injected skill, 36.6% with two injected skills, and 100% with all three skills injected.

denominator.how_counted: Each injection-position configuration evaluated on 72 cases from the fixed 24-task subset, with 24 cases per attack objective

results.claim: Composition size does not monotonically improve stealth: on the same 24-task subset, ASR stays 100% at all three composition sizes while overall DR ranges from 4.2% to 34.7%.
results.setting: Two-, three-, and four-skill CoRedSkill compositions on the same 24-task subset (72 cases), audited by SkillScan and SkillSpector with Deepseek and GLM
results.quote: ASR remains 100% at all three sizes, while overall DR ranges from 4.2% to 34.7% (Figure 2 and Appendix Table A3).

denominator.how_counted: Each composition size is evaluated on the same 72 cases from the fixed 24-task subset

results.claim: Static package scanners without LLM analysis (SkillFortify, CiscoSkillScan) produce zero detection on CoRedSkill's injected packages.
results.setting: SkillFortify (v0.6.0) and CiscoSkillScan (v2.0.13) static checks on benchmark skill packages; HIGH or CRITICAL rating counts as detection
results.quote: | SkillFortify | CoRedSkill (Ours) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
results.locator: Appendix Table A2 (also §4.3: 'SkillFortify and CiscoSkillScan both have zero DR for CoRedSkill')

denominator.how_counted: Static audit of each injected skill package on the benchmark (EXF/TAM/PRV columns, 50 cases each); HIGH or CRITICAL risk rating counts as a detection

limitations.statement: Attack construction relies on predefined attack specifications and workflow interfaces; automatic adaptation to arbitrary existing skill packages has not been evaluated.
limitations.quote: Attack construction in CoRedSkill relies on predefined attack specifications and workflow interfaces, and automatic adaptation to arbitrary existing skill packages has not been evaluated.

limitations.statement: Preservation of skill utility is verified only against output acceptance criteria on 150 offline evaluation cases, without dynamic service interactions or long-term operation.
limitations.quote: We verify preservation of skill utility against output acceptance criteria for 150 offline evaluation cases, without evaluating dynamic service interactions or long-term operation.

limitations.statement: Runtime defense evaluation only measures offline detection on execution records, not how online blocking affects subsequent execution and attack outcomes.
limitations.quote: Our runtime defense evaluation measures the detection capabilities of risk and policy rules using execution records, without evaluating how online blocking affects subsequent execution and attack outcomes.
