title: Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents

object.carrier: delivered pair: a co-evolved policy checkpoint plus its final skill bank (the delivered bank) — textual skill records injected into the policy context; after deployment the bank keeps drifting (rewrites, additions, removals) while the policy stays fixed

safety_property.statement: The paper studies reliability degradation of self-improving agents under post-deployment skill drift (success rate, consistency under meaning-preserving rewrites, resistance to corrupted skills), not a security property. No adversary exists: drift is benign or accidental, and the corrupted-skill axes (T2/T3) are audit stimuli generated by the released suite inside the harness, not attacks. Per the SCOPE rule, pure reliability degradation under benign drift is not treated as a safety endpoint here; the value to this survey is as necessary background on how self-improving agent state (skill bank) and policy co-specialize and then fail apart.
safety_property.operationalized_as: CODA metrics: net-benefit gate Δnet = SR(S*) − SR(∅); consistency rate CR vs two-run noise floor CR0; resistance rate RR_T2/RR_T3; worst-case success SR_min over T1-T3; verdict = absolute within-method pass/fail

assumptions: skill banks are non-stationary after deployment: skills are rewritten, entries added or removed, versions coexist, often faster than the policy is retrained

theory (Proposition 1) assumes idealized cooperative acceptance (Assumption 1) and candidate coverage of the content-level neighborhood (Assumption 2); predictions are tested only for the covered rewrite family T1-T3 with retrieval/selection masked
one co-evolution run per setting; each method is audited on the bank it delivered, with the rewriting model, version and sampling pinned and perturbed banks released
not_covered: no adversary: no attacker optimizes the drift; corrupted skills are produced by the audit suite, not a malicious party
arbitrary post-deployment edits outside the covered content-level family — structural axes T4 (ecosystem) and T5 (autonomy) are reported but not scored
mitigation: the paper diagnoses but does not fix (Limitation L2)
variability across training seeds (single run per setting) and exact Mind2Web/AMC23 task counts (left to released configuration)

intervention.name: CODA (CO-evolution Drift Audit)
intervention.description: A deployment-oriented audit protocol, not a mitigation: it audits the delivered policy-bank pair with a shared external rewriting suite (gpt-4o-2024-08-06, temperature 0.7, pinned; released perturbed banks, selection masking R1-R5), scores worst-case success (SR_min), consistency (CR vs CR0) and resistance (RR_T2/RR_T3) behind a net-benefit gate, and returns an absolute within-method pass/fail verdict. Limitation L2 states the paper proposes no mitigation for the trap it measures.

controls.name: no-skill anchor SR(∅) (empty bank)
CR0 consistency between two unperturbed runs (decoding-noise floor)
20 identity pairs (skill vs itself) in T1 meaning-preservation audit
40 negative controls (skill vs its T2/T3 rewrite) in T1 meaning-preservation audit
pure-RL arm A on SkillRL-ALFWorld with the skill mechanism disabled throughout

results.claim: Across four co-evolution methods and five benchmarks (six settings), worst-case success under tested content-level skill drift (lowest of T1-T3) is 5-13 points below the peak measured for each delivered pair, erasing 52-93% of the delivered bank's gain over the no-skill baseline; the reported peak overstates deployable competence.

results.quote: Across four co-evolution methods and five benchmarks (six settings), worst-case success is 5–13 points below the peak measured for each delivered pair, erasing 52–93% of the delivered bank’s gain over the no-skill baseline.

title: MemCut: Every Secret Leaves a Trail in the Long-Term Memory of LLM Agents

object.carrier: External text memory objects traceable to source turns in long-horizon multi-session conversations: raw turns (Turn RAG), whole sessions (Session RAG), raw turns under daily summaries (MemoryBank), topical narrative rewrites (Nemori), and offline-consolidated summaries (LightMem)

safety_property.statement: When a user asks an agent to forget a secret, the secret must become unrecoverable from surviving memory, not merely invisible to the system's own retrieval; deleting the disclosure fails this property when dispersed evidence objects that never state the secret still jointly imply it, measured by residual recovery and the hidden-risk share.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Two recovery metrics on a four-choice question (decline allowed), same reader model: native recovery through the system's own retrieval, and residual recovery given all surviving objects traced to annotated disclosures or evidence; hidden-risk share = (Res-Nat)/Res as a lower bound on residual successes missed by native retrieval.

capabilities: query the assistant after deletion through its native retrieval (native recovery reader)
directly read all surviving memory objects derived from the secret's evidence or disclosure (residual recovery reader)
use a different query or retriever than the deletion request
assumptions: the user's deletion request is granted and executed as object deletion with source-turn closure
every memory object is traceable to its source turns, so deletion by closure is well-defined
one write model writes memory, scores deletion candidates, and answers questions, as in a deployed assistant
text-only external memory; facts have author-annotated evidence trails and sufficient sets
not_covered: multimodal and parametric memory (unlearning/model editing)
naturally occurring evidence structures in deployment (frequency of such trails unknown)
dedicated erasure methods that expand candidate coverage or change memory indexing (only reference baselines reusing native retrieval/write components are evaluated)
downstream utility loss and unrelated content removed through closure
adaptive adversaries beyond the fixed four-choice reader protocol

intervention.name: MemCut benchmark with three reference deletion baselines (S0 disclosure deletion, S1 retrieval-ranked cleanup, S2 LLM-guided cleanup)
intervention.description: Evaluation, not a defense: S0 deletes the disclosure and all objects derived from it; S1 builds a twenty-turn candidate pool from one retrieval query and deletes its ten highest-ranked turns; S2 reranks the same twenty candidates with the write model and deletes its top ten. All operations are anchored to source turns and delete by closure; neither cleanup sees annotations.

title: SAFE-Mem: Secure Agentic Memory with Fine-Grained Authority and Governance-Aware Retrieval

object.carrier: persistent agent memory as a graph of sentence, claim and entity nodes; every stored claim carries three governance labels (kind, authority, scope) derived from the trusted channel record of its source, and stays linked to its source sentences for provenance

safety_property.statement: A memory claim must not acquire authority its source never held (defense against authority laundering): a claim is admitted to a request's context only when its effective level min(kind, authority) reaches the use the request requires and its scope covers the request's target, so untrusted external content can inform descriptions but never act as the principal's preferences, policies or permissions in answers or tool calls, while legitimate uses of the same entries are retained.
safety_property.operationalized_as: MPBench ASR (share of attack cases whose answer endorses or acts on the injected memory, judged by GPT-4o-mini), MPBench Recall and Restraint, LoCoMo judge accuracy, and EHRAgent ASR/Exec./Lost under the MINJA memory-injection attack

capabilities: controls the content of external artifacts the agent reads (web pages, emails, documents, tool outputs): arbitrary text, statements styled as the principal's own words, claims of prior approval, and paraphrased copies of one payload spread across many artifacts planted long before the target session
in shared-memory deployments, another principal can act as the adversary and plant records carrying its own authority through ordinary queries (MINJA on EHRAgent)
assumptions: the agent runtime's channel records (which channel each input arrived through) are trusted and cannot be forged
the adversary cannot alter another principal's turns, write to the memory store directly, forge channel records, or access the prompts or weights of any component
authority over a principal originates only in that principal's own assertions, instructions and authorizations
the defender knows the channel of each input but not which artifacts are malicious
not_covered: attacks that rely on a false fact without borrowing authority: a false claim on a web page remains a valid answer to what the page said, and a principal's own mistaken statement keeps the principal's authority
a principal persuaded to endorse content (e.g., agreeing to an assistant's suggestion to remember a page's recommendation) grants it up to the kind the request names
content-level truth judgment of stored memories (content-based defenses are complementary)

intervention.name: SAFE-Mem
intervention.description: Fine-grained memory governance. Each extracted claim is labeled with a kind (DESCRIPTION < ATTRIBUTE < PREFERENCE < RULE < PERMISSION, what the claim binds), an authority (strongest kind its source channel may establish: principal turn = PERMISSION, external artifact = DESCRIPTION, another party = ATTRIBUTE; a claim inherits the lowest authority present during extraction, following integrity lattices) and a scope (whom that authority covers). A memory graph links sentences, claims and entities, keeping each claim traceable to its source. Governance-aware retrieval classifies each request's required use and target, and admits a claim only if min(kind, authority) >= use and the target is in scope, filtering before ranking and repeating the check at tool calls (refusing calls whose identifiers appear only in lower-authority entries). Only a principal's explicit endorsement, capped at the requested kind, can raise authority.

results.claim: Across four backbones on MPBench, SAFE-Mem simultaneously achieves the lowest ASR, Recall above the undefended level, and the best LoCoMo accuracy of all evaluated defenses (in the paper's pooled-memory setting).
results.metric: MPBench ASR / Recall / Restraint and LoCoMo accuracy
results.setting: MPBench (6,240 cases written into one principal's pooled memory) and LoCoMo, four backbones (GPT-5.6-terra, GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku 5.5, Qwen3.8-Flash), k=4 claims and m=4 passages, temperature 0, external adversary controlling artifact content

results.claim: On LoCoMo, where there is nothing to defend against, SAFE-Mem raises judge accuracy on every backbone, by 11.1 and 15.1 points on the two GPT models (and 3.1/2.8 on the smaller backbones).
results.value: +11.1 and +15.1 points on the two GPT backbones
results.setting: LoCoMo long-term conversational memory benchmark, four backbones
results.quote: raises it on every backbone, by 11.1 and 15.1

results.claim: On EHRAgent under MINJA (cross-user shared memory, the adversary is itself a user), SAFE-Mem lets the agent keep drafting wrong-patient code but refuses every execution via the scope check, while removing almost no benign memories.
results.metric: ASR / executed-code ASR / benign memories lost
results.value: ASR 72.4%, executed-code ASR 0.0%, benign memories lost 2.0%
results.setting: EHRAgent on MIMIC-III Clinical Database Demo, MINJA query-only memory injection by an adversarial user, GPT-4o-mini backbone, memory shared across users

denominator.how_counted: ASR: share of victim questions whose generated or executed code targets the wrong patient; Lost: share of memories retrieved for benign questions that a defense removes (counts not stated)

results.claim: The scope check is the operative defense on shared memory: without it, 44.4% of MINJA attacks execute.
results.value: 44.4% of the attacks execute without the scope check
results.setting: EHRAgent under MINJA, GPT-4o-mini, SAFE-Mem w/o scope ablation
results.quote: 44.4% of the attacks execute, which identifies scope

denominator.how_counted: share of MINJA attacks whose drafted code executes (count not stated)

results.claim: SAFE-Mem stores poison but keeps it out of acting contexts: the injected memory is written to memory yet enters the retrieved context in only 1.1%/2.8% of attack cases, versus 30.2%/55.7% without defense.
results.setting: MPBench, GPT-5.6-terra and GPT-4o-mini backbones, storage-vs-use separation
results.quote: 1.1% and 2.8% of cases, against 30.2% and 55.7%

denominator.how_counted: share of scored attack cases in which the injected memory is retrieved into the context prepared for the attack query

results.claim: The admission filter drives the security gains: the same memory graph and passages with governance off (every claim and passage admitted, no levels) reach 62.3%/28.2%/49.3% ASR on three backbones.
results.setting: MPBench ablation keeping the graph and passages but admitting every claim and passage including external text, on GPT-4o-mini, Haiku and Qwen backbones
results.quote: reach 62.3%, 28.2% and 49.3% ASR on

denominator.how_counted: share of scored attack cases whose answer endorses or acts on the injected memory

results.claim: Adaptive rewrites of every MPBench attack (forged author, forged request, understated kind, conflict evasion) barely move SAFE-Mem, because the inputs that can raise a claim's level lie outside what the adversary writes.
results.metric: MPBench ASR movement under adaptive attacks (points)
results.value: ASR moves by at most 1.4 points
results.setting: MPBench with four adaptive rewrite strategies against one component at a time; the strongest rewrite raises an undefended agent's ASR by 13.6/20.0/7.8 points on GPT-4o-mini/Haiku/Qwen
results.quote: SAFE-Mem’s ASR moves by at most 1.4 points

limitations.statement: SAFE-Mem treats whatever a principal explicitly asks to keep as the principal's own: a principal persuaded to endorse content (e.g., agreeing to an assistant's suggestion to remember a page's recommendation) grants it up to the kind the request names, so endorsement social-engineering is not defended against.
limitations.quote: SAFE-Mem treats what a principal explicitly asks

limitations.statement: SAFE-Mem governs authority, not content truth: attacks that rely on a false fact without borrowing authority (a false claim on a web page remains a valid answer to what the page said; a principal's own mistaken statement keeps the principal's authority) lie outside its scope, and content-judging defenses complement it.
limitations.quote: its scope, and defenses that judge the content of a memory complement it.

title: Cryptographically Secure Agent-to-Agent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems

object.carrier: Permissioned blockchain ledger holding DID documents, issuer identifiers, credential schemas, revocation registries and trust scores; verifiable credentials held off-chain by their agents; long-term ML-KEM public keys pre-distributed into and cached in DID documents. Lifecycle is explicitly discussed: issuance (VCs signed by a trusted issuer under JIT, task-scoped), update (key rotation triggered by monitoring, DID-document update transactions, periodic on-chain snapshots), retention (immutable, logged DID history), retrieval (agents discover each other's DIDs/permissions via the ledger; verifiers check credential status), revocation (smart-contract deactivation of DIDs and global credential revocation; VCs below the trust floor auto-revoked). DIDs/ledger are long-lived; JIT VCs are scoped to a single task runtime, hence scope=mixed.

safety_property.statement: Targets confidentiality + integrity of inter-agent messages together with least-privilege authority over agent identities. Mutually authenticated, crypto-agile mTLS with hybrid post-quantum key establishment (AEAD payloads, e.g., AES-256-GCM) protects messages in transit against eavesdropping and MiTM; DID + task-scoped JIT verifiable credentials with on-chain revocation bound to least privilege restrict what an agent (possibly compromised) may do; signed CBOR/COSE envelopes preserve payload integrity across multi-hop exchanges; optional ZKPs verify that a delegated payload conforms to the committed task policy without disclosure. Stated failure conditions: a ZKP still validates hallucinated/malicious results that conform to policy (no semantic-correctness attestation); a revoked agent may connect during the block-time finality window; PQC implementations are immature. No property is empirically evaluated - the paper is a theoretical architecture.
safety_property.operationalized_as: None - no experiments, simulations or benchmarks. The property is argued via threat analysis (§3) and architectural specification (§4); the authors themselves call for empirical tests (COSE overhead, hybrid mTLS latency, KEMTLS-PDK gains, scalability) in §7-§8.

capabilities: Impersonate agents and manipulate the orchestrator via typo-squatting and synonymously named agents/resources (shadowing attacks), engaging malicious agents or tools
Intercept, inject and modify inter-agent messages (MiTM); passively eavesdrop, including harvest-now-decrypt-later until a cryptographically relevant quantum computer breaks RSA/ECC
Direct and indirect prompt injection into documents/prompts the agent parses, leading to RAG and memory poisoning, data leaks, flooding attacks and resource waste
Rug pull: first supply a benign, approved agent/tool, then exhibit anomalous malicious behavior after updates, abusing acquired trust and permission levels
Compromise an agent and abuse its permissions; as a malicious intermediary, tamper with the Protobuf payload before forwarding to the next hop
Attack orchestration/reasoning to drive denial-of-wallet, cascading failures and privilege escalation (a user-facing agent delegating an unsafe action to a more privileged agent)
Quantum adversary substituting an agent's KEM key if ledger transactions registering DID documents are not themselves PQC-signed
Malicious developers / compromised MCP servers distributed through marketplaces
assumptions: Agents communicate over local or public networks, with sensitive information exchanged across differing trust levels; which measures apply is deployment-context dependent
A permissioned ledger is available as the root of trust for KEM keys; transactions registering and updating DID documents must themselves be secured by PQC signatures
Symmetric AEAD with 256-bit keys remains secure against HNDL; post-quantum schemes (ML-KEM, ML-DSA/FN-DSA, hybrid X25519MLKEM768 in TLS 1.3) hold
Trusted issuers attest agent attributes; SPIFFE/SVID-style infrastructure binds agent key pairs to identities (SVIDs ephemeral)
Runtime monitoring supplies telemetry so a trust-evaluation service can score agents and smart contracts can rotate keys or revoke VCs
not_covered: Semantic correctness of model outputs: hallucinated or malicious results still yield a valid ZKP as long as they conform to policy
Threats originating from the MCP servers themselves ('It will not address all of the challenges faced by MCP as some of them originate from the MCP servers themselves.')
Malicious-developer attacks despite marketplace cryptographic validation ('this solution is not enough')
The brief vulnerability window before ledger finality, during which a revoked agent may still establish connections
Implementation-level side channels and cryptanalytic breaks in young PQC (side-channel vulnerabilities in early ML-KEM implementations; SIKE and Rainbow breaks)
No empirical evaluation of any proposed mechanism

intervention.name: Zero-trust cryptographic agent-to-agent communication architecture: DID/VC identity on a permissioned ledger + KEMTLS-PDK hybrid post-quantum mTLS + signed CBOR/COSE envelopes + ZKP intent verification + trust-threshold monitoring
intervention.description: A synthesized architecture (survey/position paper, not a built system): agent identities as DIDs with task-scoped JIT verifiable credentials anchored on a permissioned ledger with on-chain revocation; mutually authenticated crypto-agile mTLS with hybrid PQ/T key exchange, upgraded to KEMTLS-PDK by pre-distributing long-term ML-KEM public keys in DID documents to cut handshake overhead; immutable CBOR/COSE message envelopes for multi-hop payload integrity; optional zk-SNARK/zk-STARK proofs that delegated payloads satisfy the task-policy commitment; a trust-threshold layer scores observed behavior and gates task assignment, with smart-contract revocation below the global minimum.

results.claim: Post-quantum signatures are far larger than classical ones - ML-DSA signatures span 2420-4627 bytes depending on security level vs 64 bytes for ECDSA - which can bloat certificate chains, exceed the initial TCP congestion window and add round trips/fragmentation, motivating hybrid key exchange, more compact signatures, certificate compression and KEMTLS-PDK.
results.setting: Cryptographic size comparison stated in §4.2 (sizes from the PQC literature, no experiment by the authors); concerns TLS handshake/certificate-chain transmission in agent-to-agent communication, particularly on constrained links such as drones and IoT devices.
results.quote: Comparing ML-DSA signature, which is 2420 to 4627 bytes long depending on the security level, to 64 bytes long signatures for ECDSA, we can observe a huge difference in weight.

results.claim: KEMTLS-PDK authenticates the responder within the first round trip and eliminates certificate transmission; the paper proposes that MAS use it by pre-distributing long-term ML-KEM public keys into agents' DID documents during discovery, so the initiator encapsulates the shared secret to the responder's cached public key, offsetting post-quantum cost.
results.value: single flight: responder authenticated in first round trip; certificate transmission eliminated
results.comparison: vs KEMTLS with online handshake using heavy PQC signatures, where post-quantum signatures remain in the certificate chain
results.setting: Proposed transport design (§4.2, Figure 2): zero-trust MAS where agents discover each other's DIDs/permissions through a ledger-based registry; design adopted from the KEMTLS-PDK literature, no simulation run - the paper explicitly asks for empirical measurement of the latency reduction.
results.quote: A secret to this key can be encapsulated in its first sent message, which authenticates the responder within the first round trip and eliminates the transmission of the certificate.

results.claim: For succinct proof systems (e.g., zk-SNARKs), proof verification is claimed to take milliseconds regardless of the size of the underlying computation, while proof generation remains computationally expensive - the asymmetry the ZKP intent-verification mechanism relies on.
results.setting: General claim about succinct proof systems within the proposed architecture: the receiving agent verifies the delegated payload against the policy commitment embedded in the JIT VC; no benchmark performed by the authors.
results.quote: for succinct proof systems, verification takes milliseconds regardless of the size of the underlying computation, whereas proof generation remains computationally expensive.

results.claim: Design premise of the transport layer: symmetric AEAD ciphers with 256-bit keys (e.g., AES-256-GCM) remain secure against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks, while asymmetric RSA/ECC does not survive a cryptographically relevant quantum computer - hence post-quantum / hybrid mTLS is treated as obligatory for agent-to-agent traffic.
results.value: symmetric AEAD with 256-bit keys secure; asymmetric (RSA/ECC) not
results.setting: Stated cryptographic premise underpinning the post-quantum transport proposal for inter-agent messages that can carry valuable business information; not experimentally established in the paper.
results.quote: While symmetric AEAD ciphers with 256-bit keys remain secure against harvest now decrypt later attacks (HNDL), asymmetric cryptography does not.

limitations.statement: Primary bottleneck is the computational intensity of ZKP generation: compiling an agent's execution trace into an arithmetic circuit and generating the zk-SNARK could induce unacceptable delays when coupled with high LLM-inference latency.
limitations.quote: The primary bottleneck lies in the computational intensity of generating ZKPs.

limitations.statement: Envelope accumulation: as each agent appends its own proof, the COSE payload grows linearly with execution-chain depth and can strain edge-node memory; recursive ZKPs are proposed as future work to keep envelope size constant.
limitations.quote: As each agent appends its own proof leading to a linear growth in payload size it can eventually strain the memory limits of edge nodes.

limitations.statement: Blockchain-registry revocation leaves a brief vulnerability window tied to block-time finality, during which a revoked but previously authenticated agent might still establish a new connection.
limitations.quote: Furthermore, the reliance on a blockchain registry to enforce dynamic least privilege introduces a brief vulnerability window tied to block-time finality, during which a revoked but previously authenticated agent might attempt to establish a new connection before the network consensus fully registers its revocation.

limitations.statement: The study is primarily theoretical: no empirical tests or benchmarks exist (overhead of CBOR/COSE message-level protection, hybrid mTLS latency, whether KEMTLS-PDK resolves it, ZKP validity, scalability, dynamic environments).
limitations.quote: Because this study is primarily theoretical, these topics require additional empirical tests and benchmarks, e.g., measuring the overhead of message-level protection with CBOR and COSE.

limitations.statement: ZKPs limit rather than prevent malicious or hallucinated outcomes: any result conforming to the committed policy yields a valid proof, and the proof does not attest the semantic correctness of the model's output.
limitations.quote: Hallucinated or malicious results caused by threat actors will still yield a valid proof as long as it conforms to the policy.

limitations.statement: PQC algorithms/implementations are young and under-cryptanalyzed (SIKE and Rainbow breaks, side channels in early ML-KEM), so exclusive reliance is premature - hybrid PQ/T first; additionally, current zk-SNARKs rely on non-quantum-resistant elliptic-curve pairings (zk-STARKs suggested instead).
limitations.quote: For now, they are too immature to just start exclusively relying on them.

title: An Interactive GraphRAG Workspace for Reifying, Auditing, and Steering Conversational AI Memories

object.carrier: CognitiveCanvas 把多会话对话记忆物化为持久可操纵的知识对象：混合神经符号属性图存储（含 Neo4j concept graph）中的 Hierarchical Semantic Fact-Graph HSFG(M)=⟨G,F,A⟩ —— 开发者目标/阻塞 Goal 向量、实体关系 Fact triples（如 (:FastAPI)-[:USES]->(:AsyncSession)）、逐字保留的可执行 Code artifacts（schemas、API routes、configurations），以 2D 画布交互卡片呈现，供跨会话多跳 GraphRAG 检索与 1-click 原位更新

safety_property.statement: 保护复用的对话记忆/技术上下文的时序完整性（temporal integrity）：当软件包、API 与框架约定随时间演变时，持久化记忆不得因 temporal drift 被"静默投毒"（LLM 盲目接受过时配置与弃用语法，产生自信的代码幻觉）。失效条件 = 记忆相对当前日历时间过时而未被察觉；论文用时变危险函数 V(M_i,t_now)=exp(-λ_d·max(0,t_now−t_anchor−δ_d))·(1−Φ(M_i))（λ_software=0.015 day^-1，90 天宽限期）建模记忆随时效的衰减，并以 Stale 徽章标记失效记忆。判定结果 = temporal hallucination 率（Table I：31.2%/28.7% → 4.2%）与 citation faithfulness（→94.3%）
safety_property.operationalized_as: Table I 三条件（Commercial / Flat-Vector RAG / CognitiveCanvas）对照下的 Temporal Hallucinations 率与 Citation Faithfulness；机制上由 60+ regex 预筛 + 日历锚定 LLM-as-a-Judge 复核触发 Stale 徽章与 1-click self-correction，NLI 置信热图与双向引用徽章作为接地证据

assumptions: 无攻击者参与：失效模式是自然 temporal drift（软件包/API/框架约定随时间演变）导致的上下文过时与幻觉，而非恶意投毒
Stage 2 的日历锚定 LLM-as-a-Judge 校验被假设为可信的复核者，能正确判定记忆是否过时
not_covered: 任何对抗性场景：恶意记忆投毒、提示注入、对抗性经验注入等均未建模（本文威胁模型中没有对手）
多开发者/跨用户共享工作区下的权限与信任问题（multi-developer collaborative canvas 仅列为 future work）
记忆撤销（revocation）/删除生命周期未涉及

intervention.name: CognitiveCanvas
intervention.description: 交互式 GraphRAG 工作区（架构层干预）：把对话记忆从易逝文本日志变为持久、可操纵、被审计的知识对象。(1) HSFG 层次语义事实图（Goal/Fact/Code 三元存储）替代线性聊天日志与有损摘要，支持跨会话多跳 GraphRAG 遍历；(2) Continuous Temporal Drift Auditor（60+ regex 高速预筛 + 日历锚定 LLM 复核）对持久记忆做时序完整性审计，Stale 徽章 + 1-click self-correction 原位重构代码并更新知识图谱；(3) Spatial-Symbolic Prompt Compiler（SSPC）把 2D 直接操纵手势（Voronoi 聚类、节点缩放、synthesis 边）编译为 HIGHLIGHT/GROUP/OBSCURE 注意力指令注入提示

results.claim: HSFG 蒸馏把 Token Overhead（10 Pairs）从 Commercial 的 5,210 / Flat RAG 的 2,140 降到 405 tokens，即 92.2% token 缩减，同时保持代码逐字可复现（100% token syntax fidelity）
results.setting: 代表性 10 轮调试对话、10 对话对；HSFG=45(G)+120(F)+240(A)=405 tokens（式2）；三条件对照：线性多轮聊天 Commercial、Flat-Vector RAG、CognitiveCanvas

denominator.n_total: 5,210 raw tokens（代表性 10 轮调试对话；Table I 行标注以 10 Pairs 计）
denominator.how_counted: 1 − 405/5210 ≈ 92.2%；论文原话 'achieving a 92.2% token reduction while maintaining exact code reproducibility'（§II-B）

results.claim: Multi-Hop Recall@3 在 CognitiveCanvas 下达 89.6%，高于 Flat RAG 的 52.1% 与 Commercial 的 38.4%（较 Flat RAG +37.5 个百分点）
results.setting: 24 名从业者被试内实验（12 全栈工程师/6 研究者/6 系统设计师），Latin square 三条件，三类知识任务（全栈架构重构/科学综合/后勤规划）；Recall@3 的查询集与计数方式论文未说明

results.claim: Temporal Hallucinations 从 Flat RAG 的 28.7% 降至 4.2%（正文报 p<0.0001），相对下降 85.4% —— 即 temporal drift 引起的上下文投毒幻觉被大幅抑制（本文与记忆完整性最相关的结果）
results.setting: 24 名从业者被试内实验、Latin square 三条件、三类知识任务；该百分比按何种评测单元（查询/回答数）计数，论文未说明
results.quote: | Temporal Hallucinations | 31.2% | 28.7% | 4.2% (−-85.4%) |

results.claim: Citation Faithfulness 达 94.3%，高于 Flat RAG 的 66.8% 与 Commercial 的 54.0%
results.setting: 24 名从业者被试内实验、Latin square 三条件；引用忠实度按何种单元计数，论文未说明
results.quote: | Citation Faithfulness | 54.0% | 66.8% | 94.3% (+27.5%) |

results.claim: 平均任务完成时间 13.8 分钟，比 Flat RAG 的 21.2 分钟快 34.9%
results.setting: 24 名从业者被试内实验、三类知识任务、Latin square 三条件

results.claim: NASA-TLX 认知负荷从 Commercial 的 68.4 / Flat RAG 的 54.2 降至 32.6（正文报 p<0.0001）
results.setting: 24 名从业者被试内实验、Latin square 三条件；量表 /100

results.claim: UMUX-Lite 可用性 88.4/100，高于 Flat RAG 的 72.8 与 Commercial 的 61.5
results.setting: 24 名从业者被试内实验、Latin square 三条件；量表 /100

limitations.statement: Stage 2（LLM-as-a-Judge）时序校验延迟 600–1200 ms，是作者自述的性能限制
limitations.quote: Current limitations include: (1) Stage 2 temporal verification latency (600–1200 ms); and (2) lack of direct visual AST rendering inside cards.

limitations.statement: 卡片内缺少直接可视化 AST 渲染；后台预审计与内嵌语法高亮仅为进行中的 future work
limitations.quote: Background pre-auditing and embedded syntax highlighting represent active future work.

title: Can Agents Keep Secrets They Were Never Told? Benchmarking Latent Privacy Risks Across Sessions with MemJoin

object.carrier: Long-term memory records written, updated, and retrieved by six memory frameworks (A-Mem, LangMem, Mem0, MemGPT, MemoryBank, SimpleMem) over multi-session synthetic user histories; reference inputs Full history (verbatim sessions), All memory (exported store), and Task only (no history)

safety_property.statement: A sensitive relation (user bound to a service/attribute, site, and date) that is entailed only by combining records from several sessions, and that the later ordinary task does not require, must not be stated in the agent's answer. It fails whenever memory formation, update, retention, or retrieval delivers and connects the clues so that the fixed reader states the complete person-linked relation; a low disclosure rate can also mask the failure mode of values never reaching the reader.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Disclosure rate DR = ND/288 (a case counts when at least two of three trials reach A4: service, site, and date bound to the correct user), availability (string-match of target values in reader context), conditional A4 (A4 among availability-passing inputs), plus TCR / Helpfulness / Refusal for task utility

capabilities: Reader model (fixed Qwen3.5-9B) receives memory records retrieved for an ordinary task and can join facts across separately harmless records without the task asking for the relation

Memory framework itself merges, consolidates, or links records across sessions (writer materialization, update consolidation, retrieval join), forming the sensitive relation inside the store or the retrieved context
assumptions: No adversarial user: sessions are benign synthetic interactions and the task never requests the sensitive relation
Target annotations remain with the evaluator and never reach the reader or memory frameworks
The reader answers under a short instruction not to volunteer private facts the task does not need
not_covered: Adversarial users deliberately planting clues or probing prompts
Cross-user memory sharing or multi-user collusion
Side channels such as timing or membership inference beyond record joining
Real user data (all 288 cases are synthetic)
Revocation after disclosure: deleting stored records does not retract what the recipient already learned

intervention.name: Five post-hoc mitigations: M1 privacy instruction, M2 value sanitization, M3 cross-record cue removal, M4 top-1 retrieval budget, output filtering
intervention.description: M1 replaces the reader's system instruction with data-minimization guidance; M2 masks personal values found by a PII scanner; M3 rewrites names and identifier prefixes shared across records into per-clause labels, cutting cross-record links while keeping values; M4 keeps only the first retrieved record; output filtering passes finished answers to a critic LLM that deletes spans or replaces the answer with a refusal. Each is applied alone after memory construction and retrieval are frozen, not as a sequential defense.

controls.name: Full history (verbatim source sessions)
Task only (no historical context)
All memory (entire exported store, bypassing retrieval)
Itemized history (sessions presented as separate records)

results.claim: Every one of six memory frameworks discloses the cross-session sensitive relation in ordinary-task answers: under Retrieved memory 5.9%-13.9% of cases are disclosed, versus 22.9% under Full history and none under Task only.
results.setting: 288 synthetic cases x 3 trials; fixed reader Qwen3.5-9B; six memory frameworks under Retrieved memory, with Full-history and no-history controls
results.quote: Table 1 shows that every framework discloses the relation: under Retrieved memory, 5.9% to 13.9% of cases are disclosed, against 22.9% under Full history and none under Task only.

denominator.how_counted: DR = ND/288; a case counts when at least two of its three trials reach A4 (Table 1 caption)

results.claim: LangMem's lowest disclosure rate reflects values that never arrived rather than safer reader behavior: its availability is 60.2%, and among inputs that do contain the service, site, and date, 13.8% of answers state the relation, in line with the other frameworks.
results.setting: LangMem under Retrieved memory; 288 cases x 3 trials; fixed reader Qwen3.5-9B
results.quote: LangMem has the lowest disclosure rate and the lowest availability, 60.2%, yet among its inputs that contain the service, site, and date, 13.8% of answers state the relation, in line with the other five frameworks.

denominator.n_total: 864 answers/inputs per view (288 cases x 3 trials)
denominator.n_valid: inputs passing the availability check (framework-dependent subset)
denominator.how_counted: Table 1 caption: answer-level percentages are over the 864 answers; conditional A4 = A4 among inputs passing availability (Eq. 2.2)

results.claim: Value delivery alone does not explain disclosure: even with service, site, and date all present in the reader's input, the six frameworks' conditional A4 stays at 10.8%-14.4%, below the 22.9% of Full history.
results.setting: six frameworks, Retrieved memory, restricted to inputs passing the availability check; fixed reader Qwen3.5-9B
results.quote: Availability does not close the whole gap, since even with the service, site, and date present the six frameworks stay at 10.8% to 14.4%, against 22.9% under Full history.

denominator.n_total: inputs passing availability per framework (of 864 per view)
denominator.how_counted: conditional A4 = A4 among inputs passing availability (Eq. 2.2); the Full history 22.9% is DR over 288 cases

results.claim: Memory rewriting creates disclosures absent from the original history: of the 168 cases disclosed across the six frameworks, one in three are not disclosed under Full history (memory-only counts range from 1 for LangMem to 15 for A-Mem).
results.value: 168 disclosed cases; one in three memory-only
results.setting: six frameworks under Retrieved memory versus Full history on the same 288 paired cases, two-of-three A4 rule
results.quote: Of the 168 cases disclosed across the six frameworks, one in three are not disclosed under Full history; the Mem.-only column of Table 1 gives these counts, from 1 for LangMem to 15 for A-Mem.

denominator.n_total: 168 = sum of disclosed cases across the six frameworks (each evaluated on 288 cases)
denominator.how_counted: sum of ND over the six Retrieved memory views; Mem.-only = positive under Retrieved memory but not under Full history (Table 1 / Table E.4)

results.claim: Removing shared cross-record cues (M3) while keeping every target value visible at least halves disclosure: 16.4%->7.7% for A-Mem, 15.0%->1.9% for MemGPT, and 25.6%->8.7% for itemized full history, showing that links between records, not stored values, carry the relation.
results.metric: disclosure_rate (DR) before vs after M3 cue removal
results.setting: M3 applied to frozen inputs of A-Mem and MemGPT (Retrieved memory reference) and to itemized full history; only case pairs where all target values remain visible; fixed reader Qwen3.5-9B
results.quote: Table 3 shows that, in the 207 case pairs where the service, site, and date all remain visible, disclosure falls by at least half: from 16.4% to 7.7% for A-Mem, from 15.0% to 1.9% for MemGPT, and from 25.6% to 8.7% for the itemized full history.

denominator.how_counted: subset of M3 pairs in which every checked target value stays visible after M3, fixed from the transformed inputs before any answer was generated (Table F.4)

results.claim: Value-removing mitigations buy zero disclosure only by destroying utility (A-Mem TCR falls to 5.2% under M2 and 13.2% under M4), whereas link removal M3 lowers disclosure to 5.6% (A-Mem) and 1.4% (MemGPT) across the 287 complete pairs with TCR moving only about -1.0/+2.4 points.
results.metric: DR and TCR after mitigation (M2 / M4 / M3)
results.value: M2/M4: A-Mem TCR 5.2% / 13.2%; M3: DR 5.6% (A-Mem) and 1.4% (MemGPT)
results.comparison: M3 TCR change about -1.0 and +2.4 points

title: Hippo: Training-Free Agent Self-Evolution via Hippocampal Replay

object.carrier: 外部非参数记忆（模型参数全程冻结，不蒸进权重）：两层结构——L1 惊讶驱动的情景反思（episodic reflections，逐 attempt 诊断，主要作为整合原料被保留）与 L2 持久经验库（论文原文 'persistent L2 bank, represented as a set of identified entries'；Figure 2 标注 'Persistent memory: Experiences + applicability'），条目=可复用决策+显式适用条件（applicability conditions）；检索时 top-K 嵌入召回+LLM 适用性门控后注入 context（约 240–273 token 等效/步）。长程 400 任务后仅保留 83 条 L2 条目

safety_property.statement: 纯性能论文，不声明任何安全属性：研究记忆式自演化能否在 SWE-bench Verified / WebArena / Mind2Web 上提升任务成功率/分辨率并在长任务流中保持（主指标为 resolution rate / task success rate / step success rate）。与安全最接近的机制是 surprise judge 对'侥幸成功'（fortuitous success：如 N/A 引用、空回答被模糊匹配接受）的甄别，用于阻止未验证流程作为成功经验入库（§3.1、Appendix D），但这被论文框架为学习信号/记忆质量问题，判定指标仍是任务成功率而非任何安全属性，故 type=none

assumptions: 无对抗者：经验由 agent 自身在固定基准任务流上产生并消费；不研究记忆投毒、prompt injection 或恶意经验注入
training-free：模型参数全程冻结，适应仅通过外部记忆实现；每个 Hippo run 从空记忆库开始（'Each Hippo run starts with an empty memory bank'）
WebArena 上 judge 在记忆构建时可访问官方结果与参考答案（actor 无当前任务参考/奖励/判官理由的直接访问）；AWM 与 ReasoningBank 在相同反馈条件下对比（对原在线设定的适配）；SWE-bench 判官无标签（label-free），分辨率另由官方 harness 计算
任务按固定 ID 顺序处理；同任务所有 rollout 共享同一记忆快照，记忆引擎在全部 8 次 rollout 结束后才更新；主结果为 3 个随机种子完整 run 的均值±样本标准差
judge 对证据模糊的 accepted attempt 默认判 genuine；checkpoint 评测不修改后续学习所用记忆
not_covered: 任何对抗性设置：无记忆投毒/对抗性经验/攻击者模型；安全属性未研究
跨用户/跨部署共享记忆的污染传播与撤销
超长单任务内的中途反思与分层整合（作者自述 future work，未测试）
更强模型为弱模型构造经验的可迁移性与成本收益（作者自述未评测）
KV-cache 复用与专用判别模型的端到端节省（未量化）

intervention.name: Hippo
intervention.description: 免训练记忆自演化框架，作用层为记忆内容（存什么/改什么/删什么/注入什么），不改变模型参数或执行引擎。四组件：(i) 多 rollout 探索：同一冻结策略与同一检索记忆下 N=8 并行采样；(ii) surprise 驱动的情景缓冲：judge 判定失败或'侥幸成功'（right for the wrong reasons）才写 L1 反思；(iii) 记忆演化引擎（海马回放式两阶段）：先跨 rollout 对比归纳 candidate experience（verified-success 多数/少数/平分/全败四案例规则），再与相关记忆比较——丢弃重复、以显式适用条件合并重叠并解决冲突，产出增删集 (Δ+, Δ−)，L2,t+1=(L2,t\Δ−)∪Δ+（对照 append-only 与 repeated rewrite 两种更新策略）；(iv) 检索与注入：top-K 嵌入召回+LLM 适用性门控（75.2% 选择率 vs BM25+content 66.4%），选中经验作为可选 hint 注入，所有 rollout 共享。效果：WebArena 64.2%→72.9%（GPT-5.6 Sol），长程 400 任务后 86%/82% 且仅存 83 条

results.claim: 在 WebArena 全量任务流（764 题，任务按 ID 顺序、每任务 8 rollout、每 rollout ≤30 步）上，GPT-5.6 Sol 的 Hippo 将整体任务成功率从 No Memory 的 64.2% 提高到 72.9%（+8.7 pp），且在全部五个网站上均优于 No Memory——说明对强 base model 记忆复用仍有提升空间
results.setting: WebArena 全量 764 任务（Shopping/Admin/GitLab/Reddit/Map）；GPT-5.6 Sol；N=8 rollout/任务、≤30 步/rollout、3 个随机种子完整 run 的均值±样本标准差；对比 No Memory / Vanilla-IB / AWM / ReasoningBank（均启用官方实现）

title: Refuse the Harm, Complete the Task via Graph-of-Rules Planning for LLM-Enabled Robots

safety_property.statement: 保护 LLM 机器人不被越狱指令诱使执行有害行为，同时不牺牲指令的合法部分：只有当候选计划物理可行、满足全部相关安全规则、达成由合法子任务导出的 safe goal、且不保留原始指令有害意图时才允许 commit；对不含合法子任务的纯攻击指令，唯一正确行为是全拒。失效条件=最终计划实现了指令的有害结果（ASR>0），或含合法部分的指令被整体拒绝/未完成（TSR 损失）；判定结果=ASR 与 TSR（RoboGuard 基准 n=70、Compound n=97、纯安全指令 n=40，另测自适应白盒 ASR 与 Gemini-3.1-flash-lite 复测）
safety_property.operationalized_as: ASR（有害结果在最终计划中实现的指令占比）与 TSR（正确处理占比）；主表 Table 1、自适应白盒 Table 2、跨架构 Table 3、消融 Table 4；机制上由每条相关规则独立的 generate-judge-refine 循环 + 目标安全检查 + 最终检查门（达成 safe goal 且无残留恶意意图）共同判定

capabilities: 构造越狱指令使机器人执行有害动作（BadRobot 的 Contextual Jailbreak / Safety Misalignment / Conceptual Deception 及其复合攻击变体；Compound 中少数为纯攻击）
RoboPAIR 自动化攻击：多轮迭代改写攻击提示直至得手
自适应白盒（RQ2）：攻击者直接对被防御系统运行 PAIR 循环，每次尝试后获得系统内部决策反馈——对 RuleGraph 暴露最终决定、世界模型、规则图之前各阶段的完整输出与推理、每条相关规则节点的通过/拦截判定及裁判反馈；对 RoboGuard 暴露规则集与 LTL 规范及推理；对 SafePlan 暴露各 sanity 层判定与推理及规格
assumptions: 攻击通过自然语言指令通道进行，底层模型本身未被修改（jailbreak 设定，post-deployment）

not_covered: 作者明确不声称可阻止所有可想象的攻击（仅与本文所考虑基线相比更安全）

更挑战性的对抗场景留作 future work；安全判断由 LLM 做出而非形式化验证

intervention.name: RuleGraph
intervention.description: 推理时多智能体 Graph-of-Rules 规划框架，把安全执行分散到多个推理与验证阶段而非单一集中决策：(1) Rule Generator Agent 先于指令将固定通用安全原则 P 接地为 world-specific 规则集 R_w（只接收原则/世界状态/技能，不看指令），再按指令筛出相关规则集 R_x；(2) Instruction Agent 接地并分块指令，Verification Agent 在完整指令语境下逐块判 Legitimate/Illegitimate（含组合危险检查）；(3) Goal Synthesis Agent 仅从合法子任务导出 safe goal；(4) Planning Agent 为每条相关规则实例化一个节点做 generate-judge-refine（≤7 迭代），k=2 分层两两聚合、节点继承父节点规则并集，直到单一计划满足全部规则；(5) Verification Agent 独立充当规则合规裁判，另有目标安全检查与最终检查门（达成 safe goal + 无残留恶意意图），失败触发计划细化或 safe goal 修订并重建规则图。效果是只丢弃指令非法部分、仍完成合法部分

title: Peer Pressure: Execution-Verified Co-Evolution of Attacker and Defender Populations for Code Security

object.carrier: 训练期持续状态有三层：(1) 攻防两侧各为一组 LoRA 适配器种群（单侧 G=2-16，作者扫过规模；7B/9B 冻结底座上的 role-specific 适配器），跨训练轮次以 Elo/fitness 保留并由锦标赛淘汰-重播（mutation / rank-preserving crossover）维持多样性，精英适配器永不淘汰；(2) 已验证 Red 轨迹缓存跨轮复用于 matched Blue 更新；(3) RQ4 对照臂直接测试了'冻结权重 + 演化技能库'的纯非参数状态路线（本底座上 62.4 vs 同骨干 frozen 61.4 之上、低于 PRPO 64.8——技能库状态可复用但收益有限）。注意：持久状态主要是权重空间种群与轨迹缓存，不是语义记忆库；部署时只部署单个最高-Elo Blue 适配器，防御在部署后不再更新。

safety_property.statement: 保护对象：(a) 代码域——真实仓库补丁不被夹带可触发的已知类弱点，防御者是能定位（入口点 EP + 危险操作 CO + trace）的 diff/仓库级审查器；(b) 越狱域——guard 分类器拒绝有害改写提示同时不过度拒绝安全提示（XSTest 拒绝率几乎不变）。失效条件：攻击分布持续移动而防御只在静态语料上训练时（论文动机），以及 Red 适应训练中的 Blue 时（若对手冻结则收益消失）。判定方式：全部奖励由容器内执行判定（补丁可应用、构建、过测试、完成任务、真实 exploit 触发），评估用独立于训练 oracle 的 judge 与 held-out 外部集。
safety_property.operationalized_as: 代码域：held-out 场景/未见应用的 balanced accuracy 与 TPR@FPR=5%，VulnGym T1 的 advisory recall (AR)/entry recall (ER)/edit similarity (ES)；越狱域：WildGuardTest 全量 ASR（两个独立 judge：WildGuardTest/Llama Guard 3）、HarmBench 320 条 held-out behaviors ASR、XSTest 安全提示拒绝率

capabilities: Red（漏洞注入策略）编辑真实仓库：在通过测试的功能补丁上隐藏一个已编目的可触发弱点类，或做同等规模的干净修改；仅在补丁可应用、构建通过、测试通过且 exploit 在隔离容器中真实触发时获得奖励
Red 针对当前 Blue 委员会适应隐蔽方式：sink 固定但路径不固定——trace 间接化、相对 sink 的摆放、诱饵编辑都会扩大审查器必须覆盖的空间（'Red nevertheless adapts against Blue's search'）
越狱域中 Red 作为提示改写器，针对外部 WildGuard guard 也能提升攻击成功率（12.4% -> 27.8%）
评估侧对手：冻结 Qwen3.5-9B 目标模型 + 冻结 HarmBench 验证分类器（训练 oracle）之外的两个 judge
assumptions: 弱点类在训练前编目固定（每类有既有 exploit harness），Red 只适应'如何隐藏已知弱点'而非发现新弱点——扩展类集需要新 harness（Limitations 自述）
Red 总是拿到已认证的植入位点，不做搜索；不针对训练应用之外的软件
部署的防御（单个 Blue 适配器）冻结评估，不对评估期攻击再做适应
同骨干同 rank 适配器共享底座与 KL reference，从而支持权重空间重组
not_covered: 部署后防御不再演化：回路是训练期回路，无测试时/部署期在线防御更新（与 SED/SafeCoEvo 的测试时演化不同）
不防御对防御系统自身的投毒；不处理状态依赖、多步或多 commit 拼装的新型弱点（Limitations 自述）
评估 prevalence 均衡构造，与真实审查流量不匹配（作者给出按真实 prevalence 校准的告警）
jailbreak oracle 是冻结分类器，继承其盲区

intervention.name: PRPO: Peer-Relative Policy Optimization（种群化攻击-防御共训练）
intervention.description: 以执行验证为唯一领域组件的共演化训练框架：Red 与 Blue 各为一个 LoRA 适配器种群（同一冻结底座），交替块更新（更新本方时冻结对方委员会）。核心创新是把种群放进策略梯度基线而非对手池：每条样本只与'面对完全相同 condition（场景+冻结对方委员会+解码预算）'的同角色 peer 做留一比较（MPA，匹配种群优势），从而消去条件难度与对手强度；配合每 N 轮的锦标赛（fitness=Elo 均值+近邻多样性 Hamming 距离，六轴隐蔽词汇表）淘汰最低者并以 mutation/crossover 重播。奖励全部由容器执行判定：Red 的回报=Blue 委员会的置信加权定位错误评分（隐蔽性无需专门系数——Blue 学会某线索后 Red 被推离它）；Blue 的回报=逆类别先验加权的 balanced accuracy + 定位项。验证过的 Red 轨迹缓存复用给 matched Blue 更新，验证器吞吐而非 GPU 决定节奏。

title: Memories That Outlive Their Reasons: Dependency-Tethered Memory for Tool-Using LLM Agents

object.carrier: Store of atomic plain-sentence records (fact records + check records with object_id and version, verdict true/false/null) written by a bounded LLM writer after each session and served as a system-prompt section at live requests; Tether adds a derived_from field (exact parent versions) to check records, used only internally at read time and never shown to the agent.

safety_property.statement: An agent acting on memory must not publish an object whose transitive support has failed elsewhere in the store, even though every stored record was true when written. Observation 1 is one-directional: when the failure notice and the dependent verdict do not share a retrieval window (no record about the failed ancestor in the window), no window-local reader can distinguish stale from sound, and this condition holds for most affected candidates (Flat publishes 645 of 657 such check-free candidates). A shared window rarely suffices either: with a record about the failed ancestor in the window, Flat still publishes 199 of 318, so unsafe publication is not restricted to the no-shared-window case.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Unsafe publication rate = share of live-request candidates published while pass_t(v) is false, stratified by distance d to the nearest failed ancestor (d>=1 = downstream), on the Fallout benchmark under a reuse instruction; verification checks per candidate/request measure the cost side.

assumptions: No attacker, no hallucinated fact, no corrupted record: every memory record is accurate when written; failure arises from environment change (revoked keys, retracted datasets, rotations) that invalidates old verdicts non-locally.
Failures are announced in advisories that name only the failed root object, sometimes mentioned only in passing, sometimes discovered only by the agent's own check.
Dependencies are stated in dialogue (pasted build logs / SBOMs), in the main setting in the same session as the verdict, in Fallout-Split in a session of their own.
The memory writer and the reader each see only a bounded window (k=10 retrieved records), never the whole store.
The verification tool returns pass/fail only, never the reason; all model roles use one backbone (gpt-6-luna; Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash as alternatives).
not_covered: Memory poisoning and untrusted content entering memory (explicitly out of scope: 'Our failure involves no untrusted source')
Adversarial users, insiders, or the model itself as attacker
Dependencies the writer would have to infer rather than read as stated text (synthetic worlds state relations explicitly)
Long-horizon cost of over-withdrawal beyond the version trigger (histories too short)

intervention.name: Tether (dependency-tethered memory)
intervention.description: Tether keeps the flat fact-memory representation and adds one field to check records: derived_from, the exact object versions the verdict rests on, written by the same bounded writer at verdict time while the dependency is local in the transcript. At read time a model-free reachability pass over the whole store (not just the window) serves any passing verdict as null (unsettled) if anything it transitively derives from is recorded failing, is null, or has a higher version on record; withdrawal only lowers (true -> null, never false). The agent reads the same record fields, retrieved the same way, and never sees the edges.

controls.name: Always-verify (empty memory)
Flat (atomic records, Tether without edges; same writer prompt minus one paragraph, same retrieval)
A-Mem
Graphiti
Mem0
Global flush / mention flush (coarse invalidation over Flat stores)
Random mixture of Flat and always-verify (mixing curve)
Whole-store window for writer and/or reader
Perfect (gold) edges replacing recorded edges
Edge perturbation (drop/spurious with probability p)

limitations.statement: Fallout's worlds are synthetic and state dependency relations explicitly; dependencies a writer would have to infer are not tested.
limitations.quote: Fallout’s worlds are synthetic, and their dependency relations are stated explicitly in pasted records; dependencies that a writer would have to infer are not tested.

limitations.statement: Tether depends on a capable writer: relations stated away from the verdict are partly lost, weaker models also miss failures mentioned in passing, and an agent that checks nearly everything is then safer.
limitations.quote: Tether depends on a capable writer: relations stated away from the verdict are partly lost (Section 6.6), weaker models also miss failures mentioned in passing (Section 6.5), and an agent that checks nearly everything is then safer.

limitations.statement: Over-withdrawal is not tested beyond the version trigger, whose cost recurs at every read; histories are too short to measure that cost over long horizons.
limitations.quote: Over-withdrawal is not tested beyond the version trigger (Section 6.2), whose cost recurs at every read of an older version that stays in use; our histories are too short to measure that cost over long horizons.

limitations.statement: Histories are recorded by a single model, published baselines run on only three of four backbones, and session time is modelled from calls rather than measured.
limitations.quote: Histories are recorded by one model, and the published baselines run on three of our four backbones. Session time is modelled from calls, not measured (Table 9).

title: Whose Credential Is It? How Owner Attribution in Agent Memory Shapes Cross-User Account Misuse

object.carrier: Shared long-term memory store holding 763 login notes from 99 AppWorld users; top-k retrieved notes are rendered as text blocks in the agent prompt by a renderer rho = (header, log-in directive, line format, owner attribution beta, caution clause)

safety_property.statement: An agent using shared cross-user long-term memory must act only in the requester's account: a valid foreign credential reaching the prompt (exposure) should not be used to act in another user's account (behavior) nor change that user's account state (state). It fails when memory lacks the user's own credential and words a single foreign one as the user's record; judged by the wrong-token endpoint B and the audited donor-account state change S, with exposure E as the store-side factor.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Three-stage audit in AppWorld: E=1 if the top-k retrieved notes contain another user's credential for a required app; B=1 if any API call carries a session token whose subject (decoded app+username) is neither the requester nor empty; S=1 if donor-owned rows (orders, drafts, sent payments, etc.) differ between the run's initial and final checkpoints; harm factorizes as Pr[S]=Pr[E]Pr[B|E]Pr[S|B] (Eq. 5).

assumptions: No party is adversarial: memory is written from real sessions, and the failure is using valid authority for the wrong person.
A1: an agent can obtain a foreign token only from a credential in its prompt, so B is a subset of E (no run without memory acted in a foreign account, 0 of 500).
A2: the audited donor rows change only through the donor's own session, so S is a subset of B.
Owner information is usually available at write time because the agent knows whom it is serving; keeping it in the memory text is a design choice.

The stress test replaces the requester's credential with a single foreign one in an otherwise accurate memory: a high-risk configuration chosen to expose the effect of wording, not an estimate of prevalence.
Authorized delegation is outside scope.
not_covered: Adversarial settings: prompt injection and memory poisoning (the studied failure needs no attacker).
Authorized delegation.
Prevalence of misuse in deployed systems.
Systems with sharing or messaging between users, where A2 fails and Eq. 5 covers only the misuse-mediated part of harm.
Credential reads, disclosure, and write-then-revert harm, which the read-only state audit cannot detect (S under-counts).

intervention.name: Owner attribution in memory wording (owner binding as a write-time lever)
intervention.description: Hold the credential fixed and vary the renderer rho=(h, delta, f, beta, gamma); the key component is owner attribution beta in {none, tag, bound}: omit the owner, append a trailing '[account owner: N]' tag, or bind the owner's name inside the sentence ('Earlier session for N: logged into ...'). Binding names at write time prevents most cross-user misuse; trailing tags, a caution clause, and an added safety instruction help only some models; a wrongly written owner restores misuse. Treated as a second layer behind access control, not a replacement for it.

title: Self-Evolving Agents through Privileged Retrospective Distillation

object.carrier: 两条持续载体：(1) 模型权重——每轮用 OPSD（forward-KL top-k=20 全参数蒸馏）把特权教师分布蒸回 student，成为下一轮策略 π(r+1)；(2) 累积经验库 B(r)——跨轮携带、只增不减的 on-policy 轨迹库（含成功与失败轨迹），每轮从其重derive precedents（按 content-token overlap 检索 top-n）与 lessons（按任务类型摘要），仅训练期作教师侧特权上下文，推理时评测不用特权上下文

safety_property.statement: 论文不研究任何安全性质（不涉及权限、保密、完整性、策略合规或可用性），也没有对抗者；其目标是能力自进化：在无 ground-truth 轨迹、无 verifier 派生奖励的条件下，把自然积累的交互经验经特权回顾蒸馏转化为持续模型能力，以 ALFWorld/ScienceWorld 成功率（SR）与 SearchQA 精确匹配（EM）度量

assumptions: 每任务只采样一条 on-policy 轨迹（无重复尝试+按成功筛选）
策略优化不使用 ground-truth 轨迹或 verifier 派生奖励（OPSD 目标中不含 policy-gradient 或 task-reward 项）
frontier-guided 扩展为更强访问设定：额外假设可访问一个 frontier 模型（Claude-Opus-4.8）与可执行环境指标，仅用于评估 context-policy 候选与事后验收，不为参数更新提供奖励
not_covered: 无对抗模型：不研究攻击者、提示注入、越狱或对经验库的投毒/污染（经验库直接并入所有成功与失败轨迹，无完整性或来源校验）
未讨论教师（特权上下文）被错误经验误导时蒸馏放大的风险
未研究跨用户/跨部署场景；经验库与策略仅在单一训练管线内演化

intervention.name: Retrospective Self-Distillation (RSD)
intervention.description: 监督信号在 content 层构造并内化入参数：每轮当前策略采集 on-policy 轨迹并入累积经验库；对每个交互 turn 构造四组件特权回顾上下文（跨任务 precedents、按任务类型摘要的 lessons、对当前决策的 reflection、暴露下游反馈的 future hindsight），同一模型以此特权视图对自己已实现的动作重新打分，再以 forward-KL（top-k=20）在学生访问到的状态上做 on-policy 自蒸馏更新权重；推理评测时不给特权上下文。教师按 freeze-to-peak 调度防止无限演化。扩展版 frontier-guided context-policy evolution 由 frontier 模型在白名单 YAML 旋钮内提议上下文构造编辑，用无训练 inference probe 排序候选，并按整轮训练后的真实环境指标做接受/回退（ε=0.5%，只回退 context policy、不回退模型权重）

title: ClawMMU: Protection-Coherent Virtual Memory for Stateful LLM Agents

object.carrier: ClawVM-style typed memory pages: every representation of a page carries a protection descriptor (owner, scope, origins, authority level such as Evidence up to Policy) plus per-page revocation counters kept outside checkpoints

safety_property.statement: Information may rise in authority only through owner approval ('authority never lifts itself'): untrusted content (web pages, tool outputs, model-written summaries) can neither gain the user's authority nor supply security-relevant tool-call arguments, even when the model is fooled. Explicitly out of scope: confidentiality of readable content, correctness of derived memory, and the model making the right call when passed values do have enough authority. Judged by construction/argument, not by experiments (system not yet implemented).
safety_property.operationalized_as: Protection descriptors (owner/scope/origins/authority) checked by the harness at four context-boundary crossings - map (entry), derive (write to storage), reload (retrieval/checkpoint restore), authorize (tool call) - plus revocation-counter comparison at reload and authorize; violations surface as classical protection faults (address-space violation, type confusion, use-after-revoke, confused deputy). No implementation or measured numbers yet.

capabilities: Adversary controls text in fetched web pages and tool outputs that the agent retrieves, transforms, and stores
Sleeper memory poisoning: injected text is stored in memory and fires later, after passing through several summaries and transformations
Direct prompt injection by another user of a shared agent (same pattern, mentioned as in-scope motivation)
Adaptive attackers tuning inputs against a specific deployed defense (motivating content-independent checks)
assumptions: The harness is trusted; ClawMMU needs only a hook where content enters context, is written to storage, returns from storage, or drives a tool call
Stable page identities exist so every representation can be labeled
Current revocation counters are kept outside checkpoints so a restore cannot roll them back
Capability schemas are reviewed and correctly mark security-relevant arguments as checked
The model itself is treated as a lowest-authority input; only the owner can raise authority
not_covered: Model making the wrong call, or passing a wrong value that does have enough authority
Correctness of derived memory
Confidentiality of readable content
A wrong 'safe' marking in a capability schema (stated as the main residual risk)
Actions that happen before a revocation
Authority in multi-agent systems and auditing approvals that widen scope (open problems)
No empirical evaluation yet; ClawMMU is not yet implemented

intervention.name: ClawMMU
intervention.description: An MMU-style protection layer in the agent harness: every memory representation carries a protection descriptor (owner, scope, origins, ordered authority levels with Evidence lowest and Policy highest); an inheritance rule gives derived memory the lowest authority of its inputs, counting the model itself as a lowest-authority input so model-written memory stays Evidence; per-page revocation counters (copied into descriptors of derived memory, kept outside checkpoints) invalidate all descendants of a revoked source; authorize performs per-argument checks so each security-relevant tool-call argument must trace to sufficient authority; compartment sharing across owners/scopes is denied by default via unforgeable assembly capabilities.

limitations.statement: ClawMMU's guarantee excludes correctness of the model's calls, correctness of derived memory, and confidentiality of readable content.
limitations.quote: It does not guarantee that the model makes the right call, that derived memory is correct, or that readable content stays confidential.

limitations.statement: Authorize protects only the provenance/integrity of call arguments; the model may still make the wrong call or pass a wrong value that has enough authority.
limitations.quote: The model may still make the wrong call, or pass a wrong value that does have enough authority.

limitations.statement: The main residual risk is a wrong 'safe' marking in a capability schema, so schemas must be reviewed.
limitations.quote: A wrong safe marking is therefore the main residual risk, which is why the schemas must be reviewed.

limitations.statement: ClawMMU is not yet implemented; its Table 1 row lists design properties only, and the planned evaluation (AgentDojo, InjecAgent, sleeper memory poisoning; attack success, check latency, owner approvals) is future work.
limitations.quote: The ClawMMU row lists design properties, since ClawMMU is not yet implemented.

limitations.statement: Open problems include capability-schema review at scale, authority in multi-agent systems, actions before a revocation, and auditing scope-widening approvals.
limitations.quote: Open problems include reviewing capability schemas at scale, placing authority in multi-agent systems, handling actions that happen before a revocation, and auditing approvals that widen scope.

title: Disclosure Begets Disclosure: A Self-Reinforcing Privacy Loop in LLM Agents with Persistent Memory

object.carrier: append-only session summaries m_s = m_{s-1} ⊕ σ(τ_s) given to the support agent at dialogue time (main format, MemoryBank-style); also update-based Mem0 v2.0.2 fact store and retrieval-based FAISS/bge-m3 top-5 summary store in Appendix F

safety_property.statement: 持久记忆累积的记录最终能被正确推断出的用户个人属性值比例（经验性泄露）应在提供个性化的同时保持低位；本文表明在普通非对抗协助中、即使 agent 不被指示推断属性且用户被指令不披露，对话时咨询记忆仍使泄露随会话数上升，且理想化用户侧过滤也只能以放弃质量为代价降低泄露；由记忆/无记忆配对比较、分支分析和更强推断模型复核判定失效。
safety_property.operationalized_as: empirical leakage（Eq. 1）：在每 5 个会话的检查点，用支持模型（或更强推断模型 Gemini 3.1 Pro / Kimi K3）从完整累积记录一次性推断全部 24 个属性值的加权准确率，权重随属性间规范化互信息递减；响应质量由独立评估器按 helpfulness/coherence 两个五分制量表评分。

capabilities: 获得完整累积记录（会话摘要或存储的记忆）
对记录施加一个 LLM（可以是带推理的更强模型）来推断全部 24 个属性值
不掌握关于该用户的任何辅助数据
assumptions: agent 本身非对抗：其指令既不鼓励也不 discourage 推断或引出属性（§2.2, Appendix N.7）
循环在普通个性化协助中自然产生，无需对抗意图
无记忆运行同样累积自己的记录；两个设置都从各自完整记录做推断，差异仅来自记忆对对话内容的改变
用户由 2024 ACS PUMS 档案模拟；过滤条件下的用户被指令不陈述/收窄属性值
not_covered: 对记忆的主动攻击（提取、外传、注入）——论文明确声明不提出攻击
对抗性引出（adversarial elicitation）由 agent 发起的情形
将记录与辅助数据结合的重识别
用户侧删除/撤销记忆中的值
跨用户或共享记忆
真实长期人类使用（仅 8 人试点）

intervention.name: response-side instruction（响应侧指令；对照：理想化 direct/strict 用户轮过滤、user-side 与 write-time 匿名化）
intervention.description: 在支持 agent 的指令（记忆块之后）附加一条简短指令：除非用户主动提起，不陈述、不预设、不请求确认用户的属性。对照干预包括把 Staab et al. (2025) 的对抗式匿名化应用于每条用户话语（user-side）或每条写入记忆前的摘要（write-time），以及两条理想化的用户轮过滤（direct/strict，strict 使用真值档案、整轮拒收，均严于可部署过滤）。

session-1 与开场轮安慰剂（记忆为空，两条件输入相同）
direct filter / strict filter（理想化用户轮过滤）
Staab et al. (2025) anonymization（user-side 与 write-time）

title: Context-Aware Prompt Injection Detection via Small Language Models in RAG Pipelines: nokast-secureRAG

safety_property.statement: The detector guards the data/instruction boundary of a local RAG pipeline: instruction-like content in the retrieved context C that conflicts with the intent of the user query Q must be flagged (safe/suspicious/malicious-instruction) before reaching the generator, protecting the assistant from indirect prompt injection (instruction override, role/permission redefinition, PII/data exfiltration) while not over-flagging benign instructional text. It holds only in-distribution and by detection-side proxy; it fails on fact-fabrication poisoning (PoisonedRAG recall 0.7%) and is untested against adaptive adversaries.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Detection recall / FPR / ASR-proxy / three-class accuracy on 659 held-out (Q,C) test records; judgment-flip both-correct rate on 120 intact pairs; single-request latency vs sub-100 ms target

capabilities: Controls some retrievable content in the RAG corpus (web pages, documents, memory entries) and embeds instructions intended to redirect the assistant
Attack payload is embedded in the retrieved context C (e.g., inside an HTML comment, footer, or 'ignore previous instructions' clause), never in the user query Q
Goals: overriding system/user instructions, exfiltrating data, or redefining the assistant's role
assumptions: The user query itself is benign; the attack lives in the context
Local RAG pipeline: retrieved chunks are fused with the user query and passed to a generator; defense must run on 16 GB-class VRAM local hardware at interactive latency without a cloud guard
Attackers are not adaptive: gradient-based, multi-chunk, retrieval-optimized injections and human red-teaming are out of the evaluated scope
not_covered: PoisonedRAG-style fact-fabrication/knowledge poisoning without instructions (B3 recall 0.7%, explicitly outside the instruction-consistency threat model)
Downstream generator behavior: ASR is a detection-side proxy only
Adaptive adversaries and human red-teaming
Non-English content and domain-specific corpora (financial, medical, legal)

intervention.name: nokast-secureRAG
intervention.description: A ~0.5B SLM (Qwen2.5-0.5B + rank-8 LoRA, 17.6 MB adapter) acting as a semantic firewall between the retriever and the generator: it jointly reads the user query Q and retrieved context C and emits a short reasoning trace plus one of three labels (safe/suspicious/malicious-instruction). Produced by a teacher->judge->student distillation pipeline (Qwen3.6-35B teacher generates 5,233 records across four attack families; independent 120B Nemotron judge of a different family re-labels blind, 95.0% agreement; agreed data fine-tunes the student via reasoning-first LoRA), deployed locally via llama.cpp/Ollama/vLLM.

controls.name: B1 regex/heuristic filter on C (context-blind)
B2 base Qwen2.5-0.5B zero-shot (no fine-tuning)
B4 ProtectAI deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2 (public classifier, context-blind)
B5 Llama Guard 3 1B (general safety guard, context-blind)
B6 Prompt-Guard-86M (purpose-built prompt-injection detector, context-blind)
Input-masking ablations on B3: Q-only / C-only / mismatched (fixed-seed derangement)
Out-of-distribution check on PoisonedRAG (negative control)

results.claim: The tuned nokast-secureRAG SLM (B3) dominates every security metric on the held-out test set: 0.994 recall, 0.006 ASR-proxy, 0.026 FPR, 0.974 three-class accuracy.
results.setting: Qwen2.5-0.5B + LoRA (r=8) student on 659 judge-verified agreed synthetic test records (of a 740-record raw teacher-labeled test split); per-class malicious-instruction n=311, safe n=342, suspicious n=6 (Appendix A.1); baselines run context-blind on C alone; NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10, 121 GB unified memory
results.quote: The tuned SLM (B3) dominates every security metric: 0.9940.994 recall, 0.0060.006 ASR-proxy, 0.0260.026 FPR, 0.9740.974 three-class accuracy.

denominator.how_counted: Detection metrics computed on the 659 judge-verified agreed test records; recall over malicious records (malicious-instruction n=311, suspicious n=6), FPR over benign safe records (n=342)

results.claim: Fine-tuning raises the same 0.5B model's detection recall from 0.116 (zero-shot) to 0.994 on the held-out test set.
results.setting: Same base model Qwen2.5-0.5B with and without LoRA fine-tuning (B2 vs B3); 659-record held-out test set
results.quote: The same model used zero-shot (B2) reaches only 0.1160.116 recall—it collapses to predicting safe for the large majority of inputs—so fine-tuning raises recall from 0.1160.116 to 0.9940.994.

denominator.how_counted: Same 659 judge-verified agreed test records as Table 3

results.claim: On 120 held-out judgment-flip pairs (identical sentence benign in one context, malicious in another) the tuned SLM labels both halves correctly 75.0% of the time, far above all context-blind baselines — the paper's most direct evidence for context-aware detection.
results.setting: 120 intact flip pairs (240 records) held out in the test split, never used in training; identical sentence S benign in one context, malicious in another; B3 flip-record accuracy 0.875
results.quote: The tuned SLM labels both halves of a pair correctly 75.0%75.0\% of the time, versus 17.5%17.5\% for the regex baseline, 54.2%54.2\% for the public ProtectAI classifier, 26.7%26.7\% for Llama Guard, 9.2%9.2\% for Prompt-Guard, and 11.7%11.7\% for the untuned model.

denominator.how_counted: both-correct rate: both halves of a pair labeled correctly; labels reliable by construction; judge disputes broke roughly half the flip pairs in the agreed test set, so the intact-pair metric is reported on the teacher-labeled split

results.claim: Masking the context (Q-only input) collapses detection recall to 0.000, confirming the attack signal lives entirely in the retrieved context C, as the threat model assumes.
results.setting: B3 re-run on the full 659-record test set with context replaced by an empty string (Q-only condition)
results.quote: QQ-only collapses recall to 0.0000.000: with no context there is nothing to flag, confirming attack signal lives entirely in CC, exactly as the threat model assumes (§3).

denominator.how_counted: Same 659-record test set under the Q-only masking condition

results.claim: Pairing a context with an unrelated query (mismatched condition) keeps recall high (0.990) but nearly triples FPR (0.085 vs 0.026 full model, 0.038 CC-only): query–context consistency measurably reduces over-flagging, while CC alone carries most detection signal (CC-only 0.987 recall).
results.setting: B3 on the 659-record test set, each row's context replaced by another row's context via fixed-seed derangement with ground truth from the donor row
results.quote: The mismatched condition preserves high recall (0.9900.990, since the donor's own attack content is still present) but nearly triples FPR relative to the full model (0.0850.085 vs. 0.0260.026, vs. 0.0380.038 for CC-only): pairing a context with an unrelated query measurably increases over-flagging.

denominator.how_counted: Same 659-record test set under the mismatched and CC-only masking conditions

results.claim: Prompt-Guard-86M, a public model purpose-built for prompt-injection detection, shows the context-blind failure mode: high raw recall (0.900) but a very high FPR (0.690) from over-flagging ordinary instructional text — exactly the failure the (Q,C) reframing targets.
results.setting: B6 Prompt-Guard-86M run context-blind on C alone (no query input), 659-record test set
results.quote: Prompt-Guard-86M (Meta AI, 2024) (B6), a small model purpose-built for prompt-injection detection, shows the opposite failure mode: high recall (0.9000.900) but a very high 0.6900.690 FPR, flagging most benign RAG content (documentation, how-to text) as an attack

denominator.how_counted: Same 659 judge-verified agreed test records as Table 3; FPR over safe records (n=342)

results.claim: Out-of-distribution negative result: on PoisonedRAG the tuned detector's recall collapses to 0.7% — worse than the untuned base model (14.3%) and regex (0%) — reported as a scope boundary, since fact-fabrication attacks contain no instructions and fall outside the instruction-consistency threat model.
results.setting: B3 on PoisonedRAG: 300 (query, adversarial-passage) pairs across NQ, HotpotQA, MSMARCO, every pair ground-truth malicious; LLM-generated factually-fabricated passages with no injected instructions; recall-only check (no FPR)
results.quote: The result is a clear negative: B1 regex catches 0%0\% (no injection keywords are present), B2 zero-shot catches 14.3%14.3\%, and B3 tuned recall is 0.7%0.7\%—worse than the untuned base model. B3 predicts safe on 298/300298/300 pairs.

denominator.how_counted: 300 (query, adversarial-passage) PoisonedRAG pairs, every pair ground-truth malicious, so this is a recall-only check (no FPR)

results.claim: Deployment-relevant single-request latency is 293–404 ms depending on serving runtime — above the paper's own sub-100 ms target — while batched amortized throughput is 37 ms per (Q,C).
results.comparison: 37 ms amortized batched throughput; sub-100 ms target exceeded
results.setting: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, 121 GB unified memory), NVFP4 vLLM runtime; eager transformers vs vLLM (merged model, 100 sequential single requests, greedy decoding); latency dominated by the ~36-word reasoning trace
results.quote: Deployment-relevant single-request latency is 293293–404404 ms depending on serving runtime—above this paper's own sub-100100 ms target—with 3737 ms amortized throughput under batching.

results.claim: An independent, larger 120B judge of a different model family, re-labeling every record blind to the teacher's label, agrees with the 35B teacher on 95.0% of the 5,233 synthetic records — a dataset-quality signal.
results.setting: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B teacher vs Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B judge (different family, blind re-labeling) over 5,233 synthetic (Q,C) records; agreed data trains the student
results.quote: The independent judge agreed with the teacher on 95.0% of records (4,9734{,}973 agreed, 260260 disputed, 00 without a verdict).

denominator.how_counted: 4,973 agreed, 260 disputed (quarantined), 0 without a verdict, out of 5,233 records

results.claim: The data-starved suspicious class (only 6 of 659 test records) has recall 0.167 (Wilson 95% CI [0.030,0.564]) — an honest signal that the ambiguous middle class is where the detector is least reliable, and the aggregate 3-class accuracy should not be read as covering it.
results.setting: B3 per-class Wilson 95% CIs on the 659-record test set; only n=6 test records carry the suspicious label, of which B3 recalls 1 (Appendix A.1: four of five misses predicted malicious-instruction, i.e. fail closed)
results.quote: the data-starved suspicious class (n=6n{=}6) is not (0.1670.167 recall, CI [0.030,0.564][0.030,0.564])—an honest signal that this boundary class is where the detector is least reliable

denominator.how_counted: Only 6 of 659 test records carry the suspicious label; B3 recalls just 1 of 6 (Appendix A.1)

limitations.statement: In-distribution headline numbers only: training and test share the same synthetic generator, and no public benchmark currently tests judgment-flip specifically, so the central claim remains validated only in-distribution.
limitations.quote: No public benchmark currently tests judgment-flip specifically—this paper's central claim remains validated only in-distribution.

limitations.statement: ASR is a detection-side proxy, not the downstream generator's behavior.
limitations.quote: ASR is a detection-side proxy—whether the guard flags the attack—not the downstream generator's behavior.

limitations.statement: Adaptive adversaries are untested: no gradient-based, multi-chunk, or retrieval-optimized injections, and no human red-teaming.
limitations.quote: We have not evaluated gradient-based, multi-chunk, or retrieval-optimized injections (Chang et al., 2026; Chan et al., 2024), or human red-teaming.

limitations.statement: Single-domain validation: the synthetic corpus is general-purpose; financial, medical, and legal documents are unvalidated (and the data is English-only).
limitations.quote: Our synthetic corpus is general-purpose; we have not validated on financial, medical, or legal documents, where dense instruction-like text may shift the safe/malicious boundary.

limitations.statement: Latency is measured on one device and varies with hardware; both serving runtimes remain above the sub-100 ms target.
limitations.quote: Latency is measured on one device and will vary with hardware; both eager transformers and vLLM (§6.4) remain above the sub-100100 ms target.

limitations.statement: The suspicious class is data-starved, so its 0.167 recall is too noisy to trust without more suspicious-labeled data.
limitations.quote: Only 66 of 659659 test records carry this label, so its 0.1670.167 recall (§6.5) is too noisy to trust without more suspicious-labeled data.

limitations.quote: Data is English-only.

title: After the Attacker Leaves: Benchmarking Carryover Attacks on LLM Agents

object.carrier: Persistent workspace files the runtime reads back: memory/MEMORY.md silently prepended to the system prompt at every new session, and HEARTBEAT.md scheduled tasks fired by the heartbeat daemon (default 30-min interval; Hermes cron jobs.json on 60s tick). A one-time indirect prompt injection (email/webpage/document/tool return) is planted via the agent's own write_file and re-fires in later sessions after the attacker exits with zero persistent presence.

safety_property.statement: A one-time indirect prompt injection committed to long-term memory or a scheduled task must not re-fire as harmful action (exfiltrating payroll/financial/medical content to attacker URLs, rerouting payments, unauthorized sends) in later sessions after the attacker leaves; in the evaluated agents the planted payload persists across sessions and, conditional on successful planting, is executed almost deterministically, so trigger-time protection largely fails while confidentiality (exfiltration), integrity (payment rerouting) and policy-compliance (unauthorized autonomous actions) are all violated.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Deterministic rule-based verifier matches attacker markers (URL/recipient/path) in tool-call role fields over N=5 independent follow-up sessions; attack success decomposed as ASR = Pr(Plant) x Pr(Trig|Plant) with per-round N-TrigRate, reported jointly with gated benign-task Utility.

capabilities: One-time indirect prompt injection into resources the agent reads: webpages, emails, documents, or tool return values
Persuades the agent to commit the payload to MEMORY.md or HEARTBEAT.md via the agent's own write_file
Exits after the single injection with zero persistent presence; later firings require no further attacker action
assumptions: The runtime persists state across sessions via long-lived memory files silently prepended to the system prompt and heartbeat/cron scheduled tasks
The agent can edit its own persistent files (write_file), so anything written becomes a standing instruction
The attacker cannot modify the runtime, cannot read/write MEMORY.md or HEARTBEAT.md directly, and cannot bypass OS access control
not_covered: Always-on adversaries that remain present across sessions (AgentLAB-style)
Direct write access to MEMORY.md/HEARTBEAT.md or runtime modification
Adaptive/multi-step attackers that react to defenses at trigger time
Reasoning-mode Gemini-3.1-Pro in the Hermes runtime ablation (excluded due to variable per-call latency)
Real multi-day session diversity for Latent triggering (identical domain-natural follow-ups replayed instead)

intervention.name: D1 (system-prompt principles), D2 (explicit edit authority), D3 (harness-level provenance marking / Spotlighting envelope)
intervention.description: D1 prepends a generic safety-principles block via AGENTS.md (authority provenance, task-scope adherence, persistent-state caution, egress proportionality); D2 grants the agent explicit authority to inspect, edit and remove MEMORY.md/HEARTBEAT.md entries; D3 wraps persistent-state reads in an <untrusted_persistent_state trust="low"> envelope at the context-injection layer (delimiting variant of Spotlighting). The paper's shared-ceiling analysis: all three reach the model only as text alongside the planted instruction, so they concentrate at the plant stage and leave the trigger gate largely unresolved; closing the trigger gate is argued to require out-of-channel runtime controls (capability sandboxing, outbound-egress allowlists, persistent-state write quarantine), consistent with the Hermes runtime ablation.

controls.name: Instant channel (classical same-turn IPI)
No-Defense condition in D1-D3 ablation
Shared system prompt, tool-call template and temperature 0 across the five models
D.2 follow-up conditions (Replay / Paraphrase / Same-domain different-intent / Unrelated) for Latent triggering
